ShipSec Studio is a workflow automation platform designed for security operations and IT automation tasks. It provides a visual workflow builder interface, reliable execution via Temporal, and AI agent integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The platform enables teams to create, execute, and monitor complex automation workflows without writing code, while also supporting extensibility through a component SDK. This document provides a high-level introduction to ShipSec Studio's architecture, components, and operational model. For detailed information about specific subsystems, refer to: - Workflow system design and compilation: [Workflow System](#2) - Component architecture and execution: [Component System](#3) - AI agent and MCP integration: [AI and MCP Integration](#4) - Deployment and infrastructure: [Infrastructure and Deployment](#9) --- ## Platform Purpose and Capabilities ShipSec Studio combines three core capabilities: 1. **Visual Workflow Design**: A React Flow-based canvas for building directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of automation tasks, with real-time validation and type checking. 2. **Reliable Execution**: Temporal-based orchestration that provides durable execution, automatic retries, and state persistence for long-running workflows. 3. **AI Tool Integration**: Model Context Protocol (MCP) support that allows AI agents to dynamically discover and invoke workflow components as tools, enabling agentic automation patterns. The platform is organized as a monorepo with three primary services (frontend, backend, worker) and shared packages for contracts and SDKs. It supports both manual workflow execution and automated triggers via schedules, webhooks, and GitHub events. **Sources:** [package.json:1-68](), [bun.lock:1-350](), Diagram 1 from high-level system architecture --- ## System Architecture ### Three-Tier Service Model ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend Service" UI["React Application

Nodes are rendered using the `WorkflowNode` component, which displays component metadata, status, and handles. The `ConfigPanel` provides parameter configuration when a node is selected. State is divided into: - `workflowStore`: Design-time state (nodes, edges, viewport) - `executionStore`: Runtime state (node status, run metadata) - `workflowUiStore`: UI mode toggle (design vs. execution) - `executionTimelineStore`: Timeline playback state **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:1-133](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/WorkflowNode.tsx:1-8](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:1-100](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:1-50](), [frontend/src/store/workflowStore.ts](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts]() ### Backend Service Architecture The backend is a NestJS application that exposes RESTful APIs with OpenAPI documentation. Dispatching execution via the `TemporalService` The compilation process (`compileWorkflowGraph`) transforms the `WorkflowGraphDto` (nodes and edges) into a `WorkflowDefinition` with topologically sorted actions and dependency metadata. **Sources:** [backend/package.json:1-95](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/compile.ts](), [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts]() ### Worker Service Architecture The worker runs Temporal activities that execute workflow components. It uses service adapters to interact with infrastructure services. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Temporal Worker" Worker["Worker

Each action is executed by `runComponentActivity`, which: 1. Looks up the component in the registry 2. Resolves inputs (from other action outputs or manual overrides) 3. Executes the component via the appropriate runner 4. Persists outputs and trace events **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/runComponentActivity.ts](), [worker/src/components/index.ts:1-95](), [worker/src/adapters/]() --- ## Workflow Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Design: User opens Canvas Design --> Validation: Save workflow Validation --> Compilation: Validation passes Compilation --> Stored: compileWorkflowGraph Stored --> Execute: Manual run / Schedule trigger Execute --> Temporal: TemporalService.startWorkflow Temporal --> shipsecWorkflowRun: Workflow starts shipsecWorkflowRun --> WorkflowScheduler: Execute definition WorkflowScheduler --> runComponentActivity: Dispatch actions runComponentActivity --> ComponentExecution: Run component ComponentExecution --> TraceEvents: Emit progress TraceEvents --> SSE: Stream to frontend SSE --> ExecutionTimeline: Update UI ComponentExecution --> Completed: All succeed ComponentExecution --> Failed: Error occurred Completed --> [*] Failed --> [*] note right of Design Frontend: Canvas + WorkflowNode State: workflowStore (Zustand) Format: WorkflowGraphDto end note note right of Compilation Backend: compileWorkflowGraph Output: WorkflowDefinition Validation: type checking end note note right of WorkflowScheduler Worker: runWorkflowWithScheduler Strategy: Topological sort Join: all, any, first end note ``` **Phases:** 1. **Design**: User creates workflow in the Canvas using drag-and-drop. Nodes are stored in `workflowStore` as a `WorkflowGraphDto`. 2. **Validation**: Backend validates connections, required parameters, and type compatibility via `validateWorkflowGraph`. 3. **Compilation**: `compileWorkflowGraph` transforms the graph into a `WorkflowDefinition` with actions, dependencies, and join strategies. 4. **Execution**: Temporal workflow `shipsecWorkflowRun` executes the definition using `WorkflowScheduler` for dependency resolution. 5. **Monitoring**: Trace events are streamed via SSE to the `ExecutionTimeline` component for live visualization. **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:315-402](), [backend/src/workflows/compile.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/shipsecWorkflowRun.ts](), [worker/src/scheduler/WorkflowScheduler.ts]() --- ## Component System ShipSec Studio includes 190+ pre-built components organized into categories. Components are defined using the Component SDK and registered at worker startup. ### Component Categories | Category | Example Components | Purpose | |----------|-------------------|---------| | `core` | entry-point, http-request, logic-script | Workflow control flow and utilities | | `ai` | ai-agent, openai-provider, gemini-provider | AI model integration | | `security` | trufflehog, nuclei, prowler-scan | Security scanning tools | | `github` | clone-repo, post-pr-comment, pr-context | GitHub integration | | `it_ops` | google-workspace-license-unassign, okta-user-offboard | IT automation | | `notification` | slack | Alert and notification channels | **Sources:** [worker/src/components/index.ts:1-95](), [packages/shared/src/component-categories.ts]() ### Component Definition Structure Components are defined using the `ComponentDefinition` interface from the Component SDK: ```typescript interface ComponentDefinition { id: string; // e.g., "core.http-request" name: string; // Display name category: ComponentCategory; // Categorization inputs: InputPort[]; // Typed input ports outputs: OutputPort[]; // Typed output ports parameters: Parameter[]; // Configuration parameters execute: ExecuteFunction; // Implementation } ``` Each component receives an `ExecutionContext` with access to: - `logger`: Structured logging - `emitProgress`: Progress updates - `storage`: File storage (MinIO) - `secrets`: Encrypted secrets - `trace`: Event tracing - `http`: Fetch client **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts](), [worker/src/components/core/http-request.ts]() --- ## Data Flow and Persistence ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend State" Canvas["Canvas

(Frontend)"] ``` ### Persistence Layers 1. **Design-Time**: Workflow graphs are stored in the `workflows` table with full version history in `workflow_versions`. 2. **Execution State**: Temporal maintains workflow state, while metadata is stored in `workflow_runs`. Large payloads (>5MB) are spilled to MinIO. 3. **Observability**: Trace events are written to `execution_trace` and streamed via Kafka. Terminal output is buffered in Redis. 4. **Real-Time Updates**: Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream trace events and terminal output to the frontend's `ExecutionTimeline`. **Sources:** [backend/src/db/schema.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/shipsecWorkflowRun.ts](), [worker/src/adapters/file-storage.adapter.ts](), [worker/src/adapters/trace.adapter.ts]() --- ## Technology Stack ### Frontend Technologies | Technology | Purpose | Key Files | |-----------|---------|-----------| | React 19 | UI framework | [frontend/package.json:152]() | | Vite | Build tool | [frontend/vite.config.ts]() | | React Flow 11 | Graph visualization | [frontend/package.json:155]() | | Zustand | State management | [frontend/package.json:162]() | | TanStack Query | Server state | [frontend/package.json:134]() | | TypeScript 5.9 | Type safety | [frontend/package.json:190]() | ### Backend Technologies | Technology | Purpose | Key Files | |-----------|---------|-----------| | NestJS 10 | Application framework | [backend/package.json:28-32]() | | Temporal 1.14 | Workflow orchestration | [backend/package.json:40-42]() | | Drizzle ORM | Database access | [backend/package.json:54]() | | PostgreSQL | Primary database | [backend/package.json:63]() | | Redis | Caching, streams | [backend/package.json:56]() | | Bun | Runtime | [package.json:5]() | ### Worker Technologies | Technology | Purpose | Key Files | |-----------|---------|-----------| | Temporal Worker | Activity execution | [worker/package.json:36-40]() | | Component SDK | Component interface | [packages/component-sdk/]() | | MinIO | Object storage | [worker/package.json:50]() | | Kafka | Event streaming | [worker/package.json:48]() | | Docker | Container runtime | Via node-pty | **Sources:** [bun.lock:1-350](), [package.json:1-68](), [frontend/package.json:1-194](), [backend/package.json:1-95](), [worker/package.json:1-82]() --- ## Development Environment ### Monorepo Structure ``` shipsec-studio/ ├── frontend/ # React SPA (Vite) ├── backend/ # NestJS API server ├── worker/ # Temporal worker ├── packages/ │ ├── backend-client/ # OpenAPI-generated client │ ├── component-sdk/ # Component definition interfaces │ ├── contracts/ # Shared contracts │ └── shared/ # Shared utilities ├── docker/ # Docker Compose configs └── package.json # Workspace root ``` The monorepo uses Bun workspaces with shared dependencies. Each service has its own `package.json` with independent dependencies and scripts. ### Key Development Commands ```bash # Start infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Temporal, Redis, etc.) just infra-up # Start all services (frontend, backend, worker) just dev-stack # Run frontend only just dev-frontend # Run backend only just dev-backend # Run worker only just dev-worker ``` The `justfile` provides orchestration commands for common development tasks. Services are managed by PM2 in development mode, with hot reloading enabled. **Sources:** [package.json:1-68](), [justfile](), [pm2.config.cjs](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml]() --- ## Key Concepts ### Workflow Graph vs. Definition - **WorkflowGraphDto**: Frontend representation with nodes, edges, and viewport. Used by the Canvas for visual editing. - **WorkflowDefinition**: Backend representation with actions, dependencies, and join strategies. Used by Temporal for execution. The compilation process (`compileWorkflowGraph`) transforms the graph into a definition by performing topological sorting and resolving input mappings. ### Port Type System Ports use a typed connection system with four kinds: 1. **Primitive**: `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `secret`, `file`, `json` 2. **List**: `list` 3. **Map**: `map` 4. **Contract**: Named contracts like `mcp.tool`, with optional `credential: true` Type compatibility is checked during connection validation. Coercion is allowed for compatible primitives (e.g., `number → text`). **Sources:** [frontend/src/utils/portUtils.ts:1-201](), [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:1-288]() ### Execution Context Components receive an `ExecutionContext` object that provides: ```typescript interface ExecutionContext { logger: Logger; emitProgress: (progress: number, message?: string) => void; storage: IStorageService; secrets: ISecretsService; trace: ITraceService; http: FetchClient; abortSignal: AbortSignal; } ``` This abstraction allows components to be portable across different execution environments (inline, Docker, remote). **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/execution-context.ts]() ### MCP Tool Integration Components can be exposed as tools for AI agents by: 1. Setting `toolProvider: true` in component metadata 2. Defining a `toolSchema` (JSON Schema) 3. Connecting the component to an AI agent's `tools` port The `McpGatewayService` routes tool calls from agents to the appropriate component executions via Temporal signals. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-gateway/mcp-gateway.service.ts](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts]() --- ## Next Steps This overview provides a foundation for understanding ShipSec Studio's architecture. To dive deeper into specific subsystems: - **Workflow Design and Compilation**: See [Workflow System](#2) - **Component Development**: See [Component System](#3) and [Component SDK](#3.1) - **AI Agent Configuration**: See [AI and MCP Integration](#4) - **Execution Monitoring**: See [Execution Monitoring](#5) - **Deployment Options**: See [Infrastructure and Deployment](#9)

## Purpose and Scope This document describes the high-level architecture of ShipSec Studio, a workflow automation platform. It covers the three-tier application structure (frontend, backend, worker), communication patterns between tiers, and the technology stack. For details on specific subsystems, see: - Workflow creation and compilation: [Workflow System](#2) - Component execution model: [Component System](#3) - Monitoring and observability: [Execution Monitoring](#5) - Development environment setup: [Development Setup](#1.3) ## System Architecture ShipSec Studio follows a **three-tier architecture** with clear separation of concerns: 1. **Frontend Tier**: React application for workflow design and monitoring 2. **Backend Tier**: NestJS API server for orchestration and persistence 3. **Worker Tier**: Temporal-based execution engine for running workflows All three tiers communicate through well-defined interfaces: REST APIs, Temporal workflows, and event streams. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend Tier" UI["React App

Technology Stack and Key Dependencies | Layer | Technology | Purpose | Key Files | |-------|-----------|---------|-----------| | **Frontend** | React 19 | UI framework | [frontend/package.json:146]() | | | Vite | Build tool | [frontend/package.json:185]() | | | Zustand | State management | [frontend/package.json:155]() | | | React Flow | Graph editor | [frontend/package.json:149]() | | | openapi-fetch | Type-safe API client | [packages/backend-client/src/api-client.ts:1]() | | **Backend** | NestJS 10 | API framework | [backend/package.json:25-29]() | | | Drizzle ORM | Database access | [backend/package.json:50]() | | | @temporalio/client | Workflow orchestration | [backend/package.json:37]() | | | KafkaJS | Event streaming | [backend/package.json:53]() | | **Worker** | @temporalio/worker | Workflow execution | [worker/package.json:273]() | | | @temporalio/workflow | Workflow definitions | [worker/package.json:274]() | | | AI SDK | LLM integration | [worker/package.json:276]() | | | @modelcontextprotocol/sdk | MCP tools | [worker/package.json:264]() | | **Infrastructure** | PostgreSQL | Relational database | [backend/package.json:59]() | | | Temporal | Orchestration engine | N/A | | | Redis (ioredis) | Caching & streams | [backend/package.json:52]() | | | MinIO | Object storage | [backend/package.json:55]() | | | Kafka/Redpanda | Event bus | [backend/package.json:53]() | **Sources:** [package.json:1-68](), [backend/package.json:1-90](), [worker/package.json:254-315](), [frontend/package.json:106-187]() ## For information about setting up the development environment, see [Development Setup](#1.3). For the overall system architecture, see [Architecture Overview](#1.1). ## Workspace Organization ShipSec Studio is organized as a **Bun workspace monorepo** with seven packages: three applications (`frontend`, `backend`, `worker`) and four shared libraries (`backend-client`, `component-sdk`, `contracts`, `shared`). The workspace configuration is defined in [package.json:6-14](). ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Root Workspace" ROOT["shipsec-studio

It uses **Zustand** for state management and **React Flow** for the visual workflow editor. **Key Dependencies:** - `react@19.2.0` and `react-dom@19.2.0` - UI framework - `vite@7.1.9` - Build tool and dev server - `reactflow@11.11.4` - Visual workflow graph editor - `zustand@5.0.8` - State management - `@clerk/clerk-react@5.53.4` - Authentication - `@radix-ui/*` - UI component primitives - `@monaco-editor/react@4.7.0` - Code editor - `posthog-js@1.288.0` - Analytics - **Workspace dependencies:** `@shipsec/backend-client`, `@shipsec/shared` The frontend depends on `@shipsec/backend-client` for type-safe API communication and `@shipsec/shared` for shared constants and utilities. **Sources:** [bun.lock:106-187]() ### Backend (`@shipsec/studio-backend`) The backend is a **NestJS** application that provides REST APIs for workflow management, handles authentication, orchestrates Temporal workflows, and manages the MCP Gateway. **Key Dependencies:** - `@nestjs/core@10.4.22` and `@nestjs/common@10.4.22` - NestJS framework - `@nestjs/swagger@11.2.5` - OpenAPI documentation - `@temporalio/client@1.14.1` - Temporal client for starting workflows - `drizzle-orm@0.44.7` - Database ORM - `pg@8.17.2` - PostgreSQL driver - `kafkajs@2.2.4` - Kafka client for event streaming - `ioredis@5.9.2` - Redis client - `minio@8.0.6` - Object storage client - `@clerk/backend@2.29.5` - Authentication - `ai@6.0.49` - Vercel AI SDK for MCP Gateway - **Workspace dependencies:** `@shipsec/backend-client`, `@shipsec/component-sdk`, `@shipsec/shared`, `@shipsec/studio-worker` The backend depends on `@shipsec/component-sdk` to understand component schemas, `@shipsec/studio-worker` for accessing workflow definitions, and `@shipsec/shared` for constants. **Sources:** [backend/package.json:1-90](), [bun.lock:32-105]() ### Worker (`@shipsec/studio-worker`) The worker is a **Temporal Worker** that executes workflow runs and component activities. It registers 200+ components and handles workflow orchestration, including AI agent execution and MCP tool integration. **Key Dependencies:** - `@temporalio/worker@1.14.1` and `@temporalio/workflow@1.14.1` - Temporal worker runtime - `@temporalio/activity@1.14.1` - Activity execution context - `ai@6.0.49` - Vercel AI SDK for AI components - `@ai-sdk/openai@3.0.18`, `@ai-sdk/google@3.0.13` - LLM providers - `@ai-sdk/mcp@1.0.13`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.25.1` - MCP integration - `drizzle-orm@0.44.7` and `pg@8.17.2` - Database access - `kafkajs@2.2.4` - Event emission - `ioredis@5.9.2` - Redis for terminal streams - `minio@8.0.6` - File storage - `node-pty@1.1.0` - PTY for security tools - **Workspace dependencies:** `@shipsec/component-sdk`, `@shipsec/contracts`, `@shipsec/shared` The worker depends on `@shipsec/component-sdk` for component definitions, `@shipsec/contracts` for workflow structures, and `@shipsec/shared` for utilities. **Sources:** [bun.lock:254-315]() ## Shared Packages ### Backend Client (`@shipsec/backend-client`) The backend client is a **type-safe API client** generated from the backend's OpenAPI specification using `openapi-typescript`. It provides TypeScript types and a fetch-based client for all backend endpoints. **Key Dependencies:** - `openapi-fetch@0.12.2` - Type-safe fetch wrapper - `openapi-typescript@7.9.1` (dev) - Code generator The package is generated using the backend's OpenAPI spec via the script defined in [backend/package.json:14](). This ensures the frontend always has type-safe access to the latest API definitions. **Sources:** [bun.lock:188-201]() ### Component SDK (`@shipsec/component-sdk`) The component SDK defines the **component interface**, parameter schemas, port definitions, and execution context for all workflow components. It provides the contract between component implementations and the workflow execution engine. **Key Types:** - `ComponentDefinition` - Component metadata and configuration - `ExecutionContext` - Services injected into components during execution - `ParameterField` - Parameter schema definitions - Port types (`DataPort`, `FlowPort`, `LogicPort`, `ArrayPort`) **Key Dependencies:** - `@shipsec/shared` (workspace) - Shared utilities - `zod@4.3.6` - Schema validation - `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.25.2` (dev) - For MCP component types - `node-pty@1.1.0` (optional) - For terminal components The SDK is dependency-free of Temporal or any application framework, making it usable in both the backend (for schema validation) and worker (for execution). **Sources:** [bun.lock:202-222]() ### Contracts (`@shipsec/contracts`) The contracts package defines **shared data structures** for workflows, including `WorkflowGraphDto`, `WorkflowDefinition`, and type definitions used across the backend and worker. **Key Dependencies:** - `@shipsec/component-sdk` (workspace) - Component types - `@shipsec/shared` (workspace) - Utilities - `zod@4.3.6` - Schema definitions This package ensures that the backend's workflow compilation logic and the worker's execution logic agree on the structure of workflows. **Sources:** [bun.lock:223-239]() ### Shared (`@shipsec/shared`) The shared package contains **common utilities, constants, and helper functions** used across all applications and packages. It has minimal dependencies and serves as the foundation layer. **Key Dependencies:** - `zod@4.3.6` - Schema validation This is the only package with no workspace dependencies, making it the root of the dependency tree. **Sources:** [bun.lock:240-253]() ## Package Dependency Graph The following diagram shows the dependency relationships between packages. Note that dependencies flow from applications toward shared packages, with `@shipsec/shared` at the foundation. ```mermaid graph TD FE["frontend

Applications depend on relevant shared packages but not on each other 6. The backend has a dependency on `@shipsec/studio-worker` to access workflow definitions **Sources:** [bun.lock:32-315]() ## Build System and Package Management ### Bun Workspaces The monorepo uses **Bun 1.1.20** as the package manager and build tool, configured via `packageManager` in [package.json:5](). Bun's workspace feature resolves `workspace:*` dependencies to local packages without publishing to npm. **Workspace Resolution:** - `workspace:*` in dependencies resolves to the local package version - All packages are linked during `bun install` - Changes to shared packages are immediately available to applications **Sources:** [package.json:5-14]() ### Build and Development Scripts The root `package.json` defines scripts for coordinating all packages: | Script | Command | Purpose | |--------|---------|---------| | `dev:frontend` | `bun --cwd=frontend dev` | Start Vite dev server | | `dev:backend` | `bun --cwd=backend run dev` | Start NestJS with hot reload | | `dev` | Alias to `dev:frontend` | Default development command | | `dev:infra` | Docker Compose + PM2 | Start infrastructure and all apps | | `dev:stack` | `dev:infra` + PM2 logs | Full stack with log streaming | | `migrate` | `bun --cwd=backend run migration:push` | Push database schema changes | | `typecheck` | `tsc --build` | Type check all packages | | `test` | `bun test` | Run unit tests | | `test:e2e` | `bun test --force-exit e2e-tests` | Run end-to-end tests | | `lint` | Run linters for all packages | Check code style | | `lint:fix` | Run linters with --fix | Auto-fix code style | **Sources:** [package.json:15-36]() ### Type Generation and Code Generation Several packages use code generation: 1. **Backend OpenAPI Generation** - Script: [backend/package.json:14]() - Generates OpenAPI spec from NestJS decorators - Output consumed by `@shipsec/backend-client` 2. **Backend Client Generation** - Uses `openapi-typescript` to generate types from OpenAPI spec - Creates type-safe fetch client with path and method inference 3. **Database Migrations** - Uses `drizzle-kit push` to sync schema changes - Script: [backend/package.json:15]() **Sources:** [backend/package.json:14-15](), [bun.lock:188-201]() ## Multi-Instance Support The monorepo supports running **multiple isolated instances** on the same machine via the `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` environment variable (values 0-9). Each instance gets: - **Port offset:** Base port + (instance × 100) - **Database:** `shipsec_instance_N` in PostgreSQL - **Temporal namespace:** `shipsec-dev-N` - **Kafka topics:** Instance-scoped topic names This is handled by scripts in [package.json:20-28]() and affects PM2 configuration, Docker Compose port mappings, and application environment variables. For more details, see [Multi-Instance Support](#10.3). **Sources:** [package.json:20-28]() ## External Dependencies Summary **Frontend:** - UI: React 19, Radix UI, Tailwind CSS - Visualization: React Flow, XTerm.js, Monaco Editor - State: Zustand, Zundo (undo/redo) - Auth: Clerk - Analytics: PostHog **Backend:** - Framework: NestJS - Database: Drizzle ORM + PostgreSQL - Orchestration: Temporal Client - Messaging: KafkaJS - Storage: MinIO, Redis - Auth: Clerk - Search: OpenSearch **Worker:** - Orchestration: Temporal Worker + Workflow - AI: Vercel AI SDK, MCP SDK - Database: Drizzle ORM + PostgreSQL - Messaging: KafkaJS - Storage: MinIO, Redis - Security Tools: Node-PTY for subprocess execution **Sources:** [bun.lock:1-316]()

## Purpose and Scope The Workflow System is the core orchestration layer of ShipSec Studio, managing the complete lifecycle of workflow automation from visual design to distributed execution. This page provides an architectural overview of how workflows are represented, compiled, executed, and monitored. **Detailed subsystem documentation:** - Visual workflow design: [Workflow Builder UI](#2.1) - Graph data model: [Workflow Graph Model](#2.2) - Graph-to-definition compilation: [Workflow Compilation](#2.3) - Temporal-based execution: [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4) - REST API operations: [Workflow Management API](#2.5) - Scheduled execution: [Schedules and Automation](#2.6) - Nested workflows: [Sub-Workflows and Composition](#2.7) - Large payload handling: [Data Flow and Spilling](#2.8) --- ## Core Concepts The workflow system operates on three fundamental representations of a workflow: ### WorkflowGraph (Design-Time) The visual representation used during workflow design, persisted in the `workflows` table. Defined by `WorkflowGraphDto` in the backend and manipulated via React Flow on the frontend. **Core structure:** - **Nodes**: Visual components positioned on canvas (`WorkflowNodeDto`), each containing: - `id`: Unique node identifier - `type`: Always `'workflow'` for component nodes - `position`: Canvas coordinates `{x, y}` - `data`: `FrontendNodeData` with component reference, config, inputs - **Edges**: Connections between ports (`WorkflowEdgeDto`), defining: - `source`/`target`: Node IDs - `sourceHandle`/`targetHandle`: Port IDs for data flow - `type`: Connection type (default or custom) - **Viewport**: Canvas view state (`x`, `y`, `zoom`) **Title: WorkflowGraph Data Structure** ```mermaid graph TB Graph["WorkflowGraphDto"] Nodes["nodes: WorkflowNodeDto[]"] Edges["edges: WorkflowEdgeDto[]"] Viewport["viewport: {x, y, zoom}"] Node["WorkflowNodeDto"] NodeId["id: string"] NodeType["type: 'workflow'"] Position["position: {x, y}"] Data["data: FrontendNodeData"] Edge["WorkflowEdgeDto"] EdgeId["id: string"] Source["source: nodeId"] Target["target: nodeId"] Handles["sourceHandle/targetHandle"] NodeData["FrontendNodeData"] ComponentRef["componentId/componentSlug"] Config["config: {params, inputOverrides}"] Inputs["inputs: Record"] Label["label: string"] Graph --> Nodes Graph --> Edges Graph --> Viewport Nodes --> Node Node --> NodeId Node --> NodeType Node --> Position Node --> Data Data --> NodeData NodeData --> ComponentRef NodeData --> Config NodeData --> Inputs NodeData --> Label Edges --> Edge Edge --> EdgeId Edge --> Source Edge --> Target Edge --> Handles ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts](), [frontend/src/schemas/node.ts](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:78-106]() ### WorkflowDefinition (Runtime) The compiled, execution-ready representation generated by `compileWorkflowGraph()` and stored in `workflow_versions` table. This format is optimized for Temporal workflow execution. **Core structure:** - **version**: Schema version (currently `1`) - **title/description**: Workflow metadata - **entrypoint**: `{ref: string}` pointing to entry component - **actions**: Topologically sorted array of `WorkflowAction` objects - **nodes**: `Record` with execution metadata - **edges**: Array of `WorkflowEdge` (success/error routing) - **dependencyCounts**: Pre-computed dependency counts for scheduling - **config**: Execution settings (environment, timeout) **Each `WorkflowAction` contains:** - `ref`: Unique node reference - `componentId`: Component to execute - `params`: Static parameters - `inputOverrides`: Manual input values - **id**: Unique run identifier (`shipsec-run-{uuid}`) - **workflowId**: Parent workflow ID - **workflowVersionId**: Immutable reference to compiled definition - **workflowVersion**: Version number for display - **organizationId**: Tenant isolation - **inputs**: Runtime inputs as JSON - **status**: `'QUEUED' | 'RUNNING' | 'COMPLETED' | 'FAILED' | 'CANCELLED'` - **totalActions**: Number of actions in definition - **completedActions**: Progress counter - **temporalWorkflowId**: Temporal execution ID - **temporalRunId**: Temporal run ID (for replay) - **trigger**: Execution trigger metadata (api/schedule/webhook) - **startedAt/completedAt**: Execution timestamps **Lifecycle management:** - Created by `WorkflowsService.prepareRunPayload()` before execution - Started via `TemporalService.startWorkflow(shipsecWorkflowRun, ...)` - Updated via `setRunMetadataActivity()` during execution - Finalized via `finalizeRunActivity()` after completion **Sources:** [backend/src/database/schema.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow-run.repository.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:156-158]() --- ## Workflow Lifecycle The workflow lifecycle spans four phases with specific implementation touchpoints. **Title: Complete Workflow Lifecycle Flow** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Canvas as "Canvas

private runningActions = new Set(); private completedActions = new Set(); private failedActions = new Set(); // Execution loop async run(definition: WorkflowDefinition) { // Initialize with entrypoint this.markReady(definition.entrypoint.ref, []); while (this.readyActions.size > 0 || this.runningActions.size > 0) { // Get all ready actions const batch = Array.from(this.readyActions.entries()); this.readyActions.clear(); // Execute batch in parallel await Promise.all(batch.map(([ref, context]) => this.executeAction(ref, context) )); // Check for newly ready actions this.updateReadyActions(); } } private updateReadyActions() { for (const action of this.pendingActions) { const meta = definition.nodes[action.ref]; const joinStrategy = meta?.joinStrategy || 'all'; if (joinStrategy === 'all') { // Wait for all dependencies if (action.dependsOn.every(dep => this.completedActions.has(dep))) { this.markReady(action.ref, action.dependsOn); } } else if (joinStrategy === 'any') { // Trigger on first completion const triggered = action.dependsOn.filter(dep => this.completedActions.has(dep) ); if (triggered.length > 0) { this.markReady(action.ref, triggered); } } } } } ``` **Key features:** - **Automatic parallelism**: All ready actions execute concurrently (no thread limit) - **Join strategies**: `all` (wait for all deps), `any` (first completion), `first` (skip if already triggered) - **Failure propagation**: Failed nodes skip downstream dependencies unless error edges exist - **Context passing**: Each action receives `triggeredBy` list for multi-input handling - **State persistence**: Execution state tracked in Temporal workflow variables (survives worker restarts) **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:300-900]() ### Component Execution Individual components execute via `runComponentActivity` with full service injection: ```typescript // From run-component.activity.ts async function runComponentActivity(input: RunComponentActivityInput) { // 1. Resolve component from registry const component = componentRegistry.get(input.action.componentId); // 2. Build execution context with injected services const context: ExecutionContext = { runId: input.runId, nodeRef: input.action.ref, logger: new WorkflowLogger(...), storage: fileStorageAdapter, secrets: secretsAdapter, trace: traceAdapter, http: { fetch: ... }, emitProgress: (progress) => { ... }, }; // 3. Resolve inputs from upstream outputs and manual overrides const resolvedInputs = await resolveInputs( input.inputs, input.inputOverrides, context ); // 4. Execute component with timeout protection const output = await component.execute({ inputs: resolvedInputs, params: input.params, context, }); // 5. Emit completion trace event await recordTraceEventActivity({ type: 'NODE_COMPLETED', runId: input.runId, nodeRef: input.action.ref, outputSummary: output, }); return { output }; } ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:651-850]() ### Join Strategies Nodes with multiple incoming edges can specify how to handle parallel inputs: | Strategy | Behavior | Implementation | Use Case | |----------|----------|----------------|----------| | `all` (default) | Wait until all upstream dependencies complete | `dependsOn.every(dep => completed.has(dep))` | Merge branches, aggregate results | | `any` | Trigger after first upstream dependency completes | `dependsOn.some(dep => completed.has(dep))` | Race conditions, fallback logic | | `first` | Like `any`, but subsequent completions skip execution | Skip if already `runningActions.has(ref)` | First-wins scenarios | **Title: Join Strategy Example** ```mermaid graph TB Start["start"] BranchA["branchA
slow: 200ms"] BranchB["branchB

joinStrategy: any

joinStrategy: first
Runs once, ignores branchA"] Start --> BranchA Start --> BranchB BranchA --> MergeAll BranchB --> MergeAll BranchA --> MergeAny BranchB --> MergeAny BranchA --> MergeFirst BranchB --> MergeFirst ``` **Join strategy metadata:** - Set via `WorkflowNodeMetadata.joinStrategy` in compiled definition - Defaults to `'all'` if not specified - Applied during scheduler's `updateReadyActions()` phase - Passed to component via `metadata.joinStrategy` in `RunComponentActivityInput` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/types.ts:34-49](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts](), [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:200-300]() --- ## Workflow States and Status ### Run Status Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> QUEUED: Run created QUEUED --> RUNNING: Temporal starts execution RUNNING --> COMPLETED: All actions succeed RUNNING --> FAILED: Action error without handler RUNNING --> CANCELLED: User cancellation RUNNING --> WAITING: Human input required WAITING --> RUNNING: Input received WAITING --> CANCELLED: Timeout or manual cancel COMPLETED --> [*] FAILED --> [*] CANCELLED --> [*] ``` **Status sources:** - **Temporal**: Workflow execution status from `WorkflowExecutionInfo` - **Database**: `workflow_runs.status` field - **Trace Events**: Derived from `NODE_COMPLETED`, `NODE_FAILED` counts **Sources:** [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:100-200](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:400-500]() ### Node Execution States Individual nodes transition through states during workflow execution: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> idle: Initial state idle --> queued: Dependencies met queued --> running: Execution started running --> completed: Success running --> failed: Error thrown running --> skipped: Upstream failure completed --> [*] failed --> [*] skipped --> [*] ``` **State tracking:** - **Frontend**: `nodeStates` in `useExecutionStore` (derived from trace events) - **Worker**: Internal execution state not persisted - **Trace**: `NODE_STARTED`, `NODE_COMPLETED`, `NODE_FAILED` events **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:300-400]() --- ## Workflow Validation Validation occurs at three stages with distinct checks. ### Design-Time Validation (Frontend) Real-time validation in the Canvas component as users connect nodes: **Connection validation (`validateConnection`):** - Source and target nodes exist in graph - Component metadata found in registry - Port types compatible via `arePortTypesCompatible(sourceType, targetType)` - No self-connections (`source !== target`) - No duplicate input connections (except `tools` port which allows many-to-one) - No cycles detected via `wouldCreateCycle(connection, edges)` (DFS traversal) **Node validation (`getNodeValidationWarnings`):** - Required inputs have connections or manual values - Required parameters are set - Secrets referenced exist in secrets store - Port type mismatches highlighted **Sources:** [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:17-194](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/ValidationDock.tsx]() ### Compile-Time Validation (Backend) Graph validation before generating `WorkflowDefinition`: **`validateWorkflowGraph()` checks:** - All components registered in `componentRegistry` (throws if missing) - Entry point component exists (`core.workflow.entrypoint`) - All edges reference valid node IDs and port handles - Graph is acyclic (topological sort via Kahn's algorithm must succeed) - Required component inputs satisfied by connections or `inputOverrides` - Parameter types match component schema **Compilation steps:** 1. `validateWorkflowGraph(graph)` - throws on structural errors 2. `resolveComponentIds(graph.nodes)` - map slugs to IDs 3. `buildDependencyGraph(graph.edges)` - create adjacency list 4. `topologicalSort(actions, deps)` - detect cycles, order actions 5. Return `WorkflowDefinition` if valid **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:1-400](), [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:118-190]() ### Runtime Validation (Worker) Validation during workflow execution: **Pre-execution checks:** - `WorkflowDefinition` loaded from database matches schema version - Input mappings resolve to existing upstream action outputs - Required inputs present after resolution **Component execution validation:** - Component timeout enforcement (default 10 minutes via `startToCloseTimeout`) - Input schema validation by component SDK - Output schema compliance (validated by component implementation) - Retry policy application on transient failures **Error handling:** - Missing dependencies throw `ApplicationFailure.nonRetryable()` - Component errors trigger failure edges if defined - Workflow-level errors mark run as `FAILED` in database **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:314-850](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts]() --- ## Integration Points The workflow system integrates with other platform subsystems: | Subsystem | Integration Point | Description | |-----------|------------------|-------------| | **Component System** | `componentRegistry.get(componentId)` | Load component definitions during compilation and execution | | **Execution Monitoring** | Kafka trace events | Emit `NODE_STARTED`, `NODE_COMPLETED`, etc. for real-time monitoring | | **File Storage** | `FileStorageService` | Store/retrieve artifacts and large payloads (see Data Spilling) | | **Secrets Management** | `SecretsService` | Inject secrets into component execution context | | **MCP Gateway** | `connectedToolNodeIds` | Register tool nodes for AI agent integration | | **Schedules System** | `SchedulesService.createSchedule()` | Trigger workflow runs on cron schedules | | **Analytics** | `AnalyticsService.trackWorkflowStarted()` | Track workflow execution metrics | **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:1-500](), [worker/src/temporal/activities.ts:1-200]() --- ## Performance Characteristics ### Compilation Performance - **Graph validation**: O(V + E) where V = nodes, E = edges - **Topological sort**: O(V + E) using Kahn's algorithm - **Caching**: Compiled definitions stored in `workflow_versions` table ### Execution Performance - **Parallelism**: Independent branches execute concurrently (no thread limit) - **Determinism**: Execution order is deterministic across runs for same version - **State overhead**: Each trace event ~1KB, stored in Kafka and PostgreSQL - **Scalability**: Temporal horizontal scaling via task queue workers **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:200-250](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:100-200](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:264-410]() --- ## Error Handling and Failure Edges Workflows support explicit error handling through failure edges. ```mermaid graph TB Start["start"] RiskyNode["risky-action
May throw error"] SuccessPath["success-handler"] ErrorPath["error-handler"] End["end"] Start --> RiskyNode RiskyNode -->|success edge| SuccessPath RiskyNode -.->|failure edge
kind: 'error'| ErrorPath SuccessPath --> End ErrorPath --> End ``` **Behavior:** - **Success edges** (`kind: 'success'`): Followed when component completes successfully - **Failure edges** (`kind: 'error'`): Followed when component throws error - **No handler**: Workflow fails if error edge not defined **Implementation:** Error edges are stored in `WorkflowDefinition.edges[]` with `kind: 'error'` and processed during execution when actions fail. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/types.ts:50-100](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:250-350](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:593-706]()

## Purpose and Scope This document describes the visual workflow editor interface, including the interactive canvas, node configuration panel, component library, and connection validation system. This covers the **design mode** of the workflow system where users visually construct workflow graphs by dragging components, connecting ports, and configuring parameters. For the underlying data structure of workflows, see [Workflow Graph Model](#2.2). For how visual graphs are compiled into executable definitions, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.3). For workflow execution and monitoring, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4) and [Execution Monitoring](#5). --- ## Overview The Workflow Builder UI is a React-based visual editor built on top of React Flow. Users construct workflows by: 1. **Adding components** from the Component Library (Sidebar) 2. **Connecting nodes** by dragging edges between input and output ports 3. **Configuring nodes** via the ConfigPanel to set parameters and input overrides 4. **Validating** connections and required fields before execution The editor supports both desktop (drag-and-drop) and mobile (tap-to-place) workflows, with real-time validation and type checking. Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:1-1000]() --- ## Component Architecture The visual editor is composed of several key React components that work together to provide the workflow building experience. ```mermaid graph TB WorkflowBuilderPage["WorkflowBuilderPage"] Canvas["Canvas"] ReactFlow["ReactFlow

edges: Edge[]; setNodes: Dispatch[]>>; setEdges: Dispatch>; onNodesChange: (changes: NodeChange[]) => void; onEdgesChange: (changes: EdgeChange[]) => void; } ``` Each node contains: - `id`: unique identifier - `type`: `'workflow'` or `'terminal'` - `position`: `{x, y}` coordinates - `data`: `NodeData` with component metadata and configuration Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:78-106]() ### Connection Flow When a user connects two ports, the Canvas validates the connection and updates both edges and node input mappings: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Canvas participant validateConnection participant setNodes participant setEdges participant markDirty User->>Canvas: Drag from source port to target port Canvas->>validateConnection: validateConnection(params, nodes, edges, getComponent) validateConnection-->>Canvas: {isValid: true} Canvas->>setEdges: Add new edge with DataFlowEdge type Canvas->>setNodes: Update target node inputs mapping Canvas->>markDirty: Mark workflow as dirty Note over Canvas: If validation fails, shows toast with error ``` Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:315-402](), [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:18-171]() ### Component Placement **Desktop Flow**: User drags component from Sidebar, drops onto Canvas ```typescript // Canvas.tsx:600-616 const onDrop = useCallback((event: React.DragEvent) => { event.preventDefault(); placementState.clearPlacement(); } }, [createNodeFromComponent, mode, isPlacementActive, placementState]); ``` Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:473-652]() ### Viewport Management The Canvas automatically adjusts the viewport in several scenarios: | Scenario | Behavior | |----------|----------| | **Initial Load** | Fits all workflow nodes with 0.2 padding, maxZoom 0.85 | | **Mode Change** | Instant fit (no animation) to current nodes | | **Nodes Added/Removed** | Smooth fit animation (300ms) to all nodes | | **Panel Opened** | Zooms to Entry Point node with 0.8 padding | | **Panel Closed** | Zooms out to fit all nodes | Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:405-471](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:883-936]() --- ## WorkflowNode Component The `WorkflowNode` component renders individual workflow nodes with input/output ports, labels, and visual status indicators. workflow graph using depth-first search: ```typescript // connectionValidation.ts:176-194 function wouldCreateCycle(newConnection: Connection, existingEdges: Edge[]): boolean { const { source, target } = newConnection; const visited = new Set(); function hasPath(from: string, to: string): boolean { if (from === to) return true; if (visited.has(from)) return false; visited.add(from); const outgoingEdges = existingEdges.filter((edge) => edge.source === from); return outgoingEdges.some((edge) => hasPath(edge.target, to)); } return hasPath(target, source); } ``` Sources: User searches for component in Sidebar 2. User drags component from Sidebar 3. Browser fires `dragstart` event on `ComponentItem` 4. `ComponentItem.onDragStart` sets `event.dataTransfer` with component ID 5. User drags over Canvas 6. Canvas `onDragOver` sets `dropEffect = 'move'` 7. User releases mouse 8. Canvas `onDrop` receives component ID 9. Canvas calculates flow position from screen coordinates 10. Canvas creates new node with default parameters 11. Canvas updates `nodes` state 12. Canvas marks workflow as dirty 13. ReactFlow re-renders with new node Sources: [frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:47-54](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:600-616]() ### Adding a Component (Mobile) 1. User taps component in Sidebar 2. `ComponentItem.handleTap` calls `setPlacement(componentId, name, workflowId)` 3. Sidebar closes automatically after 150ms 4. Canvas shows with placement mode active 5. User taps desired position on Canvas 6. Canvas `handleCanvasTap` reads `placementState.componentId` 7. Canvas calls `createNodeFromComponent(componentId, x, y)` 8. Canvas clears placement state 9. Node appears at tap position Sources: [frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:58-71](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:619-652]() ### Connecting Two Nodes 1. User drags from source port (output) 2. ReactFlow shows connection preview 3. User releases on target port (input) 4. ReactFlow fires `onConnect` callback 5. Canvas calls `validateConnection(params, nodes, edges, getComponent)` 6. Validator checks: - Basic validation (not self-connection, handles exist) - Component metadata exists - Ports exist and have types - Types are compatible - No existing connection (except tool ports) - Would not create cycle 7. If valid: - Canvas adds edge to `edges` state - Canvas updates target node's `inputs` mapping - Canvas marks workflow as dirty - Canvas captures history snapshot 8. If invalid: - Canvas shows error toast with reason - No edge is created Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:315-402](), [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:18-171]() ### Configuring Node Parameters 1. User selects node (click) 2. Canvas `onNodeClick` sets `selectedNode` state 3. ConfigPanel renders with node data 4. User changes parameter value 5. ConfigPanel calls `handleParamValueChange(paramId, value)` 6. ConfigPanel updates `latestNodeConfigRef` immediately 7. ConfigPanel calls `onUpdateNode(nodeId, {config: updatedConfig})` 8. Canvas `handleUpdateNode` updates node in `nodes` array 9. Canvas marks workflow as dirty 10. Canvas debounces history snapshot (500ms) 11. If parameter affects ports: - ConfigPanel triggers port resolution API call - API returns new port definitions - ConfigPanel updates `dynamicInputs`/`dynamicOutputs` - Canvas re-renders node with new ports - Canvas removes edges for invalid ports Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:353-378](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:761-853]() --- ## Mobile-Specific Features ### Touch Gestures | Gesture | Action | |---------|--------| | **Tap component in Sidebar** | Enter placement mode, close sidebar | | **Tap canvas** | Place component at tap position (if placement active) | | **Swipe right from left edge** | Open sidebar | | **Swipe left** | Close sidebar | | **Tap outside panels** | Close config panel | | **Long press** | Open context menu (if implemented) | Sources: [frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:188-255]() ### Responsive Layout The UI adapts to mobile viewports: - **Sidebar**: Fixed position, slides in/out, full-height overlay - **ConfigPanel**: Fixed position on right, slides in/out - **Canvas**: Full screen underneath panels - **TopBar**: Compact buttons, hidden labels on small screens - **ValidationDock**: Slides up from bottom Mobile breakpoint: `768px` (tablets and below) Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:47-63](), [frontend/src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx:119-135]() ### Bottom Sheet (Mobile ConfigPanel) On mobile, the ConfigPanel can optionally render as a bottom sheet instead of a side panel. The `workflowUiStore.configPanelOpen` state controls visibility: ```typescript // Canvas.tsx:157-160 useEffect(() => { setConfigPanelOpen(Boolean(selectedNode)); }, [selectedNode, setConfigPanelOpen]); ``` Sources: [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:157-160]() --- ## Validation Dock The `ValidationDock` component displays validation warnings and errors for the current workflow, helping users identify issues before execution. ### Validation Types | Type | Description | Example | |------|-------------|---------| | **Required Input** | Input port marked as required has no connection and no manual value | "Required input 'repository' is not connected" | | **Required Parameter** | Parameter marked as required has no value | "Required parameter 'API Key' is not set" | | **Missing Secret** | Parameter/input references a secret that doesn't exist | "Parameter 'token' refers to a missing secret" | | **Type Mismatch** | Connection types are incompatible | "Type mismatch: number cannot connect to text" | | **Cycle Detected** | Graph contains a cycle | "Connection would create a cycle" | The ValidationDock aggregates warnings from `getNodeValidationWarnings` for all nodes and displays them in a collapsible panel at the bottom of the screen. Sources: [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:196-287]() --- ## Integration with Other Systems The Workflow Builder UI integrates with several other subsystems: ### Backend API - `GET /api/components` - Fetch component metadata - `POST /api/components/:id/resolve-ports` - Resolve dynamic ports - `POST /api/workflows` - Save workflow - `GET /api/workflows/:id` - Load workflow - `POST /api/workflows/:id/run` - Execute workflow ### State Stores - `workflowStore` - Persists graph to backend on save - `executionStore` - Subscribes to SSE for live execution updates - `executionTimelineStore` - Displays data flow on edges during execution ### Timeline Visualization In execution mode, the Canvas displays data flow animations on edges based on `dataFlows` from `executionTimelineStore`. See [Execution Timeline UI](#5.1) for details. ### Component SDK Components define their ports, parameters, and tool schemas. The UI dynamically renders configuration based on component metadata. ## Purpose and Scope This document describes the **WorkflowGraphDto** data structure, which represents the visual workflow as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of nodes and edges. This is the intermediate format between the Workflow Builder UI ([2.1](#2.1)) and the compiled WorkflowDefinition used for execution. For information about how this graph is compiled into executable actions, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.3). For details on workflow execution, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). The workflow graph model serves as: - The canonical representation of a workflow's visual structure - The persistence format stored in the database - The API contract between frontend and backend - The input to the DSL compiler --- ## WorkflowGraphDto Structure The workflow graph is represented by the `WorkflowGraphDto` schema, defined and validated using Zod. This is the root container for all workflow metadata and structure. ```mermaid graph TD WorkflowGraphDto["WorkflowGraphDto"] WorkflowGraphDto --> Name["name: string"] WorkflowGraphDto --> Description["description?: string"] WorkflowGraphDto --> Nodes["nodes: WorkflowNodeDto[]"] WorkflowGraphDto --> Edges["edges: EdgeDto[]"] WorkflowGraphDto --> Viewport["viewport: ViewportDto"] Nodes --> NodeArray["Array of nodes"] Edges --> EdgeArray["Array of connections"] Viewport --> ViewState["Canvas view state"] ``` **Core Fields:** | Field | Type | Required | Description | |-------|------|----------|-------------| | `name` | string | Yes | Workflow display name | | `description` | string | No | Workflow description | | `nodes` | WorkflowNodeDto[] | Yes | Array of workflow nodes (components) | | `edges` | EdgeDto[] | Yes | Array of connections between nodes | | `viewport` | ViewportDto | Yes | Canvas viewport state (pan/zoom) | **Sources:** - [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts]() (schema definition) - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:61-297]() - [backend/src/__tests__/backend-integration.test.ts:49-60]() --- ## Node Structure (WorkflowNodeDto) Each node in the workflow graph represents a component instance. The node structure follows the React Flow node format with workflow-specific data extensions. ```mermaid graph LR WorkflowNodeDto["WorkflowNodeDto"] WorkflowNodeDto --> ID["id: string"] WorkflowNodeDto --> Type["type: string
(componentId)"] WorkflowNodeDto --> Position["position: {x, y}"] WorkflowNodeDto --> Data["data: NodeData"] Data --> Label["label: string"] Data --> Config["config: NodeConfig"] Config --> Params["params:
Record"] Config --> InputOverrides["inputOverrides:
Record"] Config --> Metadata["joinStrategy?, streamId?,
groupId?, maxConcurrency?"] ``` **Node Field Specifications:** | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | string | Unique node identifier (generated client-side) | | `type` | string | Component ID (e.g., `core.workflow.entrypoint`, `core.http.request`) | | `position` | `{x: number, y: number}` | Canvas coordinates for visual layout | | `data` | NodeData | Node configuration and metadata | **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:63-79]() - [backend/src/__tests__/backend-integration.test.ts:28-43]() --- ## Node Data and Configuration The `data` field contains all configuration for a node. This includes both static parameters and dynamic runtime values. ### NodeData Structure ```mermaid graph TD NodeData["NodeData"] NodeData --> Label["label: string
(display name)"] NodeData --> Config["config: NodeConfig"] Config --> Params["params: Record
(component parameters)"] Config --> InputOverrides["inputOverrides: Record
(manual input values)"] Config --> JoinStrategy["joinStrategy?: 'all' | 'any' | 'first'
(for multi-input nodes)"] Config --> StreamId["streamId?: string
(for stream processing)"] Config --> GroupId["groupId?: string
(for parallel execution)"] Config --> MaxConcurrency["maxConcurrency?: number
(parallel limit)"] Config --> Mode["mode?: 'normal' | 'tool'
(execution mode)"] Config --> ToolConfig["toolConfig?: {...}
(tool exposure config)"] ``` ### Parameter Types The `params` object contains component-specific configuration: ```typescript // Example Entry Point component parameters { runtimeInputs: [ { id: 'fileId', label: 'File ID', type: 'file', required: true, description: 'Input file identifier' } ] } // Example HTTP Request component parameters { method: 'POST', timeout: 30000, retryCount: 3 } ``` ### Input Overrides The `inputOverrides` object contains manual values for input ports that aren't connected to other nodes: ```typescript { url: 'https://example.com/webhook', body: '{"message": "hello"}', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:95-133]() - [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:472-473]() - [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:14-42]() --- ## Frontend-Specific Node Data The frontend extends `NodeData` with additional fields for UI state management and dynamic port resolution: ```mermaid graph TD FrontendNodeData["FrontendNodeData
(extends NodeData)"] FrontendNodeData --> ComponentId["componentId?: string
(resolved component)"] FrontendNodeData --> ComponentSlug["componentSlug?: string
(legacy reference)"] FrontendNodeData --> ComponentVersion["componentVersion?: string"] FrontendNodeData --> Inputs["inputs?: Record
(connection state)"] FrontendNodeData --> Status["status?: ExecutionStatus

(resolved inputs)"] FrontendNodeData --> DynamicOutputs["dynamicOutputs?: PortMetadata[]
(resolved outputs)"] FrontendNodeData --> WorkflowId["workflowId?: string
(for webhooks)"] ``` ### Input Mappings The `inputs` field tracks which input ports are connected to which source nodes: ```typescript { // Target port 'fileId' receives data from node 'trigger' output 'fileId' fileId: { source: 'trigger', output: 'fileId' } } ``` This structure is synchronized with the edges array and used for visual feedback in the UI. **Sources:** - [frontend/src/schemas/node.ts]() (type definitions) - [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:353-382]() - [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:411-473]() --- ## Edge Structure Edges represent data flow connections between nodes. Each edge connects a source output port to a target input port. ```mermaid graph LR EdgeDto["Edge"] EdgeDto --> ID["id: string
(unique edge id)"] EdgeDto --> Source["source: string
(source node id)"] EdgeDto --> Target["target: string
(target node id)"] EdgeDto --> SourceHandle["sourceHandle?: string
(output port id)"] EdgeDto --> TargetHandle["targetHandle?: string
(input port id)"] ``` ### Edge Examples **Simple data flow:** ```typescript { id: 'e1', source: 'entry-point', target: 'http-request', sourceHandle: 'apiUrl', // Entry point output targetHandle: 'url' // HTTP Request input } ``` **Tool connection (many-to-one):** ```typescript { id: 'tool-edge-1', source: 'github-search', target: 'ai-agent', sourceHandle: 'tools', // Tool export port targetHandle: 'tools' // Agent tool port (accepts multiple) } ``` ### Edge Compilation During compilation, edges are transformed into `inputMappings` on the target node: ```typescript // Edge: trigger -> loader (fileId -> fileId) // Becomes: { ref: 'loader', inputMappings: { fileId: { sourceRef: 'trigger', sourceHandle: 'fileId' } } } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:148-161]() - [backend/src/dsl/types.ts:40-49]() - [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:315-401]() --- ## Viewport State The viewport tracks the canvas view state for the visual editor. This allows workflows to be saved with their visual layout preserved. ```mermaid graph LR ViewportDto["ViewportDto"] ViewportDto --> X["x: number
(horizontal pan)"] ViewportDto --> Y["y: number
(vertical pan)"] ViewportDto --> Zoom["zoom: number
(zoom level 0.1-2.0)"] ``` **Example:** ```typescript { x: 100, // Canvas panned 100px right y: -50, // Canvas panned 50px up zoom: 0.75 // Zoomed out to 75% } ``` The viewport state is stored with the workflow but not used during compilation or execution—it's purely for UI persistence. **Sources:** - [backend/src/__tests__/backend-integration.test.ts:56]() - [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:77]() --- ## Node Connections and Data Flow The workflow graph uses a **port-based connection model** where each component defines typed input and output ports. ### Connection Model Diagram ```mermaid graph TD SourceNode["Source Node
'http-request-1'"] TargetNode["Target Node
'json-parser'"] SourceNode --> OutputPorts["Output Ports"] OutputPorts --> StatusPort["statusCode: number"] OutputPorts --> BodyPort["body: text"] OutputPorts --> HeadersPort["headers: json"] TargetNode --> InputPorts["Input Ports"] InputPorts --> DataPort["data: text
(required)"] InputPorts --> SchemaPort["schema?: json"] BodyPort -.edge.-> DataPort Edge["Edge:
source='http-request-1'
target='json-parser'
sourceHandle='body'
targetHandle='data'"] ``` ### Connection Rules 1. **Type Compatibility**: Source and target ports must have compatible types (validated in frontend) 2. **Cardinality**: Most input ports accept only one connection (except special ports like `tools`) 3. **Manual Override**: Ports can accept either a connection OR a manual value (configured in `inputOverrides`) 4. **Priority**: Some ports support `valuePriority` to prefer manual values over connections ### Input Resolution Priority For each input port, the compiler resolves values in this order: 1. **Connection (default)**: If edge exists and no manual override configured 2. **Manual value**: If `inputOverrides[portId]` is set 3. **Manual-first ports**: If port has `valuePriority: 'manual-first'`, manual value overrides connection ```typescript // Example: Port prefers manual value const metadata = inputMetadata.get(targetKey); const prefersManual = metadata?.valuePriority === 'manual-first'; if (!prefersManual) { // Remove manual value if port is connected delete inputOverrides[targetKey]; } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:186-192]() - [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:1-195]() - [frontend/src/utils/portUtils.ts:1-195]() --- ## Dynamic Port Resolution Some components have **dynamic ports** that depend on parameter values. For example, the Entry Point component dynamically creates output ports based on its `runtimeInputs` parameter. ### Dynamic Port Resolution Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as ConfigPanel participant API as Backend API participant Component as Component.resolvePorts() participant Node as Node State UI->>UI: User changes parameter UI->>API: POST /components/{id}/resolve-ports
{params} API->>Component: resolvePorts(params) Component->>Component: Generate dynamic ports Component-->>API: {inputs?, outputs?} API-->>UI: Dynamic port metadata UI->>Node: Update dynamicInputs/dynamicOutputs UI->>UI: Re-render port handles ``` ### Example: Entry Point Dynamic Outputs ```typescript // Entry Point component configuration { params: { runtimeInputs: [ { id: 'apiUrl', label: 'API URL', type: 'text', required: true }, { id: 'apiKey', label: 'API Key', type: 'secret', required: true } ] } } // Dynamically generated outputs dynamicOutputs: [ { id: 'apiUrl', label: 'API URL', connectionType: { kind: 'primitive', name: 'text' } }, { id: 'apiKey', label: 'API Key', connectionType: { kind: 'primitive', name: 'secret' } } ] ``` ### Dynamic Port Compilation During compilation, if `resolvePorts` is available, the compiler calls it to get the current port schema: ```typescript if (component?.resolvePorts) { try { const resolved = component.resolvePorts(params); if (resolved.inputs) { inputs = extractPorts(resolved.inputs); } } catch (e) { console.warn(`Failed to resolve ports for node ${id} during compilation`, e); } } ``` **Sources:** - [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:492-540]() - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:170-182]() - [backend/src/dsl/validator.ts:68-93]() --- ## Execution Metadata Nodes can include execution control metadata in their `config` object: ### Join Strategy For nodes with multiple incoming edges, `joinStrategy` determines when the node executes: | Strategy | Behavior | |----------|----------| | `all` (default) | Wait for all dependencies to complete | | `any` | Execute after any dependency completes | | `first` | Execute after the first dependency completes | ```typescript // Node configuration for "any" join strategy { config: { joinStrategy: 'any', params: { /* ... */ } } } ``` ### Parallel Execution Control | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `streamId` | string | Groups nodes into a stream for ordered processing | | `groupId` | string | Groups nodes for batch parallel execution | | `maxConcurrency` | number | Limits parallel execution within a group | **Example: Parallel API requests with concurrency limit** ```typescript { config: { groupId: 'api-batch', maxConcurrency: 5, // Max 5 concurrent requests params: { /* ... */ } } } ``` ### Tool Mode Components can be exposed as tools for AI agents: ```typescript { config: { mode: 'tool', toolConfig: { boundInputIds: ['apiKey'], // Pre-configured inputs exposedInputIds: ['query', 'limit'] // Agent-provided inputs } } } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:95-133]() - [backend/src/dsl/types.ts:51-68]() --- ## Storage and Persistence The workflow graph is stored in PostgreSQL as JSONB in the `workflows` table. ### Database Schema ```mermaid erDiagram workflows { uuid id PK text name text description jsonb graph jsonb compiled_definition varchar organization_id timestamp last_run integer run_count timestamp created_at timestamp updated_at } workflow_versions { uuid id PK uuid workflow_id FK integer version jsonb graph jsonb compiled_definition timestamp created_at varchar organization_id } workflows ||--o{ workflow_versions : "has versions" ``` ### Version History Each time a workflow is saved, a new version is created in `workflow_versions`: 1. User saves workflow → `WorkflowsService.update()` 2. Create version record → `WorkflowVersionRepository.create()` 3. Compile graph → `compileWorkflowGraph()` 4. Store compiled definition → `setCompiledDefinition()` **Version Record Structure:** ```typescript { id: 'version-uuid', workflowId: 'workflow-uuid', version: 3, graph: { /* WorkflowGraphDto */ }, compiledDefinition: { /* WorkflowDefinition */ }, createdAt: '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z', organizationId: 'org-123' } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/database/schema/workflows.ts:1-21]() - [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:1-100]() --- ## Validation Rules The workflow graph must satisfy several validation rules before it can be compiled and executed. ### Structural Validation ```mermaid graph TD Validate["Validation Rules"] Validate --> ComponentExists["All node types
reference registered components"] Validate --> SingleEntry["Exactly one
Entry Point component"] Validate --> NoCycles["No cycles in edge graph"] Validate --> ValidEdges["All edges reference
valid nodes"] Validate --> HandleExists["Source/target handles
exist on components"] ComponentExists --> Error1["Error: Component not registered"] SingleEntry --> Error2["Error: Entry Point required"] NoCycles --> Error3["Error: Workflow contains cycle"] ValidEdges --> Error4["Error: Edge references unknown node"] HandleExists --> Error5["Error: Invalid connection ports"] ``` ### Connection Validation Enforced in the frontend before edges can be created: ```typescript export function validateConnection( connection: Connection, nodes: Node[], edges: Edge[], getComponent: (slug: string) => ComponentMetadata | null, ): ValidationResult ``` **Validation Checks:** 1. **Type Compatibility**: Source and target port types must be compatible 2. **No Self-Loops**: Cannot connect node to itself 3. **Cardinality**: Most input ports can have only one connection 4. **No Cycles**: Connection would not create a cycle in the graph **Type Compatibility Matrix:** | Source → Target | text | number | boolean | json | file | secret | |-----------------|------|--------|---------|------|------|--------| | **text** | ✓ | ✓ (coerce) | ✓ (coerce) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **number** | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **boolean** | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | | **json** | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | | **file** | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | | **secret** | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ### Required Input Validation During compilation, the validator checks that all required inputs have either: - A connected edge, OR - A manual value in `inputOverrides` ```typescript // Validate required inputs have either a manual value or a connection for (const [inputId, metadata] of inputMetadata.entries()) { if (!metadata.required) continue; const hasPortMapping = Boolean(inputMappings[inputId]); const manualValue = inputOverrides[inputId]; const hasManual = manualValue !== undefined && manualValue !== null; if (!hasPortMapping && !hasManual) { throw new Error(`Required input '${inputId}' is missing`); } } ``` **Sources:** - [frontend/src/utils/connectionValidation.ts:17-195]() - [backend/src/dsl/validator.ts:37-152]() - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:195-216]() --- ## Topological Ordering Before compilation, nodes are sorted into topological order to ensure dependencies are satisfied during execution. ### Topological Sort Algorithm ```mermaid graph TD Start["Start: All nodes and edges"] Start --> BuildGraph["Build adjacency list
and incoming edge counts"] BuildGraph --> FindRoots["Find nodes with
incoming count = 0"] FindRoots --> Queue["Add to processing queue"] Queue --> Process["Process node:
Add to result list"] Process --> UpdateNeighbors["Decrement incoming count
for all neighbors"] UpdateNeighbors --> CheckZero{"Any neighbors
now have count = 0?"} CheckZero -->|Yes| AddToQueue["Add to queue"] CheckZero -->|No| NextNode AddToQueue --> NextNode["Next node in queue"] NextNode --> QueueEmpty{"Queue empty?"} QueueEmpty -->|No| Process QueueEmpty -->|Yes| ValidateResult{"All nodes processed?"} ValidateResult -->|Yes| Success["Return ordered list"] ValidateResult -->|No| CycleError["Error: Cycle detected"] ``` ### Topological Sort Implementation ```typescript function topoSort(nodes: string[], edges: { source: string; target: string }[]): string[] { const incoming = new Map(); const adjacency = new Map(); // Initialize nodes.forEach((id) => { incoming.set(id, 0); adjacency.set(id, []); }); // Build graph for (const edge of edges) { incoming.set(edge.target, (incoming.get(edge.target) ?? 0) + 1); adjacency.get(edge.source)?.push(edge.target); } // Process nodes with no dependencies const queue = nodes.filter((id) => incoming.get(id) === 0); const result: string[] = []; while (queue.length > 0) { const current = queue.shift()!; result.push(current); for (const neighbor of adjacency.get(current) ?? []) { incoming.set(neighbor, (incoming.get(neighbor) ?? 1) - 1); if (incoming.get(neighbor) === 0) { queue.push(neighbor); } } } if (result.length !== nodes.length) { throw new Error('Workflow graph contains a cycle'); } return result; } ``` **Example:** ``` Input graph: entry-point → http-request-1 → json-parser → http-request-2 ↗ Topological order: [entry-point, http-request-1, http-request-2, json-parser] or [entry-point, http-request-2, http-request-1, json-parser] ``` Both orders are valid as `http-request-1` and `http-request-2` are independent. **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:19-59]() - [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:143-190]() --- ## Graph to Definition Transformation The compilation process transforms the visual graph into an executable definition. This is a multi-step process that resolves all node configurations and dependencies. ### Compilation Pipeline ```mermaid graph TD Input["WorkflowGraphDto
(visual graph)"] Input --> FilterUI["Filter UI-only nodes
(text blocks, etc.)"] FilterUI --> ValidateComponents["Validate all components
are registered"] ValidateComponents --> TopoSort["Topological sort
by dependencies"] TopoSort --> BuildMetadata["Build node metadata
(joinStrategy, mode, etc.)"] BuildMetadata --> BuildActions["Build actions
with inputMappings"] BuildActions --> ResolveInputs["Resolve required inputs
(connections or manual)"] ResolveInputs --> ValidateGraph["Validate workflow graph"] ValidateGraph --> Output["WorkflowDefinition
(executable)"] Output --> EntryPoint["entrypoint: {ref}"] Output --> Nodes["nodes: metadata map"] Output --> Edges["edges: compiled edges"] Output --> Actions["actions: ordered list"] Output --> DepCounts["dependencyCounts: map"] ``` ### Action Generation Each node becomes a `WorkflowAction` in the compiled definition: **Graph Node:** ```typescript { id: 'http-request-1', type: 'core.http.request', data: { label: 'Fetch API', config: { params: { method: 'GET', timeout: 5000 }, inputOverrides: { url: 'https://api.example.com/data' } } } } ``` **Compiled Action:** ```typescript { ref: 'http-request-1', componentId: 'core.http.request', params: { method: 'GET', timeout: 5000 }, inputOverrides: { url: 'https://api.example.com/data' }, dependsOn: ['entry-point'], inputMappings: { apiKey: { sourceRef: 'entry-point', sourceHandle: 'apiKey' } } } ``` **Sources:** - [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:61-297]() - [backend/src/dsl/types.ts:1-86]() - [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:8-327]()
