## Purpose and Scope This document explains how visual workflow graphs (`WorkflowGraphDto`) are compiled into executable workflow definitions (`WorkflowDefinition`). The compilation process transforms the user-designed node-and-edge graph from the frontend into a structured, validated, and topologically-ordered execution plan for the Temporal worker. For information about the visual workflow builder interface, see [Workflow Builder](#2.1). For information about how compiled workflows are executed, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:270-327]() --- ## Compilation Overview The compilation process is triggered whenever a workflow is created or updated via the backend API. The `compileWorkflowGraph` function serves as the entry point for transforming the visual graph into an executable definition. ```mermaid graph LR WG["WorkflowGraphDto
(nodes + edges)"] COMP["compileWorkflowGraph()"] WD["WorkflowDefinition
(actions + dependencies)"] WG --> COMP COMP --> WD subgraph "Compilation Steps" V["Validate Schema"] CR["Resolve Components"] TS["Topological Sort"] DA["Dependency Analysis"] IM["Input Mapping"] EC["Edge Classification"] V --> CR CR --> TS TS --> DA DA --> IM IM --> EC end COMP -.-> V ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:8-116](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:270-281]() --- ## Input: WorkflowGraphDto The `WorkflowGraphDto` represents the visual workflow graph designed in the frontend canvas. It consists of nodes (representing components) and edges (representing data flow connections). ### Schema Structure | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `name` | `string` | Workflow name | | `description` | `string` (optional) | Workflow description | | `nodes` | `WorkflowNode[]` | Array of workflow nodes | | `edges` | `WorkflowEdge[]` | Array of connections between nodes | | `viewport` | `{x, y, zoom}` | Canvas viewport state | ### WorkflowNode Structure ```typescript { id: string; // Unique node identifier type: string; // Component ID (e.g., 'core.http.request') position: { x: number; y: number }; data: { label: string; // Display name config: { params: Record; // Component parameters inputOverrides: Record; // Manual input values joinStrategy?: 'all' | 'any' | 'first'; // For multi-input nodes streamId?: string; // For grouping parallel nodes mode?: 'normal' | 'tool'; // Tool mode for MCP integration }; }; } ``` ### WorkflowEdge Structure ```typescript { id: string; // Unique edge identifier source: string; // Source node ID target: string; // Target node ID sourceHandle?: string; // Source output port name targetHandle?: string; // Target input port name type?: 'default' | 'smoothstep' | ...; // Visual style } ``` **Validation Rules:** 1. At least one node must be present 2. Multiple edges to the same input port are forbidden (except for the `tools` port, which allows multiple tool connections) 3. Edge source and target nodes must exist in the nodes array **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:5-92](), [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:10-77]() --- ## Output: WorkflowDefinition The `WorkflowDefinition` is the compiled executable format consumed by the Temporal worker. It contains topologically-sorted actions with explicit dependency relationships. ### Structure | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `version` | `number` | Definition schema version (currently 2) | | `title` | `string` | Workflow title | | `description` | `string` (optional) | Workflow description | | `entrypoint` | `{ref: string}` | Reference to the entry point node | | `actions` | `Action[]` | Ordered array of actions to execute | | `nodes` | `Record` | Node metadata lookup | | `edges` | `CompiledEdge[]` | Edge metadata with kind classification | | `dependencyCounts` | `Record` | Dependency count per node | | `config` | `{environment, timeoutSeconds}` | Workflow configuration | ### Action Structure ```typescript { ref: string; // Node reference (same as node ID) componentId: string; // Component identifier params: Record; // Component parameters inputOverrides: Record; // Manual input values dependsOn: string[]; // Array of upstream node refs inputMappings: Record; } ``` ### CompiledEdge Structure ```typescript { id: string; sourceRef: string; targetRef: string; sourceHandle?: string; targetHandle?: string; kind: 'success' | 'failure'; // Edge classification } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:79-116](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:169-192]() --- ## Compilation Process ### Component Resolution and Validation ```mermaid graph TD START["Start Compilation"] LOOP["For each node"] EXTRACT["Extract componentId
from node.type"] LOOKUP["componentRegistry.getMetadata()"] CHECK{"Component
registered?"} ERROR["Throw: Component not registered"] META["Store component metadata"] NEXT["Next node"] CONTINUE["Continue to sorting"] START --> LOOP LOOP --> EXTRACT EXTRACT --> LOOKUP LOOKUP --> CHECK CHECK -->|No| ERROR CHECK -->|Yes| META META --> NEXT NEXT --> LOOP LOOP -->|Done| CONTINUE ``` The compiler first validates that all referenced components are registered in the `componentRegistry`. If an unknown component is encountered, compilation fails with an error. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:118-142](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:422-443]() --- ### Entry Point Identification The compiler identifies the workflow entry point by searching for nodes with Entry Point component types: - `core.workflow.entrypoint` - `entry-point` (legacy) The entry point is **always** used as the workflow's starting node, regardless of topological position. This ensures consistent workflow initialization. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:192-234](), [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:259-260]() --- ### Topological Sorting The compiler performs a topological sort to order actions for execution based on their dependencies. ```mermaid graph TB INIT["Initialize:
- Empty sorted list
- Zero in-degree queue
- In-degree counts"] SEED["Add nodes with
0 in-degree to queue"] LOOP{"Queue
empty?"} DEQUEUE["Dequeue node"] APPEND["Append to sorted list"] UPDATE["For each downstream node:
Decrement in-degree"] ZERO{"In-degree
= 0?"} ENQUEUE["Add to queue"] CHECK{"Sorted list size
= node count?"} SUCCESS["Return sorted actions"] CYCLE["Throw: Cycle detected"] INIT --> SEED SEED --> LOOP LOOP -->|No| DEQUEUE DEQUEUE --> APPEND APPEND --> UPDATE UPDATE --> ZERO ZERO -->|Yes| ENQUEUE ZERO -->|No| UPDATE ENQUEUE --> LOOP LOOP -->|Yes| CHECK CHECK -->|Yes| SUCCESS CHECK -->|No| CYCLE ``` **Algorithm:** 1. Calculate in-degree (number of incoming edges) for each node 2. Enqueue all nodes with zero in-degree 3. While queue is not empty: - Dequeue a node and add to sorted list - For each outgoing edge, decrement target node's in-degree - If target in-degree reaches zero, enqueue it 4. If sorted list size ≠ node count, a cycle exists **Cycle Detection:** If any nodes remain after the algorithm completes, they form a cycle. The compiler throws an error: `"Workflow graph contains a cycle"`. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:144-190](), [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:236-326]() --- ### Dependency Analysis For each node, the compiler builds two critical data structures: #### 1. Dependency Counts The `dependencyCounts` map tracks how many upstream dependencies each node has. This is used by the executor to determine when a node is ready to run. ```typescript dependencyCounts: { 'trigger': 0, // Entry point, no dependencies 'loader': 1, // Depends on trigger 'webhook': 1, // Depends on loader 'merge': 2 // Depends on branchA and branchB } ``` #### 2. dependsOn Array Each action includes a `dependsOn` array listing the references of all immediate upstream nodes: ```typescript { ref: 'webhook', componentId: 'core.http.request', dependsOn: ['loader'], // Must wait for loader to complete // ... } ``` **Parallel Execution:** Nodes with the same dependency depth can execute in parallel. For example, in a diamond pattern: ```mermaid graph LR START["start
(depth 0)"] A["branchA
(depth 1)"] B["branchB
(depth 1)"] MERGE["merge
(depth 2)"] START --> A START --> B A --> MERGE B --> MERGE ``` Both `branchA` and `branchB` have depth 1 and can execute concurrently. The `merge` node waits for both to complete (dependency count = 2). **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:236-326](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:150-262]() --- ### Input Mapping The compiler analyzes edges to build input mappings that wire upstream outputs to downstream inputs. ```mermaid graph LR SOURCE["Source Node
'loader'"] TARGET["Target Node
'webhook'"] SOURCE -->|"output: textContent"| EDGE["Edge"] EDGE -->|"input: body"| TARGET subgraph "Compiled Mapping" MAP["inputMappings: {
body: {
sourceRef: 'loader',
sourceHandle: 'textContent'
}
}"] end EDGE -.-> MAP ``` **Mapping Resolution:** For each edge: 1. Extract `source`, `target`, `sourceHandle`, `targetHandle` 2. Create mapping entry: `inputMappings[targetHandle] = { sourceRef: source, sourceHandle }` 3. If `targetHandle` is undefined, use `sourceHandle` as the target input name **Example:** ```typescript // Edge definition { source: 'loader', target: 'webhook', sourceHandle: 'textContent', targetHandle: 'body' } // Compiled into webhook action { ref: 'webhook', inputMappings: { body: { sourceRef: 'loader', sourceHandle: 'textContent' } } } ``` At runtime, the executor uses these mappings to retrieve output values from completed upstream nodes and provide them as inputs to downstream nodes. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:98-116](), [backend/src/workflows/__tests__/workflow-ai-agent.spec.ts:98-122]() --- ### Edge Classification Edges are classified into two kinds during compilation: | Kind | Description | Usage | |------|-------------|-------| | `success` | Normal data flow edge | Default for most connections | | `failure` | Error handling edge | Currently reserved for future use | Currently, all edges are classified as `success` edges. The `failure` edge type is reserved for future error handling workflows where certain nodes should only execute if an upstream node fails. **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:98-116]() --- ### Connected Tool Nodes For nodes that support MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool integration, the compiler populates a `connectedToolNodeIds` array by analyzing edges connected to the special `tools` port. ```mermaid graph LR TOOL1["Tool Node 1
(mode: 'tool')"] TOOL2["Tool Node 2
(mode: 'tool')"] AGENT["AI Agent Node"] TOOL1 -->|"targetHandle: tools"| AGENT TOOL2 -->|"targetHandle: tools"| AGENT subgraph "Compiled Agent Action" CONFIG["config: {
connectedToolNodeIds: [
'tool1',
'tool2'
]
}"] end AGENT -.-> CONFIG ``` **Algorithm:** 1. For each edge where `targetHandle === 'tools'` 2. Add the source node ID to the target node's `connectedToolNodeIds` array 3. These IDs are used at runtime to discover and register available tools for AI agents **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:328-424]() --- ## Dynamic Port Resolution Components can dynamically resolve their input and output ports based on configuration parameters. This is particularly important for the Entry Point component, which creates output ports based on runtime input definitions. ### Process ```mermaid graph TD NODE["Node in Graph"] CHECK{"Component has
resolvePorts()?"} EXTRACT["Extract node params"] CALL["Call component.resolvePorts(params)"] UPDATE["Update node.data with:
- dynamicInputs
- dynamicOutputs"] SKIP["Use static ports"] CONTINUE["Continue compilation"] NODE --> CHECK CHECK -->|Yes| EXTRACT EXTRACT --> CALL CALL --> UPDATE UPDATE --> CONTINUE CHECK -->|No| SKIP SKIP --> CONTINUE ``` ### Example: Entry Point Dynamic Outputs When an Entry Point node defines runtime inputs: ```typescript // Node configuration { params: { runtimeInputs: [ { id: 'domain', label: 'Domain', type: 'text' }, { id: 'apiKey', label: 'API Key', type: 'secret' } ] } } // Resolved dynamic outputs { dynamicOutputs: [ { id: 'domain', label: 'Domain', connectionType: {...} }, { id: 'apiKey', label: 'API Key', connectionType: {...} } ] } ``` These dynamic outputs can then be connected to downstream nodes via edges in the workflow graph. **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:445-521](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:370-383]() --- ## Compilation Integration ### Service Layer Integration The `WorkflowsService` invokes compilation during workflow creation and updates: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant WorkflowsController participant WorkflowsService participant Compiler participant Repository Client->>WorkflowsController: POST /workflows WorkflowsController->>WorkflowsService: create(dto) WorkflowsService->>Compiler: compileWorkflowGraph(graph) alt Compilation Succeeds Compiler-->>WorkflowsService: WorkflowDefinition WorkflowsService->>Repository: create workflow record WorkflowsService->>Repository: create version with graph Repository-->>WorkflowsService: WorkflowVersion WorkflowsService-->>WorkflowsController: WorkflowResponse WorkflowsController-->>Client: 200 OK else Compilation Fails Compiler-->>WorkflowsService: ValidationError WorkflowsService-->>WorkflowsController: BadRequestException WorkflowsController-->>Client: 400 Bad Request end ``` **Key Points:** - Compilation happens **before** database persistence - Invalid workflows are rejected immediately - Each save creates a new workflow version with compiled definition - The compiled definition is stored in the `workflow_versions` table **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:270-310](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:312-341]() --- ## Error Handling ### Common Validation Errors | Error | Cause | Example | |-------|-------|---------| | `Component not registered: {id}` | Node references an unknown component | Using `'custom.component'` without registering it | | `Workflow validation failed: {message}` | Schema validation failure | Missing required fields, invalid types | | `Workflow graph contains a cycle` | Circular dependency detected | Node A → Node B → Node A | | `Multiple edges connecting to the same input port` | Duplicate input connections | Two edges targeting `input.value` | | `At least one node must be present` | Empty workflow | Graph with `nodes: []` | ### Validation Timing ```mermaid graph LR REQUEST["HTTP Request"] SCHEMA["Zod Schema
Validation"] COMPILE["Workflow
Compilation"] PERSIST["Database
Persistence"] REQUEST --> SCHEMA SCHEMA -->|"Invalid Schema"| ERROR1["400 Bad Request"] SCHEMA -->|Valid| COMPILE COMPILE -->|"Compilation Error"| ERROR2["400 Bad Request"] COMPILE -->|Success| PERSIST PERSIST --> SUCCESS["200 OK"] ``` **Error Response Format:** ```json { "statusCode": 400, "message": "Workflow validation failed: Component not registered: custom.unknown", "error": "Bad Request" } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:270-281](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:312-327](), [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:118-142](), [backend/src/dsl/__tests__/compiler.spec.ts:144-190]() --- ## Commit Endpoint The `/workflows/:id/commit` endpoint provides an explicit way to validate and compile a workflow without creating a new version: ```typescript POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/commit ``` **Response:** ```json { "title": "Sample Workflow", "description": "Workflow description", "entrypoint": { "ref": "trigger" }, "actions": [ { "ref": "trigger", "componentId": "core.workflow.entrypoint", "params": {}, "dependsOn": [], "inputMappings": {} } ], "config": { "environment": "default", "timeoutSeconds": 0 } } ``` This endpoint is useful for: - Validating workflow graphs before execution - Debugging compilation issues - Previewing the compiled definition structure **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:520-573](), [openapi.json:638-718]() --- ## Compilation Result Example ### Input Graph ```typescript { name: 'Sample workflow', nodes: [ { id: 'trigger', type: 'core.workflow.entrypoint', position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, data: { label: 'Trigger', config: { params: { runtimeInputs: [{ id: 'fileId', label: 'File ID', type: 'file' }] } } } }, { id: 'loader', This document describes the REST API layer for managing workflows in ShipSec Studio. The Workflow Management API provides HTTP endpoints for creating, updating, executing, and monitoring workflows. For information about the visual workflow editor, see [Workflow Builder](#2.1). For details on workflow compilation, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.2). For execution mechanics, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). ## Overview The Workflow Management API consists of two primary layers: - **Controller Layer** (`WorkflowsController`): HTTP endpoint handlers that validate requests, apply authorization guards, and transform responses for the REST API - **Service Layer** (`WorkflowsService`): Business logic for workflow lifecycle management, version control, execution orchestration, and status tracking The API is documented using OpenAPI 3.0 and generates type-safe client libraries for frontend consumption via `@shipsec/backend-client`. **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:1-260](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:1-143]() --- ## API Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend Layer" FE_API["api.ts
Frontend API Client"] BC["@shipsec/backend-client
Type-safe Client"] end subgraph "Backend HTTP Layer" CTRL["WorkflowsController
/api/v1/workflows"] GUARDS["WorkflowRoleGuard
Auth Guards"] PIPES["ZodValidationPipe
Request Validation"] end subgraph "Business Logic Layer" SVC["WorkflowsService
Business Logic"] VSVC["VersionRepository
Version Management"] RSVC["RunRepository
Run Tracking"] TSVC["TemporalService
Workflow Execution"] end subgraph "Data Layer" DB[(PostgreSQL
workflow_records

shipsecWorkflowRun] end FE_API --> BC BC --> CTRL CTRL --> GUARDS CTRL --> PIPES CTRL --> SVC SVC --> VSVC SVC --> RSVC SVC --> TSVC VSVC --> DB RSVC --> DB TSVC --> TEMP SVC --> DB ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:244-255](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:131-143](), [frontend/src/services/api.ts:175-265]() --- ## Workflow CRUD Endpoints The API provides standard CRUD operations for workflow management. This document covers the workflow scheduling system that enables automated, time-based execution of workflows using cron expressions. Schedules define when workflows should run, what inputs to provide, and how to handle overlapping executions. For information about manual workflow execution via the API, see [Workflow Management API](#2.5). For details on workflow execution mechanics, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). --- ## Overview The scheduling system provides automated workflow execution through integration with Temporal's native schedule feature. Each schedule defines: - **Timing**: Cron expression and timezone - **Target**: Workflow and specific version to execute - **Inputs**: Runtime inputs and node parameter overrides - **Policies**: Overlap behavior and catchup windows Schedules are managed through the `SchedulesService` and persist independently of workflow definitions, allowing multiple schedules per workflow with different configurations. **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:1-20]() --- ## Schedule Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "API Layer" Controller["SchedulesController

Temporal Schedule Integration ### Schedule Dispatch Workflow When a Temporal schedule triggers, it executes the `scheduleTriggerWorkflow` which prepares the run payload and starts the main workflow: ```mermaid graph LR TemporalSchedule["Temporal Schedule
(cron trigger)"] ScheduleTriggerWF["scheduleTriggerWorkflow"] PrepareActivity["prepareRunPayloadActivity

(policy: skip) Executing --> BufferTrigger: New cron trigger
(policy: buffer) Executing --> ExecuteConcurrent: New cron trigger
(policy: allow) SkipTrigger --> [*]: Drop BufferTrigger --> Buffered ExecuteConcurrent --> Executing: Start new instance Buffered --> Executing: Previous completes ``` **Diagram: Overlap Policy State Machine** The policy mapping occurs in [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:440-450](): ```typescript private mapOverlapPolicy(policy: ScheduleOverlapPolicy): TemporalScheduleOverlapPolicy { switch (policy) { case 'allow': return TemporalScheduleOverlapPolicy.ALLOW_ALL; case 'buffer': return TemporalScheduleOverlapPolicy.BUFFER_ONE; case 'skip': default: return TemporalScheduleOverlapPolicy.SKIP; } } ``` **Sources**: [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:440-450](), [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:41-118]() --- ## Schedule Lifecycle Management ### Status Transitions ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Active: create() Active --> Paused: pause() Paused --> Active: resume() Active --> Archived: delete() Paused --> Archived: delete() Archived --> [*] note right of Active Temporal schedule running Triggers at cron times end note note right of Paused Temporal schedule paused No triggers end note note right of Archived Temporal schedule deleted Database record retained end note ``` **Diagram: Schedule Status Lifecycle** ### Management Operations | Operation | Method | Temporal Action | |-----------|--------|-----------------| | Create | `create()` | `TemporalService.createSchedule()` | | Update | `update()` | `TemporalService.updateSchedule()` | | Pause | `pause()` | `TemporalService.pauseSchedule()` | | Resume | `resume()` | `TemporalService.resumeSchedule()` | | Delete | `delete()` | `TemporalService.deleteSchedule()` | | Trigger | `trigger()` | `TemporalService.triggerSchedule()` | **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:120-192](), [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:194-225]() --- ## Schedule Input Payloads ### Payload Structure Schedules can provide both runtime inputs (to the entrypoint) and node-specific overrides: ```mermaid graph TB Payload["ScheduleInputPayload"] Runtime["runtimeInputs

Record<string, unknown>"] Payload --> Runtime Payload --> Overrides Overrides --> NodeOverride NodeOverride --> Params NodeOverride --> InputOverrides ``` **Diagram: Schedule Payload Structure** ### Example: Security Scan Schedule ```typescript { runtimeInputs: { targetDomain: "example.com", notificationEmail: "security@example.com" }, nodeOverrides: { "nuclei-scanner": { params: { severity: ["critical", "high"], timeout: 600 }, inputOverrides: {} }, "slack-notifier": { params: {}, inputOverrides: { webhookUrl: "secret:slack-webhook" } } } } ``` This payload: 1. Provides `targetDomain` and `notificationEmail` to the workflow entrypoint 2. Overrides the `nuclei-scanner` node's severity filter and timeout 3. Binds a secret webhook URL to the Slack notifier node **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:237-303](), [shared/types/workflow-schedule.ts:1-50]() --- ## Catchup Windows Catchup windows define how long Temporal should attempt to execute missed schedule triggers: ```mermaid timeline title Catchup Window Behavior section Schedule Misses Expected Run 1 : Scheduler down Expected Run 2 : Scheduler down Expected Run 3 : Scheduler down section Scheduler Restarts Catchup Window Check : Within window? Execute Missed Runs : Run 2 and Run 3 Skip Old Runs : Run 1 too old ``` **Diagram: Catchup Window Timeline** ### Configuration Set via `catchupWindowSeconds` in schedule creation: ```typescript { catchupWindowSeconds: 3600, // 1 hour // If scheduler was down for 2 hours, only runs from the last 1 hour execute } ``` A value of `0` disables catchup entirely—missed runs are skipped. **Sources**: [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:355-378]() --- ## Schedule Repository Operations ### Core Repository Methods The `ScheduleRepository` provides database operations: | Method | Purpose | Filters | |--------|---------|---------| | `create()` | Insert new schedule | Organization isolation | | `update()` | Modify schedule fields | Organization isolation | | `findById()` | Fetch single schedule | Organization + ID | | `list()` | Query schedules | Workflow ID, status, organization | | `delete()` | Remove schedule | Organization isolation | ### Query Filtering [backend/src/schedules/repository/schedule.repository.ts:45-90]() supports filtering by: - `workflowId`: All schedules for a workflow - `status`: Active, paused, or archived - `organizationId`: Multi-tenant isolation **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/repository/schedule.repository.ts:1-150]() --- ## Execution Trigger Metadata When a schedule triggers a workflow, it injects `ExecutionTriggerMetadata` to identify the trigger source: ```typescript { type: "schedule", sourceId: scheduleId, label: scheduleName, timestamp: new Date().toISOString() } ``` This metadata: 1. Enables audit trails and analytics The metadata flows through: ```mermaid graph LR Schedule["Schedule Trigger"] DispatchArgs["ScheduleTriggerWorkflowArgs
trigger: {type, sourceId}"] PrepareActivity["prepareRunPayloadActivity"] RunRecord["workflow_runs table
trigger_type, trigger_source"] Schedule --> DispatchArgs DispatchArgs --> PrepareActivity PrepareActivity --> RunRecord ``` **Diagram: Trigger Metadata Flow** **Sources**: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/schedule-trigger.workflow.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow-run.repository.ts:1-200]() --- ## Manual Schedule Triggers Schedules can be manually triggered outside their cron schedule via `SchedulesService.trigger()`: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant SchedulesService participant TemporalService participant ScheduleTriggerWF Client->>SchedulesService: trigger(scheduleId) SchedulesService->>SchedulesService: findOwnedScheduleOrThrow() SchedulesService->>TemporalService: triggerSchedule(scheduleId) TemporalService->>ScheduleTriggerWF: immediate execution ScheduleTriggerWF-->>Client: workflow started ``` **Diagram: Manual Schedule Trigger** This is useful for: - Testing schedule configurations - Responding to external events - Ad-hoc runs without modifying the schedule **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:227-235](), [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:428-432]() --- ## Schedule Versioning Schedules reference specific workflow versions to ensure consistency: | Field | Purpose | |-------|---------| | `workflowVersionId` | UUID of the workflow version | | `workflowVersion` | Semantic version number | When a workflow is updated: 1. Existing schedules continue using their pinned version 2. New schedules can target the latest version 3. Schedules can be updated to use newer versions This prevents breaking changes from affecting running schedules unexpectedly. **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:41-118](), [backend/src/database/schema/schedules.ts:1-30]() --- ## Testing Schedules The test suite [backend/src/schedules/__tests__/schedules.service.spec.ts:1-450]() verifies: ### Validation Tests - Required runtime inputs are enforced - Node overrides reference valid nodes - Workflow admin access is checked ### Lifecycle Tests - Creation registers both database and Temporal schedules - Updates synchronize both representations - Pausing/resuming affects Temporal schedule state - Deletion cleans up Temporal schedules ### Payload Tests - Empty payloads default to `{runtimeInputs: {}, nodeOverrides: {}}` - Invalid payloads are rejected during creation - Node overrides are validated against workflow definition **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/__tests__/schedules.service.spec.ts:1-450]() --- ## Timezone Handling Schedules use IANA timezone identifiers (e.g., `"America/New_York"`, `"Europe/London"`) for cron expression evaluation. Temporal's scheduler handles: - Daylight saving time transitions - Timezone offset calculations - Consistent execution times across time changes ```typescript { cronExpression: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM daily timezone: "America/New_York" // Eastern Time (handles DST) } ``` During DST transitions: - Spring forward: 9 AM EDT (UTC-4) - Fall back: 9 AM EST (UTC-5) **Sources**: [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:355-378]() --- ## Summary The scheduling system provides: 1. **Automated Execution**: Cron-based workflow triggers via Temporal schedules 2. **Flexible Input Configuration**: Runtime inputs and node overrides per schedule 3. **Robust Policies**: Overlap handling and catchup windows 4. **Lifecycle Management**: Create, update, pause, resume, and delete operations 5. **Version Pinning**: Schedules reference specific workflow versions 6. **Multi-tenant Isolation**: Organization-scoped schedule management Key code entities: - `SchedulesService` - Core scheduling logic - `TemporalService.createSchedule()` - Temporal integration - `scheduleTriggerWorkflow` - Dispatch mechanism - `ScheduleInputPayload` - Input configuration structure - `workflow_schedules` table - Persistence layer **Sources**: [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts:1-450](), [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts:355-450]()

# Sub-Workflows and Composition
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts](backend/src/schedules/schedules.service.ts) - [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts](backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/activities/mcp.activity.ts](worker/src/temporal/activities/mcp.activity.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/types.ts](worker/src/temporal/types.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts](worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts](worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts)
## Purpose and Scope This document describes how workflows can call other workflows as sub-workflows, creating hierarchical execution structures. It covers the `core.workflow.call` component, safety mechanisms including depth limits and cycle detection, timeout protection, input/output data flow, and parent-child relationship tracking. For scheduling workflows to run automatically, see [Schedules and Automation](#2.6). For the overall workflow execution engine, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). For data flow and input mappings, see [Data Flow and Spilling](#2.8). --- ## Sub-Workflow Call Component The `core.workflow.call` component enables workflows to invoke other workflows as nested operations. Each sub-workflow call creates a new Temporal child workflow execution with its own run ID, trace events, and lifecycle. **Detection and Execution Path** The workflow orchestrator detects sub-workflow calls by checking if `action.componentId === 'core.workflow.call'` [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:354](). When detected, the system follows a specialized execution path distinct from regular component execution. ```mermaid graph TD Scheduler["WorkflowScheduler
dispatches action"] Check["Check componentId
action.componentId === 'core.workflow.call'"] Validate["Validate Parameters
- workflowId (required)
- versionStrategy
- timeoutSeconds
- childRuntimeInputs"] SafetyChecks["Safety Checks
- Depth limit
- Cycle detection"] PreparePayload["prepareRunPayloadActivity
Load child workflow definition"] StartChild["startChild()
Launch Temporal child workflow"] WaitResult["Wait for child.result()
with timeout protection"] RecordOutput["Record child outputs
to parent results map"] Scheduler --> Check Check -->|"core.workflow.call"| Validate Validate --> SafetyChecks SafetyChecks --> PreparePayload PreparePayload --> StartChild StartChild --> WaitResult WaitResult --> RecordOutput Check -->|"other component"| RegularExec["Regular component
execution path"] ``` **Configuration Parameters** The component accepts the following configuration parameters [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:389-430](): | Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description | |-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------| | `workflowId` | `string` | Yes | - | Target workflow identifier to invoke | | `versionStrategy` | `'latest' \| 'specific'` | No | `'latest'` | Whether to use latest version or specific version | | `versionId` | `string` | Conditional | - | Required if `versionStrategy` is `'specific'` | | `timeoutSeconds` | `number` | No | `300` | Maximum execution time for child workflow | | `childRuntimeInputs` | `Array<{id: string}>` | No | `[]` | List of input IDs to pass from parent to child | **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:354-644]() --- ## Safety Mechanisms Sub-workflow composition includes multiple safety mechanisms to prevent resource exhaustion, infinite loops, and runaway executions. ### Depth Limit Protection The system enforces a maximum nesting depth of 10 levels to prevent stack overflow and excessive resource consumption. Each workflow tracks its depth via the `depth` parameter [worker/src/temporal/types.ts:134](). ```mermaid graph LR Root["Workflow A
depth=0"] Child1["Workflow B
depth=1"] Child2["Workflow C
depth=2"] ChildN["...
depth=N"] Limit["Workflow Z
depth=10
(MAX_SUBWORKFLOW_DEPTH)"] Error["❌ ApplicationFailure
SubWorkflowDepthError"] Root -->|"calls"| Child1 Child1 -->|"calls"| Child2 Child2 -->|"calls"| ChildN ChildN -->|"calls"| Limit Limit -->|"attempts to call"| Error ``` The depth check occurs before any child workflow preparation [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:355-363](): ``` if (depth >= MAX_SUBWORKFLOW_DEPTH) { throw ApplicationFailure.nonRetryable( `Maximum sub-workflow nesting depth (${MAX_SUBWORKFLOW_DEPTH}) exceeded`, 'SubWorkflowDepthError', [{ runId: input.runId, nodeRef: action.ref, depth }] ); } ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:355-363](), [worker/src/temporal/types.ts:134]() ### Cycle Detection The system maintains a `callChain` array tracking all workflow IDs in the current execution path. Before starting a child workflow, the system checks if the target workflow ID already exists in the call chain [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:398-404](). ```mermaid graph TD WFA["Workflow A
callChain: [A]"] WFB["Workflow B

'Circular sub-workflow call detected'"] WFA -->|"calls B"| WFB WFB -->|"calls C"| WFC WFC -->|"calls A"| AttemptA AttemptA --> Error style Error fill:#fee ``` The call chain is initialized with the root workflow ID and extended with each nesting level [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:284-288, 527](): ``` const callChain = Array.isArray(input.callChain) && input.callChain.length > 0 ? input.callChain : [input.workflowId]; // Later, when starting child: callChain: [...callChain, childWorkflowId] ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:284-288, 398-404, 527]() ### Timeout Protection Each sub-workflow call enforces a configurable timeout (default 300 seconds). The system uses `Promise.race()` to compete the child workflow execution against a sleep timer [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:533-594](). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Parent as "Parent Workflow" participant Child as "Child Workflow" participant Timer as "Sleep Timer" Parent->>Child: startChild(shipsecWorkflowRun) Parent->>Timer: sleep(timeoutMs) alt Child completes first Child-->>Parent: result (success/failure) Note over Parent: outcome.kind = 'result' Parent->>Parent: Process child result else Timer fires first Timer-->>Parent: timeout Note over Parent: outcome.kind = 'timeout' Parent->>Child: cancel() via getExternalWorkflowHandle Parent->>Parent: Throw TimeoutError end ``` When timeout occurs, the parent workflow obtains an external handle to the child and cancels it [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:567-594](): ``` if (outcome.kind === 'timeout') { const externalHandle = getExternalWorkflowHandle(child.workflowId); await externalHandle.cancel(); throw ApplicationFailure.nonRetryable( `Sub-workflow timed out after ${timeoutSeconds}s`, 'TimeoutError', [{ runId, nodeRef, childRunId, timeoutSeconds }] ); } ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:424-430, 533-594]() --- ## Input and Output Flow ### Parent-to-Child Input Mapping The `childRuntimeInputs` parameter specifies which inputs to pass from the parent workflow context to the child workflow's entry point. When `'specific'` is selected, the `versionId` parameter becomes required [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:406-422](): ``` const versionStrategy = mergedParams.versionStrategy === 'specific' ? parent results map"] ChildExec --> ResultCheck ResultCheck -->|"prepare() throws"| PrepFail ResultCheck -->|"child.result() throws"| ChildError ResultCheck -->|"result.success === false"| ChildFailure ResultCheck -->|"timeout"| Timeout ResultCheck -->|"success"| Success PrepFail --> RecordFailed ChildError --> RecordFailed ChildFailure --> RecordFailed Timeout --> RecordFailed RecordFailed --> ThrowError Success --> RecordSuccess RecordSuccess --> StoreResult ``` Error trace events include structured metadata for debugging [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:547-563](): ``` await recordTraceEventActivity({ type: 'NODE_FAILED', runId: input.runId, nodeRef: action.ref, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), message, level: 'error', error: { message, type: 'SubWorkflowError', details: { childRunId }, }, context: { activityId: 'workflow-orchestration', childRunId, }, }); ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:464-641]() --- ## Temporal Child Workflow Mechanics ### Workflow Handle Creation The system uses Temporal's `startChild()` function to create a child workflow execution [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:514-531](): ```typescript const child = await startChild(shipsecWorkflowRun, { args: [{ runId: prepared.runId, workflowId: prepared.workflowId, definition: prepared.definition, inputs: prepared.inputs ?? {}, workflowVersionId: prepared.workflowVersionId, workflowVersion: prepared.workflowVersion, organizationId: prepared.organizationId, parentRunId: input.runId, parentNodeRef: action.ref, depth: depth + 1, callChain: [...callChain, childWorkflowId], }], workflowId: prepared.runId, }); ``` The child workflow uses the same `shipsecWorkflowRun` workflow function as the parent, creating a recursive execution structure. ### Result Retrieval The parent waits for child completion by calling `child.result()`, which returns a promise that resolves when the child workflow finishes [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:533-565](): ``` outcome = await Promise.race([ child.result().then((result) => ({ kind: 'result' as const, result })), sleep(timeoutMs).then(() => ({ kind: 'timeout' as const })), ]); ``` If `child.result()` rejects (child workflow threw an error), the catch handler records a `NODE_FAILED` event before re-throwing [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:542-565](). **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:514-565]() --- ## Integration with Workflow Scheduler The `WorkflowScheduler` dispatches sub-workflow calls just like any other component [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts](). The key difference is that the handler function returns early after processing the sub-workflow, rather than executing a component activity [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:643](): ``` // After sub-workflow completes successfully return {}; // Empty return - scheduler continues with dependent nodes ``` This return value signals to the scheduler that the action completed successfully and dependent actions (based on edges from this node) can proceed. **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:354-644]()

## Purpose and Scope This document explains how data flows between nodes during workflow execution and how the system handles large payloads through a "spilling" mechanism. When component outputs exceed Temporal's message size limits, they are automatically offloaded to MinIO storage and replaced with reference markers. For information about workflow compilation and action dependencies, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.3). For details about the scheduler that orchestrates node execution, see [Workflow Scheduler](#8.5). For node execution internals, see [Component Execution Model](#3.3). --- ## Input Mappings and Data Flow During workflow execution, data flows between nodes through **input mappings**. Each workflow action defines which outputs from previous nodes should be mapped to its inputs. ### Input Mapping Structure ```typescript interface WorkflowAction { ref: string; componentId: string; inputMappings: Record; inputOverrides: Record; // Manual values (not mapped) params: Record; } ``` ### Payload Building Process The `buildActionPayload` function resolves input mappings by reading from a results map populated during workflow execution: ```mermaid graph TB ResultsMap["Results Map
(ref → output)"] Action["WorkflowAction
(inputMappings)"] BuildPayload["buildActionPayload()"] ResolvedInputs["Resolved Inputs"] Warnings["Warnings
(undefined inputs)"] ResultsMap --> BuildPayload Action --> BuildPayload BuildPayload --> ResolvedInputs BuildPayload --> Warnings ResolvedInputs --> ComponentExecution["Component Execution"] Warnings --> ValidationCheck["Validation Check"] ``` **Diagram: Input Resolution Flow** When a node is ready to execute: 1. The scheduler calls the run function with the action reference 2. `buildActionPayload` iterates over `inputMappings` 3. For each mapping, it looks up `sourceRef` in the results map 4. It extracts the value at `sourceHandle` from the source output 5. If the value is `undefined`, a warning is recorded 6. Manual `inputOverrides` take precedence over mapped values Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:323-326](), [worker/src/temporal/input-resolver.ts:14](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:135-177]() ### Handling Undefined Inputs ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> CheckMapping CheckMapping --> SourceExists: sourceRef in results? SourceExists --> HandleExists: Yes SourceExists --> UndefinedWarning: No HandleExists --> ValueExists: sourceHandle in output? ValueExists --> ReturnValue: Yes ValueExists --> UndefinedWarning: No UndefinedWarning --> CheckRequired: Record warning CheckRequired --> ThrowError: Required input CheckRequired --> AllowUndefined: Optional input ReturnValue --> [*] AllowUndefined --> [*] ThrowError --> [*] ``` **Diagram: Input Resolution State Machine** The system distinguishes between required and optional inputs using component port metadata: - Inputs marked with `required: false` allow `undefined` values - Inputs with `connectionType.kind === 'any'` accept `undefined` - Missing required inputs cause the workflow to fail with a `ValidationError` Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:398-450](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:159-177]() --- ## Spilling Mechanism To avoid Temporal's 2MB message size limit, the system automatically "spills" large payloads to MinIO object storage. ### Threshold and Detection ```typescript // Constant defining when to spill const TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB // Spilled data marker structure interface SpilledDataMarker { __spilled__: true; storageRef: string; // MinIO file ID (UUID) originalSize: number; // Size in bytes before spilling __spilled_handle__?: string; // Optional: field to extract } // Detection function function isSpilledDataMarker(value: unknown): boolean { return ( typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && '__spilled__' in value && (value as any).__spilled__ === true ); } ``` Sources: [packages/component-sdk/src/spill.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:10]() ### Spill Operation (Writing Large Data) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Component participant Activity as runComponentActivity participant Storage as FileStorageAdapter participant MinIO Component->>Activity: return output (e.g., 10MB) Activity->>Activity: JSON.stringify(output) Activity->>Activity: Check size > 5MB Activity->>Activity: Generate UUID (fileId) Activity->>Storage: uploadFile(fileId, "output.json", buffer) Storage->>MinIO: PUT object MinIO-->>Storage: Success Storage-->>Activity: Success Activity->>Activity: Replace output with marker Note over Activity: { __spilled__: true,
storageRef: fileId,
originalSize: 10485760 } Activity-->>Component: Return spilled marker ``` **Diagram: Output Spilling Sequence** The spilling process occurs after component execution but before returning to the workflow: 1. Component returns output (any JSON-serializable data) 2. Activity serializes output to JSON and measures size 3. If size exceeds `TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES`: - Generate a random UUID as the storage reference - Upload serialized output to MinIO with content type `application/json` - Replace the entire output with a spilled marker 4. Return the marker (or original output if below threshold) to Temporal workflow Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:492-518](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:326-351]() ### Unspill Operation (Reading Large Data) When a downstream node receives inputs, the activity checks for spilled markers and resolves them: ```mermaid graph TB ReceivedInputs["Received Inputs
(params + inputs)"] CheckSpilled{"For each value:
isSpilledDataMarker?"} UseDirectly["Use value directly"] CheckCache{"In spilledObjectsCache?"} DownloadFile["downloadFile(storageRef)"] ParseJSON["JSON.parse(content)"] AddToCache["Add to cache"] ExtractField{"Has __spilled_handle__?"} ExtractValue["Extract field from object"] UseFullObject["Use full object"] ResolvedInputs["Resolved Inputs"] ReceivedInputs --> CheckSpilled CheckSpilled -->|No| UseDirectly CheckSpilled -->|Yes| CheckCache CheckCache -->|Hit| ExtractField CheckCache -->|Miss| DownloadFile DownloadFile --> ParseJSON ParseJSON --> AddToCache AddToCache --> ExtractField ExtractField -->|Yes| ExtractValue ExtractField -->|No| UseFullObject UseDirectly --> ResolvedInputs ExtractValue --> ResolvedInputs UseFullObject --> ResolvedInputs ``` **Diagram: Unspilling Data Flow** The unspill operation in `runComponentActivity`: ```typescript async function unspill(obj: Record, contextLabel: string) { for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(obj)) { if (isSpilledDataMarker(value)) { // Check cache first to avoid redundant downloads let fullData: any; if (spilledObjectsCache.has(value.storageRef)) { fullData = spilledObjectsCache.get(value.storageRef); } else { // Download from storage const content = await globalStorage.downloadFile(value.storageRef); fullData = JSON.parse(content.buffer.toString('utf8')); spilledObjectsCache.set(value.storageRef, fullData); } // Extract specific field if handle provided const handle = value.__spilled_handle__; if (handle && handle !== '__self__') { obj[key] = fullData[handle]; // Extract field } else { obj[key] = fullData; // Use entire object } } } } ``` Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:229-288](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:179-230]() ### Handle-Based Field Extraction The `__spilled_handle__` field enables efficient partial data extraction. When only a specific field from a large object is needed: ```typescript // Example: Node A produces large output const outputA = { largeArray: [...], // 8MB summary: { count: 100 } // 1KB }; // After spilling, the marker might be: { __spilled__: true, storageRef: "uuid-123", originalSize: 8388608, __spilled_handle__: "summary" // Only extract 'summary' field } // Node B receives only summary (1KB) instead of downloading full 8MB ``` This optimization reduces memory usage when workflows chain through large datasets but only require metadata or summaries. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:254-273](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:202-220]() --- ## Secret Masking in Data Flow To prevent sensitive data from appearing in logs and traces, the system masks secret values during Node I/O recording. ### Secret Port Identification ```typescript interface ComponentPortMetadata { id: string; editor?: 'secret' | 'text' | ...; connectionType?: { kind: 'primitive' | 'contract' | 'any'; name?: 'secret' | 'string' | ...; credential?: boolean; }; } // A port is secret if: // 1. editor === 'secret', OR // 2. connectionType.kind === 'primitive' AND name === 'secret', OR // 3. connectionType.kind === 'contract' AND credential === true ``` ### Masking Pipeline ```mermaid graph LR RawInputs["Raw Inputs
(includes secrets)"] ExtractPorts["extractPorts()
(from input schema)"] IdentifySecrets["Identify Secret Ports"] MaskValues["Replace with '***'"] MaskedInputs["Masked Inputs
(safe for logging)"] NodeIORecord["nodeIO.recordStart()"] RawInputs --> ExtractPorts ExtractPorts --> IdentifySecrets IdentifySecrets --> MaskValues MaskValues --> MaskedInputs MaskedInputs --> NodeIORecord ``` **Diagram: Secret Masking Flow** Masking functions: | Function | Purpose | Applies To | |----------|---------|------------| | `maskSecretInputs()` | Mask input values before recording | Component inputs + parameters | | `maskSecretOutputs()` | Mask output values before recording | Component outputs | | `maskSecretParameters()` | Mask parameter values | Parameters with `editor: 'secret'` | Special cases: - If a port with `id === '__self__'` is secret, the entire output is replaced with `'***'` - For object outputs, only secret fields are masked: `{ username: 'alice', password: '***' }` - Dynamic ports (from `resolvePorts`) are masked using the resolved schema, not the base schema Sources: [worker/src/temporal/utils/component-output.ts:62-158](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:204-219]() --- ## Node I/O Recording The system records all inputs and outputs for each node execution to enable debugging and inspection. ### Recording Lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Workflow participant Activity as runComponentActivity participant NodeIO as KafkaNodeIOAdapter participant Kafka participant Storage as FileStorageAdapter Workflow->>Activity: Execute node Activity->>Activity: maskSecretInputs(inputs) Activity->>NodeIO: recordStart({ inputs }) NodeIO->>NodeIO: Check if inputs need spilling alt Inputs > 5MB NodeIO->>Storage: uploadFile(spilledInputs) Storage-->>NodeIO: storageRef NodeIO->>NodeIO: Replace with spilled marker end NodeIO->>Kafka: Publish NODE_IO_START event Activity->>Activity: component.execute() Activity->>Activity: maskSecretOutputs(outputs) Activity->>NodeIO: recordCompletion({ outputs, status }) NodeIO->>NodeIO: Check if outputs need spilling alt Outputs > 5MB NodeIO->>Storage: uploadFile(spilledOutputs) Storage-->>NodeIO: storageRef NodeIO->>NodeIO: Replace with spilled marker end NodeIO->>Kafka: Publish NODE_IO_COMPLETION event ``` **Diagram: Node I/O Recording Sequence** ### Storage and Retrieval Node I/O data is published to the `telemetry.node-io` Kafka topic (instance-specific). Each event contains: ```typescript interface NodeIOStartEvent { runId: string; nodeRef: string; workflowId?: string; organizationId?: string | null; componentId: string; inputs?: Record; // Masked, potentially spilled } interface NodeIOCompletionEvent { runId: string; nodeRef: string; componentId?: string; outputs: Record; // Masked, potentially spilled status: 'completed' | 'failed' | 'skipped'; errorMessage?: string; } ``` Consumers can reconstruct the full data flow by: 1. Reading events from Kafka (or querying from the database if persisted) 2. Detecting spilled markers in input/output fields 3. Downloading full data from MinIO using `storageRef` 4. Secrets remain masked as `'***'` throughout Sources: [packages/component-sdk/src/interfaces.ts:196-227](), [worker/src/adapters/node-io.adapter.ts](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:208-220](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:521-530]() --- ## Complete Data Flow Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Workflow Execution" EntryPoint["Entrypoint Node
receives runtime inputs"] BuildPayload["buildActionPayload()

(in-memory)"] end EntryPoint --> BuildPayload BuildPayload --> UnspillInputs UnspillInputs --> Cache Cache -.cache miss.-> MinIO MinIO -.download.-> Cache UnspillInputs --> MaskInputs MaskInputs --> RecordStart RecordStart --> Kafka RecordStart --> Execute Execute --> CheckSize CheckSize --> SpillOutput SpillOutput -.upload.-> MinIO SpillOutput --> MaskOutputs MaskOutputs --> RecordComplete RecordComplete --> Kafka RecordComplete --> ResultsMap ResultsMap --> NextNode NextNode --> BuildPayload ``` **Diagram: End-to-End Data Flow Architecture** ### Key Properties | Property | Description | |----------|-------------| | **Transparency** | Components never see spilled markers; unspilling happens before execution | | **Efficiency** | Spilled data cached per run to avoid redundant downloads | | **Security** | Secrets masked before any logging or persistence | | **Reliability** | Large outputs don't exceed Temporal limits; workflow history remains bounded | | **Debugging** | Full I/O trail preserved in Kafka for inspection | Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:156-1774](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:118-646](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:48-504](), [worker/src/adapters/node-io.adapter.ts]()

The Component System provides a modular, extensible architecture for defining reusable workflow building blocks. Components are self-contained units that expose inputs, outputs, and parameters through Zod schemas, execute via configurable runners (inline, Docker, or remote), and can be exposed as agent-callable tools. This page documents the component definition structure, SDK interfaces, registry mechanism, and execution model. For information about how components are executed within workflows, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). For details on component execution monitoring, see [Component Execution Model](#3.3). For AI agent tool integration, see [AI and MCP Integration](#4). --- ## Component Definition Structure A component is defined using the `ComponentDefinition` interface, which specifies metadata, schemas, execution logic, and optional tool provider configuration. ### Core Component Interface ```mermaid graph TB ComponentDefinition["ComponentDefinition<I,O,P>"] ComponentDefinition --> Metadata["Metadata

## Overview The Component SDK provides the core interfaces and utilities for defining executable workflow components in ShipSec Studio. It is a workspace package (`@shipsec/component-sdk`) that establishes the contract between component authors and the execution engine. **Scope of this document:** - `ComponentDefinition` interface and type system - Schema builders for inputs, outputs, and parameters - `ExecutionContext` and service interfaces - Runner configurations (inline, docker, remote) - Tool provider configuration for AI agent integration - Retry policies and error handling **Related pages:** - For component registry and discovery, see [Component Registry](#3.2) - For component execution orchestration, see [Component Execution Model](#3.3) - For runner implementation details, see [Runners and Isolation](#3.4) - For AI agent tool integration, see [Tool Execution Patterns](#4.6) Sources: [packages/component-sdk/package.json:1-38](), [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:1-542]() --- ## ComponentDefinition Interface The `ComponentDefinition` interface is the central abstraction for all workflow components. It defines the component's structure, behavior, and integration points. ```mermaid graph TB ComponentDefinition["ComponentDefinition<I,O,P>"] ComponentDefinition --> Metadata["Metadata

} }); ``` The generic parameters `` flow through to the `execute` function, providing IDE autocomplete and compile-time validation. The Component Registry is the central catalog of all executable components available in ShipSec Studio workflows. It contains over 200 components organized into functional categories including Core utilities, AI integrations, Security tools, IT automation, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. Components are registered at worker startup and made available to both the workflow compiler and the visual workflow builder. For information about how components execute at runtime, see [Component Execution Model](#3.2). For parameter configuration UI, see [Parameter Configuration](#3.3). For MCP-specific tooling, see [AI & MCP Integration](#4). ## Component Registration Architecture Components are registered through a central import file that loads all component modules at worker initialization. Each component module calls `componentRegistry.register()` from `@shipsec/component-sdk` to make itself available. ```mermaid graph TB WorkerInit["Worker Initialization
