# Component Execution Model
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [packages/component-sdk/src/__tests__/context.test.ts](packages/component-sdk/src/__tests__/context.test.ts) - [packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts](packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts) - [packages/component-sdk/src/interfaces.ts](packages/component-sdk/src/interfaces.ts) - [worker/src/__tests__/worker-integration.test.ts](worker/src/__tests__/worker-integration.test.ts) - [worker/src/adapters/loki-log.adapter.ts](worker/src/adapters/loki-log.adapter.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/dynamic-port-resolution.test.ts](worker/src/temporal/__tests__/dynamic-port-resolution.test.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts](worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-scheduler.test.ts](worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-scheduler.test.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts](worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/utils/component-output.ts](worker/src/temporal/utils/component-output.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts](worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts) - [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts](worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts)
This document explains how components execute within the ShipSec Studio workflow engine. It covers the activity invocation pattern, service injection architecture, input/output resolution, and the lifecycle of component execution from workflow dispatch through result recording. For information about the available components and their categorization, see [Component Registry](#3.1). For details on how parameters are configured in the UI, see [Parameter Configuration](#3.3). For the broader workflow execution context, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). ## Overview Components in ShipSec Studio execute as Temporal activities within the workflow orchestration layer. The execution model follows a dependency injection pattern where components receive an `ExecutionContext` containing all necessary services (storage, secrets, logging, tracing) without directly coupling to infrastructure implementations. The execution flow is: 1. **Workflow orchestration** schedules a component action 2. **Activity invocation** calls `runComponentActivity` with action inputs 3. **Service injection** creates `ExecutionContext` with adapter instances 4. **Input resolution** unspills data, resolves secrets, validates required inputs 5. **Component execution** runs component logic with parsed inputs/params 6. **Output handling** spills large payloads, records node I/O, emits trace events 7. **Error handling** records failures, applies retry policies Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:118-635](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:314-847](), [packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts:53-217]() ## Component Resolution and Registry Lookup ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Workflow Layer" WF["shipsecWorkflowRun"] ACTION["WorkflowAction
{ref, componentId, params}"] end subgraph "Activity Layer" ACT["runComponentActivity"] REG["componentRegistry.get()"] end subgraph "Component Registry" META["ComponentMetadata"] DEF["ComponentDefinition"] PORTS["Input/Output Ports"] end WF -->|"schedules action"| ACTION ACTION -->|"RunComponentActivityInput"| ACT ACT -->|"componentId"| REG REG -->|"returns"| META META --> DEF META --> PORTS DEF -->|"execute function"| ACT PORTS -->|"validation schema"| ACT ``` **Diagram: Component Resolution Flow** When the workflow scheduler dispatches an action, it invokes `runComponentActivity` with the component ID. The activity looks up the component definition in the global `componentRegistry` which was populated at worker startup by importing all component modules. The registry returns a `ComponentMetadata` object containing: - `definition`: The component's execute function and configuration - `inputs`/`outputs`: Port metadata for validation and masking - `requiresSecrets`: Flag determining if secrets service is injected If the component is not found, a `NotFoundError` is thrown and the workflow fails with a non-retryable error. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:123-131](), [packages/component-sdk/src/registry.ts]() ## Activity Invocation Pattern The workflow invokes components via Temporal activities, which provide: - **Isolation**: Each component runs in a separate activity execution context - **Retry policies**: Configurable per-component retry behavior - **Timeout protection**: `startToCloseTimeout` prevents infinite execution - **Heartbeat support**: Long-running components can report progress ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant WF as "shipsecWorkflowRun" participant SCHED as "runWorkflowWithScheduler" participant PROXY as "proxyActivities" participant ACT as "runComponentActivity" participant COMP as "component.execute()" WF->>SCHED: "executeWorkflow(definition)" SCHED->>SCHED: "schedule actions by dependencies" loop "For each action" SCHED->>WF: "run(actionRef, context)" WF->>WF: "buildActionPayload(action, results)" WF->>WF: "create RunComponentActivityInput" WF->>PROXY: "runComponentWithRetry(input)" Note over PROXY: "Applies retry policy from action.retryPolicy" PROXY->>ACT: "invoke activity" ACT->>ACT: "resolve inputs + secrets + spilled data" ACT->>COMP: "execute({inputs, params}, context)" COMP-->>ACT: "return output" ACT->>ACT: "check output size, spill if needed" ACT-->>PROXY: "RunComponentActivityOutput" PROXY-->>WF: "output + activeOutputPorts" WF->>WF: "results.set(actionRef, output)" end ``` **Diagram: Activity Invocation Sequence** The workflow uses `proxyActivities` to create typed activity stubs that handle serialization, retry policies, and timeouts. Retry policies are mapped from the component's `ComponentRetryPolicy` to Temporal's retry options via `mapRetryPolicy()`. Tool-mode components skip normal execution and instead register themselves as available tools for AI agents (see [Tool Execution Patterns](#4.5)). Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:676-847](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:140-154]() ## ExecutionContext and Service Injection The `ExecutionContext` is the primary interface through which components interact with platform services. It follows a dependency injection pattern where service adapters are initialized once at worker startup and then injected into each component execution. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Worker Initialization" WORKER["dev.worker.ts
main()"] INIT["initializeComponentActivityServices()"] end subgraph "Service Adapters" FS["FileStorageAdapter
(MinIO)"] SEC["SecretsAdapter
(PostgreSQL)"] ART["ArtifactAdapter
(MinIO + DB)"] TRACE["KafkaTraceAdapter"] LOGS["KafkaLogAdapter"] NODEIO["KafkaNodeIOAdapter"] TERM["RedisTerminalStreamAdapter"] AGENT["KafkaAgentTracePublisher"] end subgraph "Activity Execution" ACT["runComponentActivity"] CTX["createExecutionContext()"] end subgraph "Component" COMP["component.execute(args, context)"] API["context.storage
context.secrets
context.logger
context.trace"] end WORKER --> INIT INIT -.->|"global refs"| FS INIT -.->|"global refs"| SEC INIT -.->|"global refs"| ART INIT -.->|"global refs"| TRACE INIT -.->|"global refs"| LOGS INIT -.->|"global refs"| NODEIO INIT -.->|"global refs"| TERM INIT -.->|"global refs"| AGENT ACT -->|"reads global refs"| CTX FS -->|"injected into"| CTX SEC -->|"injected if requiresSecrets"| CTX ART -->|"scoped factory"| CTX TRACE -->|"wrapped as scoped"| CTX LOGS -->|"as logCollector"| CTX NODEIO -->|"direct ref"| CTX TERM -->|"as terminalCollector"| CTX AGENT -->|"direct ref"| CTX CTX --> COMP COMP --> API ``` **Diagram: Service Injection Architecture** ### Service Adapter Initialization Service adapters are initialized once when the worker starts and stored in global variables. The `initializeComponentActivityServices()` function accepts adapter instances that implement SDK interfaces (`IFileStorageService`, `ISecretsService`, etc.) and stores them in module-level variables. This pattern allows: - **Test isolation**: Tests can provide mock implementations without starting infrastructure - **Infrastructure abstraction**: Components depend on interfaces, not concrete implementations - **Performance**: Adapters maintain connection pools (Kafka producers, Redis clients) across executions Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:79-231](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:79-97]() ### ExecutionContext Creation For each component execution, `createExecutionContext()` builds a context object containing: | Property | Type | Description | |----------|------|-------------| | `runId` | string | Unique identifier for the workflow run | | `componentRef` | string | Node reference (action.ref) | | `logger` | Logger | Structured logging to stdout/stderr | | `emitProgress` | function | Emit NODE_PROGRESS trace events | | `storage` | IFileStorageService? | File upload/download (always injected) | | `secrets` | ISecretsService? | Secret retrieval (only if `requiresSecrets: true`) | | `artifacts` | IArtifactService? | Scoped artifact upload (run + component context) | | `trace` | IScopedTraceService? | Trace event recording with context enrichment | | `logCollector` | function? | Kafka log sink | | `terminalCollector` | function? | Redis terminal stream sink | | `agentTracePublisher` | AgentTracePublisher? | AI agent step tracing | | `metadata` | ExecutionContextMetadata | Activity metadata (activityId, attempt, streamId, etc.) | | `http` | InstrumentedHttpClient | HTTP client with automatic trace recording | The context object is frozen to prevent accidental mutation. The `trace` service is wrapped to automatically inject `runId`, `nodeRef`, and `context` metadata into all trace events. Sources: [packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts:53-217](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:154-201]() ### Conditional Service Injection Not all services are injected into every component: - **Secrets service**: Only injected if `component.requiresSecrets === true`. This prevents components from accidentally accessing secrets without explicit declaration. - **Artifacts service**: Scoped to the current run, workflow, and component. Uses `ArtifactServiceFactory` to create per-execution instances with appropriate metadata. - **Terminal collector**: Only available if `TERMINAL_REDIS_URL` is configured in the worker environment. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:141-151](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:152-173]() ## Input Resolution Pipeline Before component execution, the activity resolves all inputs through a multi-stage pipeline: 1. **Build action payload** - Extract inputs from upstream node outputs 2. **Unspill data** - Download large payloads from storage 3. **Resolve secret references** - Replace secret IDs with actual values 4. **Validate required inputs** - Check for missing required inputs 5. **Parse inputs/params** - Apply Zod schemas for type safety ```mermaid graph TD START["RunComponentActivityInput"] subgraph "Stage 1: Payload Building" BUILD["buildActionPayload()
Maps upstream outputs to inputs"] SPILLED{"Is value
__spilled__?"} end subgraph "Stage 2: Unspilling" DOWNLOAD["downloadFile(storageRef)"] PARSE["JSON.parse(buffer)"] EXTRACT["Extract handle from full data"] end subgraph "Stage 3: Secret Resolution" SECRET_CHECK{"Input/param
editor = 'secret'?"} SECRET_GET["secrets.get(secretId)"] SECRET_REPLACE["Replace ID with value"] end subgraph "Stage 4: Validation" PORTS["Resolve dynamic ports
(component.resolvePorts)"] REQUIRED["Filter required inputs"] VALIDATE{"All required
present?"} end subgraph "Stage 5: Parsing" PARSE_IN["component.inputs.parse()"] PARSE_PARAM["component.parameters.parse()"] EXECUTE["component.execute({inputs, params})"] end START --> BUILD BUILD --> SPILLED SPILLED -->|"Yes"| DOWNLOAD SPILLED -->|"No"| SECRET_CHECK DOWNLOAD --> PARSE PARSE --> EXTRACT EXTRACT --> SECRET_CHECK SECRET_CHECK -->|"Yes"| SECRET_GET SECRET_CHECK -->|"No"| PORTS SECRET_GET --> SECRET_REPLACE SECRET_REPLACE --> PORTS PORTS --> REQUIRED REQUIRED --> VALIDATE VALIDATE -->|"Fail"| ERROR["Throw ValidationError"] VALIDATE -->|"Pass"| PARSE_IN PARSE_IN --> PARSE_PARAM PARSE_PARAM --> EXECUTE ``` **Diagram: Input Resolution Pipeline** Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:222-442]() ### Spilled Data Unspilling Large payloads exceeding `TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES` (128 KB) are stored in MinIO during upstream execution and replaced with spilled data markers: ```typescript { __spilled__: true, storageRef: "uuid-of-file", __spilled_handle__: "fieldName" | "__self__", originalSize: 524288 } ``` The activity maintains a `spilledObjectsCache` map to avoid re-downloading the same file multiple times when multiple inputs reference it. If the marker has a `__spilled_handle__` property, the activity extracts that specific field from the downloaded JSON object. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:222-280](), [packages/component-sdk/src/constants.ts]() ### Secret Reference Resolution When users select a secret from the secrets store in the UI, the configuration stores the secret ID (UUID). The activity resolves these references by: 1. **Identifying secret fields**: Check if input/param has `editor: 'secret'` or `connectionType.name: 'secret'` 2. **Resolving ports**: Call `component.resolvePorts(params)` for dynamic port definitions 3. **Fetching values**: Call `globalSecrets.get(secretId)` to retrieve the actual secret value 4. **Replacing IDs**: Update the inputs/params object with the resolved value This happens for both: - **Input overrides**: Secrets selected in node configuration (stored in `action.inputOverrides`) - **Parameters**: Secrets in component parameters (stored in `action.params`) Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:288-387]() ### Required Input Validation Not all undefined inputs should fail validation. The activity filters warnings to only required inputs by checking port metadata: | Condition | Required? | |-----------|-----------| | `port.required === false` | No | | `port.connectionType.kind === 'any'` | No (any includes undefined) | | Port not found in metadata | Yes (safe default) | | Otherwise | Yes | Warnings for missing optional inputs are logged as `warn` level trace events, while missing required inputs throw a `ValidationError` that fails the activity. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:390-442]() ## Component Execution Once inputs are resolved and validated, the activity executes the component: ```typescript const output = await component.execute( { inputs: parsedInputs, params: parsedParams }, context ); ``` The component receives: - **Parsed inputs/params**: Type-safe objects validated against Zod schemas - **ExecutionContext**: Frozen object with injected services The component can: - Log via `context.logger.info()`, `context.logger.error()`, etc. - Emit progress via `context.emitProgress("Processing...")` - Upload files via `context.storage.uploadFile(...)` - Retrieve secrets via `context.secrets.get(key)` - Upload artifacts via `context.artifacts.upload(...)` - Make HTTP requests via `context.http.get(url)` (automatically traced) - Write terminal output via `context.terminalCollector?.(...)` The execution is synchronous from the activity's perspective - `execute()` returns a Promise that the activity awaits. Long-running operations can use Temporal heartbeats to prevent timeouts. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:462-467](), [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts]() ### Human-in-the-Loop Suspension If a component returns an output with `pending: true`, the activity detects this as a suspension point (approval gate, form submission, etc.). The workflow will handle the suspension by creating a human input request and waiting for signal resolution. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:468-475](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:868-1001]() ## Output Handling After successful component execution, the activity processes the output through several stages: ### Output Spilling If the output exceeds `TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, the activity uploads it to MinIO and replaces it with a spilled marker: ```typescript const outputStr = JSON.stringify(output); const size = Buffer.byteLength(outputStr, 'utf8'); if (size > TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES && globalStorage) { const fileId = crypto.randomUUID(); await globalStorage.uploadFile(fileId, 'output.json', Buffer.from(outputStr), 'application/json'); output = { __spilled__: true, storageRef: fileId, originalSize: size }; } ``` Downstream nodes will automatically unspill this data during their input resolution phase. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:483-509]() ### Node I/O Recording The activity records both inputs and outputs via `globalNodeIO`: **Start recording** (before execution): ```typescript await globalNodeIO?.recordStart({ runId: input.runId, nodeRef: action.ref, workflowId: input.workflowId, organizationId: input.organizationId, componentId: action.componentId, inputs: maskSecretInputs(component, { ...inputs, ...params }) }); ``` **Completion recording** (after execution): ```typescript await globalNodeIO?.recordCompletion({ runId: input.runId, nodeRef: action.ref, componentId: action.componentId, outputs: maskSecretOutputs(component, output), status: 'completed' }); ``` Secret masking replaces secret values with `'***'` before recording to prevent leaking credentials in node I/O inspection UI. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:204-211](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:513-519]() ### Trace Event Emission The activity emits trace events at key lifecycle points: | Event Type | When | Data | |------------|------|------| | `NODE_STARTED` | Before execution | activityId, attempt, correlationId | | `NODE_PROGRESS` | During execution | From `context.emitProgress()` or logs | | `NODE_COMPLETED` | After successful execution | outputSummary, activatedPorts | | `NODE_FAILED` | After error | error message, type, stack, details | The `NODE_COMPLETED` event includes an `outputSummary` created by `createLightweightSummary()` which truncates large outputs to prevent bloating the trace log. If the component returned `activeOutputPorts`, these are included in the trace event's `data.activatedPorts` field. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:213-217](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:523-530]() ## Error Handling and Retry Policies When a component throws an error, the activity: 1. **Extracts error metadata**: Message, type, stack, details, fieldErrors (for ValidationError) 2. **Truncates long messages**: Limits to `ERROR_LOG_LIMIT` (600 chars) to prevent Temporal history bloat 3. **Records trace event**: `NODE_FAILED` with full error details 4. **Records node I/O failure**: Status `'failed'` with error message 5. **Determines retryability**: Checks `error.retryable` property 6. **Throws ApplicationFailure**: With appropriate retry policy ```typescript if (isRetryable) { throw ApplicationFailure.retryable(errorMsg, finalErrorType, [details]); } throw ApplicationFailure.nonRetryable(errorMsg, finalErrorType, [details]); ``` Component-level retry policies are configured in the workflow definition's `action.retryPolicy` and mapped to Temporal retry options via `mapRetryPolicy()`: ```typescript { maximumAttempts: policy.maxAttempts, initialInterval: policy.initialIntervalSeconds * 1000, maximumInterval: policy.maximumIntervalSeconds * 1000, backoffCoefficient: policy.backoffCoefficient, nonRetryableErrorTypes: policy.nonRetryableErrorTypes } ``` Sources: [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:533-631](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:140-154]() ## Service Adapter Implementations The worker initializes concrete implementations of SDK service interfaces. These adapters handle the actual infrastructure interactions: ### File Storage Adapter **Implementation**: `FileStorageAdapter` (MinIO) ```typescript const minioClient = new Client({ endPoint: minioEndpoint, port: minioPort, useSSL: minioUseSSL, accessKey: minioAccessKey, secretKey: minioSecretKey }); const storageAdapter = new FileStorageAdapter(minioClient, db, minioBucketName); ``` Implements `uploadFile()`, `downloadFile()`, `getFileMetadata()` with automatic bucket creation and metadata persistence to PostgreSQL. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:115-133](), [worker/src/adapters/file-storage.adapter.ts]() ### Secrets Adapter **Implementation**: `SecretsAdapter` (PostgreSQL) Retrieves secrets from the `secrets` table with optional version selection. Secrets are encrypted at rest in the database. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:135](), [worker/src/adapters/secrets.adapter.ts]() ### Trace Adapter **Implementation**: `KafkaTraceAdapter` Publishes trace events to the `telemetry.trace.*` Kafka topic. Uses instance-scoped topics when `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` is set (e.g., `telemetry.trace.instance-0`). Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:157-161](), [worker/src/adapters/kafka-trace.adapter.ts]() ### Log Adapter **Implementation**: `KafkaLogAdapter` Publishes structured logs to the `telemetry.logs.*` Kafka topic. Each log entry includes: - `runId`, `nodeRef`, `stream` (stdout/stderr), `level`, `message` - Optional metadata: `activityId`, `attempt`, `correlationId`, `streamId`, `joinStrategy`, `triggeredBy` Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:178-189](), [worker/src/adapters/kafka-log.adapter.ts]() ### Node I/O Adapter **Implementation**: `KafkaNodeIOAdapter` Publishes node inputs/outputs to the `telemetry.node-io.*` Kafka topic. Large payloads are automatically spilled to MinIO via the injected `FileStorageAdapter`. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:169-176](), [worker/src/adapters/kafka-node-io.adapter.ts]() ### Terminal Stream Adapter **Implementation**: `RedisTerminalStreamAdapter` Writes PTY/stdout/stderr chunks to Redis streams for real-time terminal output. Each chunk is timestamped and associated with a specific node execution. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:191-204](), [worker/src/adapters/redis-terminal-stream.adapter.ts]() ### Agent Trace Publisher **Implementation**: `KafkaAgentTracePublisher` Publishes AI agent execution traces (steps, tool calls, reasoning) to the `telemetry.agent-trace.*` Kafka topic for UI visualization. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:163-167](), [worker/src/adapters/kafka-agent-trace.adapter.ts]() ### Artifact Adapter **Implementation**: `ArtifactAdapter` (Factory Pattern) Uses a factory pattern to scope artifacts to specific run/component contexts. Each factory invocation creates an `IArtifactService` instance that automatically tags uploads with: - `runId`, `workflowId`, `workflowVersionId` - `componentId`, `componentRef` - `organizationId` Artifacts can be uploaded to multiple destinations (`run`, `library`) and are stored in MinIO with metadata in PostgreSQL. This document describes the runner system in ShipSec Studio's component architecture. Runners are execution strategies that abstract how and where component logic executes. The system supports inline (in-process), Docker (containerized), and remote (HTTP/gRPC) execution modes, providing flexibility in isolation, resource management, and security boundaries. For information about component definitions and the SDK, see [Component SDK](#3.1). For details on how components are orchestrated during workflow execution, see [Component Execution Model](#3.3). --- ## Runner Types Overview Components declare their execution strategy using a `runner` configuration. The system supports three runner kinds, each with distinct isolation characteristics and use cases. ```mermaid graph TB Component["ComponentDefinition
(defines runner config)"] subgraph "Runner Types" Inline["InlineRunnerConfig
kind: 'inline'"] Docker["DockerRunnerConfig
kind: 'docker'"] Remote["RemoteRunnerConfig
kind: 'remote'"] end subgraph "Execution Strategies" InlineExec["runComponentInline()
Direct function call"] DockerExec["runComponentInDocker()
Container spawn"] RemoteExec["Remote HTTP/gRPC
(stub)"] end subgraph "Execution Context" Context["ExecutionContext
Services + Metadata"] Storage["IFileStorageService"] Secrets["ISecretsService"] Trace["ITraceService"] Terminal["terminalCollector"] end Component --> Inline Component --> Docker Component --> Remote Inline --> InlineExec Docker --> DockerExec Remote --> RemoteExec InlineExec --> Context DockerExec --> Context RemoteExec --> Context Context --> Storage Context --> Secrets Context --> Trace Context --> Terminal ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:18-56](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:519-540]() --- ## Runner Configuration Types ### InlineRunnerConfig The inline runner executes component logic directly in the worker process. This is the most lightweight option with no isolation boundaries. | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `kind` | `'inline'` | Identifies inline execution mode | | `concurrency` | `number` (optional) | Reserved for future concurrency controls | **Usage Example:** ```typescript { runner: { kind: 'inline' } } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:20-23]() ### DockerRunnerConfig The Docker runner executes component logic in an isolated container. This provides process isolation, resource limits, and security boundaries. | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `kind` | `'docker'` | Identifies Docker execution mode | | `image` | `string` | Docker image name (e.g., `'projectdiscovery/subfinder:latest'`) | | `command` | `string[]` | Command to execute in the container | | `entrypoint` | `string` (optional) | Override container's default entrypoint | | `env` | `Record` (optional) | Environment variables to inject | | `network` | `'none' \| 'bridge' \| 'host'` (optional) | Network isolation mode (default: `'none'`) | | `platform` | `string` (optional) | Platform architecture (e.g., `'linux/amd64'`) | | `containerName` | `string` (optional) | Custom container name for `--name` flag | | `volumes` | `Array` (optional) | Host paths to mount into container | | `timeoutSeconds` | `number` (optional) | Maximum execution time (default: 300) | | `stdinJson` | `boolean` (optional) | Whether to write params as JSON to stdin (default: true) | | `detached` | `boolean` (optional) | Start container and return immediately (for services) | | `autoRemove` | `boolean` (optional) | Keep `--rm` flag when detached | | `ports` | `Record` (optional) | Port mappings (host → container) | **VolumeMount Structure:** ```typescript { source: string; // Host path target: string; // Container path readOnly?: boolean; // Mount as read-only } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:25-44]() ### RemoteRunnerConfig The remote runner (not yet implemented) will execute component logic via HTTP or gRPC endpoints. This enables distributed execution and language-agnostic components. | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `kind` | `'remote'` | Identifies remote execution mode | | `endpoint` | `string` | HTTP/gRPC endpoint URL | | `authSecretName` | `string` (optional) | Secret name for authentication | **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:47-51]() --- ## Inline Runner Execution The inline runner provides the simplest execution path with no isolation or containerization overhead. ### Execution Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Activity as runComponentActivity participant SDK as runComponentWithRunner participant Inline as runComponentInline participant Component as component.execute() participant Context as ExecutionContext Activity->>SDK: runComponentWithRunner(runner, execute, params, context) SDK->>Inline: runComponentInline(execute, params, context) Inline->>Component: execute(params, context) Component->>Context: logger.info(...) Component->>Context: emitProgress(...) Component->>Context: storage.downloadFile(...) Component-->>Inline: return output Inline-->>SDK: return output SDK-->>Activity: return output ``` **Implementation:** The inline runner is a simple pass-through that directly invokes the component's execute function: ```typescript export async function runComponentInline( execute: (params: I, context: ExecutionContext) => Promise, params: I, context: ExecutionContext, ): Promise { return execute(params, context); } ``` **Characteristics:** - **No isolation**: Executes in the same process as the Temporal worker - **Shared memory**: Component can access worker memory and state - **Fast startup**: No container or process creation overhead - **Full service access**: Direct access to all `ExecutionContext` services **Use Cases:** - Lightweight data transformations - Built-in workflow control components (`core.workflow.entrypoint`, `core.branching.switch`) - Components that need tight integration with the worker runtime **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:77-83](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:525-527]() --- ## Docker Runner Execution The Docker runner provides strong isolation by executing components in containers. This is the primary execution strategy for security tools and external scanners. ### Docker Execution Lifecycle ```mermaid graph TB Start["runComponentInDocker()"] subgraph "Setup Phase" CreateTemp["Create temp directory
mkdtemp()"] WriteInput["Write input.json
(params serialized)"] BuildArgs["Build docker args
(--rm, -i, --network, etc)"] end subgraph "Execution Mode Selection" CheckMode{"Mode?"} Detached["Detached Mode
-d flag"] Interactive["Interactive Mode"] end subgraph "Interactive Execution" CheckTerminal{"Terminal
collector?"} PTY["runDockerWithPty()
node-pty spawn"] StandardIO["runDockerWithStandardIO()
child_process spawn"] end subgraph "Container Execution" Docker["Docker container runs"] ReadEnv["Container reads
SHIPSEC_INPUT_PATH"] WriteOut["Container writes
SHIPSEC_OUTPUT_PATH"] Stdout["Logs to stdout/stderr"] end subgraph "Output Collection" ReadFile["readOutputFromFile()
Read result.json"] Fallback["Fallback to stdout
if file missing"] end subgraph "Cleanup" Remove["Remove temp directory
rm -rf"] end Start --> CreateTemp CreateTemp --> WriteInput WriteInput --> BuildArgs BuildArgs --> CheckMode CheckMode -->|detached| Detached CheckMode -->|interactive| Interactive Interactive --> CheckTerminal CheckTerminal -->|Yes| PTY CheckTerminal -->|No| StandardIO PTY --> Docker StandardIO --> Docker Detached --> Docker Docker --> ReadEnv ReadEnv --> WriteOut WriteOut --> Stdout Stdout --> ReadFile ReadFile -->|File exists| Remove ReadFile -->|File missing| Fallback Fallback --> Remove Remove --> End["Return output"] ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:85-204](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:214-258]() ### Container Communication Patterns The Docker runner uses three methods for data exchange with containers: #### 1. File-Based I/O (Preferred) Containers read inputs from and write outputs to mounted files: ``` Host: /tmp/shipsec-run-/ ├── input.json (written by runner) └── result.json (written by container) Container: /shipsec-output/ ├── input.json (read by container) └── result.json (written by container) ``` **Environment Variables Provided:** - `SHIPSEC_INPUT_PATH=/shipsec-output/input.json` - `SHIPSEC_OUTPUT_PATH=/shipsec-output/result.json` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:10-12](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:104-151]() #### 2. Stdin/Stdout (Legacy Fallback) For backwards compatibility, the runner can write JSON to stdin and read from stdout: ```typescript // Write params to stdin (default behavior) proc.stdin.write(JSON.stringify(params)); proc.stdin.end(); // Read output from stdout (fallback if result.json doesn't exist) ``` **Note:** Stdin writing is disabled in PTY mode to avoid polluting terminal output. **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:378-396](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:239-253]() #### 3. Environment Variables Configuration and credentials are passed via environment variables: ```typescript dockerArgs.push('-e', `${key}=${value}`); dockerArgs.push('-e', `SHIPSEC_INPUT_PATH=${CONTAINER_OUTPUT_PATH}/input.json`); dockerArgs.push('-e', `SHIPSEC_OUTPUT_PATH=${CONTAINER_OUTPUT_PATH}/${OUTPUT_FILENAME}`); ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:145-151]() ### Docker Security Features #### Network Isolation The runner defaults to `network: 'none'` to prevent unauthorized network access: ```typescript dockerArgs.push('--network', network); // Default: 'none' ``` **Network Modes:** - `none`: No network access (default, most secure) - `bridge`: Standard Docker bridge network - `host`: Use host networking (least secure, rarely needed) **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:31](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:116]() #### Volume Mounts Containers run with minimal volume mounts by default. Additional mounts must be explicitly configured: ```typescript if (Array.isArray(volumes)) { for (const vol of volumes) { if (!vol || !vol.source || !vol.target) continue; const mode = vol.readOnly ? ':ro' : ''; dockerArgs.push('-v', `${vol.source}:${vol.target}${mode}`); } } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:131-137]() #### Container Labels Containers are labeled for tracking and cleanup: ```typescript '--label', `shipsec.runId=${context.runId}`, '--label', `shipsec.nodeRef=${context.componentRef}`, ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:117-118]() #### Automatic Cleanup The `--rm` flag ensures containers are removed after execution: ```typescript dockerArgs.push('--rm'); // Always included for non-detached mode ``` Temp directories are cleaned up in the finally block: ```typescript finally { await rm(outputDir, { recursive: true, force: true }).catch((err) => { context.logger.warn(`Failed to cleanup temp directory ${outputDir}: ${err.message}`); }); } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:114](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:199-202]() --- ## PTY Support for Terminal Streaming The Docker runner provides two execution modes for interactive output: standard I/O and PTY (pseudo-terminal). ### PTY vs Standard I/O ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Execution Context" Context["ExecutionContext"] Terminal["terminalCollector?"] end subgraph "Mode Selection" Check{"Has terminal
collector?"} end subgraph "Standard I/O Mode" StdIO["child_process.spawn()
stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']"] StdoutData["proc.stdout.on('data')"] StderrData["proc.stderr.on('data')"] StdEmit["Emit to terminalCollector
stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'"] end subgraph "PTY Mode" PTY["node-pty.spawn()
cols: 120, rows: 40"] PtyData["ptyProcess.onData()"] PtyEmit["Emit to terminalCollector
stream: 'pty'"] ANSI["ANSI escape codes preserved"] end Context --> Terminal Terminal --> Check Check -->|No| StdIO Check -->|Yes| PTY StdIO --> StdoutData StdIO --> StderrData StdoutData --> StdEmit StderrData --> StdEmit PTY --> PtyData PtyData --> PtyEmit PtyEmit --> ANSI ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:160-193](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:404-517]() ### PTY Implementation The runner uses the `node-pty` library for pseudo-terminal emulation: ```typescript async function loadPtySpawn(): Promise { if (cachedPtySpawn) { return cachedPtySpawn; } try { const mod = await import('node-pty'); cachedPtySpawn = mod.spawn; return cachedPtySpawn; } catch (error) { console.warn('[Docker][PTY] node-pty module not available:', error.message); return null; } } ``` **PTY Characteristics:** - **ANSI escape codes**: Color, cursor movement, and formatting preserved - **Interactive emulation**: Behaves like a real terminal - **TTY flag**: Uses `-t` instead of `-i` for Docker - **No stdin writing**: JSON input disabled to avoid terminal pollution **Fallback Behavior:** If `node-pty` is unavailable or PTY spawn fails, the runner falls back to standard I/O: ```typescript if (!spawnPty) { context.logger.warn('[Docker][PTY] node-pty unavailable; falling back to standard IO'); const argsWithoutTty = dockerArgs.filter(arg => arg !== '-t'); return runDockerWithStandardIO(argsWithoutTty, params, context, timeoutSeconds); } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:14-15](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:63-75](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:410-416]() ### Terminal Chunk Emission Both execution modes use `createTerminalChunkEmitter` to stream output to the terminal collector: ```typescript const emitChunk = createTerminalChunkEmitter(context, 'pty'); ptyProcess.onData((data) => { emitChunk(data); stdout += data; // Also capture for fallback }); ``` The emitter handles chunking and timing metadata for replay: ```typescript export interface TerminalChunkInput { runId: string; nodeRef: string; stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr' | 'console' | 'pty'; chunkIndex: number; payload: string; recordedAt: string; deltaMs: number; origin?: string; runnerKind?: RunnerKind; } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:420-421](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:475-478](), [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:58-68]() --- ## Detached Container Mode For long-running services (like MCP servers), the Docker runner supports detached execution: ```typescript if (runner.detached) { // Use -d instead of -i const detachedArgs = dockerArgs.map(arg => arg === '-i' ? '-d' : arg); if (!detachedArgs.includes('-d')) { detachedArgs.splice(1, 0, '-d'); } // Optionally keep --rm for auto-cleanup const persistentArgs = runner.autoRemove ? detachedArgs : detachedArgs.filter(arg => arg !== '--rm'); capturedStdout = await runDockerWithStandardIO(persistentArgs, params, context, timeoutSeconds, runner.stdinJson, true); // Return container ID immediately return { containerId: capturedStdout.trim(), status: 'running', endpoint: env.ENDPOINT || `http://localhost:${env.PORT || 8080}` } as unknown as O; } ``` **Detached Mode Behavior:** - Container starts in background (`-d` flag) - Runner returns immediately with container ID - Container continues running after activity completes - Optional auto-remove when container exits **Use Case:** MCP server components that need to stay alive for the duration of a workflow run. **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:164-180]() --- ## Docker Path Resolution The runner resolves the Docker binary path to handle different installation locations: ```typescript async function resolveDockerPath(context?: ExecutionContext): Promise { if (cachedDockerPath) return cachedDockerPath; const commonPaths = [ '/usr/local/bin/docker', '/opt/homebrew/bin/docker', // macOS Homebrew '/usr/bin/docker', // Linux standard '/bin/docker', ]; for (const path of commonPaths) { try { await access(path, constants.X_OK); context?.logger.debug(`[Docker] Resolved docker path to: ${path}`); cachedDockerPath = path; return path; } catch { // Continue to next path } } // Fallback to PATH search context?.logger.info(`[Docker] Could not find docker. Fallback to using "docker" from PATH.`); cachedDockerPath = 'docker'; return 'docker'; } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:18-43]() --- ## Remote Runner Execution (Stub) The remote runner is currently a stub that falls back to inline execution: ```typescript case 'remote': context.logger.info(`[Runner] remote execution stub for ${runner.endpoint}`); context.emitProgress('Remote execution not yet implemented; returning inline output'); return runComponentInline(execute, params, context); ``` **Planned Features:** - HTTP/gRPC-based component execution - Language-agnostic component implementations - Distributed execution across multiple workers - Custom authentication via `authSecretName` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:530-533]() --- ## Runner Selection in Component Execution The `runComponentWithRunner` function dispatches to the appropriate execution strategy: ```typescript export async function runComponentWithRunner( runner: RunnerConfig, execute: (params: I, context: ExecutionContext) => Promise, params: I, context: ExecutionContext, ): Promise { switch (runner.kind) { case 'inline': return runComponentInline(execute, params, context); case 'docker': return runComponentInDocker(runner, params, context); case 'remote': context.logger.info(`[Runner] remote execution stub for ${runner.endpoint}`); context.emitProgress('Remote execution not yet implemented; returning inline output'); return runComponentInline(execute, params, context); default: throw new ConfigurationError(`Unsupported runner type: ${(runner as any).kind}`, { configKey: 'runner.kind', details: { runnerKind: (runner as any).kind }, }); } } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:519-540]() --- ## Component Activity Integration The Temporal activity `runComponentActivity` uses the runner system transparently: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Temporal as Temporal Workflow participant Activity as runComponentActivity participant Registry as componentRegistry participant Runner as runComponentWithRunner participant Docker as Docker Daemon Temporal->>Activity: Execute component action Activity->>Registry: componentRegistry.get(componentId) Registry-->>Activity: ComponentDefinition (with runner config) Activity->>Activity: Resolve spilled inputs
Parse parameters
Create ExecutionContext Activity->>Runner: runComponentWithRunner(runner, execute, params, context) alt runner.kind === 'docker' Runner->>Docker: docker run --rm -i --network=none ... Docker->>Docker: Execute container Docker-->>Runner: Exit code + output else runner.kind === 'inline' Runner->>Runner: component.execute(params, context) end Runner-->>Activity: Component output Activity->>Activity: Check for spilling
Record node I/O Activity-->>Temporal: Return output ``` **Key Points:** - Activity code is agnostic to runner type - Runner config comes from component definition - All runners receive the same `ExecutionContext` - Output handling (spilling, masking) is identical across runners **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:118-646](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:519-540]() --- ## Error Handling and Timeouts ### Timeout Management Docker execution enforces timeouts to prevent runaway containers: ```typescript const timeout = setTimeout(() => { proc.kill(); reject(new TimeoutError(`Docker container timed out after ${timeoutSeconds}s`, timeoutSeconds * 1000, { details: { dockerArgs: formatArgs(dockerArgs) }, })); }, timeoutSeconds * 1000); ``` **Default Timeout:** 300 seconds (5 minutes) **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:278-283]() ### Error Types The runner system uses typed errors for better diagnostics: ```typescript // Container execution failures throw new ContainerError(`Docker container failed with exit code ${code}: ${stderr}`, { details: { exitCode: code, stderr, stdout, dockerArgs: formatArgs(dockerArgs) }, }); // Timeout errors throw new TimeoutError(`Docker container timed out after ${timeoutSeconds}s`, timeoutSeconds * 1000, { details: { dockerArgs: formatArgs(dockerArgs) }, }); // Configuration errors throw new ConfigurationError(`Unsupported runner type: ${(runner as any).kind}`, { configKey: 'runner.kind', details: { runnerKind: (runner as any).kind }, }); ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:365-368](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:278-283](), [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:535-538]() --- ## Runner Configuration Examples ### Security Scanner (Docker) ```typescript { id: 'security.trufflehog', label: 'TruffleHog Secret Scanner', runner: { kind: 'docker', image: 'trufflesecurity/trufflehog:latest', command: ['git', 'scan', '--json', '.'], network: 'none', timeoutSeconds: 600, volumes: [ { source: '/var/run/docker.sock', target: '/var/run/docker.sock', readOnly: true, }, ], }, } ``` ### Data Transformer (Inline) ```typescript { id: 'core.transform.json', label: 'JSON Transformer', runner: { kind: 'inline', }, } ``` ### MCP Server (Docker Detached) ```typescript { id: 'mcp.aws-cloudtrail', label: 'AWS CloudTrail MCP Server', runner: { kind: 'docker', image: 'shipsecai/mcp-aws-cloudtrail:latest', command: ['node', '/app/dist/index.js'], env: { PORT: '8080', }, network: 'bridge', ports: { '0.0.0.0:0': 8080, // Random host port }, detached: true, autoRemove: true, timeoutSeconds: 3600, }, } ``` **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/types.ts:20-56]() --- ## Isolation Comparison Matrix | Aspect | Inline | Docker (network=none) | Docker (network=bridge) | Remote | |--------|--------|-----------------------|-------------------------|--------| | **Process Isolation** | None | Full | Full | Full | | **Memory Isolation** | Shared | Isolated | Isolated | Isolated | | **Network Access** | Full | None | Limited | Full | | **File System Access** | Full | Mounted volumes only | Mounted volumes only | N/A | | **Startup Overhead** | ~0ms | ~100-500ms | ~100-500ms | ~50-200ms | | **Resource Limits** | None | Configurable (cgroups) | Configurable (cgroups) | External | | **Security Boundary** | None | Strong | Medium | Strong | | **Use Case** | Trusted code | Untrusted scanners | Services needing network | External systems | **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/runner.ts:77-540]() --- ## Summary The runner system provides a flexible abstraction for component execution with three isolation levels: 1. **Inline Runner**: Direct in-process execution for trusted, lightweight components 2. **Docker Runner**: Containerized execution with strong isolation for security tools and external scanners 3. **Remote Runner**: (Planned) HTTP/gRPC-based execution for distributed systems Key capabilities: - **PTY support** for rich terminal output with ANSI codes - **File-based I/O** for reliable data exchange with containers - **Network isolation** with configurable network modes - **Detached mode** for long-running services - **Automatic cleanup** of containers and temporary files - **Timeout enforcement** to prevent runaway execution All runners receive a consistent `ExecutionContext` with service interfaces, making component code independent of the execution strategy.

Parameter configuration is the system that allows users to customize component behavior through the workflow builder UI. This page documents how component parameters are defined, rendered, validated, and passed to the worker for execution. Parameters differ from inputs (which receive data from upstream nodes) and outputs (which send data downstream); parameters are static configuration values set during workflow design. For information about dynamic port resolution based on parameter values, see [Dynamic Port Resolution](#3.4). For details on how parameters are passed to components during execution, see [Component Execution Model](#3.2). ## Overview The parameter configuration system consists of three layers: 1. **Definition Layer**: Components declare parameters in their metadata with type information, validation rules, and UI hints 2. **UI Layer**: The `ParameterField` component renders appropriate input controls based on parameter type 3. **Storage Layer**: Parameter values are persisted in the workflow graph as part of node configuration The system supports both simple scalar types (text, number, boolean) and complex types (JSON, arrays, custom editors) with specialized UI components for domain-specific configuration tasks. **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/workflow/ParameterField.tsx:1-45](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:860-893]() ## Parameter Types Each parameter has a `type` field defined in `ComponentParameterType` that determines its rendering and validation behavior. The system supports the following parameter types: | Type | Description | UI Control | Use Case | |------|-------------|------------|----------| | `text` | Single-line text input | `` | Simple strings, IDs, names | | `textarea` | Multi-line text input | `

## Purpose & Scope This document covers the AI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration subsystem in ShipSec Studio. It explains how AI agents execute multi-turn conversations, dynamically discover and call tools via the MCP Gateway, and how tools are registered, managed, and executed across different transport types. For workflow execution mechanics, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). For component system details, see [Component System](#3). For authentication and authorization, see [Authentication and Authorization](#6.5). --- ## Overview The AI & MCP integration enables workflows to use LLM-powered agents that can dynamically discover and invoke tools. The system consists of: - **AI Agent Component**: Executes in the Temporal worker, manages conversation state, and orchestrates tool calls - **MCP Gateway**: Backend service that aggregates tools from multiple sources and routes tool calls - **Tool Registry**: Redis-backed cache of discovered tools and their metadata - **MCP Servers**: External or internal tool providers accessed via HTTP or STDIO transports - **Discovery System**: Temporal workflows for async tool discovery and caching ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Worker (Temporal)" AGENT["AI Agent Component

messages: AgentMessage[]; // role: 'system' | 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool' } ``` System prompt handling (`ensureSystemMessage`) ensures the system message is always first, replacing it if the prompt changes between turns. Memory trimming (`trimConversation`) keeps only the most recent `memorySize` messages (excluding system prompt) to manage context window size. **Sources:** [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:56-61](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:256-290]() ### Model Provider Configuration The agent supports three LLM providers via the AI SDK: ```mermaid graph LR AGENT["AI Agent"] subgraph "Providers" OPENAI["OpenAI

Error if no key found **Sources:** [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:32-42](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:227-254](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:602-673]() ### Tool Discovery and Gateway Connection When `connectedToolNodeIds` are present in the execution context metadata, the agent: 1. **Generates Session Token**: Calls `/internal/mcp/generate-token` with `runId`, `organizationId`, and `allowedNodeIds` 2. **Connects to Gateway**: Uses `createMCPClient` to establish HTTP connection to gateway at `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_URL` (`http://localhost:3211/api/v1/mcp/gateway`) 3. **Discovers Tools**: Gateway returns available tools scoped to the connected node IDs 4. **Registers Tools**: Tools are passed to `ToolLoopAgent` for execution ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as AI Agent participant Token as getGatewaySessionToken participant Gateway as MCP Gateway participant MCP as createMCPClient Agent->>Token: Generate session token Token->>Gateway: POST /internal/mcp/generate-token Gateway-->>Token: { token: "..." } Token-->>Agent: sessionToken Agent->>MCP: createMCPClient({ url, headers }) MCP->>Gateway: HTTP MCP Initialize Gateway-->>MCP: Server initialized Agent->>MCP: client.tools() MCP->>Gateway: listTools() Gateway-->>MCP: tools[] MCP-->>Agent: ToolSet { toolName: { execute, inputSchema } } Agent->>Agent: ToolLoopAgent({ tools }) ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:47-48](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:467-500](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:561-581]() ### Tool Loop Execution The agent uses `ToolLoopAgent` from the AI SDK to orchestrate multi-step reasoning with tool calls: ```typescript const agentSettings: ToolLoopAgentSettings = { id: `${sessionId}-agent`, model, instructions: resolvedSystemPrompt, temperature, maxOutputTokens: maxTokens, stopWhen: stepCountIs(stepLimit), onStepFinish: (stepResult) => { // Emit tool inputs/outputs for observability for (const call of stepResult.toolCalls) { agentStream.emitToolInput(call.toolCallId, call.toolName, input); } for (const result of stepResult.toolResults) { agentStream.emitToolOutput(result.toolCallId, result.toolName, output); } }, tools: discoveredTools, }; ``` The `onStepFinish` callback emits tool call events to `AgentStreamRecorder` for real-time streaming to the frontend via execution inspector. Tool results are stored in conversation state as `tool` role messages for multi-turn context. **Sources:** [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:673-694](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:708-723](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:726-747]() --- ## MCP Gateway Architecture The MCP Gateway (`McpGatewayService`) aggregates tools from multiple sources and provides a unified MCP server interface per workflow run. ### Session-Scoped Server Instances The gateway maintains a cache of `McpServer` instances keyed by `runId` and `allowedNodeIds`: ```typescript // Cache key format: "runId" or "runId:nodeId1,nodeId2" private readonly servers = new Map(); private readonly registeredToolNames = new Map>(); ``` Multiple agents in the same run can have different tool scopes by providing different `allowedNodeIds`, resulting in separate cache entries. This prevents tool leakage between agents with different security contexts. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:30-42](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:55-97]() ### Access Validation Before serving tools, the gateway validates run access: ```mermaid graph TD REQUEST["Gateway Request

tool registration"] REQUEST --> VALIDATE VALIDATE --> REPO REPO --> CHECK_ORG CHECK_ORG -->|"No"| FORBIDDEN CHECK_ORG -->|"Yes"| PROCEED ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:123-138]() ### Tool Registration Flow The gateway registers tools from three sources: ```mermaid graph TB START["registerTools()

Generate callId Gateway->>Temporal: signalWorkflow('executeToolCall') Temporal->>Workflow: Signal received Workflow->>Workflow: Store signal in toolCallQueue Workflow->>Activity: Execute component Activity-->>Workflow: Component output Workflow->>Workflow: Store result in toolCallResults Gateway->>Gateway: pollForToolCallResult()
Loop with queryWorkflow Gateway->>Temporal: queryWorkflow('getToolCallResult') Temporal->>Workflow: Query callId Workflow-->>Temporal: { success, output } Temporal-->>Gateway: Result Gateway-->>Gateway: Return to AI agent ``` The gateway generates a unique `callId` and polls for results via `getToolCallResult` query with a 60-second timeout and 500ms interval. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:583-641](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:643-674]() ### External Tool Proxying External tools are called via persistent MCP clients: ```typescript // Persistent client pool - reused across tool calls private readonly externalClients = new Map(); async getOrCreateExternalClient(endpoint: string): Promise { const existing = this.externalClients.get(endpoint); if (existing) return existing; const transport = new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL(endpoint), { ... }); const client = new Client({ name: 'shipsec-gateway-client', version: '1.0.0' }, { ... }); await client.connect(transport); this.externalClients.set(endpoint, client); return client; } ``` The stdio-proxy rejects re-initialization, so clients must be reused for the lifetime of the run. Tool calls use a 30-second timeout with 3 retries, evicting broken clients on failure. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:41-42](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:471-528](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:530-580]() ### HTTP Transport Controller The `McpGatewayController` handles HTTP requests using Streamable HTTP transport: ```mermaid graph TB REQUEST["HTTP Request

On SSE disconnect, the transport and gateway server are cleaned up. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts:14-126]() --- ## Tool Registry The `ToolRegistryService` maintains a Redis-backed cache of tool registrations and metadata. ### Tool Registration Types ```typescript interface RegisteredTool { toolName: string; type: 'component' | 'mcp-server' | 'local-mcp'; nodeId: string; componentId?: string; description?: string; inputSchema?: Record; endpoint?: string; serverId?: string; status: 'pending' | 'ready' | 'failed'; exposedToAgent?: boolean; parameters?: Record; credentials?: Record; } ``` **Component Tools** (`type: 'component'`): - Registered via `POST /internal/mcp/register-component` - Executed via Temporal signals to workflow - Support parameter overrides and credential injection **MCP Server Tools** (`type: 'mcp-server'`): - Pre-registered in database via MCP Servers page - Tools discovered and cached in Redis - Proxied via persistent HTTP/STDIO clients **Local MCP Tools** (`type: 'local-mcp'`): - Ephemeral STDIO servers spawned per run - Discovered on-the-fly, no pre-registration - Docker container lifecycle managed by worker **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:1-400]() (interface definitions in this file) ### Redis Storage Schema | Key Pattern | Value | Purpose | |-------------|-------|---------| | `mcp:tools:{runId}` | Hash | Tool registrations for run | | `mcp:tools:{runId}:{nodeId}` | JSON | Pre-discovered tools for server | | `mcp:credentials:{runId}:{nodeId}` | JSON | Resolved credentials | | `mcp:containers:{runId}` | Set | Container IDs to cleanup | | `mcp-discovery:{cacheToken}` | JSON | Discovery results cache | Tool registrations expire after 24 hours. Discovery caches expire after 1 hour. **Sources:** Tool registry implementation details inferred from [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts]() and [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:188-394]() ### Tool Readiness Polling Agents poll for tool readiness before execution: ```typescript // Activity in worker async areAllToolsReadyActivity(runId: string, requiredNodeIds: string[]): Promise { const response = await fetch(`${BACKEND_URL}/internal/mcp/tools-ready`, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ runId, requiredNodeIds }), }); const result = await response.json(); return result.ready; } ``` The activity polls with exponential backoff (100ms → 5000ms) up to 60 seconds. This prevents race conditions where agent connects before tools are registered. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:60-64]() and related worker activity implementation --- ## MCP Server Management The frontend MCP Library page (`McpLibraryPage`) provides CRUD operations for custom MCP servers. ### Server Configuration | Field | Type | Required | Purpose | |-------|------|----------|---------| | `name` | string | Yes | Display name | | `description` | string | No | Server description | | `transportType` | 'http' \| 'stdio' | Yes | Connection method | | `endpoint` | string | HTTP only | HTTP URL | | `command` | string | STDIO only | Binary/script to execute | | `args` | string[] | STDIO only | Command arguments | | `headers` | Record | HTTP only | Authentication headers | | `healthCheckUrl` | string | No | Health check endpoint | | `enabled` | boolean | Yes | Enable/disable server | | `groupId` | string | No | MCP group membership | HTTP headers support secret references: `{{secret:secretId}}` values are resolved via `SecretResolver` before tool discovery. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:225-253](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:138-220]() ### Header Encryption Server headers are encrypted at rest using `McpServersEncryptionService`: ```typescript interface EncryptedHeaders { ciphertext: string; iv: string; authTag: string; keyId: string; } ``` The service uses AES-256-GCM encryption with a master key from environment. Header keys (not values) are exposed in API responses for UI display, but values remain encrypted until tool execution. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:74-88](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:145-164]() ### Health Check Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as MCP Library Page participant API as MCP Servers API participant Service as McpServersService participant Temporal as Temporal Service participant Worker as Discovery Activity UI->>API: POST /api/v1/mcp-servers/:id/test API->>Service: testServerConnection(auth, id) alt HTTP Server Service->>Service: Direct MCP protocol test Service-->>API: { success, toolCount } else STDIO Server Service->>Temporal: startWorkflow('mcpDiscoveryWorkflow') Temporal->>Worker: discoverMcpToolsActivity Worker->>Worker: Spawn Docker container Worker->>Worker: Connect via stdio-proxy Worker->>Worker: List tools Worker->>Worker: Cleanup container Worker-->>Temporal: { tools } Temporal-->>Service: Discovery result Service->>Service: Update health status Service->>Service: Upsert tools to DB Service-->>API: { success, toolCount } end API-->>UI: Health check result ``` STDIO servers require Temporal workflows for proper container lifecycle management. HTTP servers can be tested directly from the backend. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:445-495]() --- ## MCP Discovery System The discovery system pre-discovers tools before saving server configurations, enabling preview and validation. ### Discovery Workflow The `mcpDiscoveryWorkflow` handles single-server discovery: ```typescript interface DiscoveryInput { transport: 'http' | 'stdio'; name: string; endpoint?: string; headers?: Record; command?: string; args?: string[]; image?: string; cacheToken?: string; } interface DiscoveryResult { workflowId: string; status: 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed'; tools?: McpTool[]; toolCount?: number; error?: string; errorCode?: string; } ``` The workflow: 1. Validates input (HTTP requires `endpoint`, STDIO requires `command`) 2. Calls `discoverMcpToolsActivity` with 30-second timeout 3. Caches results to Redis if `cacheToken` provided 4. Returns structured result with tool list A query handler `getDiscoveryResult` allows polling for status updates. **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:10-222]() ### Discovery Activity Implementation For STDIO servers, the activity spawns Docker containers: ```mermaid graph TB START["discoverMcpToolsActivity

Container lifecycle is managed with `AbortController` for cleanup on timeout or error. **Sources:** Worker discovery activity implementation (referenced in workflow but detailed implementation not in provided files) ### Group Discovery `mcpGroupDiscoveryWorkflow` discovers multiple servers with a single container: ```typescript interface GroupDiscoveryInput { servers: DiscoveryInput[]; image?: string; cacheTokens?: Record; } interface GroupDiscoveryResult { workflowId: string; status: 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed'; results?: GroupDiscoveryResultEntry[]; } ``` The workflow calls `discoverMcpGroupToolsActivity`, which spawns one container and sequentially discovers tools from each server. Results are cached individually using the `cacheTokens` map. **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:224-318]() ### Discovery UI Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant UI as McpLibraryPage participant API as Discovery API participant Temporal as Temporal Service participant Worker as Discovery Workflow participant Redis User->>UI: Configure server (endpoint/command) User->>UI: Click "Test & Discover" UI->>API: POST /api/v1/mcp/discover API->>Temporal: startWorkflow('mcpDiscoveryWorkflow') Temporal->>Worker: Start discovery API-->>UI: { workflowId, cacheToken, status: 'started' } loop Poll every 2 seconds UI->>API: GET /api/v1/mcp/discover/:workflowId API->>Temporal: queryWorkflow('getDiscoveryResult') Temporal->>Worker: Query workflow state Worker-->>Temporal: Current status Temporal-->>API: { status, tools, toolCount } API-->>UI: Discovery status alt Status: completed UI->>UI: Display tool preview UI->>UI: Enable save button else Status: failed UI->>UI: Display error message end end User->>UI: Click "Save" UI->>API: POST /api/v1/mcp-servers
{ ...config, cacheToken } API->>Redis: Get cached tools Redis-->>API: tools[] API->>API: Create server + insert tools API->>Redis: Delete cache API-->>UI: Server created ``` The `cacheToken` (UUIDv4) links the discovery result to the server creation, allowing instant tool availability without re-discovery. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:703-771](), [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts:1-172](), [frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts:1-140]() ### MCP Group Templates Predefined server groups (e.g., AWS MCPs) are registered in code: ```typescript interface McpGroupTemplate { slug: string; name: string; credentialContractName: string; defaultDockerImage: string; servers: { name: string; transportType: 'http' | 'stdio'; command?: string; args?: string[]; recommended: boolean; defaultSelected: boolean; }[]; } ``` Templates are synced to the database via `POST /api/v1/mcp-groups/sync-templates`. Users import templates via the MCP Library, triggering group discovery before creation. **Sources:** [frontend/src/services/mcpGroupsApi.ts:33-56](), [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:979-1112]() --- ## Tool Execution Patterns ### Tool Mode Nodes Nodes with `mode: 'tool'` register themselves as callable tools: ```mermaid graph LR NODE["Workflow Node

externalSources.filter((source) => { // Direct match if (allowedNodeIds.includes(source.nodeId)) return true; // Hierarchical match: 'parent' matches 'parent/child' for (const allowedId of allowedNodeIds) { if (source.nodeId.startsWith(`${allowedId}/`)) return true; } return false; }) : externalSources; ``` This enables single-connection discovery of all tools in a group. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:310-341]() ### Execution Timeline ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Workflow as shipsecWorkflowRun participant Agent as ai-agent component participant Activity as registerComponentToolActivity participant Registry as Tool Registry (Redis) participant Gateway as MCP Gateway participant Temporal as Temporal Service Note over Workflow,Registry: Phase 1: Tool Registration (pre-agent) loop For each tool-mode node Workflow->>Activity: Register component tool Activity->>Registry: Store tool metadata end Note over Agent,Temporal: Phase 2: Agent Execution Workflow->>Agent: Execute with connected tools Agent->>Agent: getGatewaySessionToken() Agent->>Gateway: Create MCP client Gateway->>Registry: Get tools for run + nodeIds Gateway-->>Agent: ToolSet { tool1, tool2, ... } Agent->>Agent: ToolLoopAgent.generate() loop Tool calls Agent->>Gateway: Execute tool Gateway->>Temporal: signalWorkflow('executeToolCall') Temporal->>Workflow: Deliver signal Workflow->>Workflow: Execute component Workflow->>Workflow: Store result Gateway->>Temporal: queryWorkflow('getToolCallResult') Temporal->>Workflow: Query result Workflow-->>Gateway: Tool output Gateway-->>Agent: Tool result end Agent-->>Workflow: Final response ``` Tool registration happens during workflow execution before the agent node runs. The agent polls for tool readiness before connecting to the gateway. **Sources:** Workflow execution flow [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:174-449](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:583-641]() --- ## Key Implementation Details ### Thread Safety and Scaling The gateway uses in-memory caches (`servers`, `registeredToolNames`, `externalClients`) which are NOT thread-safe across multiple backend instances: ```typescript // SCALING LIMITATION: Single-instance design private readonly servers = new Map(); private readonly externalClients = new Map(); ``` For horizontal scaling, implement: - **Sticky sessions** via load balancer affinity (simplest) - **Redis pub/sub** for cache invalidation - **Stateful gateway pods** dedicated to MCP handling **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:28-41](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts:19-21]() ### Error Handling Tool call errors are gracefully handled: ```typescript // Component tool execution try { const result = await this.callComponentTool(tool, runId, args); await this.logToolCall(runId, tool.toolName, 'COMPLETED', tool.nodeId); await this.temporalService.signalWorkflow({ signalName: 'toolCallCompleted', args: { status: 'completed', output: result } }); } catch (error) { await this.logToolCall(runId, tool.toolName, 'FAILED', tool.nodeId, { error }); await this.temporalService.signalWorkflow({ signalName: 'toolCallCompleted', args: { status: 'failed', errorMessage } }); return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: `Error: ${errorMessage}` }], isError: true }; } ``` Failed tool calls return error messages to the agent, allowing it to retry or handle gracefully. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:229-291]() ### Tool Call Logging All tool calls are logged to the trace repository: ```typescript await this.traceRepository.append({ runId, type: 'NODE_PROGRESS', nodeRef: tool.nodeId, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), sequence: lastSeq + 1, level: status === 'FAILED' ? 'error' : 'info', message: `Tool ${status}: ${toolName}`, error: details.error, outputSummary: details.output, data: { duration, toolName }, }); ``` This provides observability in the execution timeline without disrupting the workflow graph state. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:140-172]() --- This document covers the complete AI & MCP integration subsystem, from agent execution through tool discovery, registration, and execution across multiple transport types.

## Purpose and Scope The AI Agent Component (`core.ai.agent`) provides multi-turn conversational AI capabilities within ShipSec Studio workflows. The `closeDiscovery` function calls `mcpClient.close()`. Sources: [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:765-769]() ### Testing with Mock Overrides The component supports dependency injection for testing via `context.metadata.aiSdkOverrides`: ```typescript interface AiSdkOverrides { ToolLoopAgent?: typeof ToolLoopAgent; stepCountIs?: typeof stepCountIs; createOpenAI?: typeof createOpenAI; createGoogleGenerativeAI?: typeof createGoogleGenerativeAI; createMCPClient?: typeof createMCPClient; } ``` This enables unit tests to mock AI SDK components without network calls. Sources: [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:66-72](), [worker/src/components/ai/__tests__/ai-agent.test.ts:1-332]() --- ## Key Design Decisions ### Why Inline Runner? The agent uses `runner: { kind: 'inline' }` rather than an activity runner. This means it executes directly in the workflow context, not as a separate Temporal activity. Benefits: - Allows synchronous MCP client connections - Simplifies tool call orchestration - Enables direct access to workflow signals/queries Trade-off: Longer-running agent loops extend workflow task time. ### Why Persistent External Client Pool? The MCP Gateway maintains `externalClients` as a persistent cache because stdio-proxy servers reject re-initialization: ```typescript private readonly externalClients = new Map(); ``` Once connected, the same client instance must be reused for both discovery and tool calls. If a call fails, the client is evicted and recreated on the next attempt. Sources: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:41]() ### Why Session Token with allowedNodeIds? The session token encodes `allowedNodeIds` to scope tool access per agent. This enables: - Multiple agents in same workflow with different tool sets - Fine-grained permission control - Cache isolation (different cache keys for different scopes) Sources: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:64-70]()

## Purpose and Scope The **MCP Gateway** is a backend service that enables AI agents to dynamically discover and call tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It acts as a bridge between AI agents executing in workflows and both internal component-based tools and external MCP servers. The gateway: - **Exposes an MCP server interface** to AI agents via Streamable HTTP transport - **Acts as an MCP client** to external MCP servers (HTTP and STDIO) - **Routes tool calls** to the appropriate execution backend (Temporal workflows for component tools, proxied connections for external tools) - **Scopes tool visibility** based on session tokens (per runId and allowedNodeIds) For information about: - AI agent configuration and usage, see [AI Agent Component](#4.1) - Managing and discovering MCP servers, see [MCP Server Management](#4.3) - MCP discovery workflows, see [MCP Discovery System](#4.4) - How tools execute within workflows, see [Tool Execution Patterns](#4.5) Sources: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:1-697](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts:1-127]() --- ## Architecture Overview The MCP Gateway operates as a **stateful proxy** between AI agents and tool execution backends. Each workflow run with AI agents gets isolated tool environments through session-scoped server instances. ### Gateway Dual Role ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Worker (AI Agent)" AGENT["AI SDK Agent

Sources: [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:542-770]() --- ## Scaling Considerations ### Current Limitations The gateway has **in-memory state** for active sessions, making it a single-instance design [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:29-36](): ```typescript // Cache of servers per runId // NOTE: This is in-memory state for active sessions. Single-instance design. // SCALING LIMITATION: For horizontal scaling, implement one of: // - Redis pub/sub for cache invalidation across instances // - Sticky sessions via load balancer affinity (simplest) // - Stateful instances dedicated to MCP gateway private readonly servers = new Map(); private readonly transports = new Map(); ``` ### Recommended Scaling Strategies 1. **Sticky sessions** (simplest): Configure load balancer to route requests from the same `runId` to the same backend instance. This preserves the in-memory session state. 2. **Redis session storage**: Serialize `McpServer` state (tool registrations) to Redis and reconstruct on any instance. This requires careful handling of external client connections. 3. **Dedicated MCP gateway instances**: Run the gateway as a separate service with its own load balancer, separate from the main API instances. ### Tool Registry Scaling The `ToolRegistryService` uses Redis for distributed state, so it scales horizontally without issues. The gateway service is the primary scaling concern. Sources: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:29-42](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts:18-21]()
