The Tool Registry is a Redis-backed ephemeral storage service that maintains tool metadata and encrypted credentials during workflow execution. It serves as the bridge between Temporal workflows (where tool nodes execute and resolve credentials) and the MCP Gateway (where AI agents discover and invoke tools). This registry enables dynamic tool discovery, credential isolation, and hierarchical tool filtering for multi-agent workflows. For information about how agents discover and call tools, see [Tool Execution Patterns](#4.6). For MCP server registration and lifecycle management, see [MCP Server Management](#4.4). --- ## Overview The Tool Registry (`ToolRegistryService`) implements a run-scoped tool catalog with the following characteristics: - **Ephemeral Storage**: Tools are stored per workflow run (`runId`) with a 1-hour TTL - **Credential Encryption**: All sensitive data is encrypted using `SecretsEncryptionService` - **Type Polymorphism**: Supports both internal components and external MCP servers - **Hierarchical Filtering**: Agent nodes can scope tool access using parent/child node relationships - **Readiness Tracking**: Tools have status flags (`pending`, `ready`, `error`) for synchronization **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:1-11]() ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Registration Phase" WF["Temporal Workflow
(shipsecWorkflowRun)"] CompAct["Component Activity
(runComponentActivity)"] McpAct["MCP Registration Activity
(registerMcpServerActivity)"] end subgraph "Tool Registry Service" RegComp["registerComponentTool()"] RegMcp["registerMcpServer()"] Redis[("Redis
mcp:run:{runId}:tools")] Encrypt["SecretsEncryptionService"] end subgraph "Discovery Phase" Agent["AI Agent Component
(ai-agent.ts)"] Gateway["MCP Gateway Service
(McpGatewayService)"] GetTools["getToolsForRun(runId, allowedNodeIds)"] end WF --> CompAct WF --> McpAct CompAct --> RegComp McpAct --> RegMcp RegComp --> Encrypt RegMcp --> Encrypt Encrypt --> Redis Agent --> Gateway Gateway --> GetTools GetTools --> Redis style Redis fill:#f9f9f9 style Encrypt fill:#f9f9f9 ``` **Diagram: Tool Registry Data Flow** **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:93-104](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:473-500](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:174-449]() --- ## Redis Data Model The registry uses a hash-based data structure with two key patterns: ### Primary Tool Registry Key ``` mcp:run:{runId}:tools ``` This Redis hash stores `RegisteredTool` objects keyed by `nodeId`. Each entry contains: | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `nodeId` | string | Unique workflow node ID (e.g., `"aws-mcp-group/cloudtrail"`) | | `toolName` | string | Agent-visible tool name (e.g., `"check_ip_reputation"`) | | `type` | RegisteredToolType | Tool source: `component`, `mcp-server`, `remote-mcp`, `local-mcp`, `mcp-group` | | `status` | ToolStatus | Readiness: `pending`, `ready`, `error` | | `componentId` | string? | Component ID for internal tools (e.g., `"security.abuseipdb"`) | | `inputSchema` | ToolInputSchema | JSON Schema for tool inputs | | `description` | string | Human-readable description for the agent | | `encryptedCredentials` | string? | Encrypted JSON blob of credentials/headers | | `endpoint` | string? | HTTP/stdio endpoint for MCP servers | | `containerId` | string? | Docker container ID for local MCP servers | | `serverId` | string? | Database MCP server ID for pre-registered servers | | `parameters` | object? | Static parameter overrides for component tools | | `exposedToAgent` | boolean? | Whether to expose to agents (default: true) | **TTL:** 1 hour (3600 seconds) **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:38-89](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:91]() ### Server Tools Key ``` mcp:run:{runId}:server:{nodeId}:tools ``` This Redis key-value pair stores the pre-discovered tool definitions from an MCP server as a JSON array: ```json [ { "name": "lookup_events", "description": "Lookup CloudTrail events", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } } } ] ``` **TTL:** 1 hour (3600 seconds) **Purpose:** Avoid re-discovering tools on every agent connection. The MCP Gateway reads this cache first before falling back to live discovery. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:209-223](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:228-246]() --- ## Tool Types and Status ### RegisteredToolType | Type | Source | Execution | |------|--------|-----------| | `component` | ShipSec component (190+ registry) | Temporal activity via signal | | `mcp-server` | Local MCP via stdio transport | Proxied HTTP to container | | `remote-mcp` | Remote MCP via HTTP transport | Proxied HTTP to external endpoint | | `local-mcp` | Dynamically discovered local MCP | Proxied HTTP to container | | `mcp-group` | MCP group provider node | Not directly executable; provides children | **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:20-28]() ### ToolStatus | Status | Meaning | When Set | |--------|---------|----------| | `pending` | Tool is initializing | Initial registration (not currently used) | | `ready` | Tool is available for agents | After successful registration | | `error` | Tool failed to initialize | Via `updateToolStatus()` | **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:30-33]() --- ## Registration Process ### Component Tool Registration Component tools are registered by the workflow when a tool-mode node executes. The workflow calls the internal MCP API endpoint: ``` POST /internal/mcp/register-component ``` **Flow:** 1. Tool-mode component executes (e.g., `security.abuseipdb` with `toolProvider` metadata) 2. Component resolves credentials from secrets or parameters 3. Activity calls `registerComponentTool()` via internal API 4. Registry encrypts credentials and stores in Redis 5. Gateway server is refreshed to expose the new tool **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:36-41](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:113-155]() ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant WF as "Temporal Workflow" participant Act as "runComponentActivity" participant API as "Internal MCP API" participant Reg as "ToolRegistryService" participant Enc as "SecretsEncryptionService" participant Redis as "Redis" participant GW as "McpGatewayService" WF->>Act: Execute tool-mode node Act->>Act: Resolve credentials Act->>API: POST /internal/mcp/register-component API->>Reg: registerComponentTool(input) Reg->>Enc: encrypt(credentials) Enc-->>Reg: encryptionMaterial Reg->>Redis: HSET mcp:run:{runId}:tools {nodeId} {tool} Reg->>Redis: EXPIRE key 3600 Reg-->>API: success API->>GW: refreshServersForRun(runId) GW->>GW: Update cached MCP servers API-->>Act: { success: true } ``` **Diagram: Component Tool Registration Flow** **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:113-155](), [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:36-41]() **Example Registration Payload:** ```typescript { runId: "wfrun-abc123", nodeId: "abuseipdb-check", toolName: "check_ip_reputation", componentId: "security.abuseipdb", description: "Check IP reputation using AbuseIPDB", inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: { ipAddress: { type: "string", pattern: "^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$" } }, required: ["ipAddress"] }, credentials: { apiKey: "sk-xxxxx" }, parameters: { daysToCheck: 90 } } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts:76-97]() ### MCP Server Registration MCP servers are registered with pre-discovered tools after the server container/connection is established: ``` POST /internal/mcp/register-mcp-server ``` **Flow:** 1. MCP server node executes (e.g., `mcp.library.aws-cloudtrail`) 2. Activity discovers tools via MCP protocol (`tools/list`) 3. Activity calls `registerMcpServer()` with tool list 4. Registry stores server metadata and tool definitions separately 5. Gateway can immediately expose tools without re-discovery **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:47-52](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:164-223]() **Example Registration Payload:** ```typescript { runId: "wfrun-abc123", nodeId: "aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudtrail", serverName: "aws-cloudtrail", serverId: "uuid-server-123", transport: "stdio", endpoint: "http://localhost:8081/mcp", containerId: "container-xyz789", tools: [ { name: "lookup_events", description: "Lookup CloudTrail events by time range and filters", inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: { startTime: { type: "string", format: "date-time" }, endTime: { type: "string", format: "date-time" }, eventName: { type: "string" } } } }, { name: "get_event_details", description: "Get detailed information about a CloudTrail event", inputSchema: { type: "object", properties: { eventId: { type: "string" } }, required: ["eventId"] } } ] } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts:100-165]() --- ## Tool Discovery and Filtering ### Basic Discovery Agents retrieve tools via `getToolsForRun(runId, allowedNodeIds?)`: ```typescript // Get all tools for a run const allTools = await toolRegistry.getToolsForRun('wfrun-abc123'); // Get tools scoped to specific nodes const scopedTools = await toolRegistry.getToolsForRun('wfrun-abc123', ['node-a', 'node-b']); ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:248-270]() ### Hierarchical Filtering The registry supports parent/child node relationships using the `/` separator. This enables MCP groups to expose multiple child servers while allowing agents to scope access: ```typescript // Register parent group (not exposed to agent) await toolRegistry.registerComponentTool({ runId: 'wfrun-abc123', nodeId: 'aws-mcp-group', toolName: 'aws-mcp-group', componentId: 'mcp.group.aws', exposedToAgent: false, // Provider only // ... }); // Register child servers await toolRegistry.registerMcpServer({ runId: 'wfrun-abc123', nodeId: 'aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudtrail', // Hierarchical ID serverName: 'aws-cloudtrail', // ... }); await toolRegistry.registerMcpServer({ runId: 'wfrun-abc123', nodeId: 'aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudwatch', serverName: 'aws-cloudwatch', // ... }); // Agent scoped to parent ID receives both children const tools = await toolRegistry.getToolsForRun('wfrun-abc123', ['aws-mcp-group']); // Returns: aws-mcp-group, aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudtrail, aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudwatch ``` **Matching Logic:** 1. Direct match: `nodeId === allowedNodeId` 2. Hierarchical match: `nodeId.startsWith(allowedNodeId + '/')` 3. No partial prefix match: `"aws-mcp-group-extra"` does NOT match `"aws-mcp-group"` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:262-267](), [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts:292-358]() ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Tool Hierarchy" Parent["aws-mcp-group

(mcp-server)"] Child2["aws-mcp-group/aws-cloudwatch
(mcp-server)"] Child3["aws-mcp-group/aws-s3
(mcp-server)"] end subgraph "Agent Connection" Agent["AI Agent
allowedNodeIds: ['aws-mcp-group']"] Gateway["MCP Gateway"] Filter["getToolsForRun(runId, allowedNodeIds)"] end subgraph "Tool Exposure" T1["aws-cloudtrail__lookup_events"] T2["aws-cloudtrail__get_event_details"] T3["aws-cloudwatch__get_metrics"] T4["aws-s3__list_buckets"] end Parent -.provides.-> Child1 Parent -.provides.-> Child2 Parent -.provides.-> Child3 Agent --> Gateway Gateway --> Filter Filter --> Child1 Filter --> Child2 Filter --> Child3 Child1 --> T1 Child1 --> T2 Child2 --> T3 Child3 --> T4 style Parent fill:#f9f9f9 ``` **Diagram: Hierarchical Tool Filtering** **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:262-267](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:310-341]() ### Pre-Discovered Tool Retrieval The MCP Gateway checks for pre-discovered tools before attempting live discovery: ```typescript // Check Redis cache first const preDiscoveredTools = await toolRegistry.getServerTools(runId, nodeId); if (preDiscoveredTools && preDiscoveredTools.length > 0) { // Use cached tools immediately tools = preDiscoveredTools; } else { // Fallback: discover tools on-the-fly from endpoint tools = await discoverToolsFromEndpoint(endpoint); } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:349-375]() --- ## Credential Management ### Encryption All credentials (component API keys, MCP server headers) are encrypted before storage: ```typescript // Encrypt credentials const credentialsJson = JSON.stringify(credentials); const encryptionMaterial = await encryption.encrypt(credentialsJson); const encryptedCredentials = JSON.stringify(encryptionMaterial); // Store in RegisteredTool tool.encryptedCredentials = encryptedCredentials; ``` **Encryption Material Structure:** ```typescript { ciphertext: string; // Base64-encoded encrypted data keyId: string; // Key identifier for rotation } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:130-134]() ### Decryption Credentials are decrypted on-demand when the Gateway executes a component tool: ```typescript const credentials = await toolRegistry.getToolCredentials(runId, nodeId); // Returns: { apiKey: "sk-xxxxx", token: "another-secret" } ``` **Decryption Flow:** 1. Retrieve `encryptedCredentials` from Redis 2. Parse encryption material JSON 3. Decrypt using `SecretsEncryptionService` 4. Parse decrypted JSON (or return raw string for legacy remote-mcp) **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:301-323]() **Fallback Handling:** For backward compatibility with older MCP server registrations, the service attempts to parse decrypted credentials as JSON. If parsing fails for `remote-mcp` tools, it wraps the raw string as `{ authToken: decrypted }`. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:310-318]() --- ## Integration Points ### Internal MCP API The `InternalMcpController` exposes registration endpoints secured by `x-internal-token` header: | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | |----------|--------|---------| | `/internal/mcp/register-component` | POST | Register component tool | | `/internal/mcp/register-mcp-server` | POST | Register MCP server with tools | | `/internal/mcp/cleanup` | POST | Cleanup run and return container IDs | | `/internal/mcp/tools-ready` | POST | Check if required tools are ready | | `/internal/mcp/generate-token` | POST | Generate MCP gateway session token | **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:8-73]() ### MCP Gateway Service The Gateway queries the registry during agent connections: ```typescript async registerTools(server, runId, allowedTools?, allowedNodeIds?, registeredToolNames?) { // Fetch all registered tools for the run const allRegistered = await this.toolRegistry.getToolsForRun(runId, allowedNodeIds); // Register internal component tools for (const tool of internalTools) { if (tool.exposedToAgent === false) continue; server.registerTool(tool.toolName, { ... }, async (args) => { // Execute via Temporal signal }); } // Register external MCP tools (proxied) for (const source of externalSources) { const tools = await this.toolRegistry.getServerTools(runId, source.nodeId); for (const t of tools) { const proxiedName = `${source.toolName}__${t.name}`; server.registerTool(proxiedName, { ... }, async (args) => { // Proxy to external endpoint }); } } } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:174-449]() ### AI Agent Component The agent connects to the gateway, which transparently handles tool registry access: ```typescript const sessionToken = await getGatewaySessionToken( context.runId, organizationId, connectedToolNodeIds // allowedNodeIds ); const mcpClient = await createMCPClient({ transport: { type: 'http', url: 'http://localhost:3211/api/v1/mcp/gateway', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${sessionToken}` } } }); const tools = await mcpClient.tools(); // Gateway queries registry internally ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:566-580](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:473-500]() --- ## Readiness and Synchronization ### Checking Tool Readiness Workflows can wait for required tools to be ready before starting an agent: ```typescript const ready = await toolRegistry.areAllToolsReady(runId, ['node-a', 'node-b']); if (!ready) { throw new Error('Required tools not ready'); } ``` **Logic:** Checks that all specified `nodeIds` exist in the registry with `status: 'ready'`. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:328-348]() ### Updating Tool Status Activities can mark tools as errored if initialization fails: ```typescript await toolRegistry.updateToolStatus( runId, nodeId, 'error', 'Failed to connect to MCP server: connection timeout' ); ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:353-375]() --- ## Cleanup and Lifecycle ### Run Cleanup When a workflow completes, the registry is cleaned up: ```typescript const containerIds = await toolRegistry.cleanupRun(runId); // Returns: ['container-123', 'container-456'] for Docker cleanup // Registry also deletes the Redis hash: await redis.del(`mcp:run:${runId}:tools`); ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:381-399]() **Container ID Collection:** The cleanup process identifies all stdio MCP servers (`mcp-server` or `local-mcp` type) with `containerId` fields and returns them for Docker container termination. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:386-390]() ### TTL Expiration All registry keys expire after 1 hour (3600 seconds) to prevent memory leaks from abandoned runs. This TTL is reset on each write operation: ```typescript await this.redis.hset(key, nodeId, JSON.stringify(tool)); await this.redis.expire(key, REGISTRY_TTL_SECONDS); // 3600 ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:91](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:150-152]() --- ## Testing and Validation ### Unit Tests The registry has comprehensive unit tests covering: - # MCP Server Management
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.controller.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.controller.ts) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts](backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts) - [frontend/src/components/mcp/McpDiscoveryPreview.tsx](frontend/src/components/mcp/McpDiscoveryPreview.tsx) - [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx](frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx) - [frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts](frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts) - [frontend/src/services/mcpGroupsApi.ts](frontend/src/services/mcpGroupsApi.ts)
This document describes how MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers are configured, stored, and managed in ShipSec Studio. It covers server configuration models, transport types, CRUD operations, health checking, and the frontend management interface. For information about tool discovery workflows, see [MCP Discovery System](#4.5). For details on how discovered tools are registered and cached, see [Tool Registry](#4.3). For information on how the MCP Gateway routes tool calls, see [MCP Gateway Service](#4.2). --- ## MCP Server Types ShipSec Studio supports two transport types for connecting to MCP servers: ### HTTP Transport HTTP transport servers expose MCP protocol over HTTP/HTTPS endpoints. These servers are stateless and typically hosted externally. **Configuration Requirements:** - `endpoint`: Full URL to the MCP server (e.g., `https://api.example.com/mcp`) - `headers`: Optional authentication headers (stored encrypted) - `healthCheckUrl`: Optional custom health check endpoint **Connection Testing:** HTTP servers are tested directly by the backend service using MCP protocol messages (`initialize`, `tools/list`). No container orchestration is required. Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:473-650]() ### STDIO Transport STDIO transport servers run as local processes, typically in Docker containers managed by the worker. Communication occurs via standard input/output streams. **Configuration Requirements:** - `command`: Executable command to start the MCP server - `args`: Array of command-line arguments - `image`: Optional Docker image for isolated execution (can be specified at group level) **Connection Testing:** STDIO servers are tested via Temporal workflows that spawn the container, establish STDIO communication, test the MCP protocol, and clean up. This ensures proper worker environment testing. Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:476-555]() ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "HTTP Transport" HTTPConfig["endpoint: string
headers?: Record<string, string>
healthCheckUrl?: string"] HTTPTest["Direct HTTP Test
testHttpConnectionDirect()"] HTTPConn["POST /endpoint
{ method: 'initialize' }
{ method: 'tools/list' }"] end subgraph "STDIO Transport" STDIOConfig["command: string
args?: string[]
image?: string"] STDIOTest["Temporal Workflow Test
mcpDiscoveryWorkflow"] STDIOConn["Docker Container
PTY Communication
MCP Protocol over STDIO"] end HTTPConfig --> HTTPTest HTTPTest --> HTTPConn STDIOConfig --> STDIOTest STDIOTest --> STDIOConn style HTTPConfig fill:#f9f9f9 style STDIOConfig fill:#f9f9f9 ``` Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:452-555]() --- ## Server Configuration Model MCP servers are represented by the `McpServerRecord` database schema and exposed via `McpServerResponse` DTOs. ### Core Fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | `string` (UUID) | Unique server identifier | | `name` | `string` | Human-readable server name (unique per organization) | | `description` | `string?` | Optional server description | | `transportType` | `'http' \| 'stdio'` | Transport protocol type | | `enabled` | `boolean` | Whether server is active and discoverable | | `organizationId` | `string` | Organization scope for multi-tenancy | | `groupId` | `string?` | Optional MCP group membership | ### Transport-Specific Fields | Field | Type | Required For | Description | |-------|------|--------------|-------------| | `endpoint` | `string?` | HTTP | Server URL endpoint | | `command` | `string?` | STDIO | Executable command | | `args` | `string[]?` | STDIO | Command arguments | | `headers` | Encrypted JSON | HTTP | Authentication headers (encrypted at rest) | ### Health Status Fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `lastHealthCheck` | `Date?` | Timestamp of last health check | | `lastHealthStatus` | `'healthy' \| 'unhealthy' \| 'unknown'` | Last known health status | | `healthCheckUrl` | `string?` | Optional custom health check endpoint | Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/dto/mcp-servers.dto.ts](), [backend/src/database/schema.ts]() ### Header Encryption Authentication headers are encrypted before storage using AES-256-GCM encryption. The `McpServersEncryptionService` manages encryption keys and provides secure header handling. **Encrypted Header Structure:** ```typescript { ciphertext: string; // Base64 encrypted payload iv: string; // Initialization vector authTag: string; // Authentication tag for integrity keyId: string; // Key identifier for rotation } ``` **Secret References:** Headers can reference secrets stored in the secrets table using the syntax `{{secret:SECRET_ID}}`. The `SecretResolver` resolves these references during server connection. Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:147-163](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.encryption.ts]() --- ## Server Persistence ### Database Schema MCP servers are stored in the `mcp_servers` table: ```sql CREATE TABLE mcp_servers ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL, description TEXT, transport_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, -- 'http' or 'stdio' endpoint TEXT, command TEXT, args JSONB, -- string[] headers JSONB, -- { ciphertext, iv, authTag, keyId } health_check_url TEXT, last_health_check TIMESTAMP, last_health_status VARCHAR(50), -- 'healthy', 'unhealthy', 'unknown' enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT true, organization_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, group_id UUID REFERENCES mcp_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, created_by VARCHAR(255), created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE(organization_id, name) ); ``` ### Organization Scoping All MCP servers are scoped to an organization. Queries automatically filter by `organizationId` to ensure multi-tenant isolation. Servers with `NULL` organization ID are accessible to all organizations (used for system-wide templates). # MCP Discovery System
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.controller.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.controller.ts) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts](backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts](backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts) - [frontend/src/components/mcp/McpDiscoveryPreview.tsx](frontend/src/components/mcp/McpDiscoveryPreview.tsx) - [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx](frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx) - [frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts](frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts) - [frontend/src/services/mcpGroupsApi.ts](frontend/src/services/mcpGroupsApi.ts)
The MCP Discovery System provides pre-save validation and tool discovery for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. It allows users to test server configurations and preview available tools before committing them to the database. The system uses Temporal workflows to handle asynchronous discovery operations, supports both HTTP and STDIO transports, and implements intelligent caching to avoid redundant discovery calls. For information about MCP server configuration and management, see [MCP Server Management](#4.3). For details on how discovered tools are used during workflow execution, see [Tool Execution Patterns](#4.5). ## Overview The discovery system consists of three layers: 1. **Temporal Workflows**: `mcpDiscoveryWorkflow` and `mcpGroupDiscoveryWorkflow` orchestrate discovery operations 2. **Backend API**: REST endpoints for starting discovery and polling status 3. **Frontend UI**: Pre-save preview interface in the MCP Library page Discovery is **non-blocking** and **async** - workflows run in the background while the frontend polls for status updates. Results are cached in Redis with a `cacheToken` that can be referenced when creating the server to avoid re-discovering tools. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:1-319](), [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:703-771](), [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts:1-172]() ## Discovery Workflows ### Single Server Discovery ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as "McpLibraryPage" participant API as "/api/v1/mcp/discover" participant Temporal as "Temporal Server" participant WF as "mcpDiscoveryWorkflow" participant Act as "discoverMcpToolsActivity" participant Docker as "Docker Container
(stdio only)" participant Redis as "Redis Cache" UI->>API: POST /discover
{transport, name, endpoint/command, cacheToken} API->>Temporal: startWorkflow(mcpDiscoveryWorkflow) Temporal->>WF: Execute workflow API-->>UI: {workflowId, status: 'started'} WF->>WF: Validate input
(http needs endpoint, stdio needs command) WF->>Act: discoverMcpToolsActivity alt STDIO transport Act->>Docker: Spawn container with stdio-proxy Docker-->>Act: MCP tools list else HTTP transport Act->>Act: Direct MCP protocol call Act-->>Act: MCP tools list end Act-->>WF: {tools: McpTool[]} opt cacheToken provided WF->>Redis: cacheDiscoveryResultActivity
SET mcp-discovery:{cacheToken} end WF-->>Temporal: {status: 'completed', tools, toolCount} loop Poll every 2 seconds UI->>API: GET /discover/{workflowId} API->>Temporal: Query 'getDiscoveryResult' Temporal-->>API: {status, tools, toolCount} API-->>UI: DiscoveryStatus end UI->>UI: Display preview with tool count ``` **Discovery Flow** Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:134-222](), [frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts:57-99]() The `mcpDiscoveryWorkflow` accepts `DiscoveryInput` containing: - `transport`: `'http'` or `'stdio'` - `name`: Server name for identification - `endpoint` (HTTP only): Server URL - `command` and `args` (STDIO only): Command to execute - `headers`: Optional authentication headers - `image`: Optional Docker image override (STDIO only) - `cacheToken`: Optional UUID for caching results Workflow steps: 1. **Input validation** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:146-168]() - Ensures HTTP has endpoint, STDIO has command 2. **Activity execution** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:172-179]() - Calls `discoverMcpToolsActivity` 3. **Cache storage** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:182-193]() - If `cacheToken` provided, stores results in Redis 4. **Result return** [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:196-200]() - Returns `{workflowId, status, tools, toolCount}` The workflow provides a **query handler** `getDiscoveryResult` [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:144]() that allows polling without blocking the workflow. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:134-222](), [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts:7-43]() ### Group Discovery ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend: Group Template Import" Template["McpGroupTemplateResponse
{slug, servers[], defaultDockerImage}"] UI["handleGroupTestAndDiscover()"] end subgraph "Backend: /api/v1/mcp/discover-group" Controller["POST /discover-group
GroupDiscoveryInputDto"] Service["Start mcpGroupDiscoveryWorkflow"] end subgraph "Temporal Workflow" GroupWF["mcpGroupDiscoveryWorkflow"] GroupAct["discoverMcpGroupToolsActivity"] CacheAct["cacheDiscoveryResultActivity
(per server)"] end subgraph "Worker Activity" Container["Single Docker Container
(stdio-proxy)"] Server1["Server 1 discovery"] Server2["Server 2 discovery"] ServerN["Server N discovery"] end subgraph "Redis Cache" Cache1["mcp-discovery:{token1}"] Cache2["mcp-discovery:{token2}"] CacheN["mcp-discovery:{tokenN}"] end Template-->UI UI-->Controller Controller-->Service Service-->GroupWF GroupWF-->GroupAct GroupAct-->Container Container-->Server1 Container-->Server2 Container-->ServerN Server1-->GroupWF Server2-->GroupWF ServerN-->GroupWF GroupWF-->CacheAct CacheAct-->Cache1 CacheAct-->Cache2 CacheAct-->CacheN UI-.Poll status.->Controller Controller-.Query workflow.->GroupWF style GroupWF fill:#f9f9f9 style Container fill:#f0f0f0 ``` **Group Discovery Optimization** Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:230-318](), [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:979-1112]() `mcpGroupDiscoveryWorkflow` discovers tools from **multiple servers** in a single workflow execution. This is critical for MCP groups (e.g., AWS MCPs) that contain many servers sharing the same Docker image. **Key optimization**: A single `stdio-proxy` container is spawned and reused for all servers in the group [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:260-263](). This avoids the overhead of spawning N containers for N servers. Input structure [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts:93-127](): ```typescript { image: "docker-image-for-group", servers: [ {name: "server1", transport: "stdio", command: "...", args: [...]}, {name: "server2", transport: "stdio", command: "...", args: [...]} ] } ``` Output structure includes per-server results [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:265-275](): ```typescript { workflowId: "uuid", status: "completed", results: [ {name: "server1", status: "completed", tools: [...], toolCount: 5, cacheToken: "uuid1"}, {name: "server2", status: "failed", error: "Connection timeout"} ] } ``` Each successfully discovered server gets its own `cacheToken` [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:277-292]() which is stored separately in Redis. When importing the group, these tokens are passed to create each server with cached results [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:1113-1150](). Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:230-318](), [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp-discovery.dto.ts:92-161](), [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:979-1112]() ## Transport-Specific Discovery ### HTTP Transport Discovery For HTTP servers, discovery is **fast and direct** - no Docker containers are required. ```mermaid graph LR Activity["discoverMcpToolsActivity"] Endpoint["HTTP Endpoint
e.g., https://mcp.example.com"] Initialize["POST /initialize
{protocolVersion, capabilities}"] ToolsList["POST /tools/list
{}"] Result["McpTool[]"] Activity-->Endpoint Endpoint-->Initialize Initialize-->ToolsList ToolsList-->Result Result-->Activity style Activity fill:#f9f9f9 style Endpoint fill:#f0f0f0 ``` **HTTP Discovery Flow** The activity makes two MCP protocol calls [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:577-630](): 1. **Initialize**: `POST {jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "initialize", params: {...}}` 2. **List tools**: `POST {jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "tools/list"}` Headers from `DiscoveryInput.headers` are included in both requests. This allows testing authentication before saving credentials. **Timeout**: 10 seconds per request [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:595]() Sources: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:560-650]() ### STDIO Transport Discovery STDIO servers require spawning a Docker container with the `stdio-proxy` image. This process is **slower** (5-15 seconds) but necessary to test local/binary-based MCP servers. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Act as "discoverMcpToolsActivity" participant Docker as "Docker API" participant Container as "stdio-proxy Container" participant MCP as "MCP Server Process" Act->>Docker: docker run -d
--rm --network host
{image} {command} {args} Docker->>Container: Start container Container->>MCP: Spawn process (command + args) Act->>Container: Wait for container ready Container-->>Act: Container running Act->>Container: HTTP GET /health Container-->>Act: 200 OK Act->>Container: POST /initialize Container->>MCP: JSON-RPC initialize MCP-->>Container: Server info Container-->>Act: Server info Act->>Container: POST /tools/list Container->>MCP: JSON-RPC tools/list MCP-->>Container: tools[] Container-->>Act: tools[] Act->>Docker: docker stop {containerId} Docker->>Container: Stop signal Container->>Container: Cleanup Act-->>Act: Return McpTool[] ``` **STDIO Discovery Process** Sources: Activity implementation spawns container, makes MCP calls through stdio-proxy, then cleans up container The activity [referenced in worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:109-124](): 1. Spawns Docker container with specified `image` (defaults to group's `defaultDockerImage`) 2. Executes `command` with `args` inside container 3. Waits for stdio-proxy to be ready (HTTP health check) 4. Makes MCP protocol calls through stdio-proxy HTTP interface 5. Collects tools 6. Stops and removes container **Why stdio-proxy?** Direct STDIO communication is complex - the proxy converts MCP's stdio protocol to HTTP, making it easier to test from any environment. **Container cleanup**: Containers are always cleaned up, even on failure, using `--rm` flag and explicit `docker stop` in finally blocks. {status, tools, toolCount, error}"] Handler["Query Handler: 'getDiscoveryResult'"] end subgraph "Backend API" Endpoint["GET /discover/:workflowId"] Query["temporal.query(workflowId, 'getDiscoveryResult')"] Response["DiscoveryStatusDto"] end subgraph "Frontend Polling" Poll["setInterval(2000)"] Call["mcpDiscoveryApi.getStatus(workflowId)"] Update["Update discoveryStatus state"] end WF-->State State-->Handler Handler-->WF Poll-->Call Call-->Endpoint Endpoint-->Query Query-->Handler Handler-->Query Query-->Response Response-->Call Call-->Update Update-->Poll style WF fill:#f9f9f9 style Handler fill:#f0f0f0 ``` **Query vs Result Pattern** Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:134-222]() Temporal workflows provide two ways to get results: 1. **Await workflow completion**: `await temporal.getResult(workflowId)` - blocks until done 2. **Query workflow state**: `temporal.query(workflowId, 'queryName')` - non-blocking, instant The discovery system uses **queries** for polling [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:144](): ```typescript setHandler(defineQuery('getDiscoveryResult'), () => discoveryResult); ``` This handler returns the current `discoveryResult` variable which is updated as the workflow progresses: - Initially: `{status: 'running'}` - On success: `{status: 'completed', tools, toolCount}` - On failure: `{status: 'failed', error, errorCode}` **Benefits**: - No blocking on backend - Immediate response with current state - Frontend controls polling frequency - Can check status from multiple clients Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflows/mcp-discovery-workflow.ts:134-222](), [frontend/src/services/mcpDiscoveryApi.ts:85-99]() ### Polling Implementation **Frontend polling** [frontend/src/pages/McpLibraryPage.tsx:736-761](): ```typescript const pollInterval = setInterval(async () => { try { const result = await mcpDiscoveryApi.getStatus(workflowId); # Tool Execution Patterns
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-gateway.spec.ts](backend/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-gateway.spec.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-internal.integration.spec.ts](backend/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-internal.integration.spec.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts](backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp.dto.ts](backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp.dto.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts](backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts](backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts](backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts) - [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts](backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts) - [worker/src/components/ai/__tests__/ai-agent.test.ts](worker/src/components/ai/__tests__/ai-agent.test.ts) - [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts](worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts)
## Purpose and Scope This document describes the two distinct execution patterns used when AI agents invoke tools during workflow execution. Tools are either **component-based** (internal ShipSec components executed within Temporal workflows) or **external** (MCP servers accessed via HTTP/STDIO protocols). This page covers the signal-and-poll pattern for component tools, the proxy pattern for external tools, tool naming conventions, and error handling strategies. For information about how tools are registered in the registry, see [Tool Registry](#4.3). For details on AI agent configuration and tool discovery, see [AI Agent Component](#4.1). For MCP server lifecycle management, see [MCP Server Management](#4.4). --- ## Tool Type Architecture ShipSec Studio supports two categories of tools that AI agents can invoke: | Tool Type | Registration Method | Execution Pattern | Examples | |-----------|-------------------|-------------------|----------| | **Component Tools** | `registerComponentTool` | Signal-and-Poll via Temporal | Security scanners, data processors, API clients | | **External Tools** | `registerMcpServer` | HTTP/STDIO Proxy via MCP Client Pool | AWS MCP servers, database query tools, third-party APIs | ### Component Tools Component tools are regular ShipSec workflow components that have been configured with `toolProvider` metadata. They execute within the same Temporal workflow as the AI agent, allowing synchronous communication via Temporal signals and queries. Component tools benefit from full workflow context, credential resolution, and trace integration. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:113-155](), [backend/src/mcp/dto/mcp.dto.ts:43-60]() ### External Tools External tools are standalone MCP servers that expose tools via the Model Context Protocol. They can be: - **STDIO servers**: Containerized MCP servers with stdio transport (type `mcp-server`) - **HTTP servers**: Remote MCP endpoints accessed via HTTP (type `remote-mcp`) - **MCP group children**: Tools from MCP groups with hierarchical node IDs External tools are accessed through a persistent client pool to avoid re-initialization overhead. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:164-223](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:41-42]() --- ## Component Tool Execution: Signal-and-Poll Pattern ### Component Tool Execution Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as "AI Agent
(ai-agent.ts)" participant Gateway as "MCP Gateway
(McpGatewayService)" participant Temporal as "Temporal Workflow
(shipsecWorkflowRun)" participant Registry as "Tool Registry
(Redis)" participant Worker as "Temporal Worker
(runComponentActivity)" Agent->>Gateway: Call tool "check_ip_reputation" Gateway->>Registry: Get tool metadata + credentials Registry-->>Gateway: Tool config, encrypted credentials Gateway->>Gateway: Generate callId = runId:nodeId:timestamp Gateway->>Temporal: Signal "executeToolCall"
{callId, nodeId, componentId, arguments} Note over Temporal: Enqueue tool call request Temporal->>Worker: Execute runComponentActivity Worker->>Worker: Decrypt credentials
Resolve inputs
Execute component Worker-->>Temporal: Return output Temporal->>Temporal: Store result in map[callId] loop Poll for result (max 60s) Gateway->>Temporal: Query "getToolCallResult"(callId) alt Result ready Temporal-->>Gateway: {success: true, output: data} else Not ready yet Temporal-->>Gateway: null Gateway->>Gateway: Wait 500ms end end Gateway->>Temporal: Signal "toolCallCompleted"
{nodeRef, toolName, output, status} Gateway-->>Agent: Return tool result ``` **Diagram: Component tool execution using Temporal signal-and-poll pattern** ### Signal Phase When a component tool is invoked, the MCP Gateway signals the running Temporal workflow with an `executeToolCall` signal. This signal includes: - **`callId`**: Unique identifier for this invocation (`runId:nodeId:timestamp`) - **`nodeId`**: The workflow node representing this tool - **`componentId`**: The component definition ID (e.g., `security.abuseipdb`) - **`arguments`**: Tool inputs from the agent - **`parameters`**: Parameter overrides - **`credentials`**: Decrypted credentials from the registry The workflow enqueues the tool call and schedules a `runComponentActivity` to execute it asynchronously. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:585-641]() ### Poll Phase After signaling, the gateway enters a polling loop that queries the workflow for the result: ```typescript // Simplified polling logic from mcp-gateway.service.ts:646-674 while (Date.now() - startTime < timeoutMs) { const result = await this.temporalService.queryWorkflow({ workflowId: runId, queryType: 'getToolCallResult', args: [callId], }); if (result) { return result; // {success: boolean, output?: unknown, error?: string} } await sleep(pollIntervalMs); // Default: 500ms } ``` The workflow maintains a map of `callId → result` and responds to the query once the component execution completes. Default timeout is 60 seconds with 500ms poll intervals. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:643-674]() ### Completion Notification After retrieving the result, the gateway signals the workflow again with `toolCallCompleted` to update trace events and node status. This signal includes the tool name, output, and status (`completed` or `failed`). **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:242-251](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:269-280]() --- ## External Tool Execution: Proxy Pattern ### External Tool Execution Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as "AI Agent" participant Gateway as "MCP Gateway" participant ClientPool as "External Client Pool
(Map)" participant Registry as "Tool Registry" participant MCP as "MCP Server
(HTTP/STDIO)" Agent->>Gateway: Call tool "aws-cloudtrail__lookup_events" Gateway->>Gateway: Parse prefix: "aws-cloudtrail" Gateway->>Registry: Get server endpoint + credentials Registry-->>Gateway: endpoint, encryptedCredentials Gateway->>ClientPool: getOrCreateExternalClient(endpoint) alt Client exists in pool ClientPool-->>Gateway: Return cached client else New client needed ClientPool->>MCP: Connect via StreamableHTTPClientTransport MCP-->>ClientPool: Connection established ClientPool->>ClientPool: Cache client ClientPool-->>Gateway: Return new client end loop Retry up to 3 times Gateway->>MCP: client.callTool({name: "lookup_events", arguments}) alt Success MCP-->>Gateway: Tool result Gateway-->>Agent: Return result else Timeout/Error Gateway->>ClientPool: Evict broken client Gateway->>Gateway: Wait (1s * attempt) end end ``` **Diagram: External tool execution using persistent MCP client pool** ### Persistent Client Pool The MCP Gateway maintains a persistent client pool to avoid re-initializing MCP connections for every tool call. The stdio-proxy transport is stateful and rejects subsequent `initialize` requests, so reusing connections is essential for performance. ```typescript // From mcp-gateway.service.ts:41-42, 475-499 private readonly externalClients = new Map(); async getOrCreateExternalClient(endpoint: string): Promise { const existing = this.externalClients.get(endpoint); if (existing) return existing; const transport = new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL(endpoint)); const client = new Client({ name: 'shipsec-gateway-client', version: '1.0.0' }); await client.connect(transport); this.externalClients.set(endpoint, client); return client; } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:41-42](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:471-499]() ### Direct Tool Invocation Once a client is available, the gateway proxies the tool call directly to the MCP server: ```typescript // From mcp-gateway.service.ts:534-580 async proxyCallToExternal(source: RegisteredTool, toolName: string, args: any) { const client = await this.getOrCreateExternalClient(source.endpoint); const result = await Promise.race([ client.callTool({ name: toolName, arguments: args }), new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Timeout')), 30000) ), ]); return result; } ``` The call includes a 30-second timeout. External tools do not go through Temporal's activity system—they execute entirely outside the workflow. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:530-580]() ### Retry and Recovery If an external tool call fails, the gateway: 1. Logs the error 2. Evicts the broken client from the pool 3. Retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 3s) 4. Throws the last error if all attempts fail **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:546-579]() --- ## Tool Naming and Discovery ### Tool Naming Convention Tools are exposed to AI agents with specific naming patterns: | Tool Type | Naming Pattern | Example | |-----------|---------------|---------| | Component Tool | `{toolName}` | `check_ip_reputation` | | External Tool | `{serverName}__{toolName}` | `aws-cloudtrail__lookup_events` | The double-underscore prefix disambiguates tools from different MCP servers and prevents name collisions. The prefix is the `serverName` from the tool registry (typically the MCP server node ID). **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:396-414]() ### Tool Filtering by Node IDs AI agents specify `allowedNodeIds` when connecting to the MCP gateway. This scopes tool discovery to only nodes connected to the agent's `tools` input port. ```mermaid graph TD Agent["AI Agent Node
(tools input port)"] Group["MCP Group: aws-mcp-group
(not exposed to agent)"] Server1["MCP Server: aws-mcp-group/cloudtrail
(nodeId hierarchy)"] Server2["MCP Server: aws-mcp-group/cloudwatch"] Other["Unrelated MCP Server"] Agent -->|"allowedNodeIds: ['aws-mcp-group']"| Group Group -.->|"hierarchical match"| Server1 Group -.->|"hierarchical match"| Server2 Other -.->|"excluded"| X["❌ Not discoverable"] Server1 -->|"tools exposed"| T1["aws-cloudtrail__lookup_events
aws-cloudtrail__get_trail_status"] Server2 -->|"tools exposed"| T2["aws-cloudwatch__get_metrics
aws-cloudwatch__put_metric_data"] ``` **Diagram: Hierarchical tool filtering using allowedNodeIds** The filtering supports hierarchical node IDs with `/` separators. If `allowedNodeIds` includes `aws-mcp-group`, tools from `aws-mcp-group/cloudtrail` and `aws-mcp-group/cloudwatch` are included. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:310-341](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:248-270]() ### Tool Exposure Control Some tool-mode nodes (e.g., MCP group providers) have `exposedToAgent: false` and are not callable by agents. They exist solely for dependency wiring and readiness synchronization. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:45-49](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:205-209]() --- ## Error Handling Patterns ### Component Tool Error Handling ```mermaid graph TD Call["Tool Call Initiated"] Signal["Signal executeToolCall"] Execute["runComponentActivity"] Call --> Signal Signal --> Execute Execute -->|"success"| Success["Store result in workflow map"] Execute -->|"exception"| Error["Catch exception"] Success --> SignalComplete["Signal toolCallCompleted
{status: 'completed', output}"] Error --> SignalFail["Signal toolCallCompleted
{status: 'failed', errorMessage}"] SignalComplete --> TraceOK["Trace event: NODE_PROGRESS
level: info"] SignalFail --> TraceErr["Trace event: NODE_PROGRESS
level: error"] TraceOK --> Return["Return success to agent"] TraceErr --> ReturnErr["Return error to agent"] ``` **Diagram: Component tool error handling flow** Component tool errors are: 1. Caught during activity execution 2. Stored in the workflow result map with `success: false` 3. Signaled back via `toolCallCompleted` with status `failed` 4. Logged to the trace repository with error details 5. Returned to the agent as an error response **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:261-291]() ### External Tool Error Handling External tool errors trigger the retry logic: ```typescript // From mcp-gateway.service.ts:546-579 const MAX_RETRIES = 3; for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_RETRIES; attempt++) { try { const result = await client.callTool({name, arguments}); return result; } catch (error) { this.logger.warn(`External tool call attempt ${attempt} failed: ${error}`); this.externalClients.delete(source.endpoint); // Evict broken client if (attempt < MAX_RETRIES) { await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000 * attempt)); } } } throw lastError; ``` Failed external tools: - Log warnings for each retry attempt - Evict broken clients from the pool - Use exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 3s) - Throw the final error to the agent after 3 attempts **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:546-579]() ### Trace Event Logging All tool calls (both component and external) emit trace events at key stages: | Stage | Event Type | Level | Details | |-------|-----------|-------|---------| | Started | `NODE_PROGRESS` | `info` | Tool name, start time, nodeRef | | Completed | `NODE_PROGRESS` | `info` | Duration, output summary | | Failed | `NODE_PROGRESS` | `error` | Error message, duration | **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:140-172](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:222-241](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:264-267](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:422-440]() --- ## Execution Context and Credentials ### Component Tool Context Component tools receive a fully-resolved execution context with: - **Decrypted credentials**: Retrieved from the tool registry and decrypted before execution - **Parameter overrides**: Agent-provided parameter values merged with node defaults - **Input arguments**: Tool inputs from the agent's tool call - **Workflow services**: Access to storage, secrets, tracing, and logging via service adapters ```typescript // From mcp-gateway.service.ts:585-641 const credentials = await this.toolRegistry.getToolCredentials(runId, tool.nodeId); const inputArgs: Record = {}; const paramOverrides: Record = {}; for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(args ?? {})) { if (exposedParamSet.has(key) && !actionInputIds.has(key)) { paramOverrides[key] = value; // Agent overriding a parameter } else { inputArgs[key] = value; // Regular input } } const mergedParams = { ...tool.parameters, ...paramOverrides }; await this.temporalService.signalWorkflow({ workflowId: runId, signalName: 'executeToolCall', args: { callId, componentId: tool.componentId, arguments: inputArgs, parameters: mergedParams, credentials: credentials ?? undefined, }, }); ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:582-641]() ### External Tool Context External tools receive: - **Raw arguments**: Passed directly to the MCP server - **Encrypted headers**: HTTP headers (for authentication) are stored encrypted in the registry and passed when connecting External tools do not have access to workflow context or ShipSec service adapters. They are isolated processes that communicate solely via MCP protocol. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:183-187](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:530-544]() --- ## Summary Tool execution in ShipSec Studio follows two distinct patterns optimized for their respective use cases: - **Component tools** use the signal-and-poll pattern for tight integration with Temporal workflows, providing full context, credentials, and trace integration - **External tools** use a proxy pattern with a persistent client pool for efficient access to standalone MCP servers Both patterns support robust error handling, trace logging, and credential management, ensuring reliable tool execution regardless of the underlying implementation. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:1-697](), [worker/src/components/ai/ai-agent.ts:467-500](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:1-401]()

Execution Monitoring provides real-time visibility into workflow execution, allowing users to track progress, inspect events, view logs, and replay historical runs. The system supports both **live mode** (streaming from active runs) and **replay mode** (playback of completed runs), with seamless transitions between them. For detailed information about specific subsystems: - Timeline visualization and playback controls: see [Execution Timeline](#5.1) - Event streaming architecture: see [Event Processing Pipeline](#5.2) - Trace event types and log aggregation: see [Trace Events and Logs](#5.3) - Terminal streaming: see [Terminal Output](#5.4) - Input/output inspection: see [Node I/O Inspection](#5.5) ## Architecture Overview The execution monitoring system uses an event-driven architecture where the Temporal worker emits telemetry to Kafka, the backend multiplexes streams via Server-Sent Events (SSE), and the frontend maintains dual state stores for raw data and visual presentation. ### Data Flow Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Worker Process" WF["Temporal Workflow

Responsibility | |-------|------|----------------| | `useExecutionStore` | [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts]() | Raw telemetry aggregation: events, logs, terminal chunks, streaming connection management | | `useExecutionTimelineStore` | [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts]() | Visual presentation: timeline events, playback state, node visual states, viewport management | ### useExecutionStore Manages real-time data ingestion and SSE connection lifecycle: ```typescript interface ExecutionStoreState { runId: string | null; status: ExecutionLifecycle; runStatus: ExecutionStatusResponse | null; events: ExecutionLog[]; // Trace events liveLogs: ExecutionLog[]; // SSE log stream historicalLogs: ExecutionLog[]; // Fetched logs logMode: 'live' | 'scrubbing' | establishes SSE connection, registers event listeners - **Event deduplication**: `mergeById()` ensures no duplicate events by ID - **Node state derivation**: `deriveNodeStates()` converts events to node status badges - **Terminal buffering**: Maintains per-node-per-stream circular buffers (max 500 chunks) - **Log mode switching**: Toggles between live SSE logs, historical API-fetched logs, and scrubbing logs **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:14-68](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:119-158]() ### useExecutionTimelineStore Transforms raw events into number; // Presentation duration (ms) eventDuration: number; // Authoritative event duration currentTime: number; // Playhead position (ms) playbackMode: 'live' | 'replay'; nodeStates: Record; timelineStartTime: number | null; clockOffset: number | null; // Server-client time sync } ``` Key responsibilities: - **Event normalization**: `prepareTimelineEvents()` converts timestamps to **Live clock**: `tickLiveClock()` advances presentation time using RAF loop and clock offset - **Viewport tracking**: Manages timeline zoom and scroll position **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:66-99](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:145-209](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:260-474]() ## Event Processing Pipeline ### SSE Event Types The backend multiplexes five event types over a single SSE connection: | Event Type | Data Structure | Store Handler | |------------|----------------|---------------| | `trace` | `{ events: ExecutionLog[], cursor?: string }` | `useExecutionStore` merges into `events` array | | `logs` | `{ logs: LogEntry[], cursor?: string }` | `useExecutionStore` merges into `liveLogs` array | | `terminal` | `{ chunks: TerminalStreamChunk[], cursor?: string }` | `useExecutionStore` appends to `terminalStreams` | | `dataflow` | `{ packets: DataPacket[] }` | `useExecutionTimelineStore.appendDataFlows()` | | `status` | `ExecutionStatusResponse` | `useExecutionStore` updates `runStatus` | ### Connection Lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as ExecutionInspector participant ES as useExecutionStore participant API as api.executions participant Backend as SSE Endpoint participant Kafka UI->>ES: monitorRun(runId) ES->>ES: stopPolling() if existing ES->>ES: pollOnce() initial fetch ES->>API: stream(runId, cursors) API->>Backend: GET /runs/:id/stream Backend->>Kafka: Subscribe to topics Backend-->>API: EventSource connection loop Streaming Kafka->>Backend: New events Backend->>API: SSE event API->>ES: Event listener fires ES->>ES: Update state (merge/append) ES->>UI: State change triggers re-render end alt Terminal Status Detected Backend->>API: event: complete API->>ES: stopPolling() ES->>ES: disconnectStream() end ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:277-304](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:388-651]() ### Event Deduplication All event streams use ID-based deduplication to handle network retries and cursor-based resumption: ```typescript const mergeById = (existing: ExecutionLog[], incoming: ExecutionLog[]): ExecutionLog[] => { if (incoming.length === 0) return existing; const seen = new Set(existing.map((event) => event.id)); const deduped = incoming.filter((event) => { if (seen.has(event.id)) return false; seen.add(event.id); return true; }); if (deduped.length === 0) return existing; return [...existing, ...deduped]; }; ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:119-129]() ## Live Mode vs Replay Mode ### Mode Characteristics | Aspect | Live Mode | Replay Mode | |--------|-----------|-------------| | **Data Source** | SSE stream + polling | Historical API fetch | | **Playback Controls** | Disabled (follows latest) | Enabled (play/pause/seek) | | **Timeline Progression** | `tickLiveClock()` via RAF | `requestAnimationFrame` step loop | | **Auto-scroll** | Events/logs scroll to bottom | Follows playhead when playing | | **Duration** | `totalDuration` grows with clock | Fixed `eventDuration` | ### Live Mode Operation Live mode uses a clock synchronization mechanism to provide smooth timeline progression: ```typescript tickLiveClock: () => { const state = get(); if (state.playbackMode !== 'live' || !state.timelineStartTime) return; const now = Date.now(); let serverNow: number; if (state.clockOffset !== null) { // Use cached offset: serverTime = clientTime + offset serverNow = now + state.clockOffset; } else if (state.events.length > 0) { // Fallback to last event timestamp const lastEvent = state.events[state.events.length - 1]; serverNow = new Date(lastEvent.timestamp).getTime(); } else { serverNow = now; } const elapsed = Math.max(0, serverNow - state.timelineStartTime); const projectedDuration = Math.max(elapsed, state.eventDuration); set({ totalDuration: projectedDuration, currentTime: state.isLiveFollowing ? projectedDuration : state.currentTime, }); } ``` **Clock offset** is calculated once when the first live event arrives: ```typescript if (clockOffset === null) { const eventServerTime = new Date(event.timestamp).getTime(); const clientTime = Date.now(); clockOffset = eventServerTime - clientTime; } ``` This allows smooth clock advancement even between discrete events, preventing jitter in the timeline UI. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:756-796](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:822-830]() ### Mode Switching The system automatically switches from live to replay mode when a workflow completes: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Live: Run starts Live --> Live: SSE events streaming Live --> Replay: Terminal status detected Replay --> [*]: User closes inspector note right of Live isLiveFollowing = true playbackMode = 'live' Auto-scroll enabled end note note right of Replay isLiveFollowing = false playbackMode = 'replay' Playback controls enabled end note ``` Transition logic in `executionTimelineStore`: ```typescript // Detect terminal status const isTerminalStatus = runStatus && TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(runStatus.status); const statusJustChanged = prevRunStatus && !TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(prevRunStatus.status) && TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(runStatus.status); if (timelineStore.playbackMode === 'live' && statusJustChanged) { // Switch to replay mode useExecutionTimelineStore.setState({ playbackMode: 'replay', isLiveFollowing: false, isPlaying: false, }); // Reload timeline to get all final events await useExecutionTimelineStore.getState().loadTimeline(runId); // Position at end for review useExecutionTimelineStore.setState({ currentTime: finalState.totalDuration, }); } ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:918-999]() ## UI Component Hierarchy ### output: DataPacket[]; }; attempts: number; // Retry tracking retryCount: number; humanInputRequestId?: string; // For awaiting input nodes } ``` The canvas `WorkflowNode` component subscribes to this state and renders status badges, progress indicators, and error icons accordingly. **Status derivation logic:** ```typescript switch (lastEvent.type) { case 'STARTED': case 'PROGRESS': status = 'running'; break; case 'COMPLETED': status = 'success'; break; case 'FAILED': status = 'error'; break; case 'AWAITING_INPUT': status = 'awaiting_input'; break; case 'SKIPPED': status = 'skipped'; break; } ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:16-33](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:366-393]() ### Run History and Persistence `useRunStore` maintains a per-workflow cache of run metadata: ```typescript interface ExecutionRun { id: string; workflowId: string; workflowName: string; workflowVersion: number | null; status: ExecutionStatus; startTime: string; endTime?: string; duration?: number; eventCount: number; nodeCount: number; triggerType: 'manual' | 'schedule'; triggerLabel?: string; isLive: boolean; } ``` The store exposes: - `fetchRuns({ workflowId })`: Load runs for a workflow - `refreshRuns(workflowId)`: Force refresh (called after run completion) - `upsertRun(run)`: Update run metadata (called when terminal status detected) **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/runStore.ts]() (referenced in ExecutionInspector) ## Performance Considerations ### Event Throttling The timeline uses `requestAnimationFrame` for all clock updates to prevent excessive re-renders: ```typescript // Live mode clock update (max 5 FPS to reduce CPU) useEffect(() => { if (!isLiveMode) return; let frame: number; const pump = () => { tickLiveClock(); frame = requestAnimationFrame(pump); }; frame = requestAnimationFrame(pump); return () => cancelAnimationFrame(frame); }, [isLiveMode, tickLiveClock]); ``` Additionally, `tickLiveClock` includes a timestamp gate to limit updates to ~200ms intervals: ```typescript const now = Date.now(); if (liveTickTimestamp && now - liveTickTimestamp < 200) { return; // Skip update } liveTickTimestamp = now; ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:111-121](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:762-765]() ### Terminal Chunk Buffering Terminal streams maintain circular buffers to prevent memory growth: ```typescript const MAX_TERMINAL_CHUNKS = 500; // When appending chunks const merged = [...existing.chunks, chunk]; const trimmed = merged.length > MAX_TERMINAL_CHUNKS ? merged.slice(-MAX_TERMINAL_CHUNKS) : merged; ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:87](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:527-530]() ### Memoized Computations Event filtering and marker positioning use React `useMemo` to avoid recalculation on every render: ```typescript const filteredEvents = useMemo(() => { if (!selectedNodeId) return []; return events.filter((event) => event.nodeId === selectedNodeId); }, [events, selectedNodeId]); const markerData = useMemo(() => { return events.map((event) => { const normalized = event.offsetMs / safeDuration; const viewportPosition = viewportWidth >= 1 ? normalized : (normalized - clampedStart) / viewportWidth; return { id: event.id, type: event.type, viewportPosition, normalizedPosition: normalized, visible: viewportPosition >= 0 && viewportPosition <= 1, }; }); }, [events, safeDuration, clampedStart, viewportWidth]); ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/EventInspector.tsx:151-158](), [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:219-234]()

## Purpose and Scope The `ExecutionTimeline` component renders a horizontal timeline bar with interactive playback controls for workflow execution monitoring. It visualizes execution progress through event markers, a draggable scrubber, and a filled progress indicator. The component provides standard media player controls (play, pause, speed adjustment, step forward/back) and supports interactive scrubbing via click, drag, and mouse wheel zoom. This page focuses on the UI component itself. For state management and event processing, see page 5.3. For live mode vs replay mode behavior, see page 5.2. Convert to milliseconds return normalized * safeDuration }, [clampedStart, viewportWidth, safeDuration]) ``` Where: - `clampedStart`: Normalized position of viewport left edge (0-1) - `viewportWidth`: Fraction of timeline visible (1 / zoom) - `safeDuration`: Total timeline duration in milliseconds **Sources:** - [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:134-143]() ### Seek Effects When seeking, the store updates state and triggers recalculation: ```typescript seek: (timeMs: number) => { const clampedTime = Math.max(0, Math.min(timeMs, totalDuration)) set((prev) => ({ currentTime: clampedTime, isSeeking: true, // Disable auto-follow if in live mode isLiveFollowing: prev.playbackMode === 'live' ? false : prev.isLiveFollowing, })) // Recalculate node states for new position const { events, dataFlows, timelineStartTime } = get() const newStates = calculateNodeStates(events, dataFlows, clampedTime, timelineStartTime) set({ nodeStates: newStates }) // Clear seeking flag after short delay setTimeout(() => set({ isSeeking: false }), 100) } ``` **Important:** Seeking in live mode disables `isLiveFollowing`, preventing the timeline from jumping back to the end. (updatedHistory[runId] ?? null) : state.selectedNodeId ``` This ensures users don't lose their place when comparing multiple runs. **Sources:** - [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:505-541]() - [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:690-698]() --- ## Zoom and Viewport The timeline supports zoom levels from 1x (full view) to 100x (highly magnified) with intelligent viewport tracking. ### Zoom State Three state variables control zoom and viewport: | Variable | Type | Range | Purpose | |----------|------|-------|---------| | `timelineZoom` | `number` | 1-100 | Zoom factor (1 = fit to width) | | `viewportWidth` | `number` | 0.01-1 | Fraction of timeline visible (1 / zoom) | | `timelineStart` | `number` | 0-1 | Normalized left edge of viewport | **Derived Values:** ```typescript const viewportWidth = 1 / timelineZoom // e.g., zoom=2 → width=0.5 const maxStart = Math.max(0, 1 - viewportWidth) // Prevent scrolling past end const clampedStart = clamp(timelineStart, 0, maxStart) const viewportStartMs = clampedStart * safeDuration const viewportEndMs = Math.min(safeDuration, (clampedStart + viewportWidth) * safeDuration) ``` **Sources:** - [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:90-99]() ### Mouse Wheel Zoom Users can zoom with Ctrl/Cmd + mouse wheel, with the zoom centered at the cursor position: ```mermaid graph TB WheelEvent["Mouse Wheel Event
(with Ctrl/Cmd)"] CalcPivot["Calculate pivot point
at cursor position"] AdjustZoom["Adjust zoom level
(±0.5 per wheel tick)"] RecalcViewport["Recalculate viewport
to keep pivot centered"] Update["Update timelineZoom
and timelineStart"] WheelEvent --> CalcPivot CalcPivot --> AdjustZoom AdjustZoom --> RecalcViewport RecalcViewport --> Update ``` **Implementation:** ```typescript const handleWheel = useCallback((event: React.WheelEvent) => { if (!timelineRef.current) return if (event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) { event.preventDefault() // 1. Calculate pivot point at cursor (0-1 in viewport) const rect = timelineRef.current.getBoundingClientRect() const pivotRatio = clamp((event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width, 0, 1) // 2. Convert to normalized timeline coordinate const pivotPoint = clampedStart + pivotRatio * viewportWidth // 3. Adjust zoom level const delta = event.deltaY > 0 ? -0.5 : 0.5 // Zoom in/out const nextZoom = clamp(timelineZoom + delta, 1, 100) if (nextZoom === timelineZoom) return // Already at limit // 4. Calculate new viewport to keep pivot centered const nextViewportWidth = 1 / nextZoom const nextMaxStart = Math.max(0, 1 - nextViewportWidth) const nextStart = clamp( pivotPoint - nextViewportWidth * pivotRatio, 0, nextMaxStart ) // 5. Update state setTimelineZoom(nextZoom) setTimelineStart(nextStart) } else if (timelineZoom > 1) { // Regular wheel scrolling pans the viewport when zoomed event.preventDefault() const delta = (event.deltaY / 500) * viewportWidth setTimelineStart((prev) => clamp(prev + delta, 0, maxStart)) } }, [timelineZoom, viewportWidth, clampedStart, maxStart, setTimelineZoom]) ``` This provides smooth zooming that feels natural, with the area under the cursor staying in place. **Sources:** - [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:178-201]() ### Viewport Auto-Tracking When playing or seeking, the viewport automatically pans to keep the playhead visible: ```typescript useEffect(() => { // Calculate guard zones (15% of viewport on each side) const guard = viewportWidth >= 1 ? 0 : viewportWidth * 0.15 const lowerBound = clampedStart + guard const upperBound = clampedStart + viewportWidth - guard // Pan viewport if playhead moves outside bounds if (normalizedProgress < lowerBound) { setTimelineStart(clamp(normalizedProgress - guard, 0, maxStart)) } else if (normalizedProgress > upperBound) { setTimelineStart(clamp(normalizedProgress - (viewportWidth - guard), 0, maxStart)) } }, [normalizedProgress, viewportWidth, clampedStart, maxStart]) ``` The 15% guard zones prevent the playhead from getting too close to the edges, providing better context. **Sources:** - [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:123-132]() ### Overview Minimap When zoomed, a minimap appears below the main timeline showing the full timeline with the viewport region highlighted: ```tsx {timelineZoom > 1 && (
