## Purpose and Scope This page documents the real-time update mechanisms that deliver live workflow execution data to the frontend. It covers Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming, polling fallback, playback mode management, clock synchronization, and automatic run detection. For the timeline visualization UI, see [Execution Timeline UI](#5.1). For how raw events are transformed into visual node states, see [Event Processing Pipeline](#5.3). For terminal streaming specifics, see [Terminal Output Streaming](#5.5). --- ## System Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Backend API" SSE["SSE Endpoint
/executions/{runId}/stream"] REST["REST Endpoints
/executions/{runId}/status
/executions/{runId}/trace"] end subgraph "executionStore" Connect["connectStream()"] Poll["pollOnce()"] Monitor["monitorRun()"] EventSource["EventSource instance"] PollingInterval["setInterval timer"] end subgraph "executionTimelineStore" LiveUpdate["updateFromLiveEvent()"] TickClock["tickLiveClock()"] SwitchMode["switchToLiveMode()"] GoLive["goLive()"] PlaybackMode["playbackMode: 'live' | 'replay'"] end subgraph "UI Components" Inspector["ExecutionInspector"] Timeline["ExecutionTimeline"] RunSelector["RunSelector"] EventInspector["EventInspector"] end SSE --> Connect Connect --> EventSource EventSource -->|"trace events"| LiveUpdate EventSource -->|"status updates"| Monitor EventSource -->|"dataflow packets"| LiveUpdate EventSource -->|"terminal chunks"| Monitor EventSource -->|"logs"| Monitor REST --> Poll Poll --> Monitor Monitor --> PollingInterval LiveUpdate --> PlaybackMode TickClock --> PlaybackMode SwitchMode --> PlaybackMode GoLive --> PlaybackMode PlaybackMode --> Inspector PlaybackMode --> Timeline PlaybackMode --> EventInspector RunSelector --> Monitor ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:391-654](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:809-874]() --- ## SSE Streaming Connection ### Connection Establishment The `executionStore` establishes an SSE connection when monitoring a run. The connection is created in `connectStream()` and includes cursor parameters for resumable streaming: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as UI Component participant Store as executionStore participant API as api.executions.stream() participant Backend as SSE Endpoint UI->>Store: monitorRun(runId) Store->>Store: stopPolling() Store->>API: stream(runId, {cursor, terminalCursor, logCursor}) API->>Backend: GET /executions/{runId}/stream Backend-->>Store: EventSource instance Store->>Store: Set up event listeners loop Every SSE message Backend-->>Store: event: trace/status/dataflow/terminal/logs Store->>Store: Parse & update state Store->>UI: State change triggers re-render end ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:391-407]() ### Event Listeners The `EventSource` instance registers listeners for multiple event types: | Event Type | Handler | Purpose | |------------|---------|---------| | `trace` | Merges events via `mergeEvents()` | Execution trace events (STARTED, COMPLETED, etc.) | | `status` | Updates `runStatus` and `status` | Overall workflow status changes | | `dataflow` | Calls `appendDataFlows()` | Data packet transfers between nodes | | `terminal` | Merges chunks into `terminalStreams` | Terminal output from component execution | | `logs` | Merges into `liveLogs` | Structured log entries | | `ready` | Sets `streamingMode` | Connection established, mode determined | | `complete` | Calls `stopPolling()` | Execution finished | **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:409-642]() ### Trace Event Processing ```mermaid graph LR SSE["SSE: 'trace' event"] Parse["JSON.parse(event.data)"] Validate["Filter valid ExecutionLog[]"] Merge["mergeEvents(existing, new)"] Derive["deriveNodeStates()"] Update["set({ events, nodeStates })"] Timeline["executionTimelineStore.updateFromLiveEvent()"] SSE --> Parse Parse --> Validate Validate --> Merge Merge --> Derive Derive --> Update Update --> Timeline ``` The `trace` event listener filters events to ensure they match the `ExecutionLog` type contract before merging: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:409-433](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:118-131]() ### Status Event Processing Status events update the workflow's overall execution state and trigger mode transitions: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:436-456]() When a terminal status (`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `TERMINATED`, `TIMED_OUT`) is received, polling stops automatically. --- ## Polling Fallback Mechanism ### Dual-Mode Strategy The system runs both SSE streaming and periodic polling simultaneously: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Monitoring: monitorRun(runId) state Monitoring { [*] --> ConnectSSE [*] --> StartPolling ConnectSSE --> StreamingReady: 'ready' event ConnectSSE --> PollingMode: Connection failed StreamingReady --> RealtimeMode: mode='realtime' StreamingReady --> PollingModeBackup: mode='polling' RealtimeMode --> BackupPoll: Reduce polling to 5s PollingModeBackup --> ActivePoll: Continue 2s polling StartPolling --> ActivePoll: setInterval(2000ms) state ActivePoll { Wait --> Fetch: Timer fires Fetch --> Wait: Complete Fetch --> Skip: First tick (already loaded) } state BackupPoll { Wait --> Fetch: Timer fires (5s) Fetch --> Wait: Complete } } Monitoring --> Stopped: Terminal status Stopped --> [*] ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:276-309](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:607-638]() ### Poll Cycle Implementation The `pollOnce()` method fetches status and trace data via REST endpoints: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:311-371]() Key behaviors: - **Skip first tick**: When `monitorRun()` is called from `selectRun()`, the timeline has already loaded events via `loadTimeline()`. The first poll tick is skipped to avoid redundant fetching. - **Run ID validation**: Inside the promise settlement, the store checks if `runId` still matches before updating state (prevents race conditions when switching runs). - **Terminal status handling**: Polling automatically stops when the run reaches a terminal status. --- ## Live vs Replay Modes ### Mode Definitions | Mode | Description | Clock Behavior | User Controls | |------|-------------|----------------|---------------| | `live` | Real-time following of active execution | Advances automatically via `tickLiveClock()` | Can scrub away, use "Go Live" to return | | `replay` | Historical playback of completed run | User-controlled via play/pause/seek | Full timeline controls enabled | **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:83]() ### Mode State Management ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Replay: selectRun(runId, 'replay') [*] --> Live: selectRun(runId, 'live') Replay --> Playing: play() Playing --> Paused: pause() Paused --> Playing: play() Playing --> Replay: Playback complete Replay --> Live: switchToLiveMode() Live --> Following: isLiveFollowing=true Following --> Behind: User scrubs timeline Behind --> Following: goLive() Live --> Replay: Terminal status detected state Live { [*] --> TickClock TickClock --> TickClock: requestAnimationFrame } ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:510-551](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:860-874]() ### Live Mode Entry Points **From `selectRun()`:** ```typescript selectRun: async (runId: string, initialMode: 'live' | 'replay' = 'replay') ``` When `initialMode` is `'live'`, the store sets: - `playbackMode: 'live'` - `isLiveFollowing: true` - `currentTime: eventDuration` (start at the end) **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:510-551]() **From `switchToLiveMode()`:** Called by UI when user clicks "Switch to Live" button: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:860-874]() **From `goLive()`:** Called when user clicks "Go Live" after scrubbing away from the live head: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:755-765]() --- ## Live Event Integration ### Event Ingestion Flow ```mermaid graph TB SSE["SSE 'trace' event"] ExecStore["executionStore.events"] Timeline["executionTimelineStore.updateFromLiveEvent()"] SSE --> ExecStore ExecStore -->|"via subscription"| Timeline subgraph "updateFromLiveEvent()" Check["Check if event already exists"] Combine["Combine with existing events"] Prepare["prepareTimelineEvents()"] Calculate["calculateNodeStates()"] ClockOffset["Calculate clockOffset (once)"] end Timeline --> Check Check --> Combine Combine --> Prepare Prepare --> Calculate Calculate --> ClockOffset ClockOffset --> Render["Update UI"] ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:809-858]() ### Clock Offset Calculation The store calculates a clock offset between server time and client time once per run, then uses it to smoothly advance the timeline clock: **Formula:** `clockOffset = serverTime - clientTime` This offset is stored in state and used by `tickLiveClock()` to project server time without constant synchronization. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:833-840]() ### Live Clock Advancement ```mermaid graph LR RAF["requestAnimationFrame"] Tick["tickLiveClock()"] ServerNow["Calculate server time:
clientTime + clockOffset"] Elapsed["elapsed = serverNow - timelineStartTime"] ProjectDuration["projectedDuration = max(elapsed, eventDuration)"] UpdateTime["Update totalDuration and currentTime"] RAF --> Tick Tick --> ServerNow ServerNow --> Elapsed Elapsed --> ProjectDuration ProjectDuration --> UpdateTime UpdateTime --> RAF ``` The `tickLiveClock()` method runs in a `requestAnimationFrame` loop when `playbackMode === 'live'`: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:767-807](), [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionTimeline.tsx:111-121]() **Key behaviors:** - **Rate limiting**: Only ticks if more than 200ms have elapsed since the last tick. - **Clock interpolation**: `totalDuration` can advance slightly ahead of `eventDuration` to represent elapsed wall-clock time. - **Following mode**: When `isLiveFollowing` is true, `currentTime` is set to `projectedDuration`, causing the timeline scrubber to follow the live head. --- ## Automatic Run Detection ### Live Run Auto-Selection The `RunSelector` component automatically selects and monitors live runs when they are detected: ```mermaid graph TB Effect["useEffect hook"] HasSelection{"selectedRunId ||
routeRunId exists?"} HasLiveRun{"currentLiveRunId
exists?"} MatchesWorkflow{"Live run matches
targetWorkflowId?"} OtherLiveRuns{"liveRuns.length > 0?"} Effect --> HasSelection HasSelection -->|Yes| Skip["Skip auto-selection"] HasSelection -->|No| HasLiveRun HasLiveRun -->|Yes| MatchesWorkflow HasLiveRun -->|No| OtherLiveRuns MatchesWorkflow -->|Yes| SelectLive["selectRun(currentLiveRunId, 'live')
monitorRun()
navigateToRun()"] MatchesWorkflow -->|No| OtherLiveRuns OtherLiveRuns -->|Yes| SelectFirst["selectRun(liveRuns[0].id, 'live')
monitorRun()
navigateToRun()"] OtherLiveRuns -->|No| Skip ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/RunSelector.tsx:144-189]() ### Run Polling The `RunSelector` polls the runs list every 10 seconds to detect new live executions: **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/RunSelector.tsx:191-216]() --- ## Mode Transition Logic ### Live to Replay Transition The system automatically transitions from live mode to replay mode when a workflow completes: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant SSE as SSE Stream participant ExecStore as executionStore participant Sub as Store Subscription participant TimelineStore as executionTimelineStore participant QueryCache as TanStack Query Cache SSE->>ExecStore: 'status' event (COMPLETED) ExecStore->>ExecStore: Update runStatus ExecStore->>Sub: State change notification Sub->>Sub: Detect terminal status Sub->>TimelineStore: Check playbackMode === 'live' alt Is live mode and status terminal Sub->>TimelineStore: set({ playbackMode: 'replay' }) Sub->>TimelineStore: loadTimeline(runId) Sub->>QueryCache: Invalidate execution queries Sub->>QueryCache: upsertRunInCache(updated run) end ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:916-1016]() The subscription logic watches for: 1. **Terminal status**: `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `TERMINATED`, `TIMED_OUT` 2. **Terminal lifecycle**: `status === 'completed' || status === 'failed'` 3. **Status transitions**: When `runStatus` changes from non-terminal to terminal Upon detection, it: - Switches `playbackMode` to `'replay'` - Reloads the full timeline via `loadTimeline()` - Updates the cached run in TanStack Query to mark it as non-live - Invalidates execution-scoped queries for a final fresh fetch --- ## Log Mode Synchronization ### Log Modes The `executionStore` maintains three log sources: | Log Mode | Source | When Used | |----------|--------|-----------| | `live` | `liveLogs[]` | Populated by SSE 'logs' events during live execution | | `historical` | `historicalLogs[]` | Fetched via REST when loading a replay timeline | | `scrubbing` | `scrubberLogs[]` | Fetched for a specific time range during timeline scrubbing | **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:23-30](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:770-777]() ### Mode Switching The `ExecutionInspector` synchronizes log mode with timeline playback mode: **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:226-234]() - **Live mode**: Display `liveLogs` (updated via SSE) - **Replay mode**: Display `historicalLogs` (fetched once at timeline load) - **Scrubbing mode**: Display `scrubberLogs` (fetched for visible time range) --- ## Connection Lifecycle ### Initialization ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Starting: startExecution() Starting --> Running: Execution ID received Running --> Monitoring: monitorRun(runId) state Monitoring { [*] --> ConnectSSE [*] --> PollSetup ConnectSSE --> Connected: EventSource created PollSetup --> Polling: setInterval started state Connected { Connecting --> Ready: 'ready' event Ready --> Streaming: Receiving events } state Polling { Wait --> Fetch Fetch --> Wait } } Monitoring --> Cleanup: stopPolling() Cleanup --> Idle ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:182-233](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:276-309]() ### Cleanup When stopping monitoring: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:373-380](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:656-662]() --- ## Performance Considerations ### Deduplication All event streams use ID-based deduplication to prevent duplicate processing: **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:118-131]() ### Throttling - **Live clock ticks**: Rate-limited to every 200ms - **Polling**: 2 seconds in normal mode, 5 seconds when SSE is in realtime mode - **SSE chunks**: Processed incrementally as they arrive **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:773-776](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:619-633]() ### State Batching Store updates use Zustand's built-in batching to minimize React re-renders. Multiple state changes within the same tick are coalesced into a single update. --- ## Error Handling ### SSE Connection Errors ```mermaid graph TB Connect["connectStream()"] Try["try { api.executions.stream() }"] Error["catch (error)"] Log["console.error()"] Fallback["Polling continues"] Connect --> Try Try -->|"Connection fails"| Error Try -->|"EventSource.onerror"| Close["source.close()"] Error --> Log Close --> Log Log --> Fallback ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:644-653]() The system gracefully degrades to polling-only mode if SSE connection fails. The `streamingMode` state tracks the current mode: - `'connecting'`: SSE connection in progress - `'realtime'`: SSE delivering real-time events - `'polling'`: SSE failed, polling active - `'none'`: No monitoring active **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:38]() ### Run ID Mismatch Protection Both `pollOnce()` and SSE event handlers validate that the current `runId` still matches before updating state, preventing race conditions when users switch between runs rapidly. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:322-324](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:343-344]()

This document describes the trace event and log system used to monitor workflow execution. Trace events are structured lifecycle markers emitted during node execution (e.g., `NODE_STARTED`, `NODE_COMPLETED`), while logs are free-form messages with severity levels. Both are streamed via Kafka and persisted to PostgreSQL for real-time and historical analysis.

For information about the overall execution monitoring architecture, see [Execution Monitoring](#5). For details on how events flow through the SSE streaming pipeline, see [Event Processing Pipeline](#5.2). For terminal output streaming, see [Terminal Output](#5.4).

---

## Trace Event Types

Trace events mark discrete lifecycle transitions for workflow nodes. The system defines the following event types:

| Event Type | Description | Emitted When |
|------------|-------------|--------------|
| `STARTED` | Node execution begins | Action activity starts, before component execution |
| `PROGRESS` | Incremental progress update | Long-running operations report partial completion |
| `COMPLETED` | Node execution succeeds | Action activity completes successfully |
| `FAILED` | Node execution fails | Action activity throws an error |
| `AWAITING_INPUT` | Node pauses for human input | Human-in-the-loop component creates input request |
| `SKIPPED` | Node execution bypassed | Conditional logic or join strategy skips the node |
| `HTTP_REQUEST_SENT` | HTTP request initiated | HTTP component sends request |
| `HTTP_RESPONSE_RECEIVED` | HTTP response received | HTTP component receives response |
| `HTTP_REQUEST_ERROR` | HTTP request fails | HTTP component encounters network error |

**Sources:** [openapi.json:986-991](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:366-392](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:154-157]()

## Event Structure

All trace events conform to a shared schema with the following fields:

```mermaid
graph LR
    TraceEvent["TraceEvent"]
    TraceEvent --> Core["Core Fields"]
    TraceEvent --> Optional["Optional Fields"]
    TraceEvent --> Meta["Metadata"]
    
    Core --> id["id: string (UUID)"]
    Core --> runId["runId: string"]
    Core --> nodeId["nodeId: string"]
    Core --> type["type: EventType"]
    Core --> level["level: info|warn|error|debug"]
    Core --> timestamp["timestamp: ISO 8601"]
    
    Optional --> message["message?: string"]
    Optional --> error["error?: ErrorObject"]
    Optional --> outputSummary["outputSummary?: object"]
    Optional --> data["data?: object"]
    
    Meta --> activityId["activityId?: string"]
    Meta --> attempt["attempt?: number"]
    Meta --> correlationId["correlationId?: string"]
    Meta --> streamId["streamId?: string"]
    Meta --> joinStrategy["joinStrategy?: all|any|first"]
    Meta --> triggeredBy["triggeredBy?: string"]
    Meta --> failure["failure?: FailureInfo"]
    Meta --> retryPolicy["retryPolicy?: RetryPolicy"]
```

**Diagram: Trace Event Schema Structure**

### Core Fields

- **`id`**: Unique identifier for the event (UUID v4), used for deduplication during SSE streaming
- **`runId`**: Workflow run identifier, used to group events by execution
- **`nodeId`**: Node reference (matches `node.id` in workflow graph)
- **`type`**: Event type enumeration (see table above)
- **`level`**: Severity level for filtering (`info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug`)
- **`timestamp`**: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event was emitted

### Optional Fields

- **`message`**: Human-readable event description
- **`error`**: Structured error object containing `message`, `stack`, `code`, `type`, `details`, and `fieldErrors`
- **`outputSummary`**: Abbreviated output data for display (e.g., HTTP status code, file count)
- **`data`**: Arbitrary event payload (e.g., HTTP request/response details, progress percentage)

### Metadata

The `metadata` field captures execution context:

- **`activityId`**: Temporal activity ID for correlation with Temporal history
- **`attempt`**: Retry attempt number (1-based, increments on retries)
- **`correlationId`**: Links related events across nodes (e.g., HTTP request/response pairs)
- **`streamId`**: Groups parallel node executions in the same stream
- **`joinStrategy`**: Join strategy for nodes with multiple dependencies (`all`, `any`, `first`)
- **`triggeredBy`**: Node reference that triggered this node (for dependency tracing)
- **`failure`**: Failure information containing `at` (timestamp) and `reason` (error details)
- **`retryPolicy`**: Retry configuration with `maxAttempts`, `initialIntervalSeconds`, `maximumIntervalSeconds`, `backoffCoefficient`, and `nonRetryableErrorTypes`

**Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:148-178](), [openapi.json:974-1090]()

## Log Structure

Logs are distinguished from trace events by their free-form nature. While trace events have a fixed schema, logs can contain arbitrary structured or unstructured data.

### Log vs Event Distinction

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Trace Events"
        TE["Structured lifecycle markers"]
        TE --> TE1["Fixed event types"]
        TE --> TE2["Node-scoped"]
        TE --> TE3["Timeline visualization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logs"
        L["Diagnostic messages"]
        L --> L1["Arbitrary content"]
        L --> L2["Multiple sources (component, activity)"]
        L --> L3["Log viewer display"]
    end
    
    Both["Both use same schema base"]
    Both --> TE
    Both --> L
```

**Diagram: Trace Events vs Logs**

Logs share the base trace event schema but are used differently:
- **Events**: Lifecycle markers used for timeline visualization and node state calculation
- **Logs**: Diagnostic output displayed in the log viewer, often with longer messages and stack traces

### Log Levels

Logs are categorized by severity:

| Level | Purpose | UI Color (Dark Mode) |
|-------|---------|---------------------|
| `debug` | Verbose diagnostic information | `text-slate-300` |
| `info` | Informational messages | `text-sky-200` |
| `warn` | Warnings that don't halt execution | `text-amber-200` |
| `error` | Errors that halt node execution | `text-red-300` |

The frontend log viewer supports filtering by level. A level filter of `warn` shows warnings and errors, but excludes `info` and `debug`.

## Emission Pipeline (Worker Side)

The worker emits trace events and logs using service adapters injected into the execution context.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Component
    participant Activity as "runComponentActivity"
    participant TraceService as "KafkaTraceAdapter"
    participant LogService as "KafkaLogAdapter"
    participant Kafka
    participant DB as "PostgreSQL"
    
    Activity->>TraceService: emit(STARTED event)
    TraceService->>Kafka: telemetry.trace.instance-N
    Kafka->>DB: Persist via connector
    
    Component->>LogService: log.info("Processing file...")
    LogService->>Kafka: telemetry.logs.instance-N
    Kafka->>DB: Persist via connector
    
    Component->>TraceService: emit(PROGRESS event)
    TraceService->>Kafka: telemetry.trace.instance-N
    
    Component->>TraceService: emit(COMPLETED event)
    TraceService->>Kafka: telemetry.trace.instance-N
```

**Diagram: Event and Log Emission Flow**

### KafkaTraceAdapter

The `KafkaTraceAdapter` implements the `TraceService` interface and publishes trace events to Kafka.

**Key Methods:**
- **`emit(event: TraceEventPayload)`**: Publishes an event to `telemetry.trace.instance-{N}` topic
- **`started(nodeId, message?, metadata?)`**: Helper for emitting `STARTED` events
- **`progress(nodeId, message?, metadata?)`**: Helper for emitting `PROGRESS` events
- **`completed(nodeId, outputSummary?, metadata?)`**: Helper for emitting `COMPLETED` events
- **`failed(nodeId, error, metadata?)`**: Helper for emitting `FAILED` events

Events include the `runId`, `organizationId`, and `workflowId` from the execution context.

**Sources:** [worker/src/adapters/kafka-trace.adapter.ts:1-200]() (inferred from architecture)

### KafkaLogAdapter

The `KafkaLogAdapter` implements the `LogService` interface and publishes logs to Kafka.

**Key Methods:**
- **`log(level, message, data?)`**: Publishes a log entry with the specified level
- **`info(message, data?)`**: Convenience method for info-level logs
- **`warn(message, data?)`**: Convenience method for warn-level logs
- **`error(message, errorOrData?)`**: Convenience method for error-level logs
- **`debug(message, data?)`**: Convenience method for debug-level logs

Logs are published to `telemetry.logs.instance-{N}` topic with the same base schema as trace events, but `type` is set to the log level.

**Sources:** [worker/src/adapters/kafka-log.adapter.ts:1-150]() (inferred from architecture)

### Component Emission Example

Components receive injected services via the execution context:

```typescript
// Example from a component's execute function
async execute(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<Output> {
  const { trace, log } = context.services;
  
  // Emit structured trace event
  await trace.started(context.nodeRef, 'Starting HTTP request');
  
  // Emit diagnostic log
  log.info('Fetching data from API', { url: this.config.url });
  
  try {
    const response = await fetch(this.config.url);
    
    // Progress update
    await trace.progress(context.nodeRef, 'Response received', {
      data: { statusCode: response.status }
    });
    
    // Success
    await trace.completed(context.nodeRef, { 
      statusCode: response.status,
      contentLength: response.headers.get('content-length')
    });
    
    return { data: await response.json() };
  } catch (error) {
    log.error('HTTP request failed', error);
    await trace.failed(context.nodeRef, error as Error);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Storage and Persistence

Trace events and logs flow through Kafka and are persisted to PostgreSQL for historical querying.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Kafka Topics"
        T1["telemetry.trace.instance-N"]
        T2["telemetry.logs.instance-N"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PostgreSQL"
        DB1["trace_events table"]
        DB2["Indexes on runId, nodeId, timestamp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Consumers"
        SSE["Backend SSE Stream"]
        Persist["Kafka Connect Sink"]
    end
    
    T1 --> SSE
    T2 --> SSE
    T1 --> Persist
    T2 --> Persist
    Persist --> DB1
    
    DB1 --> Query["Historical Queries"]
```

**Diagram: Storage Architecture**

### Kafka Topics

Events and logs are published to instance-scoped Kafka topics:
- **`telemetry.trace.instance-{N}`**: Trace events
- **`telemetry.logs.instance-{N}`**: Log entries

The instance suffix (`instance-0` through `instance-9`) isolates different development environments running on the same machine.

### PostgreSQL Schema

Trace events are persisted to the `trace_events` table:

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | UUID | Event unique identifier (primary key) |
| `run_id` | VARCHAR | Workflow run identifier |
| `node_id` | VARCHAR | Node reference |
| `type` | VARCHAR | Event type |
| `level` | VARCHAR | Log level |
| `timestamp` | TIMESTAMP | Event timestamp |
| `message` | TEXT | Event message |
| `error` | JSONB | Error object |
| `output_summary` | JSONB | Output summary |
| `data` | JSONB | Event data |
| `metadata` | JSONB | Event metadata |
| `organization_id` | VARCHAR | Organization identifier |
| `workflow_id` | VARCHAR | Workflow identifier |

**Indexes:**
- `idx_trace_events_run_id` on `run_id` for run-scoped queries
- `idx_trace_events_node_id` on `node_id` for node-scoped log filtering
- `idx_trace_events_timestamp` on `timestamp` for time-range queries

### ExecutionStore

The `ExecutionStore` manages execution state and maintains three log collections:

- **`historicalLogs`**: Full log history loaded from `/runs/:runId/logs` endpoint
- **`liveLogs`**: Real-time logs received via SSE stream
- **`scrubberLogs`**: Time-range filtered logs for timeline scrubbing

**Log Modes:**
- **`live`**: Display `liveLogs` (updated via SSE)
- **`historical`**: Display `historicalLogs` (loaded once)
- **`scrubbing`**: Display `scrubberLogs` (fetched for time range)

**Key Methods:**
- **`fetchHistoricalLogs(runId)`**: Loads complete log history from backend
- **`fetchLogsForTimeRange(startTime, endTime)`**: Fetches logs for timeline scrubbing
- **`setLogMode(mode)`**: Switches between log display modes
- **`getDisplayLogs()`**: Returns the active log collection based on current mode
- **`getNodeLogs(nodeId)`**: Filters logs by node ID
- **`getNodeLogCounts(nodeId)`**: Returns log counts by level for a node

**Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:1-50](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:63-66]()

### Event Merging and Deduplication

Events from SSE streams are deduplicated by ID:

```typescript
// From executionStore.ts
const mergeById = (existing: ExecutionLog[], incoming: ExecutionLog[]): ExecutionLog[] => {
  if (incoming.length === 0) return existing;
  const seen = new Set(existing.map((event) => event.id));
  const deduped = incoming.filter((event) => {
    if (seen.has(event.id)) return false;
    seen.add(event.id);
    return true;
  });
  if (deduped.length === 0) return existing;
  return [...existing, ...deduped];
};
```

This prevents duplicate events when SSE reconnects or when switching between live and historical modes.

**Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:119-129]()

### ExecutionTimelineStore

The `ExecutionTimelineStore` consumes trace events to build the timeline visualization:

**Key Methods:**
- **`prepareTimelineEvents(rawEvents, workflowStartTime)`**: Converts events to timeline format with `visualTime` (0-1 normalized position)
- **`calculateNodeStates(events, dataFlows, currentTime)`**: Derives node visual states from events at the current timeline position
- **`updateFromLiveEvent(event)`**: Updates timeline with new live event, recalculating node states

**Node State Calculation:**
The store derives `NodeVisualState` for each node based on event history:
- **Status**: Inferred from last event type (`STARTED` → `running`, `COMPLETED` → `success`, etc.)
- **Progress**: Percentage based on event count and completion status
- **Event counts**: Total events observed and expected
- **Retry information**: Extracted from event metadata (`attempt` field)

**Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:145-209](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:260-419]()

The log viewer in `ExecutionInspector` displays logs with filtering and syntax highlighting.

**Key Takeaways:**
- Trace events are structured lifecycle markers with a fixed schema, while logs are diagnostic messages with arbitrary content
- Events are emitted by workers via Kafka, persisted to PostgreSQL, and streamed to frontend via SSE
- The frontend maintains separate log collections for live, historical, and scrubbing modes
- Event deduplication by ID prevents duplicate display during SSE reconnection
- Node visual states are derived from event history by analyzing event types and metadata

## Purpose and Scope Node I/O Inspection captures and displays the inputs and outputs for each node during workflow execution. This system records the data flowing between nodes, enabling developers to debug data transformations, verify component behavior, and understand how information propagates through the workflow graph. This page covers the data packet model, capture mechanisms, storage strategies, and the UI for inspecting node-level I/O. For broader execution monitoring, see [Trace Events and Logs](#5.3). For component-specific console output, see [Terminal Output](#5.4). For handling large payloads that exceed Temporal's limits, see [Data Spilling](#2.5). ## Data Packet Model The frontend defines a `DataPacket` interface that represents a single data transfer between nodes: ```mermaid graph LR SourceNode["Source Node
(produces output)"] TargetNode["Target Node
(receives input)"] DataPacket["DataPacket
sourceNode, targetNode
inputKey, payload
timestamp, size, type"] SourceNode -->|"output"| DataPacket DataPacket -->|"maps to input"| TargetNode ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:35-45]() ### DataPacket Fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for this data transfer | | `sourceNode` | `string` | Node ID that produced the output | | `targetNode` | `string` | Node ID receiving the input | | `inputKey` | `string?` | Specific input port on target node | | `payload` | `any` | The actual data being transferred | | `timestamp` | `number` | Unix timestamp (milliseconds) | | `size` | `number` | Payload size in bytes | | `type` | `'file' \| 'json' \| 'text' \| 'binary'` | Data type classification | | `visualTime` | `number` | Normalized position (0-1) for timeline rendering | The `visualTime` field enables the timeline to position packets correctly relative to the workflow's total duration, supporting both live execution and historical replay. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:35-45]() ## Data Capture and Streaming Architecture ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Worker as "Temporal Worker

Large Payload Storage" participant Backend as "Backend
SSE Endpoint" participant Timeline as "ExecutionTimelineStore" participant NodeIO as "NodeIOInspector" Note over Worker: Node completes execution Worker->>Worker: "Capture inputs/outputs" alt Payload < threshold Worker->>Kafka: "Emit DataPacket with payload" else Payload > threshold Worker->>MinIO: "Store large payload" Worker->>Kafka: "Emit DataPacket with spilled marker" end Backend->>Kafka: "Subscribe to dataflow topic" Kafka->>Backend: "Stream DataPackets" Backend->>Timeline: "SSE event: dataflow" Timeline->>Timeline: "normalizeDataPackets()" Timeline->>Timeline: "appendDataFlows()" Timeline->>Timeline: "calculateNodeStates()" NodeIO->>Timeline: "Query nodeStates[nodeId].dataFlow" NodeIO->>NodeIO: "Render inputs/outputs" ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:716-742](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:456-467]() ### NodeIOService (Worker) The worker's `NodeIOService` captures node inputs and outputs during execution. This service: 1. Records inputs when a node starts execution (resolved from upstream outputs) 2. Captures outputs when a node completes successfully 3. Emits DataPackets to Kafka for real-time streaming 4. Stores large payloads in MinIO using spilled data markers (see [Data Spilling](#2.5)) The service is injected into components via `ExecutionContext` alongside other infrastructure adapters like `TraceService` and `LogService`. **Sources:** Based on architecture diagrams and [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:35-45]() ### Event Streaming via SSE The backend multiplexes DataPackets through Server-Sent Events (SSE) alongside trace events and logs: 1. Backend subscribes to `telemetry.dataflow.*` Kafka topics 2. Incoming packets are forwarded to connected SSE clients 3. Frontend receives `dataflow` events containing arrays of packets 4. `ExecutionTimelineStore.appendDataFlows()` merges packets into state **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:456-467]() ## Data Normalization and Timeline Integration ### Normalizing Raw Packets The `normalizeDataPackets` function transforms raw packets from the backend into the timeline's coordinate system: ```mermaid graph TD Raw["RawDataPacket[]
from SSE/API"] Filter["Filter invalid packets
(missing required fields)"] Convert["Convert timestamp string -> number"] CalcVisual["Calculate visualTime
(offset / totalDuration)"] Normalized["DataPacket[]
ready for rendering"] Raw --> Filter Filter --> Convert Convert --> CalcVisual CalcVisual --> Normalized ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:211-258]() The normalization process: 1. **Validates required fields:** Filters out packets missing `id`, `sourceNode`, `targetNode`, or `timestamp` 2. **Converts timestamps:** Transforms ISO strings to Unix milliseconds for calculations 3. **Computes visual time:** Calculates packet position relative to timeline start and duration 4. **Clamps values:** Ensures `visualTime` stays within [0, 1] bounds 5. **Infers types:** Determines data type from payload or defaults to `'json'` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:211-258]() ### Associating Packets with Nodes The `calculateNodeStates` function builds per-node data flow records: ```typescript interface NodeVisualState { status: NodeStatus; progress: number; // ... other fields dataFlow: { input: DataPacket[]; // Packets where targetNode === nodeId output: DataPacket[]; // Packets where sourceNode === nodeId }; } ``` This structure enables the UI to: - Show all inputs received by a node - Display all outputs produced by a node - Correlate I/O with node execution timeline **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:16-33](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:260-474]() ### Live Updates via `appendDataFlows` During live execution, new DataPackets arrive continuously via SSE. The `appendDataFlows` action: 1. Receives raw packet array from SSE event handler 2. Normalizes packets using current timeline parameters 3. Appends to existing `dataFlows` array (deduplication happens upstream) 4. Recalculates node states to include new packets 5. Triggers React re-render for UI update **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:716-742]() ## Frontend Presentation: NodeIOInspector ### Component Integration The `NodeIOInspector` component is accessible via the "I/O" tab in the `ExecutionInspector` sidebar: ```mermaid graph TB EI["ExecutionInspector
(main timeline sidebar)"] Tabs["Tab Selector
events | logs | agent | artifacts | io | network"] NIO["NodeIOInspector
(I/O tab content)"] Timeline["ExecutionTimelineStore
nodeStates, dataFlows"] EI --> Tabs Tabs -->|"inspectorTab === 'io'"| NIO NIO --> Timeline Timeline -->|"nodeStates[selectedNodeId].dataFlow"| NIO ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:412-417](), [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:583]() ### Tab Activation The I/O inspector is rendered when `inspectorTab` state equals `'io'`: ```typescript {inspectorTab === 'io' && } ``` Users can switch between tabs to view different aspects of execution: - **Events:** Timeline events and progress markers - **Logs:** Structured log output - **Agent:** AI agent conversation traces - **Artifacts:** Generated files and reports - **I/O:** Node inputs and outputs (this inspector) - **Network:** HTTP request/response logs **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:377-427]() ### Node Selection Context The inspector shows I/O data for the currently selected node from the timeline. When no node is selected, it may display a summary view or prompt to select a node. The selection is managed by `ExecutionTimelineStore`: ```typescript const { selectedNodeId, nodeStates } = useExecutionTimelineStore(); const nodeState = selectedNodeId ? nodeStates[selectedNodeId] : null; const inputs = nodeState?.dataFlow.input ?? []; const outputs = nodeState?.dataFlow.output ?? []; ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:86-89]() ## Data Visualization Patterns ### Input Display For each input DataPacket where `targetNode === selectedNodeId`: - **Source identification:** Shows which upstream node produced the data - **Input port mapping:** Displays the `inputKey` if available (e.g., `"url"`, `"config"`) - **Timestamp:** When the input was received - **Payload preview:** Truncated or formatted preview of the data - **Type indicator:** Badge showing `file`, `json`, `text`, or `binary` - **Size information:** Human-readable size (bytes, KB, MB) ### Output Display For each output DataPacket where `sourceNode === selectedNodeId`: - **Destination nodes:** Shows which downstream nodes received this output - **Output type:** Classification of produced data - **Payload inspection:** Full or truncated view with expand/collapse - **Spilled data handling:** Link to download large payloads from MinIO ### Value Preview and Download The inspector supports: 1. **Inline preview:** For small JSON/text values, display formatted content 2. **Expandable sections:** Collapsible views for larger objects 3. **Download links:** For files or large payloads stored in MinIO 4. **JSON formatting:** Syntax-highlighted display for structured data 5. **Binary indicators:** Special rendering for binary/blob data types **Sources:** Based on common patterns in [frontend/src/components/timeline/EventInspector.tsx:328-334]() and similar inspection components ## Live vs. Replay Modes ### Live Mode Behavior When `playbackMode === 'live'`: - DataPackets stream continuously via SSE - `appendDataFlows()` adds packets as they arrive - Node states update in real-time to show latest I/O - Inspector auto-scrolls to show newest data - Users can pause auto-scroll by manually scrolling up **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:744-754]() ### Replay Mode Behavior When `playbackMode === 'replay'`: - All DataPackets loaded upfront via `api.executions.getDataFlows(runId)` - `currentTime` scrubbing filters visible packets by timestamp - Only packets with `timestamp <= absoluteCurrentTime` are shown - Enables "time travel" debugging of data flow **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:545-601]() ### Timeline Scrubbing and I/O Visibility The `calculateNodeStates` function respects `currentTime` to show only packets up to the playback position: ```typescript const absoluteCurrentTime = startTime + currentTime; const filteredPackets = dataFlows.filter((packet) => { const packetTime = new Date(packet.timestamp).getTime(); return packetTime <= absoluteCurrentTime; }); ``` This creates a "replay" experience where I/O data appears progressively as the timeline advances. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:275-293]() ## Historical Data Access ### API Endpoint Historical DataPackets are retrieved via: ```typescript const dataFlowResponse = await api.executions.getDataFlows(runId); const packets = dataFlowResponse.packets ?? []; ``` This endpoint returns all DataPackets for a completed run, enabling full I/O inspection after execution. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:545-601]() ### Caching Strategy The `ExecutionTimelineStore` caches DataPackets per run: 1. Initial load populates `dataFlows` array 2. Live updates append to the array 3. Cache persists until run selection changes 4. New run selection clears cache and reloads **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:505-540]() ## Integration with Data Spilling For payloads exceeding Temporal's size limits, the worker uses spilled data markers: ```typescript interface SpilledDataMarker { __spilled: true; minioPath: string; size: number; contentType: string; } ``` The NodeIOInspector detects spilled markers and: 1. Displays size and type information 2. Provides download button linking to MinIO object 3. Shows preview if content type is previewable (text, JSON) 4. Handles authentication via signed URLs from backend This mechanism is transparent to users but critical for inspecting large file transfers or bulk data operations. **Sources:** [Data Spilling](#2.5) system (cross-reference) ## Performance Considerations ### Packet Limiting To avoid memory bloat during long-running workflows: - Kafka topic retention limits historical packet count - Frontend may implement windowing for very large packet arrays - MinIO provides efficient storage for actual payloads - Metadata (size, type, timestamp) always available even if payload archived ### Selective Loading The inspector may implement on-demand payload fetching: 1. Show metadata for all packets immediately 2. Load full payload only when user expands a specific packet 3. Cache expanded payloads in memory 4. Evict old payloads when memory pressure increases This pattern is similar to how Terminal Output lazy-loads chunks. **Sources:** Based on patterns in [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:661-708]() --- **Summary:** Node I/O Inspection provides granular visibility into data flowing through workflow nodes. The system captures inputs/outputs in the worker, streams them via Kafka and SSE, normalizes timestamps for timeline alignment, and presents them in the `NodeIOInspector` component. Support for both live and replay modes enables real-time monitoring and post-execution analysis, while data spilling handles large payloads transparently.

The frontend application is a React-based single-page application (SPA) built with Vite, TypeScript, and React Router. It provides visual workflow design, execution monitoring, and system management through a component-based architecture. State management uses Zustand stores, API communication uses TanStack Query with a typed OpenAPI client, and UI components are built with shadcn/ui (Radix UI primitives). **Technology Stack:** - **Build tool**: Vite 5.x with TypeScript - **Framework**: React 18.x with React Router 6.x - **State management**: Zustand stores with persistence - **Data fetching**: TanStack Query v5 with typed API client - **UI components**: shadcn/ui (Radix UI) with Tailwind CSS - **Canvas rendering**: React Flow for workflow visualization For detailed information about specific workflow builder components, see page 2.1. For execution monitoring UI, see page 5.1. ## Purpose and Scope This document describes the application layout system that provides the primary navigation structure for ShipSec Studio. The `AppLayout` component serves as the root layout wrapper, managing a collapsible sidebar with navigation links, user authentication display, and the main content area. This page covers sidebar behavior (desktop vs mobile), hover-to-expand mechanics, swipe gestures, and route-based state management. For documentation about the workflow-specific top bar with save/run actions, see [TopBar and Actions](#6.2). For page-specific layouts like the workflow list or secrets manager, see [Workflow List](#6.3) and [Secrets Management](#6.4). --- ## Architecture Overview The layout system consists of three primary components: `AppLayout` (main wrapper), `AppTopBar` (page header for non-workflow pages), and `TopBar` (workflow-specific header). ## Purpose and Scope This document describes the frontend state management architecture, including the separation between server state (TanStack Query) and client state (Zustand stores), query conventions, store structures, and state synchronization patterns. For API communication layer details, see [API Client Architecture](#6.3). For authentication state management, see [Authentication and Authorization](#6.4). --- ## Architecture Overview ShipSec Studio's frontend separates **server state** (data fetched from the backend) from **client state** (UI-only concerns). Server state is managed exclusively through **TanStack Query**, while client-only state uses **Zustand** stores. ### Two-Tier State Management ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "React Components" WorkflowBuilder["WorkflowBuilder"] Canvas["Canvas"] ExecutionInspector["ExecutionInspector"] ConfigPanel["ConfigPanel"] end subgraph "TanStack Query - Server State" QueryClient["QueryClient"] useWorkflows["useWorkflows()"] useComponents["useComponents()"] useWorkflowRuns["useWorkflowRuns()"] useExecutionStatus["useExecutionStatus()"] QueryCache["Query Cache"] end subgraph "Zustand Stores - Client State" workflowStore["workflowStore"] executionStore["executionStore"] executionTimelineStore["executionTimelineStore"] workflowUiStore["workflowUiStore"] authStore["authStore"] end subgraph "Backend API" API["/api/v1/*"] end WorkflowBuilder --> useWorkflows WorkflowBuilder --> workflowStore Canvas --> useComponents Canvas --> workflowStore ExecutionInspector --> useWorkflowRuns ExecutionInspector --> executionTimelineStore ConfigPanel --> workflowStore useWorkflows --> QueryClient useComponents --> QueryClient useWorkflowRuns --> QueryClient useExecutionStatus --> QueryClient QueryClient --> QueryCache QueryClient --> API workflowStore -.sync.-> executionStore executionStore -.updates.-> executionTimelineStore ``` **Sources:** [frontend/docs/state.md:1-150]() --- ## Server State: TanStack Query All data fetched from the backend flows through TanStack Query hooks located in `src/hooks/queries/`. The separation ensures predictable data fetching, automatic caching, and background refetching. ### Query Client Configuration The `QueryClient` is configured with sensible defaults for retry behavior, refetch policies, and stale time. ```mermaid graph LR QueryClient["QueryClient
defaultOptions"] QueryClient --> Retry["retry: 1"] QueryClient --> Refetch["refetchOnWindowFocus: false"] QueryClient --> Stale["staleTime: 30000ms"] QueryClient --> Cache["gcTime: 300000ms"] ``` **Configuration:** - **Retry**: 1 retry on failure to reduce unnecessary network requests - **Refetch on Focus**: Disabled to prevent unexpected data changes when user returns to tab - **Stale Time**: 30 seconds - data is considered fresh for 30s before background refetch - **Garbage Collection**: 5 minutes - cached data is kept in memory for 5 minutes after last use **Sources:** [frontend/docs/state.md:20-34](), [frontend/src/lib/queryClient.ts]() ### Query Key Conventions All query keys are defined in `src/lib/queryKeys.ts` using factory functions that return readonly tuples. Every key includes the current `organizationId` for multi-tenant isolation. ```typescript // Query key structure export const queryKeys = { workflows: { list: () => ['workflows', getOrgScope()] as const, summary: () => ['workflowsSummary', getOrgScope()] as const, detail: (id: string) => ['workflow', getOrgScope(), id] as const, }, runs: { global: () => ['runs', getOrgScope()] as const, byWorkflow: (id: string) => ['runs', getOrgScope(), { workflowId: id }] as const, }, components: { all: () => ['components', getOrgScope()] as const, }, executions: { status: (runId: string) => ['executionStatus', getOrgScope(), runId] as const, trace: (runId: string) => ['executionTrace', getOrgScope(), runId] as const, nodeIO: (runId: string) => ['executionNodeIO', getOrgScope(), runId] as const, }, } ``` **Key Principles:** 1. **Org-scoped**: Every key includes `getOrgScope()` for tenant isolation 2. **Hierarchical**: Broader keys enable bulk invalidation (`['workflows']` invalidates all workflow queries) 3. **Type-safe**: `as const` ensures readonly tuples for TypeScript inference 4. **Factory functions**: Keys are functions that return tuples, not static values **Sources:** [frontend/docs/state.md:36-68]() ### Common Query Hooks Query hooks encapsulate data fetching logic and provide typed access to server data. Each hook is defined in `src/hooks/queries/`. | Hook | File | Purpose | Key Dependencies | |------|------|---------|------------------| | `useWorkflows()` | `useWorkflowQueries.ts` | Fetch workflow list | `queryKeys.workflows.list()` | | `useWorkflow(id)` | `useWorkflowQueries.ts` | Fetch single workflow | `queryKeys.workflows.detail(id)` | | `useWorkflowsSummary()` | `useWorkflowQueries.ts` | Fetch workflow summaries with run counts | `queryKeys.workflows.summary()` | | `useComponents()` | `useComponentQueries.ts` | Fetch component registry | `queryKeys.components.all()` | | `useWorkflowRuns(workflowId)` | `useRunQueries.ts` | Fetch runs for workflow | `queryKeys.runs.byWorkflow(workflowId)` | | `useExecutionStatus(runId)` | `useRunQueries.ts` | Poll execution status | `queryKeys.executions.status(runId)` | | `useSecrets()` | `useSecretQueries.ts` | Fetch secrets list | `queryKeys.secrets.all()` | | `useApiKeys()` | `useApiKeyQueries.ts` | Fetch API keys | `queryKeys.apiKeys.all()` | | `useSchedules()` | `useScheduleQueries.ts` | Fetch schedules with filters | `queryKeys.schedules.all(filters)` | | `useWebhooks()` | `useWebhookQueries.ts` | Fetch webhooks | `queryKeys.webhooks.all()` | | `useGitHubInstallations()` | `useGithubQueries.ts` | Fetch GitHub App installations | `queryKeys.github.installations()` | | `useMcpServers()` | `useMcpQueries.ts` | Fetch MCP servers | `queryKeys.mcpServers.all()` | **Hook Pattern Example:** ```typescript // From useWorkflowQueries.ts export function useWorkflows() { const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.workflows.list(), queryFn: () => api.workflows.list(), staleTime: 60000, // 60 seconds }); return { data: data ?? [], isLoading, error }; } ``` **Sources:** [frontend/docs/state.md:69-140](), [frontend/src/hooks/queries/useWorkflowQueries.ts](), [frontend/src/hooks/queries/useComponentQueries.ts:31-35](), [frontend/src/hooks/queries/useRunQueries.ts]() ### Query Options and Prefetching For complex queries that need to be accessed from multiple contexts (stores, components, programmatic access), query options are defined as reusable objects in `src/lib/executionQueryOptions.ts`. ```typescript // From executionQueryOptions.ts export const executionStatusOptions = (runId: string) => ({ queryKey: queryKeys.executions.status(runId), queryFn: () => api.executions.status(runId), staleTime: 5000, retry: 2, }); export const executionTraceOptions = (runId: string) => ({ queryKey: queryKeys.executions.trace(runId), queryFn: () => api.executions.trace(runId), staleTime: 30000, }); ``` These options enable: - **Programmatic fetching**: `queryClient.fetchQuery(executionStatusOptions(runId))` - **Prefetching**: `queryClient.prefetchQuery(executionTraceOptions(runId))` - **Manual invalidation**: `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.executions.status(runId) })` **Sources:** [frontend/src/lib/executionQueryOptions.ts](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:5-9]() --- ## Client State: Zustand Stores Zustand stores manage client-only state that doesn't directly correspond to backend resources. All stores are located in `src/store/`. ### Store Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Core Workflow Stores" workflowStore["workflowStore

mode, selectedTab, panels"] end subgraph "Execution Stores" executionStore["executionStore

componentId, workflowScope"] apiKeyUiStore["apiKeyUiStore
lastCreatedKey"] end workflowStore -.notify.-> executionStore executionStore -.update.-> executionTimelineStore authStore -.scope.-> workflowStore authStore -.scope.-> executionStore ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:1-556](), [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:1-787](), [frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:36-41]() ### workflowStore Manages workflow metadata, graph state, and dirty tracking. **State Shape:** ```typescript interface WorkflowStoreState { metadata: { id: string | null; name: string; currentVersion: number | null; }; isDirty: boolean; // Additional fields for graph serialization } ``` **Key Actions:** - `setWorkflowName(name: string)` - Update workflow name - `markDirty()` - Mark workflow as having unsaved changes - `clearDirty()` - Clear dirty state after save - `reset()` - Reset to initial state **Usage Pattern:** ```typescript const { metadata, isDirty, markDirty } = useWorkflowStore(); ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx:27-79](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:36-49]() ### executionStore Manages execution lifecycle, live logs, terminal streams, and SSE connections. **State Shape:** ```typescript interface ExecutionStoreState { runId: string | null; streamingMode: 'realtime' | 'polling' | 'none' | 'connecting'; } ``` **Key Actions:** - `startExecution(workflowId, options)` - Start new workflow run - `stopExecution()` - Cancel running execution - `monitorRun(runId, workflowId)` - Connect to SSE stream for live updates - `connectStream(runId)` - Establish SSE connection - `disconnectStream()` - Close SSE connection - `pollOnce()` - Manually fetch latest execution status - `fetchHistoricalLogs(runId)` - Load full log history for replay - `setLogMode(mode)` - Switch between live/scrubbing/historical logs - `getDisplayLogs()` - Get current log set based on mode **Streaming Architecture:** ```mermaid graph LR Component["ExecutionInspector"] Store["executionStore"] SSE["EventSource

setInterval(10s)"] Component -->|startExecution| Store Store -->|status: 'running'| SSE SSE -->|onmessage| Store Store -.fallback.-> Polling Polling -->|pollOnce| Store Store -->|liveLogs| Component ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:19-556](), [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:26-235]() ### executionTimelineStore Manages timeline playback, event visualization, and node visual states. Uses `subscribeWithSelector` middleware for fine-grained reactivity. **State Shape:** ```typescript interface TimelineState { selectedRunId: string | null; events: TimelineEvent[]; dataFlows: DataPacket[]; totalDuration: number; eventDuration: number; timelineStartTime: number | null; clockOffset: number | null; currentTime: number; playbackMode: 'live' | 'replay'; isPlaying: boolean; playbackSpeed: number; progress: number; startTime: number; endTime?: number; eventCount: number; totalEvents: number; lastEvent: TimelineEvent | null; dataFlow: { input: DataPacket[]; output: DataPacket[] }; attempts: number; retryCount: number; } ``` **Key Actions:** - `selectRun(runId, mode)` - Load timeline for run - `loadTimeline(runId)` - Fetch and prepare timeline events - `play() / pause()` - Control playback - `seek(timeMs)` - Jump to specific time - `setPlaybackSpeed(speed)` - Change playback rate (0.1x - 10x) - `selectNode(nodeId)` - Select node for inspection - `selectEvent(eventId)` - Seek to event and highlight - `updateFromLiveEvent(event)` - Append event during live execution - `goLive()` - Resume live following mode - `tickLiveClock()` - Advance interpolated clock for live runs **Timeline Preparation:** ```typescript // From executionTimelineStore.ts const prepareTimelineEvents = ( rawEvents: ExecutionLog[], workflowStartTime?: number | null, ) => { // Sort events by timestamp // Calculate offsetMs and visualTime for each event // Return normalized timeline }; inspectorTab: 'events' | 'logs' | 'agent' | 'artifacts' | 'io' | 'network'; configPanelOpen: boolean; libraryOpen: boolean; showDemoComponents: boolean; } ``` **Key Actions:** - `setMode(mode)` - Switch between design and execution modes - `setInspectorTab(tab)` - Change inspector tab - `setConfigPanelOpen(open)` - Toggle config panel visibility - `setLibraryOpen(open)` - Toggle component library - `toggleDemoComponents()` - Show/hide demo components **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:29-122](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:38-150](), [frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:19-232]() ### authStore Manages authentication state and organization context. **State Shape:** ```typescript interface AuthStoreState { user: User | null; return orgId; }; ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/authStore.ts](), [frontend/src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx:29-85](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:36-106]() ### Additional Stores | Store | Purpose | Key State | |-------|---------|-----------| | `themeStore` | Theme management | `theme: 'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'`, `startTransition()` | | `commandPaletteStore` | Command palette state | `isOpen: boolean`, `open()`, `close()` | | `placementStore` | Component placement on mobile | `componentId`, `workflowScope`, `setPlacement()` | | `apiKeyUiStore` | Last created API key | `lastCreatedKey: string \| null` | **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:38-89](), [frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:43-78](), [frontend/src/components/workflow/ConfigPanel.tsx:50-329]() --- ## State Synchronization Patterns State synchronization coordinates between TanStack Query, Zustand stores, and React components. ### SSE Streaming for Live Execution When a workflow execution starts, the frontend establishes a Server-Sent Events (SSE) connection to receive real-time updates. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as ExecutionInspector participant Store as executionStore participant SSE as EventSource participant Timeline as executionTimelineStore UI->>Store: startExecution(workflowId) Store->>Store: set status='running' Store->>Store: monitorRun(runId) Store->>SSE: new EventSource(/stream) loop Live Updates SSE->>Store: event: LOG Store->>Store: merge liveLogs Store->>Timeline: updateFromLiveEvent(event) Timeline->>Timeline: append to events Timeline->>Timeline: recalculate nodeStates Timeline->>UI: re-render timeline end SSE->>Store: event: STATUS_CHANGE Store->>Store: update runStatus Note over Store,SSE: Connection closed on
terminal status ``` **SSE Event Types:** - `LOG` - New log entry - `STATUS_CHANGE` - Run status update - `PROGRESS` - Node progress update - `TERMINAL_OUTPUT` - PTY/stdout/stderr data **Fallback Polling:** If SSE connection fails or is unsupported, the store falls back to polling every 10 seconds. **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:349-458](), [frontend/src/components/timeline/ExecutionInspector.tsx:196-234]() ### Store-to-Component Synchronization React components subscribe to Zustand stores using selectors for optimal re-rendering. **Selector Pattern:** ```typescript // Efficient: Only re-renders when selectedNodeId changes const selectedNodeId = useExecutionTimelineStore((state) => state.selectedNodeId); // Inefficient: Re-renders on any store change const store = useExecutionTimelineStore(); ``` **Derived State:** ```typescript // From Canvas.tsx const { nodeStates } = useExecutionStore(); useEffect(() => { if (mode !== 'execution') { // Clear visual states in design mode setNodes((nds) => nds.map((node) => ({ ...node, data: { ...node.data, status: 'idle' }, }))); return; } // Sync execution states to canvas nodes setNodes((nds) => nds.map((node) => { const executionState = nodeStates[node.id]; if (executionState && executionState !== node.data.status) { return { ...node, data: { ...node.data, status: executionState }, }; } return node; })); }, [mode, nodeStates, setNodes]); ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/workflow/Canvas.tsx:278-313]() ### Cross-Store Coordination Stores coordinate through direct reads and selective subscriptions. **Timeline Store ↔ Execution Store:** ```typescript // Timeline store uses subscribeWithSelector for efficient updates export const useExecutionTimelineStore = create()( subscribeWithSelector((set, get) => ({ // State and actions })) ); // Execution store notifies timeline of live events updateFromLiveEvent(event: ExecutionLog) { const timeline = useExecutionTimelineStore.getState(); timeline.updateFromLiveEvent(event); } ``` **Workflow Store → Execution Store:** ```typescript // Execution store reads workflow metadata startExecution: async (workflowId: string) => { const workflowMetadata = useWorkflowStore.getState().metadata; // Use metadata for execution context } ``` **Sources:** [frontend/src/store/executionTimelineStore.ts:1-5](), [frontend/src/store/executionStore.ts:179-234]() ### Query Invalidation Strategy ```mermaid graph TB Action["User Action
(save, delete, create)"] Mutation["TanStack Mutation"] Invalidate["queryClient.invalidateQueries()"] Action --> Mutation Mutation --> Invalidate Invalidate --> WorkflowList["Invalidate workflows.list()"] Invalidate --> WorkflowDetail["Invalidate workflows.detail(id)"] Invalidate --> RunsList["Invalidate runs.byWorkflow(id)"] WorkflowList --> Refetch1["Auto refetch active queries"] # Authentication and Authorization
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts](backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts](backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts](backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts](backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts) - [frontend/src/App.tsx](frontend/src/App.tsx) - [frontend/src/services/api.ts](frontend/src/services/api.ts) - [openapi.json](openapi.json) - [packages/backend-client/src/api-client.ts](packages/backend-client/src/api-client.ts) - [packages/backend-client/src/client.ts](packages/backend-client/src/client.ts)
This document describes the authentication and authorization system in ShipSec Studio, covering user authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), organization context management, and permission enforcement in the UI. For information about securing infrastructure services (OpenSearch Security, TLS certificates), see [Security Modes](#10.2). ## Overview ShipSec Studio implements a flexible authentication system that supports multiple authentication providers: - **Clerk** - Third-party authentication service for production deployments with organization management - **Local Auth** - Simple authentication mode for development using admin credentials Authorization is enforced through role-based access control, where users with administrator roles can manage workflows, secrets, and other resources, while non-admin users have read-only access. **Sources:** [frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:32-33](), [frontend/src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx:29](), [frontend/src/store/authStore.tsx]() ## Authentication Flow ### End-to-End Authentication Flow The authentication system coordinates between frontend auth providers, API client middleware, and backend guards: ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Frontend Authentication" AuthProvider["AuthProvider wrapper"] useAuth["useAuth() hook"] authStore["useAuthStore()"] ClerkProvider["ClerkProvider (Clerk mode)"] LocalCreds["adminUsername/adminPassword (Local mode)"] end AuthProvider --> useAuth AuthProvider --> ClerkProvider AuthProvider --> LocalCreds useAuth --> authStore subgraph "API Client Layer" apiClient["createShipSecClient()"] The Workflow List page displays all workflows in the current organization, showing their metadata, latest run status, and providing controls for navigation and management. This is the landing page of the application (route `/`) and serves as the primary entry point for users to access their workflows. For information about editing individual workflows, see [Workflow Builder](#2.1). For managing workflow execution history, see [Workflow Management API](#2.4). ## Page Purpose and Location The WorkflowList component renders at the root route `/` and provides a table-based interface for browsing all workflows. It displays workflow metadata including name, node count, latest run status, and timestamps. This handles scenarios where the frontend loads before the backend is ready. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:115-187]() ### State Variables | Variable | Type | Purpose | |----------|------|---------| | `workflows` | `WorkflowMetadataNormalized[]` | Parsed and ordered workflow list | | `isLoading` | `boolean` | Loading state for initial fetch | | `error` | `string \| null` | Error message from fetch failure | | `retryCount` | `number` | Current retry attempt (display) | | `retryCountRef` | `React.MutableRefObject` | Actual retry count (prevents state race) | | `workflowToDelete` | `WorkflowMetadataNormalized \| null` | Workflow pending deletion | | `isDeleteDialogOpen` | `boolean` | Delete confirmation dialog visibility | | `isDeleting` | `boolean` | Deletion in progress state | **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:78-93]() ## Workflow Display Structure ### Table Columns The workflow table displays the following columns: | Column | Desktop | Mobile | Description | |--------|---------|--------|-------------| | Drag Handle | ✓ | ✓ | `GripVertical` icon for reordering | | Name | ✓ | ✓ | Workflow name, truncated at 200px | | Nodes | ✓ | ✓ | Badge showing node count (`workflow.nodes.length`) | | Status | ✓ | ✓ | Latest run status badge or "NOT TRIGGERED" | | Last Run | ✓ | Hidden | Formatted timestamp of `workflow.lastRun` | | Last Updated | ✓ | Hidden (sm) | Formatted timestamp of `workflow.updatedAt` | | Actions | ✓ (if admin) | ✓ (if admin) | Delete button | **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:392-432]() ### WorkflowRowItem Component ```mermaid graph TB WRI["WorkflowRowItem"] SORT["useSortable({id: workflow.id})"] RS["useRunStore"] ROW["TableRow"] CELLS["TableCell components"] WRI --> SORT WRI --> RS SORT --> |attributes, listeners| DH["Drag Handle Cell"] SORT --> |transform, transition| STYLE["CSS style"] RS --> |getLatestRun| BADGE["Status Badge"] ROW --> DH ROW --> CELLS CELLS --> NAME["Name + truncate"] CELLS --> NODES["Node count badge"] CELLS --> BADGE CELLS --> DATES["Timestamps"] CELLS --> DELETE["Delete button"] style WRI fill:#f9f9f9 style SORT fill:#e0e0ff style RS fill:#ffe0e0 ``` Each row is a `WorkflowRowItem` component that integrates with `useSortable` for drag functionality. The component fetches the latest run status from `useRunStore` on mount. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:509-598]() ## Status Badge System ### Badge Display Logic ```mermaid flowchart TD START["WorkflowRowItem render"] FETCH["useRunStore.getLatestRun(workflow.id)"] CHECK{latestRun exists?} START --> FETCH FETCH --> CHECK CHECK -->|Yes| BADGE1["Badge with latestRun.status
getStatusBadgeClassFromStatus()"] CHECK -->|No| BADGE2["Badge: 'NOT TRIGGERED'
status: 'NONE'"] BADGE1 --> DISPLAY["Display in Status column"] BADGE2 --> DISPLAY style BADGE1 fill:#e0ffe0 style BADGE2 fill:#ffe0e0 ``` Status badges use the `getStatusBadgeClassFromStatus` utility to apply appropriate styling based on run status (COMPLETED, FAILED, RUNNING, etc.). The "NOT TRIGGERED" state indicates a workflow has never been executed. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:538-546](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:518-519]() ## Drag-to-Reorder Implementation ### Order Persistence The reordering system uses three key functions: 1. **getSavedOrder()**: Retrieves workflow ID array from `localStorage` key `workflow-list-order` 2. **saveOrder(ids)**: Persists workflow ID array to `localStorage` 3. **applyOrder(items, savedOrder)**: Sorts workflows based on saved ID positions ```mermaid flowchart LR DRAG["User drags row"] EVENT["handleDragEnd event"] FIND["Find old/new index"] MOVE["arrayMove(workflows, oldIndex, newIndex)"] SAVE["saveOrder(reordered.map(w => w.id))"] STATE["setWorkflows(reordered)"] DRAG --> EVENT EVENT --> FIND FIND --> MOVE MOVE --> SAVE SAVE --> STATE style SAVE fill:#ffe0e0 ``` The `arrayMove` function from `@dnd-kit/sortable` handles the reordering logic. The component saves only workflow IDs (not full objects) to minimize `localStorage` usage. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:51-74](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:100-113]() ### Sensor Configuration ```typescript const sensors = useSensors( useSensor(PointerSensor, { activationConstraint: { distance: 5 } }), useSensor(KeyboardSensor, { coordinateGetter: sortableKeyboardCoordinates }), ); ``` The `PointerSensor` requires 5px of movement before activating to prevent accidental drags when clicking rows. The `KeyboardSensor` enables keyboard-based reordering for accessibility. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:95-98]() ## Workflow Actions ### Navigation to Workflow Builder Clicking a workflow row navigates to `/workflows/${workflow.id}` via the `onRowClick` handler. This triggers the workflow builder page in design mode. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:447](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:552]() ### Workflow Deletion Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Row as WorkflowRowItem participant Dialog as DeleteDialog participant API as api.workflows.delete() participant State as workflows state User->>Row: Click delete button Row->>Dialog: setWorkflowToDelete(workflow) Row->>Dialog: setIsDeleteDialogOpen(true) Note over Dialog: Show confirmation
Workflow name + ID User->>Dialog: Click "Delete workflow" Dialog->>API: delete(workflow.id) alt Success API-->>Dialog: 200 OK Dialog->>State: filter out deleted workflow Dialog->>Dialog: Close dialog else Error API-->>Dialog: Error message Dialog->>Dialog: Display error in dialog Note over Dialog: User can retry or cancel end ``` The deletion flow requires explicit confirmation via a dialog showing the workflow name and ID. The dialog remains open if deletion fails, allowing the user to retry. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:195-229](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:460-494]() ## Permission-Based Access Control ### Role Checking ```mermaid graph TB AUTH["useAuthStore"] ROLES["roles array"] CHECK["hasAdminRole(roles)"] PERM["canManageWorkflows"] AUTH --> ROLES ROLES --> CHECK CHECK --> PERM PERM --> |true| CREATE["Show 'New Workflow' button"] PERM --> |true| DELETE["Show delete actions"] PERM --> |true| REORDER["Enable drag-and-drop"] PERM --> |false| READONLY["Read-only banner"] READONLY --> DISABLE["Disable all actions"] style PERM fill:#e0e0ff style READONLY fill:#ffe0e0 ``` The `hasAdminRole` utility determines whether the current user has workflow management permissions. Users without admin roles see a read-only banner and cannot create, delete, or reorder workflows. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:84-86](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:253-258]() ### Read-Only Mode UI When `canManageWorkflows` is false: - Informational banner displays: "You are viewing workflows with read-only access..." - Delete buttons are disabled - "New Workflow" button in AppLayout is disabled - Drag handles remain visible but actions are disabled via `isReadOnly` checks **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:253-258](), [frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:343-366]() ## Backend Connection Retry Logic ### Retry Mechanism ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Loading: Initial fetch Loading --> Success: API responds Loading --> CheckError: API error CheckError --> IsConnectionError{Connection error?} IsConnectionError --> CheckRetries{retryCount < 30?}: Yes IsConnectionError --> DisplayError: No (other error) CheckRetries --> ScheduleRetry: Yes CheckRetries --> DisplayError: No (max retries) ScheduleRetry --> WaitDelay: setTimeout(2000ms) WaitDelay --> Loading: Retry attempt Success --> [*]: Display workflows DisplayError --> TryAgain: User clicks "Try Again" TryAgain --> Loading: Reset retryCount ``` The retry logic handles the common development scenario where the frontend loads before the backend is ready. It uses a `ref` to track the actual retry count to avoid race conditions with React state updates. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:115-117](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:160-186]() ### Error Detection Connection errors are identified by checking if the error message includes: - `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` - `Failed to fetch` - `fetch` (generic) Other errors (authentication, validation, etc.) immediately display without retrying. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:163-185]() ## Mobile Responsiveness ### Responsive Column Visibility | Screen Size | Hidden Columns | |-------------|----------------| | < 640px (sm) | Last Run, Last Updated | | 640px - 768px (md) | Last Updated | | ≥ 768px | All columns visible | The table uses Tailwind's responsive classes (`hidden sm:table-cell`, `hidden md:table-cell`) to hide columns on smaller screens while maintaining the essential information (name, nodes, status, actions). **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:399-428](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:576-581]() ### Mobile Optimizations - Reduced padding: `py-4 md:py-8`, `px-3 md:px-4` - Smaller text sizes: `text-xl md:text-2xl` - Horizontal scroll enabled on table container: `overflow-x-auto` - Touch-friendly drag activation threshold: 5px - Mobile-specific loading indicators with spinner **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:252-265]() ## Integration Points ### API Integration The component uses the centralized `api.workflows.list()` method to fetch workflows, which returns an array of workflow metadata objects that are then normalized using `WorkflowMetadataSchema.parse()`. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:148]() ### Run Store Integration Each `WorkflowRowItem` component: 1. Calls `fetchRuns({ workflowId: workflow.id })` on mount 2. Retrieves latest run via `getLatestRun(workflow.id)` 3. Displays run status in the Status column This decoupled approach allows the workflow list to display current run information without embedding run fetching logic directly in the list component. **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:518-519](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:532-534]() ### Analytics Tracking The component tracks two events: - `Events.WorkflowListViewed`: Fired on successful workflow load with `workflows_count` - `Events.WorkflowCreateClicked`: Fired when user clicks "New Workflow" button **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:159](), [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:242-248]() ## Empty States ### No Workflows State When `workflows.length === 0` after successful load: - Displays `Workflow` icon (Lucide) - Message: "No workflows yet" - Subtext: "Create your first workflow to get started" - "Create Workflow" button (disabled if read-only) **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:373-383]() ### Error State When fetch fails after exhausting retries: - Displays `AlertCircle` icon - Title: "Failed to load workflows" - Error message from API - "Try Again" button to reset and retry **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:364-372]() ### Loading State During initial load or retries: - Skeleton table with 5 placeholder rows - Retry count banner: "Waiting for backend... (N/30)" - Animated loading spinner **Sources:** [frontend/src/pages/WorkflowList.tsx:279-363]()

## Purpose and Scope The Backend Services layer implements the NestJS-based API server that orchestrates workflow management, execution dispatch, and integration services for ShipSec Studio. This page documents the service layer architecture, core business logic classes, and their interactions with the database and Temporal. For information about the Temporal worker that executes components, see [Worker Services](#8). For database schema details, see [Database Schema](#7.3). For MCP-specific backend implementation, see [MCP Backend Services](#7.2). **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts](), [openapi.json]() --- ## Service Layer Architecture The backend follows NestJS module conventions with controllers exposing HTTP endpoints and services containing business logic. It encapsulates CRUD operations, graph compilation, version management, and execution dispatch to Temporal. ### Key Methods and Responsibilities | Method | Purpose | Key Operations | |--------|---------|----------------| | `create()` | Create new workflow | Validate graph → Insert record → Create version → Set user role | | `update()` | Update existing workflow | Validate graph → Update record → Create new version | | `findById()` | Retrieve workflow by ID | Fetch record → Resolve ports → Build response | | `commit()` | Compile and validate workflow | Compile graph → Validate definition → Save compiled definition | | `run()` | Execute workflow | Resolve version → Prepare payload → Dispatch to Temporal | | `prepareRunPayload()` | Build execution payload | Resolve definition → Create run record → Return PreparedRunPayload | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:146-165](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:292-332]() ### Workflow Execution
