WorkflowsService->>VersionRepository: resolveWorkflowVersion() VersionRepository-->>WorkflowsService: WorkflowVersionRecord WorkflowsService->>Compiler: compileWorkflowGraph(graph) Compiler-->>WorkflowsService: WorkflowDefinition WorkflowsService->>RunRepository: createRun() RunRepository-->>WorkflowsService: WorkflowRunRecord WorkflowsService->>WorkflowsService: prepareRunPayload() WorkflowsService->>TemporalService: startWorkflow(runId, payload) TemporalService->>Temporal: client.workflow.start() Temporal-->>TemporalService: WorkflowHandle TemporalService-->>WorkflowsService: { runId, temporalRunId, status } WorkflowsService-->>WorkflowsController: WorkflowRunHandle WorkflowsController-->>Client: 201 Created { runId, status } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:759-859](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:597-642](), [backend/src/temporal/temporal.service.ts]() ### PreparedRunPayload [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:861-975]() --- ## WorkflowsController: HTTP Endpoints The `WorkflowsController` exposes RESTful endpoints under `/api/v1/workflows`. All routes use DTOs validated with Zod schemas via `nestjs-zod`. ### Core Workflow Endpoints | Route | Method | Controller Method | Purpose | |-------|--------|------------------|---------| | `/workflows` | POST | `create()` | Create workflow from graph | | `/workflows` | GET | `findAll()` | List all workflows | | `/workflows/{id}` | GET | `findOne()` | Get workflow by ID | | `/workflows/{id}` | PUT | `update()` | Update workflow graph | | `/workflows/{id}` | DELETE | `remove()` | Delete workflow | | `/workflows/{id}/metadata` | PATCH | `updateMetadata()` | Update name/description only | | `/workflows/{id}/commit` | POST | `commit()` | Compile and validate | | `/workflows/{id}/run` | POST | `run()` | Execute workflow | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:239-596](), [openapi.json:64-797]() ### Run Management Endpoints | Route | Method | Purpose | |-------|--------|---------| | `/workflows/runs` | GET | List workflow runs with filters | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}` | GET | Get run metadata | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/status` | GET | Get Temporal execution status | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/result` | GET | Get workflow output | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/config` | GET | Get run inputs/version | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/trace` | GET | Get execution trace events | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/events` | GET | Get timeline events | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/dataflows` | GET | Get data flow packets | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/cancel` | POST | Cancel running workflow | | `/workflows/runs/{runId}/stream` | GET | SSE live updates | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:314-869](), [openapi.json:246-485]() ### Request/Response Flow ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Client Request" HTTPRequest["HTTP Request

{ runId, status, ... }"] end HTTPRequest --> ZodPipe Body --> ZodPipe ZodPipe --> Guard Guard --> Method Method --> Service Service --> ResolveVersion Service --> PreparePayload Service --> DTO DTO --> JSON ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:597-642](), [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:106-120]() --- ## Repository Layer Repositories abstract database operations using Drizzle ORM. Each repository handles a specific table and enforces multi-tenancy via `organizationId` filtering. ### Repository Classes | Repository | Table | Primary Methods | |------------|-------|----------------| | `WorkflowRepository` | `workflows` | `create()`, `update()`, `findById()`, `list()`, `delete()`, `saveCompiledDefinition()` | | `WorkflowVersionRepository` | `workflow_versions` | `create()`, `findById()`, `findLatestByWorkflowId()`, `findByVersion()` | | `WorkflowRunRepository` | `workflow_runs` | `createRun()`, `findByRunId()`, `cacheTerminalStatus()`, `updateTriggerMetadata()` | | `WorkflowRoleRepository` | `workflow_roles` | `upsert()`, `hasRole()`, `delete()` | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow-version.repository.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow-run.repository.ts]() ### Multi-Tenancy Enforcement All repository methods accept an `options` parameter with `organizationId` filtering: ```typescript interface WorkflowRepositoryOptions { organizationId?: string | null; } // Example: findById enforces org isolation async findById(id: string, options: WorkflowRepositoryOptions = {}): Promise { const conditions = [eq(workflowsTable.id, id)]; if (options.organizationId !== undefined) { conditions.push(eq(workflowsTable.organizationId, options.organizationId)); } const [record] = await this.db .select() .from(workflowsTable) .where(and(...conditions)) .limit(1); return record; } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:27-30](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:78-95]() --- ## Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) The backend uses Zod schemas with `nestjs-zod` to define DTOs for request validation and response serialization. ### Key DTO Schemas | DTO Class | Zod Schema | Purpose | |-----------|------------|---------| | `WorkflowGraphDto` | `WorkflowGraphSchema` | Input for create/update workflows | | `WorkflowResponseDto` | `WorkflowResponseSchema` | Output for workflow GET requests | | `RunWorkflowRequestDto` | `RunWorkflowRequestSchema` | Input for POST /workflows/{id}/run | | `WorkflowVersionResponseDto` | `WorkflowVersionResponseSchema` | Output for version GET requests | | `PrepareRunRequestDto` | `PrepareRunRequestSchema` | Internal run preparation payload | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:1-261]() ### Graph Validation The `WorkflowGraphSchema` includes custom refinements to validate edge connectivity: ```typescript WorkflowGraphSchema = z.object({ name: z.string(), nodes: z.array(WorkflowNodeSchema).min(1), edges: z.array(WorkflowEdgeSchema), viewport: WorkflowViewportSchema.default({ x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 }), }) .refine((data) => { // Enforce single-source rule: each input port can only receive one edge const portInputs = new Set(); for (const edge of data.edges) { const targetHandle = edge.targetHandle ?? edge.sourceHandle; if (!targetHandle) continue; // Exception: 'tools' port allows multiple connections for AI agents if (targetHandle === 'tools') continue; const key = `${edge.target}:${targetHandle}`; if (portInputs.has(key)) return false; // Duplicate connection portInputs.add(key); } return true; }, { message: 'Multiple edges connecting to the same input port are not allowed...', }); ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:58-92]() --- ## Compilation and Validation The backend compiles visual workflow graphs into executable `WorkflowDefinition` objects before execution. Extract params + inputMappings"] ResolveEntrypoint["Find entrypoint

[]) { incoming.set(neighbor, (incoming.get(neighbor) ?? 1) - 1); if (incoming.get(neighbor) === 0) { queue.push(neighbor); } } } // Detect cycles if (result.length !== nodes.length) { throw new Error('Workflow graph contains a cycle'); } return result; } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/dsl/compiler.ts:19-59]() --- ## Temporal Integration The backend interacts with Temporal through the `TemporalService` class, which wraps the Temporal client SDK. ### Workflow Dispatch ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Service as WorkflowsService participant Temporal as TemporalService participant Client as Temporal Client participant Server as Temporal Server participant Worker as Temporal Worker Service->>Service: prepareRunPayload() Service->>Temporal: startWorkflow(runId, payload) Temporal->>Client: workflow.start(options) Note over Temporal,Client: options = {

The Workflows Service is the core business logic layer in the backend that orchestrates workflow lifecycle management. It handles workflow creation, versioning, compilation, execution orchestration via Temporal, and run querying. This service sits between the WorkflowsController (REST API layer) and the database/Temporal infrastructure, implementing authorization checks, data transformations, and workflow state transitions. For frontend workflow design and visualization, see [Workflow Builder](#2.1). For the actual execution engine that runs workflows, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). For the HTTP API endpoints exposed to clients, see [Workflow Management API](#2.4). --- ## Core Responsibilities The `WorkflowsService` class implements the following responsibilities: | Responsibility | Methods | Description | |---|---|---| | **Workflow CRUD** | `create()`, `update()`, `updateMetadata()`, `findById()`, `list()`, `delete()` | Manage workflow records and validate graph structure | | **Version Management** | Version creation on each save, `commit()` for compilation | Track workflow history and enable rollback | | **Compilation Orchestration** | `commit()` delegates to `compileWorkflowGraph()` | Convert visual graph to executable definition | | **Run Preparation** | `prepareRunPayload()`, `getCompiledWorkflowContext()` | Resolve versions, validate inputs, generate run IDs | | **Execution Orchestration** | `run()`, `startPreparedRun()` via `TemporalService` | Start workflow executions with idempotency | | **Run Queries** | `listRuns()`, `getRun()`, `getRunStatus()`, `getRunResult()`, `getRunConfig()` | Query execution metadata and results | | **Access Control** | `requireOrganizationId()`, `requireWorkflowAdmin()`, `requireRunAccess()` | Enforce RBAC and organization isolation | | **Dynamic Port Resolution** | `resolveGraphPorts()`, `resolveNodePorts()` | Populate dynamic inputs/outputs for components | | **Data Flow Analysis** | `buildDataFlows()` | Derive data flow packets from trace events | Sources: [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts:130-1143]() --- ## Architecture Overview The following diagram shows the `WorkflowsService` class structure and its dependencies on repositories and external services: ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Controller Layer" WC["WorkflowsController

This document covers the backend services that manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) server configurations, tool discovery, and the runtime gateway that enables AI agents to call tools via the MCP protocol. These services bridge the gap between pre-configured MCP servers (stored in PostgreSQL), runtime tool registration (cached in Redis), and live agent sessions (proxied through the MCP gateway). For MCP server UI and discovery workflows, see [MCP Discovery System](#4.5). For how AI agents consume these tools, see [AI Agent Component](#4.1) and [MCP Gateway Service](#4.2). ## Service Architecture The MCP backend services are organized into three layers: **Configuration Management** (persistent MCP server definitions), **Runtime Registry** (ephemeral tool metadata during workflow runs), and **Gateway Proxy** (live MCP protocol sessions for AI agents). ### Backend Service Dependency Graph ```mermaid graph TB Controller["McpServersController
/api/v1/mcp-servers"] Service["McpServersService"] Repo["McpServersRepository"] Encryption["McpServersEncryptionService"] GatewayCtrl["McpGatewayController
/api/v1/mcp/gateway"] GatewayService["McpGatewayService"] ToolRegistry["ToolRegistryService"] InternalCtrl["InternalMcpController
/internal/mcp"] DB[("PostgreSQL
mcp_servers
mcp_server_tools")] Redis[("Redis
mcp:run:{runId}:tools")] SecretResolver["SecretResolver"] TemporalService["TemporalService"] Controller --> Service Service --> Repo Service --> Encryption Service --> SecretResolver Service --> TemporalService Repo --> DB GatewayCtrl --> GatewayService GatewayService --> ToolRegistry GatewayService --> TemporalService InternalCtrl --> ToolRegistry InternalCtrl --> GatewayService ToolRegistry --> Redis ToolRegistry --> Encryption Service -.reads during discovery.-> ToolRegistry ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:1-50](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:1-50](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:1-100]() The services are decoupled through dependency injection: | Service | Responsibility | Persistence | |---------|---------------|-------------| | `McpServersService` | CRUD operations for MCP server configurations | PostgreSQL (`mcp_servers`, `mcp_server_tools`) | | `ToolRegistryService` | Runtime tool metadata cache for active workflow runs | Redis (TTL: 1 hour) | | `McpGatewayService` | In-memory MCP server instances, tool proxying, and component tool execution | In-memory (stateful) | | `McpServersEncryptionService` | AES-256-GCM encryption for headers and credentials | N/A (stateless) | | `McpGroupsService` | Template-based MCP server group management | PostgreSQL (`mcp_groups`, `mcp_group_servers`) | ## MCP Server Management `McpServersService` manages the lifecycle of MCP server configurations, including creation, validation, health checking, and tool discovery. ### MCP Server Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Created: createServer() Created --> Discovering: testServerConnection() Discovering --> Healthy: tools discovered Discovering --> Unhealthy: connection failed Healthy --> Enabled: enabled=true Healthy --> Disabled: enabled=false Unhealthy --> Enabled: toggleServer() Unhealthy --> Disabled: toggleServer() Enabled --> Runtime: Workflow starts Disabled --> Disabled: (not registered) Runtime --> ToolRegistry: registerMcpServer() ToolRegistry --> Gateway: Agent connects Gateway --> Cleanup: Workflow ends Cleanup --> [*]: cleanupRun() note right of Created McpServersRepository.create() Stores: name, transport, endpoint, command, args, encrypted headers end note note right of Discovering McpServersService.testServerConnection() - HTTP: Direct MCP protocol test - STDIO: Temporal workflow (spawns container) Updates: lastHealthStatus, lastHealthCheck end note note right of ToolRegistry ToolRegistryService.registerMcpServer() Redis key: mcp:run:{runId}:tools Redis key: mcp:run:{runId}:server:{nodeId}:tools TTL: 1 hour end note ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:138-220](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:452-511](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:164-223]() ### Transport Type Validation MCP servers support two transport types, each with distinct configuration requirements: | Transport | Required Fields | Execution Context | Use Case | |-----------|----------------|-------------------|----------| | `http` | `endpoint` (URL) | Direct HTTP client | Pre-deployed MCP servers (e.g., cloud APIs) | | `stdio` | `command`, optional `args` | Docker container (via Temporal worker) | Local MCP servers (e.g., Steampipe, AWS MCP) | The service validates transport-specific requirements in `validateTransportConfig()`: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:515-535]() ### Health Check and Tool Discovery When `testServerConnection()` is called: 1. **HTTP Transport**: Direct MCP protocol test via `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` - Connects to endpoint, calls `tools/list` - Fast validation (<2s) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:537-585]() 2. **STDIO Transport**: Temporal workflow execution - Spawns Docker container with `command` and `args` - Temporal worker executes discovery via `discoverMcpToolsActivity` - Cleans up container after discovery - Timeout protection (60s default) - [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:587-651]() Discovered tools are persisted via `McpServersRepository.upsertTools()`, which preserves the `enabled` state of existing tools while adding new ones. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:452-651](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts:317-371]() ### Header Encryption Headers (typically authentication tokens) are encrypted using `McpServersEncryptionService`: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:148-163]() The encryption material includes: - `ciphertext`: AES-256-GCM encrypted payload - `iv`: Initialization vector (12 bytes) - `authTag`: Authentication tag for integrity verification - `keyId`: Key version for key rotation support Encryption uses the `SECRET_STORE_MASTER_KEY` environment variable (32 bytes hex). **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:148-163](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.encryption.ts:1-100]() ### Secret Resolution Headers can reference secrets using the `{{secret:}}` syntax. The `SecretResolver` interpolates these references during tool registration: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:653-709]() This enables MCP servers to use centralized secret management instead of storing credentials directly in headers. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.service.ts:653-709](), [backend/src/secrets/secret-resolver.ts:1-100]() ## Tool Registry Service `ToolRegistryService` provides a Redis-backed cache for tool metadata during workflow execution. This bridges the gap between persistent MCP server configurations and ephemeral workflow runs. ### Registry Key Schema ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Redis Keys" RunTools["mcp:run:{runId}:tools
(Hash)"] ServerTools["mcp:run:{runId}:server:{nodeId}:tools
(String)"] end subgraph "Run Tools Hash Fields" Field1["{nodeId} → RegisteredTool JSON"] Field2["{nodeId} → RegisteredTool JSON"] FieldN["..."] end subgraph "Server Tools Value" ToolList["[{name, description, inputSchema}, ...]"] end RunTools --> Field1 RunTools --> Field2 RunTools --> FieldN ServerTools --> ToolList note1["TTL: 3600 seconds (1 hour)"] RunTools -.-> note1 ServerTools -.-> note1 ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:106-108](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:228-246]() ### RegisteredTool Structure The `RegisteredTool` interface represents a tool entry in the registry: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:38-89]() Key fields: - **`nodeId`**: Unique workflow node identifier (e.g., `"mcp-library"`, `"aws-mcp-group/cloudtrail"`) - **`toolName`**: Agent-visible tool name (e.g., `"aws-cloudtrail__lookup_events"` for proxied tools) - **`type`**: `"component"` | `"mcp-server"` | `"mcp-group"` | `"remote-mcp"` | `"local-mcp"` - **`exposedToAgent`**: Whether tool should be visible to AI agents (default: `true`) - **`encryptedCredentials`**: AES-256-GCM encrypted credentials/headers ### Component Tool Registration Component tools are registered when a workflow node runs in tool mode: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:113-155]() The worker calls this via the internal API endpoint `POST /internal/mcp/register-component` with the tool's metadata, credentials, and input schema. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:113-155](), [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:36-41]() ### MCP Server Registration MCP servers are registered with pre-discovered tools to avoid on-the-fly discovery during agent sessions: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:164-223]() This method: 1. Encrypts headers if provided 2. Creates a `RegisteredTool` entry with type `"mcp-server"` (stdio) or `"remote-mcp"` (http) 3. Stores pre-discovered tools in a separate Redis key for the gateway to use 4. Sets TTL to 1 hour The worker calls this via `POST /internal/mcp/register-mcp-server` after spawning MCP containers or configuring HTTP endpoints. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:164-223](), [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:47-52]() ### Hierarchical Node ID Filtering The registry supports hierarchical node IDs using the `/` separator. When an agent specifies `allowedNodeIds: ["aws-mcp-group"]`, tools with node IDs like `"aws-mcp-group/cloudtrail"` and `"aws-mcp-group/cloudwatch"` are also included: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:248-270]() This enables MCP groups to register child servers dynamically while scoping tool discovery to the parent node. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:248-270](), [backend/src/mcp/__tests__/tool-registry.service.spec.ts:292-344]() ## MCP Gateway Service `McpGatewayService` manages in-memory MCP server instances and proxies tool calls between AI agents and tool providers. It is the runtime orchestration layer that enables agents to discover and execute tools. ### Gateway Request Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as "AI Agent
(worker)" participant Gateway as "McpGatewayController
/mcp/gateway" participant Service as "McpGatewayService" participant Server as "McpServer
(in-memory)" participant Registry as "ToolRegistryService" participant Temporal as "TemporalService" participant External as "External MCP
(HTTP/STDIO)" Agent->>Gateway: POST /mcp/gateway (Initialize) Note over Agent,Gateway: Authorization: Bearer {session token}

Service-->>Gateway: McpServer instance Gateway-->>Agent: Session initialized Agent->>Gateway: POST /mcp/gateway (Call Tool) Gateway->>Server: handleRequest(req, res) alt Component Tool Server->>Service: toolHandler(args) Service->>Temporal: signalWorkflow("executeToolCall", {nodeId, args}) Service->>Service: pollForToolCallResult(runId, callId) Service->>Temporal: queryWorkflow("getToolCallResult", callId) Temporal-->>Service: {success, output} Service-->>Server: {content: [{type: "text", text: JSON.stringify(output)}]} else External MCP Tool Server->>Service: Agent->>Gateway: GET /mcp/gateway (SSE stream) Note over Agent,Gateway: Keep-alive connection Gateway->>Service: cleanupRun(runId) on close Service->>Server: server.close() ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.controller.ts:25-125](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:55-97](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:174-449]() ### Server Instance Caching The gateway maintains an in-memory map of MCP server instances per run: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:29-36]() The cache key includes `allowedNodeIds` to support multiple agents with different tool scopes in the same workflow run: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:64-70]() This enables each agent to see only the tools connected to its `tools` input port. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:55-97]() ### Tool Registration Logic When a server instance is created, the gateway registers all available tools: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:177-202]() For each registered tool: 1. **Component Tools** (type: `"component"`): - Register with tool name from registry - Handler calls `callComponentTool()` which signals Temporal workflow - [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:204-295]() 2. **External Tools** (type: `"mcp-server"`, `"remote-mcp"`): - Load pre-discovered tools from Redis or database - Register with prefixed name: `{serverName}__{toolName}` - Handler calls `proxyCallToExternal()` which forwards to MCP server - [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:298-448]() **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:177-449]() ### Component Tool Execution Component tools are executed via Temporal's signal-and-poll pattern: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:585-641]() This flow: 1. Generates unique `callId` for the tool invocation 2. Sends `executeToolCall` signal to the workflow with tool metadata 3. Polls the workflow via `getToolCallResult` query until result is available 4. Returns tool output or error to agent The workflow executes the component via `runComponentActivity` and stores the result in an in-memory map queryable by `callId`. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:585-674]() ### External Tool Proxying External MCP tools are proxied through a persistent client pool: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:475-499]() The client pool ensures: - **Connection reuse**: STDIO containers remain running for the workflow duration - **Stateful protocol**: MCP servers initialized once, reused for all tool calls - **Automatic retry**: 3 retries with exponential backoff on transient failures - **Timeout protection**: 30-second timeout per tool call **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:475-580]() ### Trace Event Logging All tool calls are logged to the execution trace for observability: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:140-172]() Events include: - `NODE_PROGRESS` events with `STARTED`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` status - Tool name, duration, and output summary - Enables timeline visualization of agent tool usage **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:140-172]() ## Internal API The `InternalMcpController` exposes endpoints for workflow workers to register tools and generate session tokens. ### Internal API Endpoints | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | Called By | |----------|--------|---------|-----------| | `/internal/mcp/generate-token` | POST | Generate session token for agent-gateway communication | AI Agent component | | `/internal/mcp/register-component` | POST | Register component tool in Redis | Component SDK (tool-mode nodes) | | `/internal/mcp/register-mcp-server` | POST | Register MCP server with pre-discovered tools | MCP server components | | `/internal/mcp/cleanup` | POST | Clean up Redis cache and get container IDs to stop | Workflow cleanup logic | | `/internal/mcp/tools-ready` | POST | Check if all required tools are registered | Workflow scheduler (dependency resolution) | **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:1-73]() ### Session Token Generation Session tokens are JWTs with `runId`, `organizationId`, and `allowedNodeIds` claims: [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:18-34]() The `McpAuthGuard` validates these tokens on gateway requests: [backend/src/mcp/mcp-auth.guard.ts:1-100]() This ensures agents can only access tools from their allowed node scope. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:18-34](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-auth.guard.ts:1-100]() ### Tool Registration Refresh When tools are registered after an MCP session has initialized, the gateway refreshes all cached servers for that run: [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:36-41]() This re-registers tools on existing `McpServer` instances without requiring agent reconnection. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/internal-mcp.controller.ts:36-41](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-gateway.service.ts:103-121]() ## Database Schema MCP server configurations and discovered tools are stored in PostgreSQL tables. ### Schema Overview ```mermaid erDiagram mcp_servers ||--o{ mcp_server_tools : "has many" mcp_groups ||--o{ mcp_servers : "contains" mcp_servers { uuid id PK string name UK string transport_type string endpoint string command string[] args jsonb headers string health_check_url timestamp last_health_check string last_health_status boolean enabled uuid organization_id FK uuid group_id FK uuid created_by timestamp created_at timestamp updated_at } mcp_server_tools { uuid id PK uuid server_id FK string tool_name text description jsonb input_schema boolean enabled timestamp discovered_at } mcp_groups { uuid id PK string slug UK string name text description uuid[] server_ids boolean enabled string default_docker_image uuid organization_id FK timestamp created_at timestamp updated_at } ``` **Sources:** [backend/src/database/schema/mcp-servers.schema.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/database/schema/mcp-groups.schema.ts:1-100]() ### mcp_servers Table Stores MCP server configurations: - **`headers`**: JSONB with encrypted structure: `{ciphertext, iv, authTag, keyId}` - **`transport_type`**: `"http"` or `"stdio"` - **`enabled`**: Whether server should be registered during workflow runs - **`last_health_status`**: `"healthy"`, `"unhealthy"`, or `"unknown"` - **`group_id`**: Optional foreign key to `mcp_groups` table **Sources:** [backend/src/database/schema/mcp-servers.schema.ts:1-100]() ### mcp_server_tools Table Stores discovered tools from MCP servers: - **`tool_name`**: Tool identifier from MCP protocol's `tools/list` - **`input_schema`**: JSON Schema for tool arguments (JSONB) - **`enabled`**: Whether tool should be exposed to agents (default: `true`) - **`discovered_at`**: Timestamp of last discovery Tools are upserted during health checks via `McpServersRepository.upsertTools()`, preserving the `enabled` state. **Sources:** [backend/src/database/schema/mcp-servers.schema.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts:317-371]() ### mcp_groups Table Stores MCP server group templates (e.g., AWS MCPs, GitHub MCPs): - **`slug`**: Unique identifier matching template file (e.g., `"aws"`) - **`server_ids`**: Array of UUIDs referencing `mcp_servers` table - **`default_docker_image`**: Docker image for stdio servers in this group Groups are synced from YAML templates via `McpGroupsService.syncTemplates()`. **Sources:** [backend/src/database/schema/mcp-groups.schema.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/mcp-groups/mcp-groups.service.ts:1-100]() ## Encryption and Security ### Header Encryption MCP server headers (typically authentication tokens) are encrypted using AES-256-GCM: [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.encryption.ts:1-100]() The encryption service: - Uses `SECRET_STORE_MASTER_KEY` environment variable (32 bytes hex) - Generates random 12-byte IV per encryption - Returns `{ciphertext, iv, authTag, keyId}` for storage - Supports key rotation via `keyId` field **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.encryption.ts:1-100]() ### Credential Encryption in Registry When tools are registered in the Redis cache, credentials are encrypted using `SecretsEncryptionService`: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:129-134]() The same service decrypts credentials when retrieving tool metadata: [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:301-323]() This ensures credentials are never stored in plaintext in Redis. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:129-134](), [backend/src/mcp/tool-registry.service.ts:301-323]() ### Session Token Authentication MCP gateway requests are authenticated using JWT session tokens: 1. Agent requests token via `POST /internal/mcp/generate-token` with `runId` and `allowedNodeIds` 2. `McpAuthService` generates JWT with claims 3. Agent includes token in `Authorization: Bearer {token}` header 4. `McpAuthGuard` validates token and extracts claims 5. Gateway validates `runId` access and filters tools by `allowedNodeIds` **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp/mcp-auth.service.ts:1-100](), [backend/src/mcp/mcp-auth.guard.ts:1-100]() ### Organization Isolation All MCP server queries filter by `organizationId` or allow `NULL` (shared servers): [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts:48-74]() This ensures organizations cannot access each other's MCP server configurations. **Sources:** [backend/src/mcp-servers/mcp-servers.repository.ts:48-74]()

This page documents the PostgreSQL database schema used by ShipSec Studio to persist workflow definitions, execution metadata, MCP server configurations, and supporting data. The schema is managed using Drizzle ORM with table definitions in TypeScript.

For information about how data flows through the system during execution, see [Data Flow and Spilling](#2.8). For details on workflow versioning and compilation, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.3).

---

## Overview

The database serves as the source of truth for:

- **Workflow metadata**: Visual graph definitions, compiled workflow definitions, and version history
- **Execution tracking**: Run metadata, execution traces, node I/O records, and terminal output archives
- **MCP integration**: Server configurations, group definitions, and encrypted credentials
- **Scheduling**: Cron schedules with input payloads and Temporal integration state
- **File storage metadata**: File registry with MinIO object references
- **Access control**: Workflow-level role assignments for multi-user environments

All tables use UUID primary keys (except auto-increment IDs where appropriate) and include `organizationId` columns for multi-tenancy support.

Sources: [backend/src/database/schema/workflows.ts:1-21]()

---

## Core Workflow Tables

### workflows

The `workflows` table stores the master workflow records with both visual graph representation and compiled executable definitions.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    workflows {
        uuid id PK
        text name
        text description
        jsonb graph
        varchar organization_id
        jsonb compiled_definition
        timestamp last_run
        integer run_count
        timestamp created_at
        timestamp updated_at
    }
```

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key, auto-generated |
| `name` | `text` | Workflow display name |
| `description` | `text` | Optional description |
| `graph` | `jsonb` | Visual workflow graph (nodes, edges, viewport) conforming to `WorkflowGraphDto` |
| `organizationId` | `varchar(191)` | Multi-tenancy organization identifier |
| `compiledDefinition` | `jsonb` | Compiled `WorkflowDefinition` with actions, dependencies, and execution metadata |
| `lastRun` | `timestamp with time zone` | Timestamp of most recent execution |
| `runCount` | `integer` | Total number of executions (default: 0) |
| `createdAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Record creation timestamp |
| `updatedAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Last modification timestamp |

The `graph` field stores the complete visual representation as a `WorkflowGraphDto`, while `compiledDefinition` contains the executable `WorkflowDefinition` generated by the DSL compiler. Updates to the workflow graph do not automatically recompile the definition—compilation is triggered explicitly via the commit API.

Sources: [backend/src/database/schema/workflows.ts:9-20](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:39-55]()

### workflow_versions

The `workflow_versions` table maintains a complete history of workflow graph changes. Each save operation creates a new version record.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key, auto-generated |
| `workflowId` | `uuid` | Foreign key to `workflows.id` |
| `version` | `integer` | Sequential version number |
| `graph` | `jsonb` | Snapshot of `WorkflowGraphDto` at this version |
| `compiledDefinition` | `jsonb` | Compiled definition for this version |
| `organizationId` | `varchar(191)` | Organization identifier |
| `createdAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Version creation timestamp |

Workflow runs reference a specific version, ensuring execution uses the exact graph and definition that existed when the run was initiated. This enables safe concurrent editing and rollback capabilities.

Sources: [backend/src/workflows/__tests__/workflows.service.spec.ts:82-121](), [backend/src/workflows/__tests__/workflows.controller.spec.ts:68-114]()

### workflow_runs

The `workflow_runs` table tracks all workflow executions with metadata, inputs, and trigger context.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `runId` | `varchar` | Primary key, format: `shipsec-run-{uuid}` |
| `workflowId` | `uuid` | Foreign key to `workflows.id` |
| `workflowVersionId` | `uuid` | Foreign key to `workflow_versions.id` |
| `workflowVersion` | `integer` | Denormalized version number |
| `temporalRunId` | `varchar` | Temporal workflow run identifier |
| `totalActions` | `integer` | Number of actions in the workflow definition |
| `inputs` | `jsonb` | Runtime inputs provided at execution time |
| `inputPreview` | `jsonb` | Summary of runtime inputs and node overrides for display |
| `triggerType` | `varchar` | Trigger source: `manual`, `schedule`, `api`, `github_app` |
| `triggerSource` | `varchar` | Identifier of triggering entity (e.g., schedule ID) |
| `triggerLabel` | `varchar` | Human-readable trigger description |
| `status` | `varchar` | Cached execution status (updated from Temporal) |
| `organizationId` | `varchar(191)` | Organization identifier |
| `createdAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Run creation timestamp |
| `updatedAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Last status update timestamp |

The `runId` serves as both the database primary key and the Temporal workflow ID. The `temporalRunId` distinguishes multiple execution attempts of the same workflow ID. Status is cached from Temporal to avoid repeated queries, with updates triggered by execution events or explicit refresh.

Sources: [backend/src/workflows/__tests__/workflows.service.spec.ts:243-301](), [backend/src/workflows/__tests__/workflows.controller.spec.ts:272-308]()

## Execution Tracking Tables

### execution_trace

The `execution_trace` table stores all execution events for real-time monitoring and historical analysis.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `bigserial` | Primary key, auto-increment |
| `runId` | `varchar` | Foreign key to `workflow_runs.runId` |
| `eventType` | `varchar` | Event type: `NODE_STARTED`, `NODE_COMPLETED`, `NODE_FAILED`, `WORKFLOW_STARTED`, etc. |
| `nodeRef` | `varchar` | Reference to workflow action/node |
| `timestamp` | `timestamp with time zone` | Event occurrence time |
| `payload` | `jsonb` | Event-specific data (outputs, errors, progress) |
| `organizationId` | `varchar(191)` | Organization identifier |

Events are written during execution via the `TraceAdapter` in the worker and consumed by the frontend via Server-Sent Events (SSE) for live timeline updates. Historical queries support event filtering by type and time range.

## MCP and Tool Tables

### mcp_servers

The `mcp_servers` table stores Model Context Protocol server configurations with encrypted credentials.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key |
| `name` | `text` | Server display name |
| `description` | `text` | Optional description |
| `transportType` | `varchar` | `http` or `stdio` |
| `endpoint` | `text` | URL for HTTP transport, null for STDIO |
| `command` | `text` | Executable path for STDIO transport |
| `args` | `jsonb` | Command arguments for STDIO transport |

## Scheduling Tables

### workflow_schedules

The `workflow_schedules` table manages cron-based automated workflow execution.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `uuid` | Primary key |
| `workflowId` | `uuid` | Foreign key to `workflows.id` |
| `workflowVersionId` | `uuid` | Foreign key to `workflow_versions.id` (pinned version) |
| `workflowVersion` | `integer` | Denormalized version number |
| `name` | `text` | Schedule display name |
| `description` | `text` | Optional description |
| `cronExpression` | `varchar` | Cron expression (5 or 6 fields) |
| `timezone` | `varchar` | IANA timezone identifier (e.g., `America/New_York`) |
| `humanLabel` | `text` | Human-readable description of cron schedule |
| `overlapPolicy` | `varchar` | `skip`, `buffer_all`, `buffer_one`, `cancel_other`, `terminate_other` |
| `catchupWindowSeconds` | `integer` | Maximum time to backfill missed runs |
| `status` | `varchar` | `active` or `paused` |
| `lastRunAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Timestamp of last triggered execution |
| `nextRunAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Predicted next execution time |
| `inputPayload` | `jsonb` | Stored runtime inputs and node overrides |
| `temporalScheduleId` | `varchar` | Temporal Schedule ID for synchronization |
| `temporalSnapshot` | `jsonb` | Cached state from Temporal |
| `organizationId` | `varchar(191)` | Organization identifier |
| `createdAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Schedule creation timestamp |
| `updatedAt` | `timestamp with time zone` | Last modification timestamp |

Schedules are synchronized with Temporal's native scheduling system. The `inputPayload` is validated against the workflow's entry point runtime inputs on creation and update. The `overlapPolicy` controls behavior when a scheduled run triggers while a previous run is still executing.

## Workflow Execution Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates how data flows through database tables during a typical workflow lifecycle:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant workflows
    participant workflow_versions
    participant workflow_runs
    participant execution_trace
    participant terminal_records
    participant files
    
    User->>workflows: Create workflow (graph)
    workflows-->>User: Return workflow.id
    
    User->>workflow_versions: Commit creates version
    workflow_versions-->>workflows: Store compiled_definition
    
    User->>workflow_runs: Execute workflow
    workflow_runs->>workflow_runs: Create run record with inputs
    Note over workflow_runs: runId, workflowVersionId, triggerType
    
    loop During Execution
        workflow_runs->>execution_trace: Write NODE_STARTED event
        workflow_runs->>execution_trace: Write NODE_COMPLETED event
        workflow_runs->>terminal_records: Archive Docker PTY output
        terminal_records->>files: Store output file in MinIO
    end
    
    workflow_runs->>workflows: Update lastRun, increment runCount
    execution_trace-->>User: Stream events via SSE
```

Sources: [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts](), [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:179-198]()

## Repository Access Patterns

All database access is mediated through repository classes that enforce organization-scoped queries:

| Repository Class | Table(s) | Key Methods |
|-----------------|----------|-------------|
| `WorkflowRepository` | `workflows` | `create()`, `update()`, `findById()`, `saveCompiledDefinition()`, `incrementRunCount()` |
| `WorkflowVersionRepository` | `workflow_versions` | `create()`, `findLatestByWorkflowId()`, `setCompiledDefinition()` |
| `WorkflowRunRepository` | `workflow_runs` | `upsert()`, `findByRunId()`, `list()`, `cacheTerminalStatus()` |
| `TraceRepository` | `execution_trace` | `insert()`, `listByRunId()`, `countByType()`, `getEventTimeRange()` |
| `ScheduleRepository` | `workflow_schedules` | `create()`, `update()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `list()` |
| `TerminalRecordRepository` | `terminal_records` | `create()`, `list()`, `findById()` |
| `WorkflowRoleRepository` | `workflow_roles` | `upsert()`, `hasRole()`, `list()` |

All repository methods accept an optional `WorkflowRepositoryOptions` parameter with an `organizationId` field. When provided, queries are automatically scoped to that organization using Drizzle's `and()` clause builder. This pattern enforces multi-tenancy at the data access layer.

Sources: [backend/src/workflows/repository/workflow.repository.ts:28-207](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.module.ts:9-14]()

## Schema Management

The database schema is managed using Drizzle ORM with TypeScript table definitions located in `backend/src/database/schema/`. Migrations are generated via `drizzle-kit` and applied automatically on application startup in development mode or manually in production.

Table definitions use typed JSONB columns to store complex structures like `WorkflowGraphDto` and `WorkflowDefinition`, validated at runtime using Zod schemas. This approach provides type safety while maintaining schema flexibility for evolving workflow features.

Indexes are automatically created for foreign key columns and frequently queried fields (e.g., `organizationId`, `runId`, `workflowId`). Additional indexes may be added based on query performance analysis.

Sources: [backend/src/database/schema/workflows.ts:1-21](), [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts](), [backend/src/dsl/types.ts:70-85]()

# OpenAPI Specification
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts](backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts](backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts](backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts) - [backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts](backend/src/workflows/workflows.service.ts) - [frontend/src/App.tsx](frontend/src/App.tsx) - [frontend/src/services/api.ts](frontend/src/services/api.ts) - [openapi.json](openapi.json) - [packages/backend-client/src/api-client.ts](packages/backend-client/src/api-client.ts) - [packages/backend-client/src/client.ts](packages/backend-client/src/client.ts)
This document describes how ShipSec Studio generates, maintains, and uses OpenAPI specifications to provide type-safe API communication between the backend and frontend. The OpenAPI specification serves as the single source of truth for API contracts, enabling automatic TypeScript client generation and runtime validation. For information about the backend API endpoints themselves, see [Backend Services](#7). For details on frontend API communication patterns, see [API Client Architecture](#6.3). --- ## Overview The OpenAPI specification is automatically generated from NestJS controller decorators and Zod validation schemas. This specification is used to: - Generate TypeScript type definitions for all API endpoints - Create a type-safe runtime client using `openapi-fetch` - Validate request/response payloads in development - Document the API for external consumers The system uses a three-layer architecture: **Specification Generation** (from NestJS), **Type Generation** (via `openapi-typescript`), and **Client Generation** (via `openapi-fetch`). --- ## Specification Generation Pipeline The OpenAPI specification is generated by a dedicated script that introspects the NestJS application and extracts API metadata. ```mermaid graph TB Controllers["NestJS Controllers
(workflows.controller.ts)"] Decorators["@nestjs/swagger Decorators
@ApiOkResponse, @ApiTags"] ZodSchemas["Zod Validation Schemas
(workflow-graph.dto.ts)"] Script["generate-openapi.ts
Script"] DocumentBuilder["DocumentBuilder
SwaggerModule.createDocument()"] Cleanup["cleanupOpenApiDoc()
nestjs-zod"] SpecFile["openapi.json
(repo root)"] Controllers --> Script Decorators --> Script ZodSchemas --> Script Script --> DocumentBuilder DocumentBuilder --> Cleanup Cleanup --> SpecFile style Controllers fill:#f9f9f9 style SpecFile fill:#f9f9f9 ``` **Sources:** [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts:1-46]() ### Generation Script The generation script is located at [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts:10-38](). It performs the following steps: 1. **Bootstrap NestJS Application**: Creates a minimal app instance with external services disabled via `SKIP_INGEST_SERVICES=true` 2. **Configure Swagger**: Uses `DocumentBuilder` to set API metadata (title, version, server URL) 3. **Extract Schema**: Calls `SwaggerModule.createDocument()` to introspect controllers and DTOs 4. **Clean Schema**: Uses `cleanupOpenApiDoc()` from `nestjs-zod` to normalize Zod-generated schemas 5. **Write File**: Outputs the cleaned specification to `openapi.json` in the repository root ```typescript const config = new DocumentBuilder() .setTitle('ShipSec Studio API') .setDescription('ShipSec backend API specification') .setVersion('0.1.0') .addServer('/api/v1', 'API v1') .build(); const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config); const cleaned = cleanupOpenApiDoc(document); ``` **Sources:** [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts:24-32]() ### Controller Annotations Controllers use `@nestjs/swagger` decorators to provide metadata for OpenAPI generation. The decorators define response schemas, operation IDs, and parameter types. **Example from WorkflowsController:** | Decorator | Purpose | Example | |-----------|---------|---------| | `@ApiTags('workflows')` | Groups endpoints by tag | Applied at controller level | | `@ApiOkResponse({ type: WorkflowResponseDto })` | Defines 200 response schema | Returns workflow data | | `@ApiCreatedResponse({ schema: { ... } })` | Defines 201 response with inline schema | Workflow execution result | | `@ApiQuery({ name: 'status', required: false })` | Documents query parameters | Optional status filter | **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:239-240](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:253](), [backend/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts:598-604]() ### Zod Schema Integration The system uses `nestjs-zod` to integrate Zod validation schemas with OpenAPI generation. DTOs extend `createZodDto()` which generates both runtime validation and OpenAPI schema metadata. ```typescript export const WorkflowGraphSchema = z.object({ name: z.string(), description: z.string().optional(), nodes: z.array(WorkflowNodeSchema).min(1), edges: z.array(WorkflowEdgeSchema), viewport: WorkflowViewportSchema.default({ x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 }), }); export class WorkflowGraphDto extends createZodDto(WorkflowGraphSchema) {} ``` The `cleanupOpenApiDoc()` function normalizes these Zod schemas into standard OpenAPI format by removing Zod-specific metadata and flattening nested schemas. **Sources:** [backend/src/workflows/dto/workflow-graph.dto.ts:58-92](), [backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts:32]() --- ## Generated Specification Structure The generated specification is written to `openapi.json` at the repository root. It follows OpenAPI 3.0 format with paths, components, and operation definitions. ```mermaid graph LR OpenAPI["openapi.json"] Paths["paths

Worker services provide the execution engine for ShipSec Studio workflows. The worker is a Temporal-based service that executes workflow definitions by running component activities, managing state transitions, and coordinating long-running operations. This document covers worker initialization, service adapter configuration, activity registration, and the worker lifecycle. For information about workflow compilation and structure, see [Workflow Compilation](#2.2). For component execution details, see [Component Execution Model](#3.2). For workflow orchestration logic, see [Workflow Execution](#2.3). --- ## Worker Architecture The worker operates as a standalone Node.js process that connects to the Temporal server and polls for tasks. It provides the runtime environment for executing workflows and activities, with injected service adapters for infrastructure access. **Temporal Worker Architecture** ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Worker Process" Worker["Worker (dev.worker.ts)"] Connection["NativeConnection"] BundledWorkflows["Bundled Workflows

(namespace + task queue)"] PG[(PostgreSQL)] MinIO[(MinIO)] Kafka[Kafka/Redpanda] Redis[(Redis)] end Worker --> Connection Connection --> Temporal Worker --> BundledWorkflows Worker --> ActivityRegistry Worker --> FileStorage Worker --> Secrets Worker --> Trace Worker --> Logs Worker --> NodeIO Worker --> Terminal Worker --> Artifacts Worker --> AgentTrace FileStorage --> MinIO Secrets --> PG Trace --> Kafka Logs --> Kafka NodeIO --> Kafka Terminal --> Redis Artifacts --> MinIO AgentTrace --> Kafka Temporal --> Worker ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:1-442](), [worker/src/temporal/workflows/index.ts:1-156]() --- ## Data Spilling Mechanism Large payloads exceeding Temporal's limits (default 2MB) are automatically spilled to MinIO storage and replaced with marker objects. **Spilled Data Marker Structure** ```typescript interface SpilledDataMarker { __spilled__: true; storageRef: string; // MinIO file ID (UUID) originalSize: number; __spilled_handle__?: string; // Optional: specific field from spilled object } ``` **Spilling Process** 1. **Check Size**: JSON-stringify output and measure byte size 2. **Upload to MinIO**: If size > `TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES`, upload as `output.json` 3. **Replace Output**: Return spilled marker instead of actual data 4. **Unspilling**: Downstream activities detect marker, download from MinIO, extract via handle **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:484-510](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:222-280]() --- ## Multi-Instance Support The worker supports running multiple isolated instances on the same machine using environment-based configuration. **Instance Isolation Strategy** | Resource | Isolation Method | |----------|------------------| | Database | Separate database per instance: `shipsec_instance_N` | | Temporal Namespace | Instance-scoped namespace: `shipsec-dev-N` | | Temporal Task Queue | Instance-scoped queue: `shipsec-dev-N` | | Kafka Topics | Topic suffix: `telemetry.logs.instance-N` | | Port Offsets | Backend: `3211 + N*100`, Frontend: `5173 + N*100` | **Instance Configuration via Environment** ```bash # Instance selection (0-9) export SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=1 # Worker connects to instance-specific resources TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=shipsec-dev-1 TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE=shipsec-dev-1 DATABASE_URL=postgresql://shipsec:shipsec@localhost:5433/shipsec_instance_1 # Kafka topic resolver adds instance suffix LOG_KAFKA_TOPIC=telemetry.logs.instance-1 EVENT_KAFKA_TOPIC=telemetry.events.instance-1 ``` **Sources:** [justfile:44-216](), [pm2.config.cjs:236-374]() --- ## Worker Lifecycle Management Workers are managed via PM2 for process monitoring, automatic restarts, and log aggregation. **PM2 Worker Configuration** ```javascript { name: `shipsec-worker-${instanceNum}`, cwd: __dirname + '/worker', script: __dirname + '/node_modules/.bin/tsx', args: 'src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts', env: { TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE: `shipsec-dev-${instanceNum}`, TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE: `shipsec-dev-${instanceNum}`, DATABASE_URL: instanceDatabaseUrl, LOG_KAFKA_BROKERS: 'localhost:9092', TERMINAL_REDIS_URL: 'redis://localhost:6379', SWC_BINARY_PATH: swcBinaryPath, // Platform-specific SWC native binding }, watch: ['src'], max_memory_restart: '1G', } ``` **Worker Commands** ```bash # Start worker (instance 0) just dev start # Start specific instance SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=2 just dev start # View worker logs pm2 logs shipsec-worker-0 # Restart worker pm2 restart shipsec-worker-0 # Worker status pm2 status ``` **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:344-375](), [justfile:44-216]() --- ## Worker Concurrency Configuration The worker is configured with concurrency limits for workflow and activity executions. ```typescript const worker = await Worker.create({ connection, namespace, taskQueue, workflowsPath, activities: { /* ... */ }, bundlerOptions: { /* ... */ }, // Concurrency limits maxConcurrentWorkflowTaskExecutions: 10, maxConcurrentActivityTaskExecutions: 10, maxConcurrentLocalActivityExecutions: 10, stickyQueueScheduleToStartTimeout: '10m', }); ``` **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:368-372]() --- ## Worker Health Monitoring The worker logs periodic heartbeats to confirm it's alive and polling for tasks. ```typescript // Heartbeat logging every 15 seconds setInterval(() => { logHeartbeat(taskQueue); }, 15000); ``` Heartbeats are logged to file-based logs (not Kafka) to avoid circular dependencies and ensure monitoring even if Kafka is down. **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/workers/dev.worker.ts:392-395]() --- ## The worker is a Temporal worker process that executes workflow definitions by running component activities. It serves as the execution runtime for the ShipSec Studio platform, bridging the gap between Temporal's orchestration layer and the component system. The worker connects to infrastructure services (Temporal, PostgreSQL, MinIO, Kafka, Redis), creates service adapter implementations of SDK interfaces, and injects these services into component execution contexts. The worker architecture consists of three primary layers: 1. **Infrastructure Layer** - Connections to Temporal, databases, message queues, and storage 2. **Service Adapter Layer** - Implementations of SDK interfaces (`IFileStorageService`, `ITraceService`, etc.) 3. **Activity Layer** - Temporal activities that execute workflow actions via the component registry For workflow orchestration details, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). For activity implementations, see [Activity Execution](#8.2). For service adapter details, see [Service Adapters](#8.3). --- ## Architectural Overview ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Temporal Server" TemporalNS["Temporal Namespace

## Overview Service Adapters provide an abstraction layer between components and infrastructure services. They implement standardized interfaces defined in the Component SDK, allowing components to access storage, secrets, tracing, and logging without coupling to specific infrastructure implementations. This design enables components to run in different environments (local development, production, testing) with different backing services while maintaining a consistent API. Service adapters are initialized in the worker process and injected into component execution contexts. The adapter pattern separates infrastructure concerns from business logic, making components portable and testable. For information about how components use these services, see [Component SDK](#3.1). For details on component execution, see [Activity Execution](#8.2). **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:1-97](), [packages/component-sdk/src/interfaces.ts:1-228]() --- ## Architecture Pattern ```mermaid graph TD Component["Component

{__spilled__: true,
storageRef: fileId}"] Next["Next Component"] Unspill["Download from MinIO"] Component --> Check Check -->|No| Direct Check -->|Yes| Spill Spill --> Marker Marker --> Next Next --> Unspill Direct --> Next ``` **Spill Threshold:** `TEMPORAL_SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024` (5 MB) **Spilling Process:** 1. **Output Size Check:** After component execution, serialize output and check size ([run-component.activity.ts:492-518]()) 2. **Upload to Storage:** If oversized, upload to MinIO with unique file ID 3. **Replace with Marker:** Return a standardized spill marker instead of actual data 4. **Input Resolution:** Next component's activity detects spill marker and downloads full data ([run-component.activity.ts:229-288]()) **Spill Marker Structure:** ```typescript interface SpilledDataMarker { __spilled__: true; storageRef: string; // MinIO file ID originalSize: number; // Original payload size in bytes __spilled_handle__?: string; // Optional: specific field within spilled object } ``` **Handle-Based Spilling:** When spilling an object with multiple fields, the system can spill the entire object once and reference individual fields via handles ([run-component.activity.ts:254-276]()). **Caching:** Downloaded spilled objects are cached per activity execution to avoid redundant downloads ([run-component.activity.ts:230](), [workflow-runner.ts:181]()). **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:229-288](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:492-518](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:179-231]() --- ## Secret Masking in Adapters Service adapters implement secret masking to prevent sensitive data from being logged or stored in trace events: **Masking Locations:** | Adapter | What Gets Masked | Implementation | |---------|------------------|----------------| | Node I/O Adapter | Inputs and outputs with `editor: 'secret'` | `maskSecretInputs()`, `maskSecretOutputs()` | | Trace Adapter | Output summaries containing secrets | `createLightweightSummary()` after masking | | Log Adapter | (handled by components, not adapter) | - | **Masking Logic:** ```typescript // From component-output.ts:62-76 export function maskSecretInputs( component: RegisteredComponent, input: unknown, resolvedInputsSchema?: unknown // For dynamic ports ): unknown { const inputPorts = extractPorts(resolvedInputsSchema ?? component.inputs); const secretPorts = getSecretPorts(inputPorts); // Filters by editor='secret' let masked = maskSecretPorts(secretPorts, input); if (component.parameters) { masked = maskSecretParameters(component, masked); } return masked; } ``` **Port-Level Masking:** Secrets are identified by: - Port metadata: `editor: 'secret'` - Connection type: `connectionType.kind === 'primitive' && name === 'secret'` - Contract credentials: `connectionType.kind === 'contract' && credential === true` **Self-Masking:** Ports with `id === '__self__'` mask the entire output as `'***'` ([component-output.ts:18-19]()). **Dynamic Port Support:** For components with `resolvePorts`, masking uses the resolved schema to ensure dynamically-created secret ports are masked ([run-component.activity.ts:204-206]()). **Sources:** [worker/src/temporal/utils/component-output.ts:13-158](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:204-219]() --- ## Adapter Testing Service adapters are tested through integration tests that verify the full worker stack: **Integration Test Pattern:** ```typescript // From worker-integration.test.ts it('should inject services into components during execution', async () => { // 1. } ``` **Step 2: Implement Adapter** ```typescript // In worker/src/adapters/my-custom.adapter.ts export class MyCustomAdapter implements IMyCustomService { constructor( private readonly client: ThirdPartyClient, private readonly config: AdapterConfig ) {} async performAction(input: string): Promise<{ result: string }> { // Call third-party service const response = await this.client.call(input); return { result: response.data }; } } ``` **Step 3: Initialize in Worker** ```typescript // In worker/src/index.ts or similar const myAdapter = new MyCustomAdapter(client, config); initializeComponentActivityServices({ storage: fileStorageAdapter, secrets: secretsAdapter, trace: traceAdapter, // Add custom adapter to options // (may require extending initializeComponentActivityServices signature) }); ``` **Step 4: Extend Execution Context** ```typescript // In packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts export interface CreateContextOptions { // ... existing options myCustomService?: IMyCustomService; } export function createExecutionContext(options: CreateContextOptions): ExecutionContext { // ... existing logic (context as any).myCustomService = options.myCustomService; return context; } ``` **Step 5: Use in Components** ```typescript // In a component async execute({ inputs, params }, context) { const result = await context.myCustomService?.performAction(inputs.query); return { data: result?.result }; } ``` **Best Practices:** 1. **Stateless Adapters:** Adapters should be stateless (except for infrastructure connections) 2. **Error Handling:** Wrap infrastructure errors in `ServiceError` for consistent error reporting 3. **Resource Cleanup:** Implement proper cleanup for long-lived connections (use `finally` blocks) 4. **Scoping:** Use factory pattern if adapter needs per-execution scoping (like `ArtifactServiceFactory`) 5. **Testing:** Provide mock implementations for unit testing **Sources:** [packages/component-sdk/src/interfaces.ts:1-228](), [packages/component-sdk/src/context.ts:37-57](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:79-97]()
