The Workflow Scheduler is the execution orchestrator within the Temporal worker that resolves dependencies, manages parallel execution, and routes workflow actions based on join strategies and edge types. It transforms a compiled `WorkflowDefinition` into an execution plan and coordinates component activity execution according to dependency constraints and failure handling rules. **Scope**: This page covers the scheduler's dependency resolution algorithm, join strategies (`all`, `any`, `first`), error edge routing, conditional execution via active ports, and parallel execution batching. For information about the overall workflow execution lifecycle, see [Workflow Execution Engine](#2.4). For details on individual component execution, see [Component Execution Model](#3.3). --- ## Purpose and Responsibilities The Workflow Scheduler (`runWorkflowWithScheduler`) is invoked by the workflow runner to execute a `WorkflowDefinition`. Its core responsibilities are: - **Dependency resolution**: Tracking which actions have completed and determining which actions are ready to execute - **Parallel execution**: Running independent actions concurrently while respecting dependency constraints - **Join strategy enforcement**: Coordinating how multi-parent actions wait for their dependencies (`all`, `any`, `first`) - **Error edge routing**: Triggering error handlers when actions fail and propagating failures downstream - **Conditional execution**: Skipping branches when parent actions deactivate output ports - **Deterministic ordering**: Ensuring trace events and execution order are consistent across runs Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:1-486](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:23-26]() --- ## Scheduler Architecture ```mermaid graph TB Definition["WorkflowDefinition
(actions, edges, nodes)"] Scheduler["runWorkflowWithScheduler"] subgraph "Internal State" NodeStates["Map<string, NodeState>
strategy, successParents,
failureParents, triggered"] ReadyQueue["ReadyItem[]
ref + context"] Pending["Set<string>
pending actions"] FailedErrors["Map<string, unknown>
failure reasons"] end subgraph "Edge Maps" SuccessEdges["Map<sourceRef, WorkflowEdge[]>
success/default edges"] FailureDeps["Map<sourceRef, targetRef[]>
error edges"] end subgraph "Execution Loop" Batch["Extract ready batch"] Parallel["Promise.all(executions)"] HandleSuccess["handleSuccess()
route active ports"] HandleFailure["handleFailure()
propagate errors"] end RunCallback["run(actionRef, context)
→ {activePorts?}"] Definition --> Scheduler Scheduler --> NodeStates Scheduler --> ReadyQueue Scheduler --> Pending Scheduler --> SuccessEdges Scheduler --> FailureDeps ReadyQueue --> Batch Batch --> Parallel Parallel --> HandleSuccess Parallel --> HandleFailure Parallel --> RunCallback HandleSuccess --> ReadyQueue HandleFailure --> FailedErrors HandleFailure --> ReadyQueue NodeStates -.tracks.-> Pending ``` **Scheduler State Management** The scheduler maintains four core data structures: | Structure | Type | Purpose | |-----------|------|---------| | `nodeStates` | `Map` | Tracks each node's join strategy, remaining parents, and trigger status | | `readyQueue` | `ReadyItem[]` | Queue of actions ready to execute with their execution context | | `pending` | `Set` | Set of action refs that have not yet completed | | `failedErrors` | `Map` | Failure reasons for actions that threw errors | Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:48-116]() --- ## Dependency Graph Construction The scheduler builds two separate edge maps during initialization: **Success Edges** (`kind: 'success'` or `kind: 'default'`): Normal execution flow edges that are followed when an action completes successfully. These edges preserve `sourceHandle` information for conditional execution. **Failure Edges** (`kind: 'error'`): Error handling edges that are followed when an action fails. These edges trigger error handlers and carry failure metadata. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Edge Classification" Edges["definition.edges[]"] Success["successEdges
Map<sourceRef, Edge[]>"] Failure["failureDependents
Map<sourceRef, targetRef[]>"] end subgraph "Parent Maps" SuccessParents["successParentsMap
Map<targetRef, Set<sourceRef>>"] FailureParents["failureParentsMap
Map<targetRef, Set<sourceRef>>"] end Edges -->|"kind === 'error'"| Failure Edges -->|"kind !== 'error'"| Success Success --> SuccessParents Failure --> FailureParents SuccessParents -.builds.-> NodeState["NodeState.successParents"] FailureParents -.builds.-> NodeState2["NodeState.failureParents"] ``` **Initial Ready Queue Population** Actions with no dependencies (both `successParents` and `failureParents` are empty) are added to the ready queue immediately. The entrypoint action is prioritized to run first if it has no dependencies. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:54-116]() --- ## Join Strategies Each node has a join strategy that determines when it becomes ready to execute after multiple parent actions complete: | Strategy | Behavior | Use Case | |----------|----------|----------| | `all` | Wait for **all** success parents to complete | Sequential pipelines, fan-in aggregation | | `any` | Execute after **first** success parent completes | Race conditions, fallback mechanisms | | `first` | Alias for `any` | Explicit race semantics | ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Join Strategy: ALL" ParentA1["Parent A"] -->|success| MergeAll["Merge Node
joinStrategy: all"] ParentB1["Parent B"] -->|success| MergeAll ParentC1["Parent C"] -->|success| MergeAll MergeAll -.waits for.-> Note1["Executes only when
A, B, and C complete"] end subgraph "Join Strategy: ANY" ParentA2["Parent A"] -->|success| MergeAny["Merge Node
joinStrategy: any"] ParentB2["Parent B"] -->|success| MergeAny ParentC2["Parent C"] -->|success| MergeAny MergeAny -.waits for.-> Note2["Executes when first
parent completes
(triggeredBy: 'Parent A')"] end ``` **Join Strategy Evaluation** For `all` strategy, the node becomes ready when `successParents.size === 0` (all parents have been removed from the set as they completed). For `any` strategy, the node becomes ready immediately when the first parent completes successfully. The `triggeredBy` field in the execution context identifies which parent triggered execution. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:86-116](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:311-336]() --- ## Parallel Execution Model The scheduler executes workflow actions in **batches of independent actions** to maximize parallelism while respecting dependencies: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Queue as readyQueue participant Scheduler as runWorkflowWithScheduler participant Batch as executions[] participant Worker as run(actionRef) Note over Queue: [nodeA, nodeB, nodeC] Queue->>Scheduler: Extract all ready items Scheduler->>Batch: batch = readyQueue.splice(0) par Execute Parallel Batch->>Worker: run('nodeA', context) Batch->>Worker: run('nodeB', context) Batch->>Worker: run('nodeC', context) end Worker-->>Scheduler: Promise.all(settled) Note over Scheduler: Sort by completedAt timestamp loop Process settled results Scheduler->>Scheduler: handleSuccess() or handleFailure() Scheduler->>Queue: Add newly ready children end Note over Queue: [nodeD, nodeE] Queue->>Scheduler: Next batch... ``` **Execution Loop** The scheduler continues until `pending.size === 0`: 1. **Extract batch**: All items in `readyQueue` are removed and marked as "running" (removed from `pending`) 2. **Parallel execution**: `Promise.all()` executes all actions concurrently via the `run` callback 3. **Settlement ordering**: Results are sorted by `completedAt` timestamp to ensure deterministic processing 4. **Child scheduling**: Successfully completed actions schedule their children; failures propagate error edges 5. **Repeat**: Loop continues until no actions remain pending Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:120-207]() --- ## Failure Handling and Error Edges When an action fails, the scheduler follows a three-step process: 1. **Schedule error handlers**: Actions connected via `kind: 'error'` edges are added to the ready queue with failure metadata 2. **Cancel success dependents**: Actions waiting on the failed action via success edges are cancelled (if they haven't already executed) 3. **Propagate failure downstream**: Cancellation cascades through the dependency graph ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Failure Propagation" FailedNode["Node A
(throws Error)"] ErrorHandler["Error Handler B
(error edge)"] SuccessChild["Success Child C
(success edge)"] DownstreamD["Downstream D
(depends on C)"] FailedNode -->|"kind: error"| ErrorHandler FailedNode -.success edge
CANCELLED.-> SuccessChild SuccessChild -.propagates
cancellation.-> DownstreamD end subgraph "Error Handler Context" Context["WorkflowSchedulerRunContext"] Failure["failure: {
at: 'Node A',
reason: {
message: 'error msg',
name: 'ErrorType'
}
}"] Context --> Failure end ``` **Failure Metadata Injection** Error handlers receive an enriched execution context containing: - `failure.at`: The ref of the action that failed - `failure.reason.message`: The error message - `failure.reason.name`: The error type (if available) This allows error handlers to access failure details without coupling to the failed action's outputs. **Cancellation Rules** For success dependents of a failed node: - **Join strategy `all`**: Immediately cancelled (requires all parents to succeed) - **Join strategy `any`**: Cancelled only if no other parents can succeed (all remaining parents have failed) Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:374-458](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-scheduler.test.ts:114-190]() --- ## Conditional Execution and Active Ports Components can return `activePorts` to control which output edges execute. This enables conditional branching without explicit branching components. **Active Port Mechanism** When a component completes, it can return: ```typescript { output: {...}, activeOutputPorts: ['success', 'created'] } ``` The scheduler uses this to determine which children to execute: ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Conditional Execution" NodeA["Node A
activePorts: ['success']"] EdgeSuccess["Edge
sourceHandle: 'success'"] EdgeError["Edge
sourceHandle: 'error'"] ChildB["Child B
(triggered)"] ChildC["Child C
(skipped)"] NodeA --> EdgeSuccess NodeA --> EdgeError EdgeSuccess -.active.-> ChildB EdgeError -.inactive.-> ChildC end subgraph "Skip Propagation" SkippedC["Child C
(skipped)"] DownstreamE["Downstream E
(also skipped)"] SkippedC -.propagates skip.-> DownstreamE end ``` **Port Matching Logic** For each outgoing edge: 1. Extract the `sourceHandle` (defaults to `'default'` if not specified) 2. Check if `activePorts` includes this handle 3. If active: Mark child as triggered (call `processChild` with `type: 'fulfilled'`) 4. If inactive: Mark child as skipped (call `processChild` with `type: 'skipped'`) **Skip Propagation** When a node is skipped: 1. Remove it from `pending` without executing 2. Mark `state.skipped = true` 3. Call `onNodeSkipped` callback (if provided) 4. Propagate skip to all success children (recursively) Children with `joinStrategy: 'all'` are skipped if **any** parent is skipped. Children with `joinStrategy: 'any'` are skipped only if **all** parents are skipped. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:216-283](), [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:285-372]() --- ## Integration with Workflow Runner The scheduler is invoked by `executeWorkflow` in the workflow runner. The integration contract is defined by `WorkflowSchedulerOptions`: ```typescript interface WorkflowSchedulerOptions { run: ( actionRef: string, context: WorkflowSchedulerRunContext ) => Promise<{ activePorts?: string[] } | null>; onNodeSkipped?: (actionRef: string) => Promise; } ``` **Execution Callback** The `run` function is responsible for: 1. Loading the component from the registry 2. Resolving inputs from previous action outputs 3. Executing the component with the provided context 4. Returning `activePorts` if the component implements conditional execution 5. Throwing errors for the scheduler to route to error edges **Temporal Activity Execution** In Temporal workflows, the `run` callback invokes `runComponentActivity`, which: - Creates an execution context with service adapters - Records trace events (`NODE_STARTED`, `NODE_COMPLETED`, `NODE_FAILED`) - Handles spilled data resolution - Masks secret inputs/outputs for tracing - Returns outputs to the scheduler **Context Enrichment** The scheduler provides each action with: - `joinStrategy`: The join strategy configured for this node - `triggeredBy`: The ref of the parent that triggered execution (for `any` strategy) - `failure`: Failure metadata (for error edge handlers) These values are accessible via `context.metadata` in component execution. Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-runner.ts:48-504](), [worker/src/temporal/activities/run-component.activity.ts:118-646]() --- ## Execution Flow Example Consider this workflow with parallel branches and a merge point: ```mermaid graph TB Start["start"] --> BranchA["branchA"] Start --> BranchB["branchB"] BranchA --> Merge["merge
joinStrategy: all"] BranchB --> Merge Merge --> End["end"] ``` **Execution Timeline**: | Time | Action | Ready Queue | Pending | |------|--------|-------------|---------| | T0 | Initialize | `[start]` | `{start, branchA, branchB, merge, end}` | | T1 | Execute `start` | `[]` | `{branchA, branchB, merge, end}` | | T2 | `start` completes → schedule children | `[branchA, branchB]` | `{branchA, branchB, merge, end}` | | T3 | Execute `branchA` and `branchB` in parallel | `[]` | `{merge, end}` | | T4 | `branchB` completes first → check merge | `[]` | `{merge, end}` | | T5 | `branchA` completes → merge ready | `[merge]` | `{merge, end}` | | T6 | Execute `merge` | `[]` | `{end}` | | T7 | `merge` completes → schedule end | `[end]` | `{end}` | | T8 | Execute `end` | `[]` | `{}` | | T9 | Workflow complete | `[]` | `{}` | **Determinism Guarantee** Even though `branchA` and `branchB` execute concurrently and may complete in any order, the scheduler ensures: - Both branches complete before `merge` executes (enforced by `joinStrategy: 'all'`) - Results are processed in completion order (`completedAt` timestamp) - Trace events reflect the actual execution order Sources: [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:150-262]() --- ## Error Handling Example Consider this workflow with error edge routing: ```mermaid graph TB Start["start"] --> Risky["risky
(may fail)"] Risky -->|"success"| Happy["happy"] Risky -->|"error"| ErrorHandler["errorHandler"] Happy --> End1["end"] ErrorHandler --> End2["end"] ``` **When `risky` fails**: 1. Scheduler catches the exception in `Promise.all` settlement 2. `handleFailure('risky', ...)` is called 3. `errorHandler` is scheduled with: ```typescript context: { joinStrategy: 'all', triggeredBy: 'risky', failure: { at: 'risky', reason: { message: 'Connection timeout', name: 'NetworkError' } } } ``` 4. `happy` is cancelled (removed from `pending`, marked as `failureTriggered: true`) 5. Workflow completes with failure, but `errorHandler` has executed **Final State**: - `failedErrors` contains: `{ risky: NetworkError, happy: WorkflowSchedulerError }` - Scheduler throws aggregate error: `"One or more workflow actions failed"` Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:374-458](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:593-688]() --- ## Deadlock Detection The scheduler includes deadlock detection to catch workflow definition errors: ```typescript while (pending.size > 0) { if (readyQueue.length === 0) { throw new WorkflowSchedulerError( 'Workflow scheduler deadlock: no ready actions while workflow still incomplete' ); } // ... execute batch } ``` This detects scenarios where: - Circular dependencies exist (should be caught during compilation, but provides runtime safeguard) - Dependency counts are incorrect in the definition - All remaining actions are waiting on failed actions (should have been cancelled) Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:120-131]() --- ## Performance Characteristics **Time Complexity**: - Initialization: O(E + A) where E = edges, A = actions - Per-action execution: O(1) to check readiness - Total execution: O(A × D) where D = average dependency fan-out **Space Complexity**: - O(A) for node states - O(E) for edge maps - O(A) for ready queue (worst case: all actions become ready simultaneously) **Concurrency**: - Independent actions execute in parallel (limited by Temporal worker concurrency) - No mutex locks or synchronization primitives (single-threaded event loop) - Deterministic execution order via timestamp sorting Sources: [worker/src/temporal/workflow-scheduler.ts:1-486]() --- ## Testing and Validation The scheduler is extensively tested for: - **Parallel execution**: Verifies independent branches run concurrently and complete in expected time bounds - **Join strategies**: Validates `all` vs `any` behavior with multiple parents - **Failure propagation**: Ensures error edges trigger and failure metadata is injected - **Skip propagation**: Confirms inactive ports cause downstream skipping - **Determinism**: Multiple runs produce identical trace sequences Key test files: - [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-scheduler.test.ts]() - Unit tests for scheduler logic - [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts]() - Integration tests with component execution Sources: [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-scheduler.test.ts:1-192](), [worker/src/temporal/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts:1-789]()

OpenSearch Security plugin disabled (`DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true`) - No TLS certificates required - No multi-tenant isolation - Direct HTTP access to OpenSearch - Faster startup (~30s) - Single-user development environment **Activation:** - No `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` in `backend/.env` - Auto-detected by `just dev` command **Infrastructure Command:** ```bash docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up -d ``` **Sources:** [justfile:131-144](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:149]() ### Secure Mode (Production-Like) **Characteristics:** - OpenSearch Security plugin enabled with TLS - Multi-tenant isolation with role-based access control - TLS certificates required (`docker/certs/root-ca.pem`) - Clerk authentication integration - Longer startup (~120s for security initialization) - Per-organization data isolation **Activation:** - `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` set in `backend/.env` - TLS certificates generated via `just generate-certs` - Auto-detected by `just dev` command **Infrastructure Command:** ```bash docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-secure.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up -d ``` **Environment Variables (Secure Mode):** ```bash OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=true NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 # Dev only OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD= OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD= ``` **Sources:** [justfile:88-116](), [justfile:449-462]() ### Security Mode Comparison ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Local Auth Mode" local_os["OpenSearch

The `db-reset-instance.sh` script demonstrates the creation pattern: ```bash docker exec shipsec-postgres \ psql -U shipsec -d postgres \ -c "CREATE DATABASE \"shipsec_instance_N\" OWNER shipsec;" ``` **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:9](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:15](), [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:52-59]() --- ## Service Configuration Details ### PostgreSQL Configuration **Environment Variables:** - Infrastructure services run in Docker (`docker-compose.infra.yml`) - Application services run via PM2 (`pm2.config.cjs`) - Auto-detects secure mode if `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` present in `backend/.env` - Supports multi-instance isolation (0-9 instances on same machine) ### Production Mode (Docker Compose) **Orchestration:** Docker Compose (all services containerized) ```bash # Start production (auto-detects security mode) just prod start # Pull and start latest release just prod start-latest # Build and start from source just prod build ``` **Architecture:** - All services containerized (`docker-compose.full.yml`) - Uses prebuilt images from GitHub Container Registry - Nginx reverse proxy as single entry point (port 80) - Auto-detects secure mode if TLS certificates exist (`docker/certs/root-ca.pem`) ### Production Mode (Kubernetes/Custom) For production deployments beyond Docker Compose, the platform can be deployed using: - Kubernetes manifests (not provided in this repository) - Custom orchestration systems - Cloud provider managed services (ECS, GKE, AKS, etc.) The Docker images published to GHCR can be deployed in any container orchestration platform: - `ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-backend:latest` - `ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-worker:latest` - `ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-frontend:latest` **Sources:** [justfile:40-356](), [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:1-452](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:1-245]() --- ## Release Process ### GitHub Actions Workflow Releases are automated via `.github/workflows/release.yml`, triggered by version tags: ```bash # Create and push a release tag git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release v1.0.0" git push origin v1.0.0 ``` **Release Workflow Steps:** ```mermaid graph TB tag_push["Git Tag Push

Troubleshooting ### Common Issues **PostgreSQL Connection Failures:** ```bash # Check PostgreSQL is ready docker exec shipsec-postgres pg_isready -U shipsec # Check instance database exists docker exec shipsec-postgres psql -U shipsec -c "\l" | grep shipsec_instance_0 # Recreate instance database ./scripts/db-reset-instance.sh 0 ``` **Temporal Namespace Issues:** ```bash # List namespaces temporal operator namespace list --address localhost:7233 # Create missing namespace temporal operator namespace create shipsec-dev-0 --address localhost:7233 # Delete and recreate (data loss!) temporal operator namespace delete shipsec-dev-0 --address localhost:7233 --yes ``` **OpenSearch Security Initialization Timeout:** ```bash # Check OpenSearch security status docker exec shipsec-opensearch curl -u admin:admin \ --cacert /usr/share/opensearch/config/certs/root-ca.pem \ https://localhost:9200/_cluster/health # Force reinitialize security just security-init --force ``` **Kafka Topic Consumer Lag:** ```bash # Check Redpanda topics docker exec shipsec-redpanda rpk topic list --brokers localhost:9092 # Delete and recreate topic (data loss!) docker exec shipsec-redpanda rpk topic delete telemetry.logs.instance-0 --brokers localhost:9092 docker exec shipsec-redpanda rpk topic create telemetry.logs.instance-0 --brokers localhost:9092 ``` ### Log Locations **PM2 Logs:** ```bash # View logs pm2 logs # Log files location ~/.pm2/logs/ ├── shipsec-backend-0-error.log ├── shipsec-backend-0-out.log ├── shipsec-frontend-0-error.log ├── shipsec-frontend-0-out.log ├── shipsec-worker-0-error.log └── shipsec-worker-0-out.log ``` **Docker Container Logs:** ```bash # View specific service logs docker logs shipsec-postgres docker logs shipsec-temporal docker logs shipsec-opensearch # Follow all infrastructure logs just infra logs ``` **Sources:** [justfile:187-189](), [justfile:498-500]()

For frontend apps, `loadFrontendEnv()` [pm2.config.cjs:166-198]() filters only `VITE_*` prefixed variables to avoid injecting backend secrets into the browser. ### Worker-Specific Configuration The worker app requires special handling for SWC native binaries used by Temporal. The `resolveSwcBinaryPath()` function [pm2.config.cjs:147-158]() detects the platform and musl vs glibc to find the correct binary path. If found, it sets `SWC_BINARY_PATH` in the worker environment [pm2.config.cjs:370](). The worker also uses `tsx` (Node.js + TypeScript) instead of Bun to avoid SWC binding conflicts [pm2.config.cjs:348-349](). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:4-164](), [pm2.config.cjs:278-286](), [pm2.config.cjs:344-375]() ## Multi-Instance Support The development environment supports running multiple isolated instances on the same machine. Each instance has: - **Separate databases**: `shipsec_instance_0`, `shipsec_instance_1`, etc. - **Separate Temporal namespaces**: `shipsec-dev-0`, `shipsec-dev-1`, etc. - **Separate Kafka topics**: `telemetry.logs.instance-0`, `telemetry.events.instance-0`, etc. - **Offset ports**: Instance 0 uses 5173/3211, Instance 1 uses 5273/3311, etc. **Multi-Instance Isolation Architecture** ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Instance 0" FE0["Frontend: 5173"] BE0["Backend: 3211"] W0["Worker"] DB0["DB: shipsec_instance_0"] NS0["Namespace: shipsec-dev-0"] T0["Topics: *.instance-0"] end subgraph "Instance 1" FE1["Frontend: 5273"] BE1["Backend: 3311"] W1["Worker"] DB1["DB: shipsec_instance_1"] NS1["Namespace: shipsec-dev-1"] T1["Topics: *.instance-1"] end subgraph "Shared Infrastructure" PG["PostgreSQL

The infrastructure's `init-db` scripts create instance databases automatically. The database URL pattern is: ``` postgresql://shipsec:shipsec@localhost:5433/shipsec_instance_{N} ``` This is set in PM2 configuration [pm2.config.cjs:241]() and overridden in the environment [pm2.config.cjs:247](). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:240-249](), [justfile:49-63]() ## Environment Setup ### Initialization Process The `just init` command [justfile:16-38]() performs the following steps: 1. **Install dependencies**: Runs `bun install` if `node_modules/` doesn't exist 2. **Create environment files**: Copies `.env.example` to `.env` for each package: - `backend/.env` from `backend/.env.example` - `worker/.env` from `worker/.env.example` - `frontend/.env` from `frontend/.env.example` ### Required Environment Files | File | Purpose | Key Variables | |------|---------|--------------| | `backend/.env` | Backend service configuration | `DATABASE_URL`, `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS`, `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` (optional) | | `worker/.env` | Worker service configuration | `OPENSEARCH_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `SECRET_STORE_MASTER_KEY` | | `frontend/.env` | Frontend build configuration | `VITE_*` prefixed variables for browser injection | **Sources:** [justfile:16-38](), [pm2.config.cjs:296-297]() ### Security Mode Detection The justfile detects security mode by checking for `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` in `backend/.env` [justfile:66-74](): ```bash CLERK_KEY=$(grep -E '^CLERK_SECRET_KEY=' backend/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"' | tr -d "'" | xargs || true) if [ -n "$CLERK_KEY" ]; then SECURE_MODE=true else SECURE_MODE=false fi ``` **Secure mode** (when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is set): - Enables OpenSearch Security plugin - Generates TLS certificates - Uses `docker-compose.dev-secure.yml` overlay - Sets `OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=true` for PM2 apps **Local mode** (when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is not set): - Disables OpenSearch Security plugin - No TLS certificates required - Uses basic `docker-compose.infra.yml` - Sets `OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=false` for PM2 apps For details on security modes, see [Security Modes](#9.3). **Sources:** [justfile:64-163]() ## Development Workflow ### Starting the Environment **For first-time setup:** ```bash just init # Install deps, create .env files just dev # Start infrastructure + apps ``` **For subsequent starts:** ```bash just dev ``` The startup sequence [justfile:78-163](): 1. **Validates environment files** - exits if missing 2. **Detects security mode** - from `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` presence 3. **Generates certificates** (secure mode only) - if `docker/certs/root-ca.pem` missing 4. **Starts infrastructure** - Docker Compose services 5. **Waits for Postgres** - 30s timeout, uses `pg_isready` 6. **Waits for OpenSearch** (secure mode only) - 120s timeout, cluster health check 7. **Updates git SHA** - runs `./scripts/set-git-sha.sh` 8. **Starts PM2 apps** - `pm2 startOrReload` with instance-specific names ### Accessing Services After startup, services are available at: | Service | URL (Instance 0) | URL (Instance N) | |---------|------------------|------------------| | Frontend | `http://localhost:5173` | `http://localhost:{5173 + N*100}` | | Backend API | `http://localhost:3211` | `http://localhost:{3211 + N*100}` | | Nginx Proxy | `http://localhost` | N/A (always routes to instance 0) | | Temporal UI | `http://localhost:8081` | N/A (shared) | | Analytics | `http://localhost/analytics` | N/A (shared, requires auth in secure mode) | **Sources:** [justfile:118-163]() ### Viewing Logs ```bash just dev logs # Stream PM2 logs for current instance ``` This runs `pm2 logs shipsec-frontend-{N} shipsec-backend-{N} shipsec-worker-{N}` [justfile:187-189](). ### Checking Status ```bash just dev status # Show PM2 and Docker status ``` This shows: - PM2 process status for instance apps - Docker container status for infrastructure **Sources:** [justfile:190-197]() ### Stopping the Environment ```bash just dev stop # Stop instance apps (and infra if instance 0) ``` The stop sequence [justfile:174-186](): 1. **Deletes PM2 apps** for the current instance 2. **Stops infrastructure** (only if instance 0, since infra is shared) ### Cleaning the Environment ```bash just dev clean # Stop and remove all data ``` This performs a complete teardown [justfile:198-212](): 1. **Deletes PM2 apps** for the current instance 2. **Removes Docker volumes** (only if instance 0) - Deletes all database data - Deletes MinIO files - Deletes Temporal history - Deletes OpenSearch indices **Sources:** [justfile:174-216]() ## Database Management ### Database Reset To reset the database for a specific instance: ```bash just db-reset # Resets current instance (determined by SHIPSEC_INSTANCE) ``` Or use the instance-specific script: ```bash ./scripts/db-reset-instance.sh 0 # Reset instance 0 ./scripts/db-reset-instance.sh 1 # Reset instance 1 ``` The `db-reset-instance.sh` script [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:1-78]() performs: 1. **Finds Postgres container** using `docker compose ps -q postgres` [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:34-42]() 2. **Drops database** `shipsec_instance_{N}` [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:47-50]() 3. **Recreates database** with correct ownership [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:52-59]() 4. **Runs migrations** using `bun --cwd backend run migration:push` [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:62-72]() ### Instance Clean To clean all instance-specific infrastructure state: ```bash ./scripts/instance-clean.sh 0 # Clean instance 0 ``` The `instance-clean.sh` script [scripts/instance-clean.sh:1-59]() performs: 1. **Resets database** via `db-reset-instance.sh` [scripts/instance-clean.sh:36-40]() 2. **Deletes Temporal namespace** (best-effort) using `temporal operator namespace delete` [scripts/instance-clean.sh:42-45]() 3. **Deletes Kafka topics** for the instance [scripts/instance-clean.sh:48-56](): - `telemetry.logs.instance-{N}` - `telemetry.events.instance-{N}` - `telemetry.agent-trace.instance-{N}` - `telemetry.node-io.instance-{N}` **Sources:** [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:1-78](), [scripts/instance-clean.sh:1-59]() ## Environment Variable Reference ### If it fails: ```bash # Manually install for your platform bun add -d @swc/core-linux-x64-gnu # or bun add -d @swc/core-darwin-arm64 ``` **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:147-163]()

This document describes the Docker Compose configuration used to deploy ShipSec Studio's infrastructure and application services. The system uses a layered compose file approach with base infrastructure, security overlays, and port exposure configurations to support both development and production deployment modes. For application service deployment (backend, frontend, worker) outside of Docker, see [Development Environment](#9.1). For production-specific deployment considerations, see [Production Deployment](#9.6). ## Compose File Architecture ShipSec Studio employs multiple Docker Compose files that can be layered together to create different deployment configurations. This allows the same base infrastructure to support both development (with PM2-managed application services) and production (with containerized application services). ```mermaid graph TD Base["docker-compose.infra.yml

This file uses `expose` directives rather than `ports`, keeping services internal to the Docker network by default. | Service | Container Name | Image | Purpose | Exposed Ports | |---------|---------------|-------|---------|---------------| | postgres | shipsec-postgres | postgres:16-alpine | Primary database | 5432 | | temporal | shipsec-temporal | temporalio/auto-setup:latest | Workflow orchestration | 7233 | | temporal-ui | shipsec-temporal-ui | temporalio/ui:latest | Temporal web UI | 8080 | | minio | shipsec-minio | minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-10-02T17-50-41Z | Object storage | 9000, 9001 | | redis | shipsec-redis | redis:latest | Cache and streams | 6379 | | loki | shipsec-loki | grafana/loki:3.2.1 | Log aggregation | 3100 | | redpanda | shipsec-redpanda | redpandadata/redpanda:v24.2.5 | Event streaming (Kafka) | 9092, 9644 | | redpanda-console | shipsec-redpanda-console | redpandadata/console:v2.7.2 | Redpanda web UI | 8080 | | opensearch | shipsec-opensearch | opensearchproject/opensearch:2.11.1 | Analytics backend | 9200, 9600 | | opensearch-dashboards | shipsec-opensearch-dashboards | Custom build | Analytics UI | 5601 | | opensearch-init | shipsec-opensearch-init | curlimages/curl:8.5.0 | One-time initialization | - | | nginx | shipsec-nginx | nginx:1.25-alpine | Reverse proxy | 80 | **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:1-244]() ### Port Exposure Strategy Infrastructure services use a layered port exposure approach: 1. **Base layer** (`docker-compose.infra.yml`): Services use `expose` only, accessible within Docker network 2. **Development overlay** (`docker-compose.dev-ports.yml`): Binds ports to `127.0.0.1` for localhost access 3. **Production**: Nginx reverse proxy provides unified entry point on port 80 ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Development Mode" DevOverlay["docker-compose.dev-ports.yml"] DevPorts["Ports bound to 127.0.0.1:

This allows services to communicate using container names as hostnames. Network configuration: ```yaml networks: default: name: shipsec-network ``` Service discovery examples: - Backend connects to database: `postgres:5432` - Worker connects to Temporal: `temporal:7233` - Frontend (in prod) served by nginx, backend proxied at `/api` In development mode, nginx uses `host.docker.internal` to connect to PM2 services on the host machine. **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:449-451](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:242-244]() ## Environment Variables Production deployments require specific environment variables to be set before starting services. ### Required Variables **Security & Authentication:** - `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` - Service-to-service authentication token (auto-generated by init script) - `SECRET_STORE_MASTER_KEY` - Encryption key for secrets storage, must be exactly 32 characters **Optional - Authentication Provider:** - `AUTH_PROVIDER` - Set to `clerk` or `local` (default: `local`) - `CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` - Clerk public key (required if using Clerk) - `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` - Clerk secret key (required if using Clerk) **Optional - GitHub Integration:** - `GITHUB_APP_ID` - GitHub App ID - `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` - PEM private key (raw or base64-encoded) - `GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` - Webhook signature verification secret - `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID` / `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET` - OAuth credentials **Optional - Analytics:** - `DISABLE_ANALYTICS` - Set to `true` to disable telemetry (default: `false`) - `VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` - PostHog API key for frontend analytics - `POSTHOG_API_KEY` - PostHog API key for backend analytics **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:6-30](), [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:294-311]() ### Frontend Build Arguments Frontend container requires build-time environment variables to embed configuration into the static bundle: ```dockerfile ARG VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3211 ARG VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:3211 ARG VITE_AUTH_PROVIDER=local ARG VITE_DEFAULT_ORG_ID=local-dev ARG VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY="" ARG VITE_GIT_SHA=unknown ARG VITE_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY="" ARG VITE_OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_URL="" ``` These are set during `docker build` and cannot be changed at runtime without rebuilding. **Sources:** [Dockerfile:84-102]() ## Multi-Instance Support The infrastructure supports running multiple isolated application instances (0-9) against shared infrastructure. Each instance has: 1. **Isolated Database:** `shipsec_instance_N` 2. **Isolated Temporal Namespace:** `shipsec-dev-N` 3. **Instance-Scoped Kafka Topics:** `telemetry.logs.instance-N` 4. **Port Offset:** Base port + (instance × 100) Multi-instance is configured via the `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` environment variable. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Shared Infrastructure" PG["PostgreSQL
(Single container)"] Temporal["Temporal
(Single container)"] Kafka["Redpanda
(Single container)"] end subgraph "Instance 0" DB0["shipsec_instance_0"] NS0["Namespace: shipsec-dev-0"] Topics0["Topics: *.instance-0"] Ports0["Ports: 3211, 5173"] end subgraph "Instance 1" DB1["shipsec_instance_1"] NS1["Namespace: shipsec-dev-1"] Topics1["Topics: *.instance-1"] Ports1["Ports: 3311, 5273"] end PG --> DB0 PG --> DB1 Temporal --> NS0 Temporal --> NS1 Kafka --> Topics0 Kafka --> Topics1 ``` **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:239-274](), [scripts/instance-clean.sh:1-59](), [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:1-78]() ## Health Checks All infrastructure services define health checks to ensure proper startup ordering and availability monitoring. | Service | Health Check Command | Interval | Retries | |---------|---------------------|----------|---------| | postgres | `pg_isready -U shipsec` | 5s | 10 | | temporal | `tctl cluster health` | 30s | 5 | | temporal-ui | `curl -sf http://localhost:8080` | 30s | 5 | | minio | `curl -f http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live` | 30s | 5 | | redis | `redis-cli ping` | 30s | 5 | | redpanda | `curl -f http://localhost:9644/v1/status/ready` | 30s | 5 | | opensearch | `curl -f http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health` | 30s | 5 | | opensearch-dashboards | `curl -f http://localhost:5601/analytics/api/status` | 30s | 5 | | nginx | `curl -sf http://localhost/health` | 30s | 5 | Health checks enable dependency ordering using `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`. **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:16-20](), [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:48-52](), [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:206-210]() ## Security Modes The system supports two security configurations: ### Standard Mode (Default) - OpenSearch security plugin disabled - No TLS encryption - Single-tenant access - Faster startup (no certificate validation) - Suitable for single-user deployments Configuration: ```yaml environment: - DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true - DISABLE_INSTALL_DEMO_CONFIG=true ``` **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:149-150]() ### Secure Mode Enabled when TLS certificates exist in `docker/certs/`: - OpenSearch security plugin enabled - TLS encryption on OpenSearch - Multi-tenant isolation - Per-organization index patterns - Backend provisions tenants via internal API Auto-detection logic in `justfile`: ```bash if [ -f "docker/certs/root-ca.pem" ]; then SECURE_MODE=true fi ``` Certificate generation: `just generate-certs` runs `docker/scripts/generate-certs.sh` **Sources:** [justfile:228-232](), [justfile:88-129]() ## Usage Patterns ### Development: Infrastructure Only Start shared infrastructure with port access: ```bash just infra up # Uses: docker-compose.infra.yml + docker-compose.dev-ports.yml ``` Application services run via PM2 on the host. **Sources:** [justfile:485-508]() ### Development: Full Stack with PM2 Start infrastructure and PM2 application services: ```bash just dev start # Auto-detects Clerk credentials → secure mode # Otherwise → local auth mode ``` Stops only instance 0 infrastructure when running `just dev stop` (shared by all instances). **Sources:** [justfile:44-217]() ### Production: Pre-built Images Start using GHCR images: ```bash just prod start-latest # Pulls: ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-{backend,frontend,worker}:latest # Uses: docker-compose.full.yml ``` **Sources:** [justfile:315-351]() ### Production: Local Build Build and start from source: ```bash just prod build # Builds local images with GIT_SHA tag # Uses: docker-compose.full.yml ``` **Sources:** [justfile:284-303]() ## Orchestration Integration The compose setup integrates with the release workflow to enable version-specific deployments: 1. **GitHub Actions** builds multi-arch images (amd64/arm64) 2. Images tagged with version: `ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-backend:X.Y.Z` 3. Latest release also tagged: `ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-backend:latest` 4. `SHIPSEC_TAG` environment variable selects version Version selection: ```bash export SHIPSEC_TAG=1.0.0 just prod start # Pulls: ghcr.io/shipsecai/studio-backend:1.0.0 ``` **Sources:** [.github/workflows/release.yml:1-341](), [docker/docker-compose.full.yml:266]()

# Security Modes
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [.gitignore](.gitignore) - [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml](docker/docker-compose.infra.yml) - [justfile](justfile) - [pm2.config.cjs](pm2.config.cjs) - [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh](scripts/db-reset-instance.sh) - [scripts/instance-clean.sh](scripts/instance-clean.sh)
ShipSec Studio supports two security modes: **Local Mode** and **Secure Mode**. Local Mode provides a simplified development experience with no authentication or multi-tenant isolation, while Secure Mode enables Clerk-based authentication, TLS encryption, and OpenSearch multi-tenancy for production deployments. For information about production deployment configuration, see [Production Deployment](#9.6). For environment variable configuration, see [Environment Variables](#9.8). ## Overview ShipSec Studio automatically detects which security mode to operate in based on the presence of specific configuration files or environment variables: - **Local Mode**: Default mode for development. No authentication required, OpenSearch security disabled, faster startup. - **Secure Mode**: Production mode with Clerk authentication, TLS certificates, and OpenSearch Security plugin enabled for multi-tenant data isolation. The mode detection logic differs between development and production environments: **Development Mode Security Detection** ```mermaid graph TD Start["just dev"] CheckEnv["Check backend/.env"] HasClerk{"CLERK_SECRET_KEY present?"} LocalMode["Local Mode"] SecureMode["Secure Mode"] Start --> CheckEnv CheckEnv --> HasClerk HasClerk -->|No| LocalMode HasClerk -->|Yes| SecureMode LocalMode --> LocalConfig["OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=false
DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true
No TLS required"] SecureMode --> SecureConfig["OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=true
Auto-generate certs if missing
Enable Security Plugin"] ``` **Production Mode Security Detection** ```mermaid graph TD Start["just prod"] CheckCerts["Check docker/certs/root-ca.pem"] HasCerts{"TLS certificates exist?"} StandardMode["Standard Mode"] SecureMode["Secure Mode"] Start --> CheckCerts CheckCerts --> HasCerts HasCerts -->|No| StandardMode HasCerts -->|Yes| SecureMode StandardMode --> StandardCompose["docker-compose.full.yml
No security plugin"] SecureMode --> SecureCompose["docker-compose.infra.yml +
docker-compose.prod.yml
Requires password env vars"] ``` Sources: [justfile:64-74](), [justfile:228-232]() ## Local Mode Local Mode is the default development configuration designed for rapid iteration without authentication overhead. ### Configuration | Component | Setting | Value | |-----------|---------|-------| | Authentication | Mode | None (local auth) | | OpenSearch | Security Plugin | Disabled (`DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true`) | | OpenSearch | TLS | Not required | | OpenSearch | Access | Direct HTTP on port 9200 | | Multi-tenancy | Isolation | None (single shared instance) | | Startup Time | Duration | ~30 seconds | ### Startup Sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant J as justfile participant ENV as backend/.env participant DC as docker-compose participant PM2 as PM2 participant OS as OpenSearch J->>ENV: Read CLERK_SECRET_KEY ENV-->>J: Not set J->>J: Set SECURE_MODE=false J->>DC: Start docker-compose.infra.yml +
docker-compose.dev-ports.yml DC->>OS: Start with DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true OS-->>DC: Ready on http://localhost:9200 J->>PM2: Start with OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=false
OPENSEARCH_URL=http://localhost:9200 PM2-->>J: Apps started J->>J: Display "local auth mode" message ``` ### Environment Variables In Local Mode, the following environment variables are configured: ```bash # PM2 Configuration (pm2.config.cjs) OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=false OPENSEARCH_URL=http://localhost:9200 NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 # Not set ``` Sources: [justfile:131-163](), [pm2.config.cjs:114-144](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:143-170]() ## Secure Mode Secure Mode enables full authentication, encryption, and multi-tenant isolation for production deployments. ### Configuration | Component | Setting | Value | |-----------|---------|-------| | Authentication | Mode | Clerk | | OpenSearch | Security Plugin | Enabled | | OpenSearch | TLS | Required (auto-generated) | | OpenSearch | Access | HTTPS with certificate validation | | Multi-tenancy | Isolation | Per-organization indices and access control | | Startup Time | Duration | ~120 seconds (includes security initialization) | ### TLS Certificate Generation Secure Mode requires TLS certificates for OpenSearch communication. If certificates don't exist when starting in Secure Mode, they are automatically generated: ```mermaid graph TB Start["Start Secure Mode"] CheckCerts{"Certificates exist?
(docker/certs/root-ca.pem)"} GenCerts["Execute docker/scripts/generate-certs.sh"] CreateCA["Generate Root CA
(root-ca.pem, root-ca-key.pem)"] CreateNode["Generate Node Certificate
(opensearch.pem, opensearch-key.pem)"] CreateAdmin["Generate Admin Certificate
(admin.pem, admin-key.pem)"] StartInfra["Start Infrastructure"] Start --> CheckCerts CheckCerts -->|No| GenCerts CheckCerts -->|Yes| StartInfra GenCerts --> CreateCA CreateCA --> CreateNode CreateNode --> CreateAdmin CreateAdmin --> StartInfra ``` The certificate generation script creates: - **Root CA**: Self-signed certificate authority - **Node Certificate**: For OpenSearch node communication - **Admin Certificate**: For administrative access All certificates use 2048-bit RSA keys and are valid for 365 days. Sources: [justfile:92-97](), [justfile:449-461]() ### Startup Sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant J as justfile participant ENV as backend/.env participant Certs as generate-certs.sh participant DC as docker-compose participant OS as OpenSearch participant PM2 as PM2 J->>ENV: Read CLERK_SECRET_KEY ENV-->>J: Set (e.g., sk_test_...) J->>J: Set SECURE_MODE=true J->>Certs: Check docker/certs/root-ca.pem exists Certs-->>J: Missing J->>Certs: Execute generate-certs.sh Certs-->>J: Certificates created J->>DC: Start docker-compose.infra.yml +
docker-compose.dev-secure.yml +
docker-compose.dev-ports.yml DC->>OS: Mount certs, enable security plugin OS->>OS: Initialize security (120s) OS-->>DC: Ready on https://localhost:9200 J->>PM2: Start with OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=true
NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 PM2-->>J: Apps started J->>J: Display "secure mode" message ``` ### Environment Variables In Secure Mode, additional environment variables are required: ```bash # Required for Secure Mode CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... # Triggers secure mode detection OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD=your-secure-password OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD=your-secure-password # PM2 Configuration OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED=true NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 # Trust self-signed certs ``` Sources: [justfile:88-130](), [pm2.config.cjs:114-116](), [justfile:246-253]() ## Mode Detection Implementation ### Development Mode Detection The `just dev` command detects the security mode by reading the `backend/.env` file: ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "justfile:64-74" ReadEnv["Read backend/.env"] ExtractKey["Extract CLERK_SECRET_KEY
using grep + cut"] CheckEmpty{"Key non-empty?"} SetSecure["SECURE_MODE=true"] SetLocal["SECURE_MODE=false"] end ReadEnv --> ExtractKey ExtractKey --> CheckEmpty CheckEmpty -->|Yes| SetSecure CheckEmpty -->|No| SetLocal ``` **Code Implementation:** ```bash # justfile:64-68 CLERK_KEY="" if [ -f "backend/.env" ]; then CLERK_KEY=$(grep -E '^CLERK_SECRET_KEY=' backend/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"' | tr -d "'" | xargs || true) fi # justfile:70-74 if [ -n "$CLERK_KEY" ]; then SECURE_MODE=true else SECURE_MODE=false fi ``` ### Production Mode Detection The `just prod` command detects the security mode by checking for TLS certificate files: ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "justfile:228-232" CheckFile["Check docker/certs/root-ca.pem"] FileExists{"File exists?"} SetSecure["SECURE_MODE=true
Use docker-compose.prod.yml"] SetStandard["SECURE_MODE=false
Use docker-compose.full.yml"] end CheckFile --> FileExists FileExists -->|Yes| SetSecure FileExists -->|No| SetStandard ``` **Code Implementation:** ```bash # justfile:228-232 if [ -f "docker/certs/root-ca.pem" ]; then SECURE_MODE=true else SECURE_MODE=false fi ``` Sources: [justfile:64-74](), [justfile:228-232]() ## OpenSearch Security Configuration When Secure Mode is enabled, the OpenSearch Security plugin provides multi-tenant data isolation. ### Security Plugin Lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Disabled: Local Mode [*] --> Enabled: Secure Mode Disabled --> Running: DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN=true Enabled --> CertsMount: Mount TLS certificates CertsMount --> SecurityInit: Run security init SecurityInit --> Running: Plugin initialized Running --> [*] note right of SecurityInit Initialization includes: - Create internal users - Configure role mappings - Set up tenant isolation - Enable TLS end note ``` ### Configuration Files | File | Purpose | Mode | |------|---------|------| | `docker/certs/root-ca.pem` | Root CA certificate | Secure | | `docker/certs/opensearch.pem` | Node certificate | Secure | | `docker/certs/admin.pem` | Admin certificate | Secure | | `docker/docker-compose.dev-secure.yml` | Secure mode Docker config | Secure | | `docker/docker-compose.infra.yml` | Base infrastructure | Both | ### Security Initialization The security initialization process configures the OpenSearch Security plugin: ```mermaid graph TD Start["Container starts"] LoadCerts["Load certificates from
/usr/share/opensearch/config/certs/"] EnablePlugin["Enable Security Plugin
(remove DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN)"] InitUsers["Initialize internal_users.yml
(admin, kibanaserver, etc.)"] InitRoles["Initialize roles_mapping.yml
(tenant isolation)"] EnableTLS["Enable TLS on port 9200"] Ready["Ready for connections
(HTTPS required)"] Start --> LoadCerts LoadCerts --> EnablePlugin EnablePlugin --> InitUsers InitUsers --> InitRoles InitRoles --> EnableTLS EnableTLS --> Ready ``` The `just security-init` command can be used to reinitialize or update the security configuration: ```bash # Initialize security index just security-init # Force reinitialize (update configuration) just security-init --force ``` Sources: [justfile:464-469](), [justfile:100-110]() ## Multi-Tenant Isolation Secure Mode enables per-organization data isolation in OpenSearch through the Security plugin's tenant system. ### Tenant Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "OpenSearch Cluster" subgraph "Tenant: org_abc123" Indices1["logs-org_abc123-*
traces-org_abc123-*"] end subgraph "Tenant: org_def456" Indices2["logs-org_def456-*
traces-org_def456-*"] end SecurityPlugin["Security Plugin
(Role Mappings)"] end subgraph "Backend Services" ClerkAuth["Clerk Authentication"] OrgContext["Organization Context"] end ClerkAuth --> OrgContext OrgContext --> SecurityPlugin SecurityPlugin --> Indices1 SecurityPlugin --> Indices2 ``` ### Access Control Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Backend participant Clerk participant OS as OpenSearch User->>Backend: Request with token Backend->>Clerk: Validate token Clerk-->>Backend: User + Organization ID Backend->>Backend: Extract orgId (e.g., org_abc123) Backend->>OS: Query with tenant header
X-Security-Tenant: org_abc123 OS->>OS: Apply tenant filter OS-->>Backend: Filtered results Backend-->>User: Response ``` ### Tenant Provisioning When a new organization is created in Clerk, the backend automatically provisions OpenSearch tenant resources: 1. **Tenant Creation**: Security plugin creates isolated tenant space 2. **Index Pattern**: Indices prefixed with `{index}-{orgId}-*` 3. **Role Mapping**: Map organization ID to tenant access 4. **Index Templates**: Apply templates for log/trace indices Sources: [justfile:88-130](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:143-170]() ## Password Management Secure Mode requires password management for OpenSearch internal users. ### Password Hashing OpenSearch requires BCrypt-hashed passwords for internal users. The `just hash-password` command generates compatible hashes: ```bash # Interactive mode (prompts for password) just hash-password # Direct mode (password as argument) just hash-password "my-secure-password" ``` **Implementation:** ```bash # justfile:472-480 hash-password password="": #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail chmod +x docker/scripts/hash-password.sh if [ -n "{{password}}" ]; then docker/scripts/hash-password.sh "{{password}}" else docker/scripts/hash-password.sh fi ``` The generated hash can be used in OpenSearch configuration files for internal users. Sources: [justfile:472-480]() ## Mode Comparison ### Feature Matrix | Feature | Local Mode | Secure Mode | |---------|-----------|-------------| | **Authentication** | None (local) | Clerk | | **OpenSearch Access** | HTTP (no TLS) | HTTPS (TLS required) | | **Security Plugin** | Disabled | Enabled | | **Multi-tenancy** | No | Yes (per-organization) | | **Certificate Generation** | Not required | Auto-generated or manual | | **Password Management** | Not required | Required (`OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD`) | | **Startup Time** | ~30 seconds | ~120 seconds | | **Use Case** | Local development | Production/multi-tenant | | **Data Isolation** | None | Organization-level | | **Analytics Access** | Direct (http://localhost/analytics) | Authenticated | ### Startup Command Comparison **Local Mode:** ```bash # Automatic (no Clerk key in backend/.env) just dev # Explicit infrastructure start docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up -d ``` **Secure Mode:** ```bash # Automatic (Clerk key present in backend/.env) just dev # Manual certificate generation just generate-certs # Explicit infrastructure start with security docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-secure.yml \ -f docker/docker-compose.dev-ports.yml up -d ``` Sources: [justfile:44-216](), [justfile:221-355]() ## Switching Between Modes ### Development: Local to Secure 1. Add Clerk credentials to `backend/.env`: ```bash CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... ``` 2. Set OpenSearch passwords: ```bash export OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD='your-secure-password' export OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD='your-secure-password' ``` 3. Restart development environment: ```bash just dev stop just dev ``` Certificates will be auto-generated on startup. ### Development: Secure to Local 1. Remove `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` from `backend/.env` 2. Restart development environment: ```bash just dev stop just dev ``` ### Production: Standard to Secure 1. Generate TLS certificates: ```bash just generate-certs ``` 2. Set required passwords: ```bash export OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD='your-secure-password' export OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD='your-secure-password' ``` 3. Start in secure mode: ```bash just prod ``` Sources: [justfile:44-163](), [justfile:221-276]() ## Configuration Reference ### Environment Variables by Mode **Both Modes:** | Variable | Purpose | Default | |----------|---------|---------| | `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` | Instance number (0-9) | `0` | | `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS` | Temporal server address | `localhost:7233` | | `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL connection | `postgresql://shipsec:shipsec@localhost:5433/shipsec_instance_0` | **Local Mode Only:** | Variable | Purpose | Default | |----------|---------|---------| | `OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED` | Security plugin status | `false` | | `OPENSEARCH_URL` | OpenSearch endpoint | `http://localhost:9200` | **Secure Mode Only:** | Variable | Purpose | Required | |----------|---------|----------| | `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` | Clerk API secret | Yes | | `OPENSEARCH_SECURITY_ENABLED` | Security plugin status | `true` | | `OPENSEARCH_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Admin user password | Yes (production) | | `OPENSEARCH_DASHBOARDS_PASSWORD` | Dashboards password | Yes (production) | | `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` | Trust self-signed certs | `0` | ### Docker Compose File Selection **Development:** ```bash # Local Mode docker-compose.infra.yml + docker-compose.dev-ports.yml # Secure Mode docker-compose.infra.yml + docker-compose.dev-secure.yml + docker-compose.dev-ports.yml ``` **Production:** ```bash # Standard Mode (no security) docker-compose.full.yml # Secure Mode (with security) docker-compose.infra.yml + docker-compose.prod.yml ``` Sources: [justfile:100-102](), [justfile:134](), [justfile:236-239](), [pm2.config.cjs:296-374]()

# Multi-Instance Support
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [.gitignore](.gitignore) - [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml](docker/docker-compose.infra.yml) - [justfile](justfile) - [pm2.config.cjs](pm2.config.cjs) - [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh](scripts/db-reset-instance.sh) - [scripts/instance-clean.sh](scripts/instance-clean.sh)
ShipSec Studio supports running up to 10 isolated development instances (numbered 0-9) on the same machine. This enables multiple developers on a shared machine, testing different workflow versions in parallel, or isolating experimental features from stable development. Each instance runs on offset ports, uses its own PostgreSQL database, Temporal namespace, and Kafka topics, while sharing common infrastructure services (PostgreSQL server, Temporal server, Redis, MinIO, Kafka broker, OpenSearch, Loki, Nginx). For information about the overall development setup, see [Development Setup](#1.3). For infrastructure service configuration, see [Docker Compose Setup](#10.1). ## Instance Numbering Instances are identified by a number from 0 to 9, configured via the `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` environment variable or a `.shipsec-instance` file in the repository root. The active instance determines: - Application port offsets (+100 per instance) - Database name (`shipsec_instance_N`) - Temporal namespace and task queue (`shipsec-dev-N`) - Kafka topic suffixes (`.instance-N`) - PM2 process names (`shipsec-*-N`) The resolution order for instance number is: 1. `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` environment variable (highest priority) 2. Contents of `.shipsec-instance` file 3. Default to instance 0 [justfile:49-57]() implements the instance resolution logic with fallback behavior. **Sources:** [justfile:44-216](), [pm2.config.cjs:240-241]() ### Instance Resolution Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["Start application"] CheckEnv{"SHIPSEC_INSTANCE
env var set?"} UseEnv["Use env var value"] CheckFile{".shipsec-instance
file exists?"} ReadFile["Read file contents"] UseDefault["Use default: 0"] Export["Export SHIPSEC_INSTANCE"] Start --> CheckEnv CheckEnv -->|Yes| UseEnv CheckEnv -->|No| CheckFile CheckFile -->|Yes| ReadFile CheckFile -->|No| UseDefault UseEnv --> Export ReadFile --> Export UseDefault --> Export Export --> AppStart["Application startup with instance N"] ``` **Sources:** [justfile:49-57]() ## Port Offsetting Each instance uses a base port plus an offset of `N * 100`, where N is the instance number. This formula ensures no port conflicts when running multiple instances simultaneously. | Service | Base Port | Instance 0 | Instance 1 | Instance 2 | Formula | |---------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|---------| | Frontend | 5173 | 5173 | 5273 | 5373 | 5173 + N*100 | | Backend | 3211 | 3211 | 3311 | 3411 | 3211 + N*100 | The Temporal worker does not expose an HTTP port, so no offset is needed. It connects to the shared Temporal server using instance-specific namespaces and task queues. [justfile:61-62]() calculates instance-specific ports for display purposes. [pm2.config.cjs:273-275]() provides the helper function `getInstancePort()` that applies the offset formula. [backend/src/main.ts:34-42]() generates CORS origins for all 10 possible instances to allow cross-origin requests during development. **Sources:** [justfile:61-62](), [pm2.config.cjs:273-275](), [backend/src/main.ts:34-42]() ### Port Mapping Diagram ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Instance 0" FE0["Frontend
:5173"] BE0["Backend
:3211"] end subgraph "Instance 1" FE1["Frontend
:5273"] BE1["Backend
:3311"] end subgraph "Instance 2" FE2["Frontend
:5373"] BE2["Backend
:3411"] end subgraph "Shared Infrastructure" PG["PostgreSQL
:5433"] TEMP["Temporal
:7233"] REDIS["Redis
:6379"] KAFKA["Redpanda
:9092"] MINIO["MinIO
:9000"] OS["OpenSearch
:9200"] end FE0 --> BE0 FE1 --> BE1 FE2 --> BE2 BE0 --> PG BE1 --> PG BE2 --> PG BE0 --> TEMP BE1 --> TEMP BE2 --> TEMP BE0 -.-> REDIS BE1 -.-> REDIS BE2 -.-> REDIS ``` **Sources:** [justfile:61-62](), [pm2.config.cjs:299](), [backend/src/main.ts:34-42]() ## Instance-Scoped Resources While infrastructure services are shared, each instance maintains isolated resources to prevent cross-contamination of data and workflows. ### PostgreSQL Databases Each instance uses a dedicated database on the shared PostgreSQL server. Database names follow the pattern `shipsec_instance_N`: - Instance 0: `shipsec_instance_0` - Instance 1: `shipsec_instance_1` - Instance 2: `shipsec_instance_2` - ... - Instance 9: `shipsec_instance_9` The `DATABASE_URL` environment variable is automatically set to point to the correct instance database: ``` postgresql://shipsec:shipsec@localhost:5433/shipsec_instance_N ``` [pm2.config.cjs:241]() constructs the instance-specific database URL. [pm2.config.cjs:244-249]() sets this as `DATABASE_URL` in the development environment, with production requiring explicit configuration. Database creation happens automatically during the first startup via the `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` initialization script [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:15](). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:241](), [pm2.config.cjs:244-249](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:4-21]() ### Temporal Namespaces and Task Queues Each instance operates within its own Temporal namespace to isolate workflow executions. The namespace and task queue names follow the pattern `shipsec-dev-N`: - Instance 0: namespace=`shipsec-dev-0`, task queue=`shipsec-dev-0` - Instance 1: namespace=`shipsec-dev-1`, task queue=`shipsec-dev-1` - Instance 2: namespace=`shipsec-dev-2`, task queue=`shipsec-dev-2` [pm2.config.cjs:323-324]() sets `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE` and `TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE` for the backend, and [pm2.config.cjs:366-367]() does the same for the worker. This ensures that workflows started by backend instance N are only executed by worker instance N, providing complete execution isolation. **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:323-324](), [pm2.config.cjs:366-367]() ### Kafka Topics Telemetry streams (traces, logs, node I/O, agent traces) use instance-scoped Kafka topics to prevent mixing events from different instances. Topic names include the instance suffix `.instance-N`: - `telemetry.logs.instance-0` - `telemetry.events.instance-0` - `telemetry.node-io.instance-0` - `telemetry.agent-trace.instance-0` However, looking at [pm2.config.cjs:304-319](), the base topic names are used without instance suffixes. This suggests topics are shared across instances in the current implementation, with producer/consumer group IDs providing isolation through instance-specific client and group IDs. Backend Kafka configuration: - `LOG_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID`: `shipsec-backend-N` - `LOG_KAFKA_GROUP_ID`: `shipsec-backend-log-consumer-N` - `EVENT_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID`: `shipsec-backend-events-N` - `EVENT_KAFKA_GROUP_ID`: `shipsec-event-ingestor-N` - `NODE_IO_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID`: `shipsec-backend-node-io-N` - `NODE_IO_KAFKA_GROUP_ID`: `shipsec-node-io-ingestor-N` - `AGENT_TRACE_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID`: `shipsec-backend-agent-trace-N` - `AGENT_TRACE_KAFKA_GROUP_ID`: `shipsec-agent-trace-ingestor-N` Worker Kafka configuration uses similar patterns [pm2.config.cjs:362-364](). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:303-319](), [pm2.config.cjs:360-364]() ### PM2 Process Names PM2 manages three processes per instance, each with an instance-suffixed name to allow independent lifecycle management: - `shipsec-frontend-N` - `shipsec-backend-N` - `shipsec-worker-N` [pm2.config.cjs:291](), [pm2.config.cjs:331](), and [pm2.config.cjs:345]() define the process names. [justfile:60]() constructs the comma-separated list of process names for PM2 commands: `PM2_APPS="shipsec-frontend-${INST},shipsec-backend-${INST},shipsec-worker-${INST}"`. **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:289-395](), [justfile:60]() ## Shared Infrastructure Infrastructure services run as singleton Docker containers serving all instances. This reduces resource consumption and simplifies management. Shared services include: | Service | Container Name | Purpose | Port | |---------|---------------|---------|------| | PostgreSQL | `shipsec-postgres` | Multi-database server | 5433 | | Temporal | `shipsec-temporal` | Multi-namespace orchestration | 7233 | | Temporal UI | `shipsec-temporal-ui` | Workflow inspection | 8081 | | Redis | `shipsec-redis` | Caching and terminal streams | 6379 | | MinIO | `shipsec-minio` | Object storage | 9000 | | Redpanda | `shipsec-redpanda` | Kafka-compatible broker | 9092 | | Redpanda Console | `shipsec-redpanda-console` | Kafka UI | 8082 | | OpenSearch | `shipsec-opensearch` | Analytics and search | 9200 | | OpenSearch Dashboards | `shipsec-opensearch-dashboards` | Analytics UI | 5601 | | Loki | `shipsec-loki` | Log aggregation | 3100 | | Nginx | `shipsec-nginx` | Reverse proxy | 80 | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml]() defines all shared infrastructure services. These containers are managed independently of instance lifecycle: starting instance 0 brings up the shared infrastructure, and stopping instance 0 tears it down. Non-zero instances assume infrastructure is already running [justfile:177-184](), [justfile:202-211](). **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:1-243](), [justfile:177-184](), [justfile:202-211]() ### Infrastructure Dependency Diagram ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Instance 0 Processes" FE0["shipsec-frontend-0"] BE0["shipsec-backend-0"] WK0["shipsec-worker-0"] end subgraph "Instance 1 Processes" FE1["shipsec-frontend-1"] BE1["shipsec-backend-1"] WK1["shipsec-worker-1"] end subgraph "Instance N Processes" FEN["shipsec-frontend-N"] BEN["shipsec-backend-N"] WKN["shipsec-worker-N"] end subgraph "Shared Docker Containers" PG[(shipsec-postgres)] TEMP[shipsec-temporal] REDIS[(shipsec-redis)] MINIO[(shipsec-minio)] KAFKA[shipsec-redpanda] OS[shipsec-opensearch] LOKI[shipsec-loki] NGINX[shipsec-nginx] end subgraph "Instance 0 Resources" DB0[("shipsec_instance_0

The workflow differs based on whether the instance is 0 (primary) or non-zero (secondary). ### Starting Instance 0 When starting instance 0, the justfile: 1. Resolves the instance number (defaults to 0) 2. Checks for required `.env` files 3. Detects auth mode (local vs secure) based on `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` presence 4. Starts Docker Compose infrastructure [justfile:102]() or [justfile:134]() 5. Waits for PostgreSQL health check [justfile:106]() or [justfile:138]() 6. Optionally waits for OpenSearch security initialization (secure mode) [justfile:109-110]() 7. Starts PM2 processes with instance-specific configuration [justfile:114-115]() or [justfile:142-144]() 8. Displays access URLs and instance information [justfile:117-169]() [justfile:76-173]() implements the `start` action logic. ### Starting Instance 1-9 When starting non-zero instances: 1. Resolves the instance number from environment 2. Checks for required `.env` files 3. Detects auth mode 4. **Skips infrastructure startup** (assumes instance 0 already started it) 5. Directly starts PM2 processes with instance-specific configuration 6. Displays access URLs with note that nginx routes to instance 0 [justfile:157-160]() The same code path handles both, with conditional infrastructure management based on instance number [justfile:177-184](). **Sources:** [justfile:44-216]() ### Stopping Instances The `just dev stop` command: 1. Resolves the active instance number 2. Deletes PM2 processes for that instance [justfile:176]() 3. Only stops Docker infrastructure if instance is 0 [justfile:177-184]() This ensures secondary instances can stop independently without affecting other running instances or shared infrastructure. **Sources:** [justfile:174-186]() ### Instance Lifecycle Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Just as justfile participant Docker participant PM2 participant DB as PostgreSQL participant Temp as Temporal User->>Just: just dev start (SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=1) Just->>Just: Resolve instance=1 Just->>Just: Check .env files Just->>Just: Detect auth mode alt Instance == 0 Just->>Docker: docker compose up -d (infra) Docker->>DB: Start postgres container Docker->>Temp: Start temporal container Just->>DB: Wait for health check Just->>Temp: Wait for ready else Instance > 0 Just->>Just: Skip infra (assume running) end Just->>PM2: pm2 startOrReload shipsec-*-1 PM2->>PM2: Start frontend-1 (:5273) PM2->>PM2: Start backend-1 (:3311) PM2->>PM2: Start worker-1 (ns: shipsec-dev-1) PM2->>DB: Connect to shipsec_instance_1 PM2->>Temp: Connect to shipsec-dev-1 Just-->>User: Instance 1 ready at :5273 User->>Just: just dev stop (SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=1) Just->>PM2: pm2 delete shipsec-*-1 alt Instance == 0 Just->>Docker: docker compose down else Instance > 0 Just->>Just: Skip infra shutdown end ``` **Sources:** [justfile:44-216]() ## Database Isolation Each instance maintains a separate PostgreSQL database on the shared server. The database initialization script creates all instance databases during first boot. ### Database Creation The PostgreSQL container uses a multi-database initialization script mounted at `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:15](). This script creates databases for all 10 possible instances on first container startup: - `shipsec_instance_0` - `shipsec_instance_1` - ... - `shipsec_instance_9` - `temporal` (Temporal system database) Each instance database is owned by the `shipsec` user with full privileges. **Sources:** [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:4-21]() ### Database URL Configuration The backend and worker processes connect to their instance database using the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable constructed by PM2 config: ```javascript const instanceDatabaseUrl = `postgresql://shipsec:shipsec@localhost:5433/shipsec_instance_${instanceNum}`; ``` [pm2.config.cjs:241]() constructs the URL, and [pm2.config.cjs:246-249]() assigns it to the environment. This configuration only applies in development; production deployments must provide explicit `DATABASE_URL` values [pm2.config.cjs:244-249](). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:240-249](), [pm2.config.cjs:297-301](), [pm2.config.cjs:357-358]() ### Schema Migrations Database migrations run automatically when the backend starts using Drizzle ORM. Each instance applies migrations independently to its own database. The migration path is managed by the backend's migration commands: ```bash bun --cwd=backend run migration:push ``` When resetting an instance database, the migration must be re-run to restore the schema [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:66](). **Sources:** [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:62-72]() ## Environment File Resolution PM2 configuration supports instance-specific environment files stored in `.instances/instance-N/` directories. The `resolveEnvFile()` function checks for instance-specific files first, then falls back to the application's root `.env` file: 1. Check `.instances/instance-N/{app}.env` 2. Fall back to `{app}/.env` [pm2.config.cjs:278-286]() implements this resolution logic. This allows per-instance customization of environment variables without modifying the main `.env` files, useful for testing different configurations simultaneously. **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:267-286](), [pm2.config.cjs:296](), [pm2.config.cjs:335](), [pm2.config.cjs:350]() ## Cleanup Operations ShipSec Studio provides scripts for cleaning instance-specific data while preserving shared infrastructure. ### Database Reset The `db-reset-instance.sh` script drops and recreates an instance database, then re-runs migrations: ```bash ./scripts/db-reset-instance.sh [instance_number] ``` Implementation steps [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:1-78](): 1. Find PostgreSQL container using Docker Compose 2. Drop database `shipsec_instance_N` 3. Create fresh database with owner `shipsec` 4. Grant all privileges 5. Run Drizzle migrations using instance-specific `DATABASE_URL` **Sources:** [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh:1-78]() ### Full Instance Cleanup The `instance-clean.sh` script performs a complete cleanup of instance resources: ```bash ./scripts/instance-clean.sh [instance_number] ``` Implementation steps [scripts/instance-clean.sh:1-59](): 1. Reset database (drop/recreate + migrations) 2. Delete Temporal namespace using `temporal` CLI (best-effort) 3. Delete instance-scoped Kafka topics from Redpanda (best-effort) Best-effort operations continue even if the target resources don't exist, ensuring idempotent cleanup [scripts/instance-clean.sh:44](), [scripts/instance-clean.sh:54](). **Sources:** [scripts/instance-clean.sh:1-59]() ### Justfile Clean Command The `just dev clean` command provides user-facing cleanup: ```bash just dev clean # Cleans active instance SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=2 just dev clean # Cleans instance 2 ``` For instance 0, this command: 1. Stops PM2 processes 2. Tears down Docker Compose infrastructure with volume removal [justfile:204-207]() For non-zero instances: 1. Stops PM2 processes only 2. Leaves shared infrastructure running [justfile:210]() **Sources:** [justfile:198-212]() ### Cleanup Workflow Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["just dev clean
(SHIPSEC_INSTANCE=N)"] StopPM2["Stop PM2 processes
shipsec-*-N"] CheckInst{"Instance
number?"} StopInfra["docker compose down -v
(remove volumes)"] Skip["Skip infra cleanup
(preserve for other instances)"] Done["Cleanup complete"] Start --> StopPM2 StopPM2 --> CheckInst CheckInst -->|0| StopInfra CheckInst -->|1-9| Skip StopInfra --> Done Skip --> Done style StopInfra fill:#ffcccc style Skip fill:#ccffcc ``` **Sources:** [justfile:198-212]() ## Nginx Routing and Instance 0 The Nginx reverse proxy always routes requests from `http://localhost` to instance 0, regardless of which instances are running. This is because Nginx configuration uses `host.docker.internal:5173` and `host.docker.internal:3211` [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:221](), which resolve to the default ports (instance 0 ports). Secondary instances (1-9) must be accessed directly via their offset ports: - Instance 1 frontend: `http://localhost:5273` - Instance 1 backend: `http://localhost:3311` - Instance 2 frontend: `http://localhost:5373` - Instance 2 backend: `http://localhost:3411` This is noted in the startup messages [justfile:156-160](): ``` 💡 Instance ${INST}: access your app directly at http://localhost:${FRONTEND_PORT} (nginx always routes to instance 0) ``` **Sources:** [justfile:156-160](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:212-229]() ## Multi-Instance Resource Summary | Resource | Scope | Naming Pattern | Configuration | |----------|-------|----------------|---------------| | Frontend Port | Instance | `5173 + N*100` | [pm2.config.cjs:273-275]() | | Backend Port | Instance | `3211 + N*100` | [pm2.config.cjs:299]() | | Database | Instance | `shipsec_instance_N` | [pm2.config.cjs:241]() | | Temporal Namespace | Instance | `shipsec-dev-N` | [pm2.config.cjs:323]() | | Temporal Task Queue | Instance | `shipsec-dev-N` | [pm2.config.cjs:324]() | | Kafka Client ID | Instance | `shipsec-{service}-{stream}-N` | [pm2.config.cjs:306-318]() | | Kafka Group ID | Instance | `shipsec-{service}-{stream}-consumer-N` | [pm2.config.cjs:306-318]() | | PM2 Process Name | Instance | `shipsec-{service}-N` | [pm2.config.cjs:291]() | | PostgreSQL Server | Shared | `shipsec-postgres` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:3]() | | Temporal Server | Shared | `shipsec-temporal` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:24]() | | Redis | Shared | `shipsec-redis` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:75]() | | MinIO | Shared | `shipsec-minio` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:56]() | | Redpanda | Shared | `shipsec-redpanda` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:105]() | | OpenSearch | Shared | `shipsec-opensearch` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:143]() | | Loki | Shared | `shipsec-loki` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:89]() | | Nginx | Shared | `shipsec-nginx` | [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:213]() | **Sources:** [justfile:44-216](), [pm2.config.cjs:240-375](), [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml:1-243]()

# PM2 Configuration
Relevant source files The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page: - [.gitignore](.gitignore) - [docker/docker-compose.infra.yml](docker/docker-compose.infra.yml) - [justfile](justfile) - [pm2.config.cjs](pm2.config.cjs) - [scripts/db-reset-instance.sh](scripts/db-reset-instance.sh) - [scripts/instance-clean.sh](scripts/instance-clean.sh)
## Purpose and Scope This document describes the PM2 (Process Manager 2) configuration for ShipSec Studio's development environment. PM2 manages the frontend, backend, and worker processes during local development, providing hot-reload capabilities and multi-instance isolation. This configuration is defined in [pm2.config.cjs]() and is invoked by the `just dev` command described in [1.3 Development Setup](#1.3). For production deployments using Docker, see [11.1 Production Setup](#11.1). For infrastructure configuration, see [10.1 Docker Compose Setup](#10.1). **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:1-395](), [justfile:44-216]() --- ## Multi-Instance Support ShipSec Studio supports running up to 10 isolated development instances (0-9) on a single machine simultaneously. Each instance runs on offset ports with separate database namespaces and Kafka topics. ### Instance Resolution The active instance is resolved in the following priority order: 1. `SHIPSEC_INSTANCE` environment variable 2. `.shipsec-instance` file in repository root 3. Default: instance `0` ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["PM2 Configuration Loading"] CheckEnv{"SHIPSEC_INSTANCE
env var set?"} CheckFile{".shipsec-instance
file exists?"} UseEnv["Use env var value"] ReadFile["Read file value"] UseDefault["Use default: 0"] SetInst["Set instanceNum"] Start --> CheckEnv CheckEnv -->|Yes| UseEnv CheckEnv -->|No| CheckFile CheckFile -->|Yes| ReadFile CheckFile -->|No| UseDefault UseEnv --> SetInst ReadFile --> SetInst UseDefault --> SetInst ``` **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:240-250](), [justfile:49-57]() ### Instance-Specific Naming Each PM2 app is named with an instance suffix to prevent conflicts: | App Type | Name Pattern | Example (Instance 2) | |----------|-------------|---------------------| | Frontend | `shipsec-frontend-${N}` | `shipsec-frontend-2` | | Backend | `shipsec-backend-${N}` | `shipsec-backend-2` | | Worker | `shipsec-worker-${N}` | `shipsec-worker-2` | **Sources:** [pm2.config.cjs:291-345](), [justfile:60-63]() --- ## Port Offsetting Strategy Each instance uses a unique port offset to avoid conflicts.
